title: Amazon Basics Slim Velvet Hangers – A Closet’s Best Friend
body: Let’s be real, if your closet is anything like mine, it’s a bit of a war zone, shirts piled on the floor, pants hanging by a thread, and the occasional stray sock living its best life. But with the Amazon Basics Slim Velvet Hangers, you can wave goodbye to wardrobe chaos and say hello to organization. These hangers are the unsung heroes of any closet, offering a sleek, non-slip design that will keep your clothes where they belong: on the hanger. The velvet coating is key here. Not only does it add a touch of luxury (your clothes deserve it), but it also keeps even your most delicate items from slipping off. Say goodbye to that moment when your favorite blouse decides it wants to take a dive off the hanger and onto the floor. Plus, the slim design means you can fit more clothes in your closet without it looking like you’re playing a game of Tetris. Pros: • Non-slip velvet coating keeps clothes from falling off (hello, organized closet!). • Slim design means you can fit more clothes in your closet without it feeling cramped. • Great for a variety of garments, from shirts to dresses to jackets—these hangers do it all. • Pack of 50, so you’re well-equipped for that closet overhaul you’ve been putting off. • Affordable and functional, who doesn’t love a good deal? Cons: • While the slim design is great for maximizing closet space, it might not be ideal for heavier coats or bulky sweaters. • The velvet texture can sometimes attract dust or pet hair, so a quick lint roll might be necessary. • Not as durable as thicker wooden hangers, so don’t expect these to last forever with heavy use (but at least they’re affordable to replace!). All in all, if you’re looking to level up your closet organization game without breaking the bank, the Amazon Basics Slim Velvet Hangers are a solid choice. They’ll keep your clothes in place, your closet looking sleek, and might even make you feel like you have your life together (no promises, though).

title: FEELING ACCOMPLISHED
body: There is an old saying about building a better mouse-trap, well thank goodness someone finally designed a better hanger. I grew-up with wire hangers. They were free and found everywhere. Hangers were in every home, alley-way, garbage and junk pile, in the back rooms of every bar and department store, and always clustered so that it would take an hour to separate an individual hanger from the pile. And while hangers had absolutely no value, they functioned as a necessary survival tool. Hangers could be used for everything from picking door locks, to unplugging toilets. I comically pretended that hangers had a life all of their own, magically reproducing in dark, hidden closet spaces where bent, tangled piles of wire, paper and cardboard secretly cohabitated. But now, because all my clothes hang neatly on stream-lined hangers with their velvet friction covering, it's a delight to hang sweaters and pants to keep my closet organized. The design of the hanger provides more efficient spacing, and your clothes stay balanced once properly aligned. I never thought I would pay for a hanger, but I do and I will! The amount of work and frustration I have saved by eliminating the ‘wires’ is well worth the price.

title: Nice frame, great value
body: My rustic white 8"x10" frame is true to size. The color looks a bit different from the product image, but it worked like a charm as I happened to be deciding between brown and brushed white. It is made of plastic, but overall I like the construction, which is lightweight to a point I could use a thumb tack to mount it fast (but certainly it will be more secure on a proper hook/nail). The black loops for mounting (there's two - for portrait and landscape display) can be turned in a weird direction on arrival, but you can just turn them to proper position for mounting. It has a whole bunch of components, including: plexiglass transparent protective cover (it is itself protected with a thin film on both sides, which you have to peel off), whitening frame - if you use it, the resulting view port becomes 5"x7", the carton back cover with four rotating "feet" to lock it in place after adding front cover and canvas. The back cover has a foot in case you want to stand it on a shelf or table. I had to fix this foot to the frame with a piece of carton (so that it didn't push against the wall). It was very easy to put together and I only read instructions after the fact. It's not the pure wood'n'glass, but you could have guessed it from the price. Yes it's a bit reflective; love it in my bathroom. Great value for the price.

title: 10/10 would buy again
body: This vacuum was my one and only prime day splurge last year and I have not regretted it even once. I researched different stick vacs and decided this model seemed like the best value for what I needed (vs. dyson and other brands). Overall summary: extremely easy to use, charge, and clean the vacuum itself. Very effective and functional, would absolutely buy again even if it died tomorrow after only one year of owning but it seems to be working about 98% as well as it was right out of the box. I specifically waited a year to write this because many reviews I read when comparing cordless vacuums prior to purchase mentioned problems after about 6 months of use. I've had none. The rest of the review is long but I know if I would have appreciated reading this input when shopping around. Battery life: I timed the use when I first got it and ran it for ~40 minutes switching between hard floor and carpet settings and it did not run out. I think it's only died on me once or twice in the entire time I've had it, and that's when I was vacuuming the entire ~3000 sq ft house in one go. Since I usually stick to just upstairs or just downstairs at a time, battery isn't an issue for me even on the high power setting. Suction/dust cup capacity: the suction is only ever affected when the dust collector cup is seriously full, and since we had two cats and one dog and were catching up on a long time of neglecting vacuuming, this was pretty often at first. Since then we've gotten through one or two full battery charges worth of cleaning without having to empty, which means the suction has been great. We use crystal cat litter that sometimes gets statically stuck to our cat's fur and he will shake it off on the carpeted floor. This vacuum has been great at getting the litter (and fur of course) out of the carpet. Not to mention actually emptying the dust cup is super easy too. Hand vac/crevice tool: switching attachments is also very easy. I had a super cheap hand vac I used to use for crevices and cleaning my car, but no more. This is great for getting in between couch cushions, car seats, cup holders, floorboards, etc. Brush roll: I have long hair and I shed a lot more than the average person. One of the biggest deciding factors between brands for me was the ability to get my hair out of the brush roll and I definitely made the right choice on this one. Even when my hair is clogging the brush roll, it has never once actually stopped it from rolling and has barely changed the effectiveness at all. When I do clean it out - it's SO easy thanks to the grooves on the roll and the bristle design. Even on other vacuums that are supposedly designed to easily clean the brush roll, it has never been this easy before. Down side: The only suggestion for improvement I have is that the tiny wheels on the front of the vacuum head were tangled with fur/dust/hair after the second or third use. Unlike the brush roll, it seems impossible to fix this. On the other hand, even though I'm not sure those wheels even roll anymore, it hasn't actually seemed to have any effect on the vacuum's functionality which is why I'm still giving five stars. If you are on the fence about getting a stick vac in general: I cannot recommend it enough and it is absolutely worth making the switch. My partner and I both have depression and ADHD which makes it very hard for us to find the motivation to clean. Since getting this vacuum I am not kidding, I have vacuumed more in the past year than I have the rest of my adult life (I'm 32! Yes, this is embarrassing!). We keep this near the kitchen within easy reach and eye sight, and it's small enough not to be in the way. We also have carpeted stairs which were the worst to have to deal with - both mentally and literally - and now I vacuum them regularly just because it's so easy. We have had multiple full size/traditional "pet" specific vacuums before and this specific model has equal or better suction power and is so much more convenient than all of them. And it fits under the couch!

title: This vacuum is amazing with great suction! I saw a store using on their doormat.
body: We have a bunch of large door floor mats in front of several doors in the house, plus some walkway doorways that collect dirt and lint balls on the carpet. Always a big project getting out the canister vacuum, hose, and carpet floor unit to vacuum, so they don't get vacuumed as often as they should. A few weeks ago I'm walking out of a local large grocery store and see one of this model of Shark stick vacuum being used on their entry doorway floor mat. I took a look and remembered "Rocket" on the carpet unit, then tracked the stick vac down here and at a big box home store. What really caught my attention was the clear plastic "catch bin" at the top! Seemed like exactly the right thing in the right place, and clear so I could see what was being picked up. Well yep, having bought one, it works even better than expected! The various comments here, before I bought, said you have to pull the "high suction" trigger to get sufficient power on carpets, and that drains the battery faster. BOTH TRUE, BUT WHEN YOU DO THAT THIS THING SUCKS LIKE CRAZY! I'm impressed with what was in the catch bin and what I could see coming up from the carpets and mats. Small bits like cat litter, large bits of stuff, lint, hairs, everything on the mats and rug walkways. I vacuumed two carpet areas in in doorways between rooms that always accumulate a lot of dirt. Then vacuumed 3 of the door mats. Then vacuumed part of a sunroom carpet where a bunch of cats live. Even on the "high suction" the battery was only 2/3 gone after all that (there are 3 LEDs that tell you charge/discharge level) but I stopped because it looked like the catch bin might be full. This was first use and I wasn't sure. Yep, completely full, and that is a large bin! One thing: INSTRUCTIONS ARE NOT CLEAR THAT THE CATCH BIN EMPTIES WITH A TRAP DOOR ON ITS BOTTOM, WHEN YOU PRESS THE EMPTY LEVER. SO IT WILL DUMP RIGHT INTO YOUR LAP IF YOU DON'T KNOW THAT UPFRONT, LIKE HAPPENED TO ME. :) Luckily it was close enough to my lap that the suddenly-open trap door hit my leg and only opened about an inch, limiting how much came out until I could move it and me to the trash can. :) Knowing how it works now, I just hold it over the trash can then trigger the bottom door release. Which is really great, you don't have to turn the catch bin upside down and shake or such. There isn't a printed set of "word" instructions with the unit, it is one of those picture instruction pamphlets. For the most part that works, as in: assemble the stick pipe into the floor unit, then the vacuum head onto the stick pipe. There apparently is a QR code on the top than can be scanned for more instructions. Pro tip: the inside of the catch bin will be dusty after you empty. I used a "computer air" spray can (for PC keyboards and such) to blow out the inside and top. There is no way to get the unit to self-stand that I've found, for storage, as other comments here have noted. I found two cabinets with a space between them wide enough to set this unit in upright. Done! Even has a plug nearby for the charger. Those LEDs near the "suction trigger" show you how the charging is coming along. 3 of them that light in sequence as it charges, then they all go off when completely charged. Charges reasonably fast. At a local big box home store I saw this unit in person, plus a whole bunch of other brands and models. Yep, I "showroomed" then ordered here for $30 less. :/ None of the brands and models had that nice, large, clear catch bin at the top back like this one has. Several brands had black or opaque catch bins and they were located in odd places. Why? To make sure I won't be able to see how full it is getting? Guys! :) This vacuum is great, for what it is, a quick and fairly powerful unit to quickly clean floor mats, doorways, and other small areas. Probably not the ideal thing for your entire living room rug, although could do it with a few re-charges and catch bin empties. Summary: just buy it already! :) A+++++

title: It’s not for every house
body: I'm not totally on board with this machine, but I'm also cheap and already have multiple other cleaning machines (Bisell carpet cleaner, Dyson corded vacuum, steam cleaner, corded hand held Dirt Devil, shop vac), so this machine fills a niche for cordless convenience in our house. Still, not sure that I’m totally sold on this. If you’re really looking a deep cleaner for a fully carpeted single home over 1700 sq ft and this is going to be your ONLY vacuum, I suggest going with a more expensive cordless vacuum or one with interchangeable battery pack. My aunt has the more expensive model with the bendable wand and it is a lot more powerful (and louder). She also has three spare batteries for it. If you’re just looking for a surface clean and some dusting, this does the job nicely. If you live in a 900 sq ft apartment, this will be probably be awesome if you have floor/closet space to store it. If you want the convenience of a wall mounted unit that charges on it's mount, this is NOT it. We live in a two story townhome just under 1800sq ft. Off the bat, I wished there was more suction power. It was almost anticlimactic when I turned it on for the first time bc it was SO quiet! Second, I wish the battery lasted longer or it could be detached and switched out for a backup battery. The battery is built into the motor/ canister house and relies on a cord plugged into it to charge. I knew it was 40 minutes of battery life going in; I underestimated how much I could actually clean in 40 minutes. I’d definitely have to break up my cleaning into sessions if this is what I am relying on to clean a whole house, top down (including furniture surfaces). Third, it would've been nice for them to design a way for the two accessories to attach off the wand or floor nozzle so that it’s always at hand and doesn’t get misplaced. Fourth: some option to mount this on the wall, even if it has to be purchased separately, would be helpful. The pluses: It’s quiet. Low price point, especially at 50% off. Light enough my kids to use with ease. There is a light on the floor nozzle. It’s great for some quick vacuuming around the dining table since my kids eat like Cookie Monster and vacuuming is a must after every meal; great on stairs and crevices that my corded Dyson was unwieldy and troublesome with. It’ll be convenient for cars, which means our car will be cleaner more often. Also, note it only takes but a few seconds to separate the top and hang it off the wand. I don't see it as a big deal to spare a few seconds to press a button for separation. It takes me longer to rewrap the cord back around my Dyson. The vacuum absolutely has the ability to stand upright on its own if the motor/canister is hung from the wand. Update 1/25/24: Been a few months. Loving it so far. Definitely vacuum a lot more often bc of how light and easy it is to use. Definitely wish it had more suction power, and affirms the idea if you are wanting a cordless as your sole vacuum cleaner, definitely invest in a pricier model. Also, wanted to add something as I was finally confident enough to recycle the packaging the vacuum came in: I have to point out the packaging is quite impressive as it is entirely paper based, which is such a welcome relief given the amount of plastics I get just from ordering a take out meal. Zero styrofoam and plastics in this packaging. Completely flattens down except for the two compressed paper fiber structures. Bravo to their packaging engineer. Update 5/17/24 Still finding it uber convenient to use, but it’s no good for the car! It’s ok on the upholstery if it’s like fresh crumbs sitting lightly on the surface. But it does not have the power to pull off things like fine dirt, sand or crushed leaves imbedded into the wiry carpet fibers of the car or crumbs wedged into seat crevices and carseats. I find my shop vac a lot more efficient for the car.

title: Durable long lasting cordless vacuum
body: I have had this vacuum for 3 years now and it’s still going. I have 2 pit bulls and 1 orange tabby who has very thick medium hair. This vacuum sucks up ALL the hair very quickly and easily. Sometimes hair gets stuck in the little wheels, sometimes the opening in the bottom gets plugged from the sheer volume of hair from my cat. But these are very small issues to me that have happened in the past with larger, corded vacuums. Since it’s cordless, I zip through the whole house in about 30 minutes, and that includes moving small items and furniture. The light on it makes it so much easier to see the stuff on the floor and I don’t have to turn on every light as I go. It doesn’t pick up large items like stuffing from dog toys, some plastics bits, larger stones, etc, but I don’t really care that I have to pick those up. It sucks up all the hair and that’s what I wanted. I nearly run the charge out in 30 minutes but I use the extra suction while going under furniture to make sure I get everything so that doesn’t surprise me. I just plug it in, it fully charges in a hour or so, and I put it away for next time. I have wood laminate floors with only a few short fiber rugs and it vacuums the rugs just fine too (wouldn’t recommend on shag). If you have just pets, this is great. If you have kids, probably go for something heavier duty.

title: Great Vacuum
body: As someone who’s always on the lookout for a vacuum that’s both powerful and easy to use, the Shark Cordless Vacuum Cleaner (IZ363HT) has completely exceeded my expectations. I originally picked it up to deal with all the pet hair around the house, and it’s been a game-changer. What I love most is how lightweight and portable it is. I don’t have to wrestle with a bulky, corded vacuum anymore, which makes cleaning way easier. The fact that it’s cordless means I can take it around the house (and even into the car) without being limited by power outlets. The 50-minute runtime is impressive too—I can easily clean my entire house in one go without worrying about it running out of battery halfway through. It’s also great for pet owners. The powerful pet hair pickup feature works wonders on furniture, rugs, and floors, pulling up every last bit of fur. The HEPA filter is an added bonus, capturing even the tiniest dust particles and ensuring that the air stays fresh while I clean. I also love how easy it is to switch between the different attachments. The crevice tool gets into those tight spots, and the dusting brush is perfect for delicate surfaces. Plus, the removable handheld makes it a breeze to clean stairs, upholstery, or any place that needs extra attention. Overall, this Shark vacuum has made my cleaning routine more efficient and enjoyable. It’s powerful, versatile, and just so easy to use. If you’re looking for a high-performing, portable vacuum, this one’s definitely worth considering.

title: My favorite purchase of the year and I bought it the first week in January
body: This vacuum is amazing. I love the different settings for different floors, the ability to store it upright without a hook, the lightweight design and how long the battery lasts. My ONLY complaint is that when you use the max power trigger it easily says it’s jammed even when it isn’t and you have to turn it back on and off again to get it back to working, BUT the power of the vacuum without the max power is already perfectly good so it’s not always necessary to use that function (and it does work just not as well).

title: Real Review- my second purchase.
body: Read for an actual real review as I just opened my second SHARK pet cordless vacuum. I got this vacuum for the first time about a year and a half ago. I’ve been through so many vacuums in the past and had all the issues. I finally buckled down after spending hundreds on new vacuums throughout the year, and got a very well know vacuum, this shark cordless pet vacuum. I bragged and recommended this vacuum to anyone that would listen. It is light weight, picks everything off the floor swiftly in one pass, and doesn’t take up a lot of room. Yes it clogged frequently. But I can expect that, as I have a rescue dog that sheds the most I’ve ever seen- maybe that’s a little dramatic , but he sheds A LOT!!! The clogging part was not the issue at all, it takes 1 minute to grab a knife, turn the locks, and remove the bottom part to clean out the matted hair. LOVE THIS FEATURE! It would be unrealistic to expect a vacuum to never ever clog. This feature makes cleaning out the vacuum SO SO EASY! This is also the only place on the vacuum that would clog. Like I said I am IN LOVE with this vacuum. But … what is so disappointing is that things don’t last. About 3 months ago , the 3 charging lights went out. I was unable to see when it was fully charged or how much battery was left. Okay, I’ll let SHARK have it, it still works great without the lights. About a month ago , the different settings (bare floor or carpet ) started going out. It wouldn’t turn on the bare floor setting and the carpet setting was real low- like how the bare floor would usually be. The “boost mode” slowly started being less powerful so I couldn’t continue using “bare floor boost mode” on my carpeted areas of the house. I love this vacuum so much I had to get another because the first one slowly stopped working after about a year. I was really hoping the first one would’ve lasted a lot longer. I’m here to say this is the BEST VACUUM especially if you have pets, but it’s disappointing that the power part of this vacuum gave up so quickly.

title: Light and easy to use
body: I was hoping for a little more suction but this vacuum is probably adequate for my light cleaning. Since I have a canister that can hold a bowling ball, my expectations were a bit too much. It picked up a lot of dog hair in a small space so I'm impressed and also , the quick dump is great. It fits in my over loaded laundry room and is ready for a quickie tidy up. I wish the tools could be clipped on but will live with it. Generally I would recommend due to ease of use and performance.

title: Nice for a cordless vacuum!
body: I went into this purchase. Not expecting this vacuum to be a strong as my corded vacuum, but I live in an old house with narrow staircases and it's a pain to haul a vacuum up and down stairs, so I mostly just leave this one upstairs. With that in mind, it's a pretty nice little vacuum. I would not want it to be my primary vacuum, but it works well as a backup. The battery length is pretty good, and it does have reasonably powerful suction. Although again, not as good as my regular corded vacuum. It does does best on flat surfaces and struggles with anything textured like entryway mats etc. I have multiple cats and so I mostly am vacuuming for litter and cat hair and it does pretty well at getting both of those things. The roller brush does get jammed fairly easily and it's mildly a pain to clean, there's not an easy way to snap it off, so in terms of design, I wish they had designed it to easily open for cleaning since periodically it loses suction power and needs to be cleaned before it'll work well again. But overall, it is really nice as a backup and I've been fairly impressed with it for a cordless vacuum.

title: I love vacuuming! (Did I just say that?)
body: Yes, I did just say that. Because this is the best vacuum ever. I don't want to say this vacuum changed my life, because that sounds incredibly pathetic, but it kind of did. I am pretty sure I have vacuumed more in the last month than I have in my entire life. I show it to people when they come to visit and give them demonstrations. Not kidding. My husband saw his parents using it and when he came home from visiting them, the first thing we did was go out and buy this vacuum. I was skeptical. Every other vacuum I've ever encountered was heavy, awkward, inconvenient, tangly, frustrating, hard to store, and broke the minute you looked at it. It didn't matter what you spent on it--a lot or a little--it was still awful. I had given up on ever finding any vacuum that was not awful. This vacuum is aptly named. I am "free" to pick it up at any time with no janky cord in my way! It doesn't cramp my "style" because it is easy-to-use and maneuver, and super light to carry around, even up and down stairs. It is very "sucky"! I can't believe all the stuff I clean out of the bagless bag (which is effortless to clean out, just unclip it from the vacuum and then open the compartment and dump everything in it into the trash--so easy!!) each time I run it through the house. The charge lasts quite a while. We have a three bedroom home with both carpet and non-carpet floors, and I can do a quick vacuum of the whole house on a single charge. The charging stand is sleek and does not get in the way, whether or not the vacuum is on it. My husband and I both have long hair and we have several cats, but it's easy to cut off any hair that gathers around the roller--no unscrewing things or wrangling with taking things apart--and it gathers cat hair like you wouldn't believe. I use it daily to keep the kitchen crumb-free and around the areas of our cats' litterboxes and food dishes, and every few days around the whole house. We still have a super intense vacuum for occasional "deep vacuuming," but on a daily/weekly/casual basis, this vacuum is the bomb (yes, I also just said that), especially because it is such a good price. We paid $100 for ours and have said numerous times that it's the best $100 we've ever spent. The only thing I wish is that I could vacuum my furniture with it. I might be able to and just don't know it; I haven't really looked at accessories yet. I'd better go! I'm sure there's a crumb on the kitchen floor that needs the attention of me and my awesome Shark Navigator Freestyle. *flies away, cape billowing out behind her* ---- Edit 5/26/14 - I have an update that I thought I should share with everyone. Sadly, my beloved vacuum died a tragic death a few weeks ago while we were on vacation. Since the last person to use it was our housesitter, I do not know the exact circumstances of its death, but I mourned. I wanted to say, though, that this in no way diminished my love of this vacuum. No vacuum lasts forever, and this one lasted for eight months with near daily use. To replace it, we tried another, more expensive, swankier cordless stick vacuum and it was truly awful (check my other reviews if you want to know which one it was). We returned that one, and I came right here and ordered another of this one. I used it this morning, and all is right with the world again. Best vacuum ever and at $100 it's a steal. I shall never stray from it again!! Honestly, I am thinking of buying a spare of this vacuum in case they decide to stop making it.

title: Best cordless I’ve ever owned
body: Why did you pick this product vs others?: Battery life is amazing, I’m able to vacuum my whole house ( 1700 sqft) the suction is top notch. I have two dogs and two cats gets all the dirt and hair up. The small attachment for furniture, perfect, gets all the hair up. Long handle, double filter Highly recommend this handheld. Functionality: Way to use, easy to dump Power: Excellent power Weight: Not heavy Flooring quality: Gets all the dirt and pet hair up Ease of cleaning: 100% easy

title: Shark needs to hire some humans to take calls.
body: I LOVE this vaccum cleaner, what better then a Shark & its cordless to boot. Very powerfull! However, it delivered missing a key component the screw, actually THE ONLY SCREW, did not come with it. When I tried to contact shipper was told to contact Shark. Well calling them is like trying to get someone on the phone from the IRS. That's impossible, so I just went to my local hardware store and the cashier paid the 17 cents it was gonna cost me for the screw. So I did not give a 5 star, cause I feel that in business, the customer should be able to contact a human at you business period. Very unprofessional in my opinion.

title: awesome product
body: This cordless pet vacuum cleaner has been a game changer in my home. It’s lightweight, easy to maneuver, and perfect for quick cleanups around pets. The suction power is impressive — it easily picks up pet hair from both carpets and hardwood floors. The self-cleaning brushroll helps prevent tangles, and the battery lasts long enough for a full cleaning session (usually around 30–40 minutes). I love how versatile it is — it converts to a handheld for furniture, stairs, and car interiors. The dustbin is easy to empty, and the HEPA filter is great for trapping allergens. If you have dogs or cats that shed, this is a must-have. The cordless design makes it so convenient, and it performs just as well as some corded vacuums. Highly recommended for pet owners looking for power, flexibility, and ease of use!

title: Insane suction 😏
body: This is the best pet hair vacuum I've ever had for the price and convenience of its use. Let me start out by saying, I clean my house every single week. Im vacuuming my bedroom and the amount of dog hair that I discovered was insane. I had no idea this dog hair was even here AND im a clean freak. The vacuum sucked up such an amazing amount of hair i had to empty the vacuum three times (and it had nothing to do with small capacity). I stuffed an entire grocery bag with hair from carpet i was supposedly cleaning every week. I will say the battery doesn't last long, but thats the price to pay for a cordless vacuum with insane suction.

title: Well made with strong suction and exceptional battery life.
body: I am in love with this vacuum. I just purchased my third one. The other two are still working perfectly, I just love having one upstairs and another one downstairs. And I've decided that I also have to have one for my vacation home. It's lightweight enough to carry around but not so lightweight that the suctioning ability suffers (like some others that I've tried). And the battery life on a single charge is plenty to get me through my frequent vac sessions. LOVE IT!!

title: It's a \"meh\" vacuum.

Unless you've got a place 2 Prop it up or wedge it, you have to take the vacuum Apart In order for it to stand up freely while charging. as you see in the video, It is too top heavy to charge In a standing position Unless you have it Propped up against your wall, and then you are risking It's scratching the wall. title: Top tier very happy
body: Top tier vacuum if your thinking of buying one do it my lady loves it and it’s not noisy at all compared to their older models. We got it for $150 before taxes. We had got one next to the trash can someone left when we first moved into our apartment it lasted us one year and it sounded a little old this is a much better upgrade and it does not sound like a jet taking off.

title: Good vacuum, needs better battery
body: I took one star away because the battery is so short on time. My home is 2200 sf, I can only vacuum half at a time because the battery runs out, I have mostly wood flooring, if I had very much carpet it would be worse, because the carpet setting uses much more battery power. Then it takes hours to recharge. The performance of the vacuum itself is great. I would buy again, just need longer battery life.

title: Great Sharp customer service!
body: The charger base quit working so I called customer service and since this model is no longer made they are sending a brand new vacuum. I purchased the original almost a year ago, so I am thrilled with the outcome. The new vacuum is higher quality as well. Thank you, Sharp Warranty services!!

title: Love this vacuum!
body: Why did you pick this product vs others?: For those of us who can't [or won't] afford a Dyson, I'm very impressed with all aspects of this vacuum. I thought my townhouse was fairly clean, and then I used this for the first time and was amazed at the amount of dirt it picked up. The ease with which it folds down to glide under dressers, sofas, beds, is terrific. It feels substantial, but isn't heavy and bulky like the 2 old vacuums it's replacing. Easy to store in an upright position. Charge easily lasts for a thorough cleaning of a one bedroom townhome.

title: Love this thing!
body: It was between this and the Bissell. I chose this because it had a bigger container. BEST BUY OF THE YEAR. I have a Dyson full vacuum cleaner that I love. But what a pain for quick cleans. I have two cats/two dogs and fur everywhere. When I first turned on the Shark I thought I would return it because it was quiet and didn't seem to have power. SO glad I didn't. It is amazing just picking up a cordless and spot cleaning. It has plenty of power, and when you need a boost, you pull up a trigger under the handle. This thing pivots beautifully and I can get it under all my furniture. I can do my hardwoods and the carpet in my room and have plenty of battery to spare. Game changer in my dog fur house. I love this thing.

title: Good vacuum for small spaces
body: It’s a pretty good vacuum, good suction, I just wish it had a wall holder because it does not stand on its own and will scratch up your walls from constantly falling over.

title: Effective and Convenient
body: Very effective on carpet, but the canister is a bit small for a larger house. Easy to use, not real fast at charging. I think I would have preferred the one with the extra joint in the wand, but didn’t know about it when I bought. Probably not much fun in tight spots like a car interior.

title: Remarkable
body: I run a veterinary clinic. Pet hair is a huge issue to say the least. We've been using a standard old style upright. The staff wanted something lighter and cordless. I ordered a generic lower priced unit that seemed to be what I needed. It was terrible. I hate returning things but this unit, although sleek and good looking, wouldn't pick up anything. I decided to upgrade to a Shark. I told my staff if it didn't do the job I'd get them a new, sleeker model but a corded one. Well they couldn't have been more impressed. The Shark did a better job than the old heavy corded upright! With just a single pass it picked up everything. It lightened their work load tremendously. Light, cordless and powerful, their nightly chore of vacuuming was now quick and easy. They love the shark! And maybe me too.

title: Best helper ever
body: I believe that this is the third or fourth one of these that I have purchased. I have one in my garage and it just laps up the little gravel pieces that come in and the dust. I have one in my basement and one in the main level of my home. I use these all the time. They are very powerful. They are very lightweight. I can do most of my house in less than 10 minutes. The amount of dirt picks up is just amazing. It’s easy to empty easy to take a part of something. It would happen to get stuck in the tube. Easy to clean. I had to replace the battery in the first one that I bought, which is probably 8 to 10 years old. Was well worth it. I have a very expensive canister vac that I can use for in my home, but I sell them take it out. The only rug I have is a braided rug, and a couple of nice heavy throw rugs. This little sweeper picks everything up off the floor or the rugs. Very satisfied with this.

title: Great!
body: Pretty solid cordless vacuum. It’s great for my kitchen, and works well on my low pile carpet too. It’s not great at picking up pet hair on carpet m, kinda just pushes it around. But it’s compact and super handy in general for a quick clean up before guests!

I'm still leaving a positive review because the product seems good and customer support was good. title: Great vacuum!!!
body: Perfect for everyday vacuuming (and I vacuum everyday). It’s light weight, maneuverable, easy to empty & has pretty good suction. I do use a more powerful vacuum twice a month but this does a great job for day to day. I have mostly hardwood floors with some area rugs and it works well on both. I can usually hit 2 &1/2 of the 3 floors in my house on one charge. In short, I Love this vacuum.

title: Pet Vacuum
body: Shark Cordless Pet Vacuum is Excellent at Vacuuming your pets! They don’t like it very much but it is good at it’s job. They tend to get stuck in the nozzle but I might have just gotten one intended for small mice and hamsters…

title: BEST EVER!!
body: Best vacuum I have ever owned. I have purchased about 3 different vacuums in the past year because I couldn't find the right one. This one has great suction on hardwood and carpets! It's lightweight! Smooth roll when vacuuming. 110% recommend.

title: Small but Mighty
body: This is the first cordless vacuum cleaner I have owned and I wish that I had bought one sooner. It is very quiet compared to other vacuum's I have owned so at first I thought it wasn't very powerful. I was mistaken, it is impressive how much this small but mighty vacuum picks up and I love that "boost" trigger setting that it has. Very versatile as well for reaching hard to reach places. Big fan of Shark products and will continue to buy.

title: Shark wins again
body: Great for quick clean up on carpet and lanoleum

title: Great purchase
body: Why did you pick this product vs others?: I love this vacuum it's a must have fir pet hairs ,I have a cat and a husky it picked up the hairs with no problem, left my floors spotless

title: User friendly
body: So far, this has been a great purchase. Very user friendly. Battery lasts about 40-45 minutes. Lots of handy attachments. Has good suction. Easy to empty and recharge. Also very quiet compared to my last electric vacuum.

title: Works amazing
body: I love all the Shark products and this one is no exception. I love that it is cordless and the charge last pretty long. It works great on floors, carpets, stairs and the car.

title: Works well easy to use.
body: This works well, it’s easy to use. I find I clean more often for a short period of time as it’s so handy to grab and easy to vacuum now. Battery lasts as long as it’s quoted in the description. I’ve used it for two months and cleaned hopper every time I’ve used it or when the container looks full. Not to mention it’s lightweight and fits under most of my furniture and the beds. I love it.

title: Simply great 👍🏼
body: Why did you pick this product vs others?: Such a great vacuum. Lightweight, easy to maneuver around the space, no fuss on and off switch with carpet to floor easy transition button. I highly recommend if you don’t want to spend an insane amount of money on a vacuum. Also so easy to charge and clean!

title: Great suction and long batter life
body: I love it. Great suction. Battery lasts long enough to vacuum the whole house. It's actually never run out of power while I've used it. It is top heavy and takes a little while to get used to it.

title: Love this vacuum
body: I had reasonable expectations that an upright would not be as good a cleaner as a more heavy duty vacuum; however, I knew it would be more convenient. My last upright was a wimp from the beginning, and didn't handle my long hair strands well. This Shark is so much better than I expected. Instead of having to pull my long hairs out of the floor brush, they neatly curl around the tube in the debris collection cup. For that alone I am a happy camper. ! I appreciate the various little devices that are so easy to use. It took me a while to notice the finger grip to easily and suddenly up the power when needed. The buttons to switch back and forth from hard flooring to carpets, to remove the power unit, and to dump out debris are easy and seamless. The light is a nice touch that helps hair and little bits show up, whether in brightly lit or shaded areas. Most of all, I love the ease of using just the power unit with various tools, all of which were included. When I store the vacuum, which I keep in a closet, I separate the power unit and place it on the floor so it is handy when needed. I am very glad it doesn't have to be stored and recharged on a wall unit, as it is not artwork to display. It is quite easy to plug it in, and handy to have the three blinking lights to know the level of the charge. I am so glad it turns itself off after reaching complete charge, so I don't have to worry about watching it. My house is surrounded by trees and a pond, and I like to keep windows and doors open when the temperature permits, which means a lot of "nature" crawls into my house. Cobwebs frequently grow in wall and furniture corners. When stored, I keep the crevice tool on the power unit so it handy to pick up to remove cobwebs and droppings from my many plants, or from dropped crumbs in the kitchen. After a long rainy season this summer, carpenter ants decided to try to set up residence in my house. They would make their way to the kitchen. I placed diatomaceous earth around areas where I saw them. Because it is recommended to get rid of ants that make it into the house, so they don't return to their nest and provide news and a path to a good area, I kept the power unit with the crevice tool handy in the kitchen. Every time I saw an ant, I quickly scooped it up. For good measure, I first sucked up a little diatomaceous earth to be waiting in the cup. Within three weeks, the ant population diminished every day until there were no visitors. After a week without ants, I used the crevice tool to pick up all the white powder. I don't think I would have been so successful with my ant problem without the convenience of this light weight, easy to use, power unit. It is now my new favorite tool. If I had a design suggestion for this vacuum, it would be to have the capability to vary the length of the handle. It is a tad long for a person under 5' tall, something I find to be true for many appliances that are likely designed by tall men.

title: Great for hraed surface floors
body: Does a great job on hardwood floors and a decent job on carpets. The handle is heavy due to the battery weight being there and could be tiresome for some folks. It has this comb-like structure near the front roller brush that traps hair and makes it into a tightly packed shape that needs to be removed after each vacuuming (we have a long-hair cat). Takes some getting used to to find all the latch releases to fold/unfold/empty the vac. Battery run time is long enough to vacuum 2800 sq. ft. of hard floor area and some small scatter rugs.

title: Too heavy but suctions very well
body: It's a little bit too heavy and the head is way too big, so it's kind of difficult to sweep narrow places. But it suctions very well and the light show the dusts very well. Charging is easy and very easy to use made. I like this product.

title: 10/10 recommend
body: Love this vacuum! It’s light weight, has a long enough battery life for me to run through every room in my house, doesn’t take super long to charge, and works GREAT! I originally purchased a different cordless vacuum and it was terrible compared to this. It has 2 different suction settings on top of a booster trigger. It doesn’t take many swipes to pick up messes.

title: it works
body: I had really hoped that this would encourage me to vacuum more than I do now, because I find the canister vacuum that I have so awkward to carry around -- especially on stairs. This one is easier to carry around, but it's not as light as I hoped. It's actually not that much lighter than the canister -- and doesn't have as powerful a motor, though it is less awkward to cat. The HEPA business is nice in theory, but it's pretty messy to empty, which seems to negate the HEPA business. Also, when the bin is very full, the dust doesn't fall out on its own & I have to pull it out with my fingers. I guess it would be best to empty it outdoors, then all the dust would not go back into the air of my home. The light on the carpet attachment is interesting in a dark room, because then you see the dust exceptionally clearly. The carpet beater part is quite noisy. Also, when I’m using it, the motor can get quite close to my ears, which is painful. But, basically it does the job -- and it's definitely easier to use on stairs than a canister, or indeed than any corded vacuum. It charges fairly quickly. It has an interesting attachment that is sort of like a crevice tool and sort of like a brush. This is useful for going under furniture. I tried using it on blinds. It was sort of tedious, tho it I think it did help. When I used that attachment without the stick, the thing became much lighter, which was nice. I'll have to revisit this review after I've had it for a while.

title: Cobran caro por la marca, pero es igual a cualquiera aspiradora
body: Tanto que alaban a está marca, que cuando la ví en especial aquí en Amazon , me decidí a comprarla de $349.99 la pusieron en $199.99 y me decidí a comprarla , para así ver , ¡si era tan buena como la pintan!. Lo primero que les haré saber es que pesa, hace bastante ruido y el pelo se termina atorando en unas pequeñas rueditas que tiene por debajo . No trae ningún aditamento para guardar las diversas piezas que trae. Allí en la 1ra foto lo podrán observar . En el rodillo no se atoran los pelos pero en la 2 da foto verán que el pelo se ve atorado por el visor del rodillo. Yo decidí sacar 3 ajustes que sujetan una cubierta por debajo, para así poder limpiar el visor, pero no se puede , ya que el rodillo no sale , asi que no se puede limpiar y dentro también se le atoran los pelos . La pieza dónde entra la basura que recoge, es muy grande , pero, eso mismo trae problema al limpiar, por qué al ser tan grande y al quedar por debajo, al querer limpiar debajo de un mueble , no se puede . Por qué esa pieza choca con el piso. Hay que mover los muebles para poder limpiarlos los muebles por debajo. ¡Gente!, yo tengo una aspiradora marca Tineco y esa me salió buenísima, no hace tanto ruido , el envase donde cae la basura es mediano y no estorba al limpiar debajo de los muebles. Y no pesa como la Shark. En fin , es cara solo por la marca . Sinceramente la Tineco no le debe envidiar nada a la Shark.

title: Noisy dirt magnet!
body: The Shark Cordless Vertex Pro is a legitimate dirt magnet – seriously, it picks up more dust bunnies than a convention of long-haired cats! My floors have never looked this good from a stick vac. However, be warned: this beast is louder than a flock of seagulls fighting over a French fry. My dog now thinks every vacuuming session is a rock concert, but hey, at least the carpets are clean.

title: Am I special?!
body: This vacuum does not stand upright. Am I doing something wrong or are we all just okay with that? I'm shocked to have spent so much money and I have to precariously rest it on something and hope for the best or lay it down every time I need to stop vacuuming for a second - which, when you're moving furniture and cat toys, is every 4 seconds. Total disappointment but everything else seems good so far!

title: Second shark vac
body: Has very good suction. Cleaning lady said "You have to hold on or else it will drag you through the church". Second shark vac we have purchased. Only downfall is the power cord will fail, and replacements cords fail just as fast.

title: Powerful suction, good run time, versatile attachment pieces… i recommend!
body: Powerful suction & long run time for a cordless! This cordless vacuum has great suction strength & long run time. It works well for pet hair, & human hair doesn’t get tangled & stuck! The add-on pieces are easy to swap out & are super helpful when I need to vacuum places other than the floor (ie: my couch, my dogs’ bed, or in a narrow space (like crumbs in my pantry, or between my stove & cabinets, or behind my couch/bed…) *TIP: Try vacuuming in the dark! (The light on the vacuum is super bright & you can see every strand of hair/speck of dirt on the hardwood floor!) My only real issue with it is it is top heavy, so it won’t stand up on its own nor stay propped up against a wall… you always have to either lay it down on the floor or remove the heavy canister part completely… Overall, I still like this cordless a lot & I’d buy it again! I recommend! 👍🏻

title: Best c I
body: I love this cordless vaccum. I cleans as good or if not better than my shark stand uo corded vaccum. It has all the attachments and I can get into all the corners. Wouldn't change a thing. I love it.

title: My favorite cleaning buddy
body: I bought this guy for quick vacuums during the week. Our main vacuum is a Shark Vertex, which I love, but it is a heavy beast. We previously had a cordless Dyson stick vacuum, but I never really thought it did a great job on the carpet. This little guy is THE BEST. It is lightweight and does such a great job. I have an australian shepherd, 2 cats, a kid, and very long hair that sheds. My vacuum needs are NOT for the weak! This does an amazing job, so much better than the Dyson on both hard floor and carpet. The suction power seems great, though I have had to unclog the tube a few times. It was very easy to do. I do find the actual dust cup a little finicky to open, but I think it's getting easier the more I use it. I love that it has the headlight so I can see that it's working and that a charge seems to last for a while...I don't have a huge house, but I can do an entire floor on one charge no problem. I've never had the battery run down, so maybe I could even do the whole house. Sometimes I use it instead of the Vertex for my bigger weekly vacuum and it still does a great job, though I do think the Vertex has an edge because of the way it separates long hair from the rest of the dust. 6 months of regular use and it's still going strong. Love it!

title: Compact and powerful
body: Great product for small cleanup situations. Wonderful for small children “play time”, lunch time accidents. Highly recommended

title: Nice
body: So far it works.

title: Read The Warranty. Not Great
body: I normally don't rate a product based on the support it gets. I try to concentrate on the features, functions, and reliability. I bought this in August of '24 from Amazon and by March of' 25 the button to get the vacuum in an upright position would not work. Unfortunately I couldn't work with Amazon directly for a replacement. I called Shark and was treated very poorly by customer support. I was hurried constantly while trying to get the link they sent to work in my chrome browser so that the person could verify that the vacuum was indeed busted. Further insult came when this nasty person told me I would have to pay $26 for return shipment and asked if I could afford it. I later verified that the 5 year warranty on this item does include a clause for the customer to pay for the return of the item and the cost depends on the item. I have been waiting more than 2 weeks for my replacement. Another troubling thing about the warranty is that the replacement item cuts the warranty down to 6 months. Doesn't seem like a great warranty. I had a bad experience with a vacuum rated highly by a leading consumer magazine and a very bad experience with customer support. To top it off I don't feel comfortable with the reduction in the warranty period. I purchased a TV that cost over 2400. One day the TV would not turn on. I called the store from which I bought it and we went through the troubleshooting steps. I received a new tv within a week and they payed for the return of the TV that would not work. No changes in the warranty. I doubt that I will buy another shark product again. The vacuum worked very well and maybe the malfunctioning button was just a bad one in the bunch. I'm expecting decent treatment when I call for service. I expect better turnaround times for warranty exchanges, especially if the product was not abused. My suggestion to others after this experience is to read the warranty for any product you are considering buying carefully.

title: Good but not for big, shedding dogs
body: Had high hopes for this vacuum and while it does okay, if you are a pet owner it doesn't quite deliver. I have a German Shepherd and a Newfoundland so I do understand that the amount of dog hair in my house is more than some people but it definitely has a hard time keeping up with us. One of the benefits is its very easy to clear clogs, which is so nice! Overall it does okay, but I might be asking too much of it with my very large, shedding dogs.

title: Overall great! Does have bristles, little misleading. Read review w/ pros & cons
body: Skip to bottom for breakdown on pros and cons. Overall good suctions. Just misleading on some things like battery life and bristles. So that’s why I’m only giving it 4 stars since it’s a nearly $300 vacuum. Suction seems overall really good as of now, but does have bristles (that was a big thing for me for the hardwood floors), and battery life only runs for around 20 minutes when using it as a vacuum, it only lasts (via the manual) for 40 minutes when using it handheld. UPDATE: I vacuumed my whole house (all hardwoods & is roughly 1500 sq ft) without the battery dying. So that definitely was a good thing. Satisfied with that! Also hook your crevice tool, or other tools to the part that attaches to the head, and Bam you have a long crevice tool that can get pretty much anywhere! I received the vacuum today, and I will update review as I go if I need to. First impression was the box was simple. Looked very generic, and I wished it had an actual name instead of just model number. I also thought it would only have powerfins and no bristles since that’s how it’s pictured and advertised. IT HAS BRISTLES. They feel soft, and I’m watching how they do on my LVP flooring but that’s very misleading because I thought it was going to be just a soft silicone fin. I’m scared it’s going to scratch my flooring. It’s overall very light, and nice sleek look to it. I used it as soon as I got it for about 10 minutes on the LVP flooring I have. It sucked up pet hair and dirt that I couldn’t even see. Worked great. I’m very satisfied with the suction so far. I did plug it in to charge after it died (before the initial charge), and it has now been 2 hours and it still isn’t fully charged. I do wish it had quicker charging. So I decided to glance through the manual to make sure I’m doing everything right. In the manual, it states with hand vac it works for up to 40 minutes, but only 25 mins on bare floor, and only 20 mins during carpet mode. If you’re using the boost (it has a boost button which is nice) vac with handheld it only works for 10 minutes on a full battery. So I would say it would only last in boost mode for about 12 minutes on bare floors, and probably less on carpet since it’s half the time almost from the hand vac times. I do wished the battery life was longer, and it’s misleading when it says the vacuum lasts around 40 minutes on a full battery. I knew it wouldn’t always last 40 minutes with different modes and flooring, but I didn’t think using the actual vacuum in standard mode on hardwoods would cut that time in almost half, to 25 minutes. Disappointed in that. I do like the design, the boost button (hate how much time it cuts off the run time before the battery dies), and I think it does a good job overall with suction this far. I also love the LED lights. I think it’s a pretty good vacuum. Wished it would come with two batteries so you could charge one and have a backup. I have an almost 1500 square foot house with all LVP flooring & a dog that sheds. So I will definitely be testing this out over the next days to get accurate timing myself. Breakdown is — Pros: 1. The style/design is sleek 2. Easy empty container 3. Boost mode button 4. Powerfins (it does have bristles though. Pics are misleading) 5. Good suction this far 6. LED lights 7. Can change battery out (only comes with 1 though) 8. Pretty easy and convenient storage Cons: 1. Battery life (states 40 mins but that’s for hand vac, only 25 mins for bare floor and 20 carpets) 2. Charging time — it’s been over 2 hours and it still isn’t fully charged. 3. Has bristles, does have powerfins — but pictures makes it look like it doesn’t have bristles and only has powerfins. It has both. This was one of the main reasonings I ordered this one was because I felt like it was safer on my flooring. 4. No “name” — just a model number. And the packaging looks generic. Not like an almost $300 vacuum. Came in a cardboard box, with the vacuum inside a plain white box.

title: Easy to use. Doesn't last very long.
body: To start with....I love this vacuum. It's lightweight, easy to empty and works great on my many carpeted stairs. Also it works over all the ruggables throughout the house. My other vacuum cleaners pull the top part away from the velcro and jam up the beater brush. This vacuum is powerful but manages not to get jammed up with the ruggables. My one big complaint: I go through one of these vacuums every year. I use it everyday on the first floor of my house. The problem: I go to start the vacuum by tapping the power button and nothing happens or for a brief moment it starts and then dies. I watched the YouTube videos on troubleshooting for this model and followed the instructions. They indicated that almost always the above "behavior" means there is a plug or jam. I keep the filters clean and have checked for jams (there haven't been). I chalk this up to a year of constant use and after all for the price I guess it shouldn't be a surprise that it doesn't last past about a year and a half. And because it would cost more than I paid for it to repair it I just by another. I have a standby corded Dyson to pick up the slack. I don't like having to dispose of my no longer working Sharks in a landfill.

title: Great Find
body: First, I am a true Dyson gal. Love their products. My Dyson stick vacuum lasted 2 years. It's run time was half of this Shark product. I mostly wanted this for my hardwood floors with area rugs to help keep dog hairs (2 labs) at bay. I selected the Shark because it was almost 1/2 the price of a replacement Dyson. All I can say is WOW. This vacuum has features the Dyson did not and picks up leaves off the floor as well as anything else the dog's drag in. It has a 40 minute run time, and you don't have to hold the trigger down while using. It has an on/off switch! It did not struggle at all while using on area rugs or switching back to the hardwood floor. The bin un-attaches from the stick so you can easily open it to empty without having to hold the whole vacuum across trash can to empty. For the price, and my need, this was a great choice. I would definitely recommend this one for sure.

When my son came, he said, “I bet we can order another battery for the first one rather than tossing it. He took a photo of the battery and ordered a new one from Amazon. It works like the new one, and it is great to have one upstairs and one downstairs. I love that it is lightweight, easy to empty, no bags. Just perfect for my needs. Highly recommend!

Would have been very disappointed given the price paid- but Shark warranty/customer service is fantastic! After a quick video chat to confirm model & serial numbers and demonstrate the issue, Shark is sending a replacement piece. I only had to pay a very reasonable shipping fee. I believe it is a 5 year warranty. So happy I checked before chucking it!

title: Best Cordless Vacuum on the Market - Especially for Households With Pets!
body: I have been a "vacuum connoisseur" since I was a teenager - my Mom kept a clean house and I inherited her enjoyment of a clean house. Vacuuming is my favorite house chore - it actually relaxes me, so I always enjoy having a great vacuum that is easy to use. Right now, we have four doggos - Husky/GSD/Malamute mix, Husky/GSD/Dingo mix, GSD/Cattledog mix, and a purebred Carolina Dog (American Dingo). As you can imagine - we have a LOT of fur around here. My dogs literally shed twice a year - six months in the spring and six months in the fall. :) I vacuum the entire house at least once a day and sometimes twice. I've had several cordless vacs - two from Dyson, one from Bissell, and two from Shark. The Dysons were dismal at picking up fur, and the Bissell was worse. And don't even get me started on the robot vacuums - we have had four (Roombas, Bobi, and Eufy) - completely ineffective and a waste of money. I got my first Shark Rocket Pet Pro vacuum in 2017, and I can't say enough about it! I have vacuumed up tons of fur with it, and it has always had great suction, great power, and it's easy to keep it clean. I just replace the filters on it every month or two, and that's all the maintenance it needs. That poor vacuum died last week (through no fault of its own). I spent three days researching cordless vacuums, and kept coming back to the Shark Rocket Pet Pro. I bought a second to replace the first, and am still in love with this vacuum. Bonus: The new one that I bought has the upgraded handle with the hook for the motor, so it can stand on its own and be easily stored. The ONLY issue I have with this vacuum (and it's not a huge problem): The self-cleaning brushroll is AMAZING! But - I have to stop once in a while and pull a ball of white Husky fur out of the floor attachment - the hole behind the brushroll that takes the debris up the long rod to the dustcup gets clogged (I tried to show a picture of it). When this gets blocked, the vacuum won't pick anything up. Again, not a deal breaker, especially with the self-cleaning brushroll, but it is the one less-than-perfect aspect of this unit. And I'm probably the only one in the world with this issue, because I have my beautiful fur-factory doggos running around here. :) Overall, I adore this cordless vac and will recommend it to everyone!

title: Great lightweight vacuum
body: This is a great little vacuum. We use it daily for quick clean ups around the house. It’s small and easily able to navigate under and around furniture. It’s cordless and perfect for those moments when someone says they’re coming over with 5 minutes notice and every second counts. I can clean our main floor on a single charge (high chairs, entryway, kitchen, living room, nursery, hallway, and bathroom) and still have some battery to spare. It charges quickly and automatically stops when fully charged. It easily picks up dirt, dust, pet hair, and the like. It has a turbo mode for larger messes but of course does not have the power of a full sized vac. The clear catch basin comes apart and can be washed in the sink with soapy warm water. I removed one star because there’s only a light when using the floor attachment; would appreciate having a light when using the hand attachment for cleaning nooks and crannies. Also because it doesn’t come with a wall mount kit for storage and charging like a Dyson would. Overall, I would recommend this vacuum for families, people with pets, dorms, offices, and beyond. We only have shark vacuums and their customer service is great!

title: The dusting tool pictured prominently with this vac does NOT come with it
body: At first, I thought that I had received a returned product that was missing a part, the Anti-Allergen Dusting Brush that is pictured prominently in Amazons graphics of this vacuum. However, the parts list does not include a dusting brush of any kind. Amazon used the WRONG illustration to depict this version of the Vortex Pro IZ662H. I had to order one from Shark, which charged almost as much for S&H as the item cost. However, I deducted only one star and it's not Shark's fault; it's Amazon's fault for their sloppy, erroneous, very misleading depiction of what they're selling. The vac, itself is highly satisfactory. It does a better job on hardwood floors than a Shark DuoClean upright vac because it somehow removes dust and debris right up to the very edge of the floor where it meets the baseboard. I've never encountered a vac in my life that can do that. And it's MUCH easier to use than the big corded upright. It's pretty noisy on high speed, but that comes with the suction power the vac develops. It's difficult to have one without the other. Thankfully, I almost never run it on high speed, which is good for the ears and for battery life. The Vortex Pro removes an amazing amount of unseen dirt; just like the full-size Shark vacs, I can hardly believe all the junk it's sucked up by the time I finish the job. The bendable handle is not only good for getting under furniture; it also allows for much less intrusive storage in our pantry with the handle in its flexed position. This is the third Shark vac, I've had, and I'm very please with all three.

title: Compact, light but awesome
body: I just finished spot vacuuming our kitchen - laminate vinyl and living room carpet - have lots to do but just had to stop and say how wonderful this little gem is...I am older but in shape and active but with some back issues..It’s light weight, easy to use and most of all it actually does as good a job as our main branded name vacuum. It is easy to unload the debris and it's amazing how many dog hairs it picks up...easy transfer from carpet to hard floors. Years ago I had a vacuum of the same brand but this one is just fantastic I can't write enough words!!

title: Couldn't love this vacuum more!
body: My daughter brought her cordless Shark over one day to help out and I fell in love. This model was on sale that particular day, so I took it as a sign and bought it. I cannot tell you how much fun vacuuming has become without a cord or a heavy canister to pull around. We have a 150 pound New Foundland/Lab/Retriever mix, and he sheds year round, so vacuuming is a daily thing. This has made it so much easier to keep his hair out of everything. It moves seamlessly from our hardwood floors to tile to our throw rugs. The hardwood floor setting let's you vacuum smaller rugs without them getting sucked up into the vacuum cleaner. The handle also collapses so that you can vacuum all the way under couches and chairs and whatnot. While the picture shows several attachments, ours only came with the crevice attachment, but we have managed quite well with that. I feel like the battery life is very good, but it all depends on the settings you use. If you want more suction, it's gonna cost you some battery. But it quite clearly displays the battery life remaining, so you always know what you're working with. And it's nice that you can detach the battery to charge it OR charge it on the vacuum cleaner. I love this machine so much!

title: Powerful, Lightweight & Cordless Freedom – Vacuuming Made Effortles
body: This vacuum is an absolute game-changer! It’s lightweight, easy to maneuver, and delivers powerful suction on both carpets and hard floors. The cordless design makes cleaning quick and hassle-free, and the battery life is impressive—I can clean multiple rooms on a single charge. The LED lights on the head are a nice touch, helping me spot dust and pet hair in corners and under furniture. It’s quiet, sleek, and easy to empty. This vacuum has turned a chore into something I actually enjoy—highly recommend!

title: Great price and same value as Hoover Linx!
body: I am on the hunt for a quick cleanup of dust and hairballs on our tile floors (about 1800 sq ft of tile alone) - mostly around the edges by the baseboards where it ends up. I didn't want to have to get our Oreck out every other day- I tend to put it off and don't want to do that. This is the FIRST cordless vac I purchased and I thought I would just buy a handheld for other things like lampshades etc. PROS: One touch of a button and ALL of the lint and hair falls right into the garbage! No paper filter to touch or suck out with another vacuum!!!! Love that feature!!! CONS: when going under the couch or something like that you bend over parallel to the floor and the unit lifts off the floor! So the suction is no longer there where it needs to be but a few inches in the air :0( Bissel Bolt Pet (pink one) 2nd vacuum I bought is good because of the lift off handvac AND the handle bends with a click of the button to go under your couch, etc and the head does not lift off! BUT the con is that you have to touch the junk inside to get it all out, ew. It sticks to the paper filter inside and it won't shake out for nothing. You can't just push a button and it falls into the trash can like this Shark does. This has a high low and brush roller on and off and has excellent suction...AND the handle bends by the touch of a button to go under items with ease. It also rotates right and left (hard to explain) so that you can go under anything! Hoover Linx, 3rd one I bought: I was expecting this one to feel less chintzy and sadly it felt cheap and sounded cheap on the tile floor...and I paid nearly $150 for it. Sure, the neat metal dial is cool and not cheap and the power indicator is ok but I really do prefer a base that it sits in to charge and not an extra stand alone gadget that i have to plug in after removing the lithiom ion battery. Mostly because I want to grab and go, I want to keep it in my laundry room charged and ready to go when I see some dust or hairballs (from our four chihuahuas) rolling around by the baseboard. This $80 Shark did just the same job but easier to get rid of the disgusting dust and hair out of the bin. So, now that i have tested all three vacs I went ahead and bought the higher level Bissell Bolt because this morning I refreshed my cart and was able to get it for $149 andit hasn't been under $199 for months. I will have to pull off the dust and hair from the filter but I think it is worth it in the long run since it has both of best worlds, a floor vac and removable hand vac in one. Maybe I can use it without the paper filter inside, my husb suggested that. We shall see. I will do a review on that one too after I test it out..

title: Trigger Pull Has No lock
body: This is a 3 star vac. Pros- Battery life: Short of an entire 2000 sq house with wall to wall, battery life is more than adequate at max setting. I didn't time it, but I would guess around 30 minutes straight. Enough for all my areas and runners 3-5x over. Power: I have moderately thick and dense rugs and this vac chews right through them without issue. Clean out: The clear container is fairly small but very easy to empty as needed. Maneuverability: I would give this a 7.5/10. It articulates well but not seamlessly. My Dyson Ball Animal 2 did a better job but it was corded, bulky, and also crapped out after way too short of a time to praise it. Accessories/Features: The attachments are great and the ability to convert to a handheld is convenient. Cons- Battery recharge: Takes a long time, I'd guess 2-3 hours. Not a big deal for someone like me who can do all of my rugs but, if I had more rugs to do and it required a recharge on maybe someone's one day a month they do a house cleaning, that could be a pretty big hinderence in work flow. Trigger- To achieve max power you need to pull a trigger to boost it. This trigger has no lock-on button. I'm a 30 y/o man who does construction and this is pretty annoying. For an elderly or frail woman, or a man with issues in his hands, this likely wouldn't even be achievable for 30 minutes of straight operation. Absolutely senseless. A ton of my tools have this feature and it would cost the manufacturer nothing to add on a plastic button and spring. Thick rugs- I have two thick bath mats and this vac simply doesn't work on them. It just gets bound up and blinks red. Not a huge deal as that's a pretty big ask of a vac in general. Side notes- Appearance- It's fairly sleek but looks don't matter to me, performance does. Initial value- I purchased this 'on sale' from $350 to $200. It's not worth $350. Maybe $200, probably closer to $150. Durability- I've owned this for exactly 30 days so I can't speak for longevity. Longevity will be the true determiner of the $200 value. Overall, I am happy with my purchase. I don't have a ton of experience with other vacuums but I do know that this is working overtime with my rugs. I have 3 cats and the vac produces tangible results extracting crazy amounts of invisible hair from the depths of the rugs. I will say that I wouldn't purchase again without an added trigger lock.

title: Best invention since the cordless phone… Awesome!
body: I’m 75 years old and have owned more vacuum cleaners than I care to think about. I purchased another brand cordless vacuum stick last month and really liked it until it died after just a few weeks… Researching for a replacement with better reliability, I found this wonderful Shark Vacuum Stick…. My initial impression was that it’s a bit heavy and slightly clunky compared to the Samsung model I just returned, but after using this baby a few times I love it. It’s AWESOME! This Shark does a great job cleaning my dark brown bamboo floors and the area rugs in my 3000 square foot house without recharging. The Samsung had to recharge after about 1500 sq Ft. Emptying the large dirt bin isn’t an unpleasant experience, and after releasing the motor/canister from the stick I was impressed with how easy disassembly and reassembly went… At my age, dust on baseboards and chair rails, as well as some dirt in corners and other hard to reach areas has become the norm. My Roomba and the corded uprights just couldn’t get those hard to reach areas on the floors, and it’s just too hard on my knees and back to crawl around more than a few times each year. I found accessories on all upright cleaners too awkward and difficult to use…. but I was inspired by the Shark’s light weight and gave it a try… All I can say is WOW! Baseboards, corners and close to furniture and cabinets are now spotless! My house hasn’t been this clean in a long time… Best of all, I’m not exhausted from the task. LOVE my Shark cordless stick vacuum!!! Time will tell about long-term reliability and battery life. Some good news I found in my research… the replacement battery cost for the Shark is about half the cost of a Samsung battery. Next time this vacuum goes on sale I’ll be buying several as presents for friends and family! My advice is buy two or three of these…. One for yourself and one for your elderly parents/grandparents… they’ll love it and thank you for it! UPDATE**** Still going strong at about 4 months use. I ordered an extra battery, which is easily swapped out. Just push a button and the battery releases. I was given two Dyson V6 cordless vacuums by a neighbor who isn’t very mechanically inclined … The Dyson isn’t the latest model, but a comparison: After ordering aftermarket batteries, it was easy to remove a few screws and replace the originals. The Shark is quieter, easier to use, and definitely easier to swap a spare battery. The Dyson is a bit prettier, and may have slightly more suction, although it’s only a one speed suction. Both will get the job done. If you want to impress someone else, get a Dyson. If you want a better all around machine at a good price, get the Shark.

title: Pretty good, especially for the price
body: I spent like 10 hours researching different cordless stick vacuums. I kept going back to the Dyson but just could not bring myself to spend 600 bucks on a vacuum when I already have an iRobot and a corded Dyson ball vacuum. Onto the review: I got this today, charged it and used it for my whole house. 1) As others have noted, the suction power when attaching the brush/pet hair end is not that strong. I held down the "max" button the whole time and it did a pretty good job, but definitely drained the battery faster. 2) It is lightweight, love the flexibility of being able to go up the stairs with this and in all the nooks and crannies without the cord. It really is a gamechanger. 3) I have both a short-haired Boston terrier and a very fluffy Australian shepherd. The upholstery option (which is just like the crevice tool with a brush head) did remove some of the hair from my couch but struggled to pick up the short hair. A bit disappointing and makes me think I should have gotten the Dyson which comes with an upholstery roller head. 4) The hardwood function does pick up a lot (check the cannister you'll be surprised) but doesn't do an exhaustive job. 5) This is a pretty darn quiet machine, my dogs were interested but not as disturbed as with the corded vacuum or iRobot. 6) Battery life: if you're holding down the "max" button, you'll get 10 - 15 minutes. I haven't tried it without using that option the whole time, I'm sure it would get longer. Overall my goal with buying this was to pick up a lot of pet hair very quickly and without having to deal with a cord. My Aussie has tumbleweeds of hair that are almost impossible to keep up with. We're talking hair all over the baseboards, and big piles of it that somehow make there way into places that the dog doesn't even go. I think this vacuum accomplishes what I wanted, which is the ability to run through the house very quickly and easily and pick up a load of hair. The brush head can be used to go over baseboards and pick that stuff up too. It's easy to discard all the grime into a garbage. The ease of use means I will be much better about keeping up with all of the hair, which is a huge burden when you have to lug a big, heavy, corded vacuum around. All around, I am happy with this purchase and feel like I got a solid value-add when thinking of the modest price. Maybe in the future I'll feel better about dropping a few hundo on the Dyson but for now, I'm happy with this buy.

title: Powerful for a stick vacuum and pretty versatile.
body: I didn't expect this stick vacuum to be as strong as a good upright or canister vacuum, and honestly it is not. It is however a very good stick vacuum that has a lot of very nice features. It works well on for our daily messes that our golden retriever puppy makes, including her shedding hair. It appeared to be doing a good job on the pine needles from the Christmas tree too, but they clogged it up pretty quickly. To unclog it you need to turn 3 screws a half a turn and remove the brush. The screws however are a plastic material and not metal, which makes me wonder about durability. I would have also appreciated a more complete printed manual as opposed to a quick start-up guide with a QR code to print it myself. Otherwise, this is a handy vacuum that quickly converts to a hand-held for steps and furniture. Note however that regardless of the product description, it only comes with the crevice tool. It does NOT come with the other 2 attachments. Amazon should correct this in the description. So far it’s effective and handy. I just hope it holds up well.
