title: BRINGS A S-M-I-L-E Every Time... :) Cat Approved! .....smart Handy Engineering. Updtd
body: Aug 12 2015 Update: Had an issue with the motor & had to call cust service. Problem was handled very quickly & efficiently! Thanks! Orig REview: I researched until I was blue in the face because I do NOT like to sweep & I didn't want to buy a problem or a disappointment. Sweeping is a pain & a chore. But to my surprise every time I use this Shark it brings a SMILE! :) Wasn't sure what t to expect with this Shark,...there were some mixed reviews & opinions were helpful. Since I own several Dyson's including a Dyson 44 (I'm not happy with the D-44 or small storage of the Black & Decker Platinum 20v hand vac) I looked at buying the dyson59. Glad I chose this Shark,...though nothing is Perfect...& this Shark is not designed for all situations. PERFORMANCE: I don't try to sweep a large house,..its just not designed for that. It's great for quick, effective clean ups but has flexibility to do larger areas too. Shark give me flexibility to keep my full-size Dyson in the closet much much longer between major cleaning. That's nice. With a cord I have no batteries to run down unexpectedly. Nice. Yes I do have to find an outlet to plug it in, but it's got a very long cord which minimizes that minor annoyance. -The dust /dirt collection cup is much biGGer than the Dyson's I've tried & much easier to dump without a mess. Plus the dirt cup is easily detachable with one hand,..very convenient, well thought out,...a major plus. -The snap connections on the shaft of my portable Dyson are so loose goosey it's like trying to sweep with a droopy wet noodle & leaks suction. Not fun. -But the Rocket is ROCK SOLID! The locking couplers on the shaft are very solid w/no loss of suction. No wet noodle feeling at all. It's a lightweight metal of some sort more durable than plastic. But I resisted buying Shark for a long time because of the huckster feel to their advertising that made me resist buying. Shark's First Class Quality Engineering surprised me. OTHER PLUSSES: * * *NEW UPDATE.... When I need to store the unit I don't use the wall hook. Instead of mounting a plastic hook somewhere to hang the Shark, I lean the Sharp upright against the wall as one unit, nothing detached,....with the bottom vac head close to the wall. It's quick, easy, nothing to disassemble, no mounting hooks involved, convent storage anywhere while minimizing storage space. -Lean Storage works for me because of two small, strategically placed rubberized feet /knobs on the underside of the dust cup that helps grab the wall so it doesn't slide down. It also creates a 3-point stability between the 2 rubberized knobs & the sweeper head flat on the floor. In this 3-point position the Shark rests nicely balanced /stabilized with minimal storage space yet ready to conveniently swing into action quickly. -smartHE (smart Handy Engineering). The placement of rubber knobs is one example of what I call smartHE (Smart Handy Engineering) or smart, handy, practical engineering features that enhance Sharks performance, reduce stress & make it flat out easier /even fun to use. These small rubber knobs do double duty cushioning /stabilizing the plastic dirt cup when laying the sweeper flat on the floor. SUGG: would be helpful if Shark could enhance this upright storage feature with some pop-out rubber feet on the sweeper head & larger rubber on the bottom of the dirt bin. The 3-point storage is easy & simply needs a wall /closet etc to lean against. The rubber under the dirt cup keeps everything stable & in place,...automatically keeping itself from walking /rolling away from the wall or falling over sideways. I store it upright like this even on smooth hardwood floors. Very convenient & gives max flexibility to store it most anywhere out of sight, in an quiet corner, etc.. Nice! With a little practice it's easy to catch on to the technique & not have problems of it falling over as some reviewers have mentioned. -Vac performance works great on medium, short carpeting, hardwood floors & tile. Don't have to change height or anything,...just flip a switch that slows the beater brush on smooth surfaces. On deeper pile carpet I go to high speed. I read the directions. Easy Peasy & effective. -***UPDATE: The Sweeper's Headlight was a BIG SURPRISE. The angle & intensity allows me to actually SEE THE DIRT dirt /dust on my medium dark hard wood floors. Nothing in the marketing describes this benefit, but it's a real help to actually see where I've swept & see the dust in areas yet to be swept. NO MORE GUESSING! As a result I haven't really used any other attachment yet. The slower brush speed setting for wood floors attracts dirt & smart handy engineering keeps the spinning roller from damaging the wood floor. Never a danger of that. -Bot the motorized animal attachment for cat hair & misc on bedding. I can immediately see the results in the transparent collection container. Use Shark for steps too, but often too lazy to switch the heads & simply use my normal floor attachment for steps too,... with great success. * * * UPDATE... WHEEL NOISE & HARDWOOD FLOORS: Not an issue for me. The two large wheels have rubberized tread which deaden click clacking over wood /tile floors & superior to all-plastic wheels wheels on most vacs. -The two small spacing rollers on the front of the sweeper head are not rubberized & do make some rolling noise on wood. Some reviews reported the noise was annoying on hard floors but on balance was not an issue for me. * * * NEW TIP: IF YOU HAVE A BAD BACK or trouble bending over you can wind the electric cord without bending. While standing upright with cord in hand, simply let out enough cord to loop it over the lower hook when draw the cord back over the upper hook then let out enough length to loop under the lower hook & repeat. The cord is flexible yet stiff enough to make this work easily. With a little practice you'll catch on easily. Works for me. -Does have a nice LOOOONG cord. But I always come to an end somewhere where an just an extra 5 feet would be nice. It's one of those things where LOOOG is never long enough! An extra 5 feet would be handy if it can be safely done. -Durability & Longevity....only time will tell. But this Shark is starting from higher quality level /features than battery powered units like Dyson44 /59. That higher quality & attention to detail usually translates to durability & longevity. GREATEST STRENGTH: HIGH QUALITY & VERSATILITY. Does not pretend to be a full size vacuum. But delivers Big time features. Shark adapts well to most situations /hardwood /tile /medium & short carpet, under furniture & hard to reach places with excellent heppa filtration that's easy to clean & refuse. No special filters to constantly buy. So it's versatile, self contained & easy to maintain filters with peak performance. It is wrist arm intensive so if you're handicapped in those areas you may want to stay with traditional floor sleepers,,,but can always give it a 30 day test /return. -Usually avail at a lower price than battery powered competitors. With Shark there's no limit on run time,...no expensive batteries to wear out or repurcha$e. Just plug & run. -TOO MUCH: Suction & cleaning performance are excellent. Some sweepers I've used have TOO MUCH suction making it tough to easily move the sweeper across the carpet because it sucks down on the floor /carpet & won't glide. No problem here w/Shark due to smart engineering that manages the suction well & picks up the dirt. With a little care & technique I can sweep even loose throw carpets without it being sucked off the floor into the sweeper head. SUGG: it would be nice if Shark had a safety overload pop-out reset switch to protect the head roller & motor if something gets caught in the roller. CONS & More SUGGS: There aren't many. Plastic wall mounting hook is a little weak. But that's not an issue for me since I use the handy 3-point storage for leaning against a wall in a closet or empty corner out of sight yet close at hand. This makes sweeping quick & effective,...not a big production. An extra 5ft on the cord would be nice. Extra lights on the sweeper head that shine not only to the front, but to the sides for larger viewing area would be nice. Adjust the motor to get rid of the annoying whine. A simple quick wheel lock to keep the unit from rolling away from the wall when storing /leaning it upright. -A larger accessory bag that closes more secure with a couple fabric loops for hanging would be nice. I don't change accessories very often & store them in the handy bag on a hook in my closet. Some reviewers prefer having all attachments on the shaft at all times, but for my taste that reduces portability & performance which is Shark. Besides, I can use my big, bulky sweeper if I want all my attachments at my fingertips. * * * UPDATE: MY CAT ALWAYS JETS out of the room whenever I start a sweeper. To my compete surprise, my cat GRACIE just calmly sat there watching me sweep away! Who knew?! Ha! SHARK IS CAT ENDORSED... :). BOTT LINE: Brings a s-m-i-l-e every time I use it. Pushing my Shark I feel smart, refined & minimal. Now when going back & pushing my full sized vac I feel clunky & out of step. Just sayin. Unexpectedly gives me a smile & lift on what used to be a chore. After owning 3/4 Dysons, I finally chose to break away from all that overpriced hype & poorly fitting cheap plastic. It was hard to convince myself to do that. I know we're just talking about a sweeper here, but the feeling of freedom & discovery was worth it. This shark delivered solutions for all the annoyances that were trapping me with Dyson & other brands. Shark's smartHE (smart Handy Engineering) features are second to none. Superior fit /finish, exceptional cleaning performance, versatility, larger collection cup easily removable, smarter design, usually less expensive... this Shark is a winner in my book. Glad I gave it a try. Our cat Grace is much happier, too. HIGHLY Recommend. EASILY EARNS 5-STARS!

title: Shark HV322 Rocket Deluxe Pro Corded Stick Vacuum - My review after 2 years of use
body: I purchased this exact model from here a little over 2 years ago. I'll contribute a long-term review since it apparently is still being produced and sold and as a review reader myself I always appreciate when someone drops back in to give insight to a product's longevity and performance. Which I'm happy to report the vacuum in still running strong and used almost daily, albeit a little worse for wear but that's because I use it pretty hard and unforgivingly. My use environment - a 1100 sq ft condo with 100% ceramic tile flooring and 2 8ft x 10ft rugs. I also have 2 cats that shed. Keep in mind that YMMV based on your own living space. For my space size/type I feel this vacuum's mix of suction power, dust cup size, power cord length, a lower speed beater-bar setting for hard floors and higher setting for rugs - all together in a stick style vacuum was a perfect match. Now if your space is much larger with wall to wall carpeting then this would not be a good choice. Stick vacuums are just not made for that kind of job and a traditional upright is probably best. If your space falls somewhere in then middle with size and/or has a mix of flooring types then... good luck with that. Maybe get both types of vacuums? Or a traditional upright that isn't super heavy has some good hard wood floor features. Or take a hybrid approach and go with an old school canister style. You get the idea, moving on... Using the vacuum - I've got to say this has been one of the best vacuums I've ever purchased. There are a few quirks I won't waste time listing and it could use more attachments but the low $150-ish price more than makes up for those minor complaints. My remember my first impressions were that it "felt" cheap and "plasticy" and thought it wouldn't last log given my taxing usage. Turns out it's done a remarkable job with heavy and demanding use and abuse. In fact if it were to give up on life tomorrow I would seriously consider just buying another to replace itself. A few more things I like that I would like to point out - I've purchased many vacuums over the years and these are the things that stand out to me about this vacuum: -> It's not cordless. I made that mistake once and learned that battery powered vacuums suck (pun intended). You can never quite finish before it runs out of juice and of course you can't use it while it's charging. The battery capacity declines over time and so does the power. You're lucky to get a year out of it. -> The cord is nice and long, I only have to change outlets once to do my entire home. -> It's motor and resulting suction power is impressive for a "stick" vacuum. Another WIN for the power cord, no cordless is going to meet that kind of power output and do it consistently for over 2 years so far. And as far as corded stick vacuums go, this one places on the more powerful side of what you typically find, almost rivalling it's full-sized traditional versions. -> 2 beater bar speeds easily changed with your thumb without stopping, this makes transitioning from hard to rug to hard again really easy. -> The dust cup is large compared to other brands/models of the same size and power class. If you battle pet hair like I do then you will appreciate the larger dust cup. I don't understand why dust cups aren't larger across the board. But I digress. -> The dust cup is easy top remove, dump and reattach with little effort or tools needed. -> The filters are very durable, I'm still on my originals and wash those frequently and wring them out but they are still in usable condition. I will need new ones eventually but not quite yet. -> It's got a nice length, so if you're tall it feels comfortable to use and it also makes getting under things easier. Some of the cheaper sticks on the market are little more than a dust buster fixed to a short pole with a handle. They feels like your using a child's toy vacuum. Alright a few minor criticisms I'll mention in case they aren't minor to you: -> There really should be a hose attachment that you can pop on to the spot that the tube detaches from on the hand unit. Same end piece as the tube but is on a hose instead. Although this complaint could be for many other models too-) -> It's a bit on the loud side, as loud as a full sized traditional vacuum, but I'd rather have loud and powerful vs less loud and less power. -> That long power cord I mentioned I liked becomes one that is a lot to circle back up on the storage hooks on the unit. Sometimes I get lazy and just kind of wad it on or behind it in the closet. A power cord retractor like on the full sized machine would be an amazing upgrade, but I don't think this feature exists on any stick vacuum for space reasons, I assume. Fine, now that I'm thinking about this stuff there are 2 significant things that I really do not like - -> There is no stand for it, you lean it up and hope it doesn't slide and fall to the floor where, invariably, the dust cup pops off makes a huge mess. Beware of leaning it up against kitchen counters. It feels like it should stay put but it won't. Seriously it will fall down. You'll see. -> 2 There is no place to attach and store the brush/upholstery attachment anywhere on the vacuum. To make it worse, there are several obvious places that would work quite well for this too. Why did I just write all that? Seriously, I need to get a life. TL:DR - is good, buy

title: Great Vacuum! Super Value!
body: We needed a new vacuum for our golden retriever puppy and after looking at a lot of choices, I decided on this one. I am so utterly tired of cordless items because the batteries never last long or perform well. So, I went with this Shark model that has a cord. I was not disappointed! This unit really picks up the dirt and small puppy hair (soon to be mounds of adult golden retriever hair!). One pass up and back and floors and carpets are spotless. I really like the detachable feature of the unit and it is not nearly as heavy as it looks from the picture. The Shark is very maneuverable around tight corners and it's easy to get under tables and sofas. I think that for most people, the dirt collection bin is more than sufficient, although I can see I'll need to empty it more often than most due to the dog hair. But hey, it's just so easy. The only thing that might have been designed better is allowing the vacuum cord to be detached from the unit when emptying the bin since the waste bin is likely to be in another room. But that is very minor. The vacuum appears to be quite durable and functions well throughout the house and in my car. I rate this as a superior 5-star buy and well worth the value. It didn't hurt that it was on sale, too. And to be clear, I am a paying customer giving an honest and personal review. I've never found anyone willing to give me anything for free! :-) I recommend this as a very good cord vacuum choice and I'm glad I bought it.

title: Great Vac for Pet Hair
body: This is our 3rd shark and we really like it because it's lightweight and easy to maneuver. The suction seems good but it's still new, so hopefully it lasts! We dropped it a star because the product description doesn't mention there isn't a way to store the 3 attachments that come with it (found it on a forum). Also, the dust cup is small, so it fills up fast for us ... We have 2 large dogs. But definitely a great buy. We definitely recommend.

title: 7 years old and still works great
body: I’m about to hit the seven year mark of owning this vacuum. I wanted something lightweight that had all of the pieces connected to the main unit so I didn’t have to go searching for them and this one fit the bill. I have a long-haired dog and a long-haired cat and I am constantly vacuuming as you can imagine. It is still working exceptionally well and I’m hoping that it lasts several more years. The way electronics and appliances are made these days- the fact that it’s lasted more than two years speaks to the quality. I am purchasing a second one as the cordless vacuum, I keep in my kitchen is about to die. Even though this one has a cord, you should know that the cord is exceptionally long. As I said, I like the fact that all of the pieces are on the single unit and it’s easy to detach to get to the long hose or to detach to make it a Dustbuster. I would highly recommend this. It picks up dirt and dog hair on wood floors, tile floors, as well as carpet. It is easy to clean and easy to dump the contents. As others have mentioned, it is slightly top heavy however you get used to it momentarily and it has not been an issue for me over all of these years.

title: Easy to use
body: I grew up with Danny Tanner as a cleanliness icon, then found Adrian Monk in my adult years. I was shopping for a good stick vac for a while, what sold me on this is that it plugs in. Considering my cleaning heroes, I require an item that will be ready on demand for as long as the cleaning requires. This maneuvers well, is light and gets the job done. Pro tip: if you have pets, you really do need to clean the filters monthly and you will likely need to clean out the head next to/above the roller from time to time, it makes a big difference. You really do get used to the way the the powerhouse hangs from the stick to stand for storage, you also do get used to setting it completely down when you need to let go of it during use. Godspeed and good cleaning!

title: Unstoppable Machine, Vacuum Cured My Depression
body: You're reading reviews for this vacuum because you have two concerns: hair and weight. Consider your problems solved. First, hair. As you can see from the attached image, I have the kind of long, extremely thick hair that strangles vacuum rollers dead in nanoseconds. This vacuum's roller has a groove carved into the plastic so you can quickly and easily slide a knife or scissor blade in, severing every hair with no hassle. Instant cleanup, no destroyed roller. The suction is no joke. There are two settings: one that is as powerful as my old vacuum on max power, and one that is TURBO CHARGED. This will demolish ground-in dirt and hair even from high-pile carpet or rugs. The suction is so powerful, even carpeting and rugs that have been pounded completely flat have the fibers physically pulled upwards, so even if your hairy little monster of a pet likes to destroy carpet or rug fibers, after vacuuming they feel plush and wonderful. Con: on Turbo mode, you will smell burning hair. The motor really is not kidding around and will set itself on fire before it allows the tiniest speck of dirt to remain on your floor. Second: weight. It's remarkably lightweight and very easy to heft around even with tiny elf arms. The maneuverability of the vacuum head is excellent and can work around such tight unwieldy places as between chair legs. All the pieces pop apart and reassemble with no trouble, so storage and transportation will never be an issue. Con: almost all of the weight is in the top handle, where the motor is. This can make it a tiny bit difficult to get the vacuum head to stay on the ground properly, and makes it nigh impossible for you just to stand the vacuum up anywhere and leave it there. Being top-heavy does it no favors. General design con: the canister is somewhat small and connected directly to the motor so you can't just pop it out, empty it into a bin, and pop it back into the vacuum. It's very easy to empty, but you are still going to have to heft the motor around with it, and the motor is obviously still going to be plugged into the wall. Good news is that the motor/handle/canister all pops free of the other bits with a simple lever press, so it's not like you need to carry the entire vacuum with you when you head to the bin. Bonus pro: there are a huge number of attachments, heads, and specialty bits and bobs in with the vacuum. I don't know what half of them are used for. Some are obviously for cleaning off stairs, or ceiling fans, or getting into crevasses, but some of them, who even knows. Literally whatever kind of application you'd like this vacuum for, there's probably a specialized nozzle for it. This is the cleanest my stairs have been in four years. Final pitch: look, I get it. I have a A Thing about money where no matter how worthy a purchase it is, a triple digit price tag makes me flinch. I put off getting a new vacuum for months and watched my own mental health spiral, knowing a contributing factor was that I was living in rising masses of dirt and grime. Danger had its element, too; a pie plate exploded (don't ask) and glass shards found themselves all over my kitchen floor, and some ended up in my feet. No vacuum to clean up the shards I couldn't see and couldn't get up with a broom and dustpan. I know being surrounded by painful messes we're powerless to fix is a 2020 mood and all, but this metaphor is a little too on the nose. I caved and bought the vacuum. I cranked her up this morning. This is the best I've felt in months. I know the price tag is a little steep compared to other lightweight vacs, but it's powerful and versatile enough that it's absolutely worth the expenditure. If you're looking for a worthwhile vacuum that will demolish human hair, pet hair, ground-in dirt, and particulates from any flooring you could possibly have, all while staying under $200, this is it.

title: Fantastic small room vacuum, much better than I expected.
body: I have a big Rainbow vacuum that I use to clean the entire house. I love the Rainbow because it uses water as a filtering medium, so suction remains strong no matter how dirty the "filter" gets and it effectively gets a new "filter" every time it's used. Its only downside is that it's large and bulky, so if I have to vacuum a small section (like, a carpet runner in a hallway) it's a bit of an ordeal to take out and set up. My basement has been converted to a space for my teenage daughter. Most of it is bare concrete (epoxy coated) but there's some carpeting here and there. Further, my daughter's pet rabbit makes its home in the basement so there's a fair amount of rabbit fur and debris (hay, bits of chewed cardboard, etc) around its area. My daughter has been "okay" with keeping the floors clean but since the Rainbow is big and bulky it wasn't as good as it should have been. So I went shopping for a small yet effective vacuum to handle this job and this Shark is where I landed. Truthfully I wasn't expecting very much, but after the first use I was shocked by how good it actually is. I wouldn't use it to clean the floors of the whole house (I can't see it's nearly-all-plastic construction lasting as long as my 35+ year old Rainbow) but I would absolutely use this for a small apartment. Or, of course, our basement. Assembly was insanely easy. I didn't have to refer to the owner's manual for anything, although after I used it I did check it out just to see if I was missing any features (I wasn't). The pieces simply slide and lock into place very securely, and are easy enough to disconnect/disassemble as needed. There are several well-marked, large release latches for this. I particularly liked how the power switch works. For hardwood (or concrete) floors, moving the switch to the first position enables the sweeper on the power head as well as suction, so you're not relying on JUST suction to pick up dirt. For carpeted floors, moving the switch forward enables the beater bar to really get into the carpet fibers. My daughter's pet rabbit roams an area of about 250 square feet, of which about half is carpeted and it hadn't been vacuumed in probably a month. After using this vacuum on it for the first time we filled the collection bin with bits of hay and rabbit fur and the carpet looked every bit as clean as when I use the Rainbow on it. The LED lights on the vacuum head is a nice touch, allowing you to more easily see dirt and debris on the floor (just look for the long shadows). Removing the power head doesn't make you blind, however, as there's a second LED on the vacuum motor that lights the area you're working on. The vacuum head isn't very tall at all, and the hose bends down enough to allow absolutely flat operation. Using this I was able to get under low-lying furniture like my daughter's desk and the nearby shelf units. Suction power is also very good, and consistent throughout its run. I expected the vacuum to be more like the handheld Dustbuster-type vacs we have in the house where power diminishes very quickly as the filter clogs up, but no. Power stayed consistent and strong even with a pretty sold mass of rabbit fur and straw filling the collection bin. Three things I don't like about it, but are minor things overall. First, it comes with a storage hook cast into the casing which is nice, but the matching hook for the wall is an extra-cost item. It's available on Amazon for an additional $24 or you can get an identical third-party unit for less than half. For a nearly-$200 vacuum cleaner, it's inexcusable for Shark to demand additional money for this piece. Second, it's top-heavy. Now, this isn't a shock considering the nature of the unit and I'm not exactly penalizing it for being what it is. But it does mean that when you're done using it for the moment (like, you want to unplug it, or you just need to move some furniture around) you're really going to want to just lay it down on the floor. More than once did I try to lean it against the wall only to have it slide down. If I wasn't paying attention it would have hit the floor hard (top-heavy, remember?) and probably damaged the plastics, which includes the collection bin. And third, the vacuum head doesn't have really good suction on the sides so cleaning the edges and corners of stairs isn't nearly as effective as cleaning the stair itself. You'll be removing the vacuum head to get into those nooks and crannies. Still, even with those issues I'd buy it again.

title: A *must have* for hard floor surfaces
body: Why did you pick this product vs others?: Another professional cleaning lady recommended this product to me. And I very happy she did! If you’re in the market for a new vacuum cleaner.. This is the one you need! Best thing I’ve found for hardwood floors. The suction is more than I expected. But, I don’t recommend it for Berber carpet. It’s too powerful and it immediately sucked up a loose piece of Berber and I had to pull it all out

title: Shark Vaccuum
body: I absolutely love this vaccuum! Its easy and compact. It’s a daily user at our house. It vacuums both hard woods & carpet floors. I can vacuum the entire house without having to switch heads to do both carpet and hardwood areas! It’s as easy as just switching the top switch to 1 (hardwood suction) or 2 (carpet/rugs with the spin brush on the bottom)

title: Great small vacuum- especially for the price
body: Happy Jaws 50th- great day to write a review for another Shark product that comes through! Was looking for a small handheld vac, and don’t want to spend big $$$. I have a Shark robot that does a great job, so I thought I’d give this a try since I really only needed something for a small patch of upstairs carpet and some hardwood stairs. Backstory- I got the “Wirecutter Recommended” $$$ one as a gift at my last place and it was ABS GARBAGE…the intake tube was tiny and the filter was poorly placed. Design flaw? Yes. It clogged in 30 sec and you spend 5 min unclogging with a wire hanger, before vacuuming for 30 sec then unclogging for 3 min and…you get it. Very happy with the Shark. Big tube, pretty big and well designed intake- you can actually vacuum a bit before you have to stop and clean. And a small container is the price you pay for portability. I don’t mind the cord, either- I don’t go far and it means: cheaper…and it doesn’t die. Good job Shark 🦈

title: Awesome! One unit that does it all.
body: Just unpacked today and cleaned a bunch of things. Worked great on the area rug and floors. So easy to switch modes! Door mats look great. And, it did a SUPER job on my cat haired sofa! Love the convertible brush thing. This is just a really well tough design. Swivels super easy, vacuums while flat. The handheld unit is a bit heavier than expected. Got a good workout 😅. Best thing I've bought in a while. Thanks Shark!!

title: Can’t stop using it!
body: I am OBSESSED with this. I needed something small for our main floor; Lots of area rugs, carpeted stairs but not fully carpeted or high pile. Previously had an off brand cordless, but knew it wasn’t getting everything up. The dust, dirt, and pet hair this thing has picked up in its short stay has been fulfilling and disgusting. It is small yet mighty. Most likely will get another one to stash upstairs. 10/10 recommend.

title: TOP HEAVY
body: Has great suction because its a corded device. The battery ones never maintained their strength. Positives: suction strength, shark brand usually very dependable, canister easy to empty and keep clean, price. Negatives.. its very top heavy. The length is long and not adjustable. I am short. With the top heaviness and length.. it is tiresome. The vacuum head is higher profile than I would like. Doesn’t fit under some furniture. The accessory pieces are a little cheezy too. .

title: Great Product but please note:
body: This product performed very well in my home which is almost all hardwood floor with 1 room with a 10x10 area rug. Please be aware of the following: 1) the unit does NOT seem to be designed to stand upright as you vacuum - easy solution is to just lay it down if needed as you go. No big deal once you accept the fact. 2) this is NOT a vacuum designed to work on large areas of plush carpet. There are other products out there for this. 3) instructions say my area rug should be vacuumed on the level 1 setting, but the level 2 setting seemed to really get out the dust 4) there are no places to store the attachments on the vacuum itself - who cares, just store them somewhere else

title: Durable and Powerful.
body: just received my replacement order I had a problem with the first delivery. NOTE: I have this same model since 2014 it is still working it is convenient, light weight and durable so many uses just purchased a second Photo attached: the vac on the right is the older one.

title: Beats the purple pricy one.
body: I bought this because the purple pricy one that starts with a D and ends with son is my husband's from his single days and while it doesnt suck thats the point of this device. This one SUCKS! Now that we are married he basically adopted my dog and we need more horsepower for her black hairs. We are neat freaks with allergies and using this device once a week keeps our home looking like we don't have a pet. Its quite loud but nothing sound proof headphones wont block while you clean. The cord is super long so I can do two rooms before replugging it. Be sure to empty it after each use for best results.

title: It’s a winner
body: Easy to assemble- intuitive- couple pieces easily snap together. Nice long cord. Light weight and easy to handle. I have a very thick area rug and other vacuum did not glide on it and would stick in place. This one glides beautifully & picked up very well. Emptying canister is easy, and bc it’s small you just empty it after each use. I used it on hardwood floor, then swept the floor to see how much it missed- which was very little. The suctions is strong. Gets close to walls and under bed. It does not stand on its own, but I leaned it against wall in closet with no issues. It also has place on back to hang from hook. I lovenit and recommend it.

title: Great, except emptying the dust bin is a \"chore!\"
body: A very good budget friendly, light weight for my multi level home. It is powerful without "chewing up my area rugs!" My only complaint : the "dust bin" is not detachable as does the more expensive model (that we currently own) I do not like to have unplug the long cord , roll it up, detach the upper part of the vacuum JUST to empty the dust bin after each vacuuming. This take several minutes!

title: I love this vac
body: This is a review of the Shark Rocket Ultra-light (box says Pet) vacuum, model # HV301, the orange and gray one that has apparently been around for years and has lots of great reviews. (See photo.) There are other models sold on the same product page, making reading reviews confusing if you don't know which model is being reviewed. Read carefully when ordering, too, to get the model you want. I've only had it a couple of days but so far I'm very pleased with it. It's pulling an appalling amount of embedded dirt from my low pile carpet and does a great job on my hard surface floors. It's very easy to use and isn't horribly loud for such strong suction. It has two speeds, one for hard floors/area rugs or using the attachments, and one for carpet. I'm not used to a vacuum with the motor at the top, but it's not heavy and I love that it lies flat to easily get under beds and swivels around furniture. The cord is about 25 feet long. It includes three attachments: upholstery, crevice, and dusting tools. These and the floor unit can attach to either the long wand or to the upper motor for use as a handheld vac. Simple and very easy to put together or separate the parts as needed. The attachments aren't stored on the vacuum, but I like that. I don't want the added bulk or weight when I'm vacuuming floors. The filters are very easy to change and only need to be removed, rinsed, and air dried once a month. Another smaller filter can go even longer. The long cord wraps for storage and the top motor part can hook lower down so it stands alone anywhere. It will also stand against a wall without moving the top part, but it won't stand alone that way in the middle of the floor. The dirt cup isn't very large but is okay. I wish the dirt cup would detach (as on some other models) so that the motor and cord don't have to be taken to the trash can, but that's one less thing to break and isn't much of an inconvenience. It has a light that lets you know if the roller brush gets clogged, but there are no illuminating lights. The roller cover removes using a coin, although I haven't needed to do that. For me, ease and simplicity of use and the excellent performance in cleaning are the important factors, and this stick vac excels at those. This is a great vacuum especially for the price. I got it on sale but at regular price it's still less expensive than many comparable vacs. Surprisingly it has a long 5-year warranty. This will supplement but won't replace my robot vac which will still be used for frequent, effortless lighter cleanings, but it will replace my ancient, heavy, falling-apart upright which apparently I haven't used nearly often enough, judging by what this vacuum is removing. I'll add this vac to the routine. The robot is great at removing pet hair but isn't nearly as good at removing embedded dirt. I wish I'd bought this Shark sooner. Especially if you have any carpet, or if you don't already have a good vacuum with attachments, I highly recommend this Shark. (No matter what type floor, if you have pets who shed, I also highly recommend the Wyze robot vac for that, between deeper cleanings.)

title: Lightweight
body: This is a great value for the price! I have 2 dogs and 2 cats and it keeps up with all the hair. Great suction and is lightweight. Has small collection container, not a deal breaker just have to dump it more often. I would buy this again.

title: This Baby Shark has a big bite
body: Finally! I've finally come to my senses and given up on the cordless vacuum. I've had 3... they always start out being incredible and ultimately the lithium batteries just don't hold up. So, I saw this little baby shark and thought I'd give it a try. I needed something light weight because of my shoulder injuries related to caring for my mom, but I also needed to be powerful. And that's exactly what this turned out to be. This shark has a real bite. I filled and emptied the container several times but that's because the crappy cordless vacuum is had kept dying so I hadn't really had a good vacuum. Until now.... love love love it.....

title: Not perfect but good
body: Generally speaking, this is a good product. The suction is decent. The only thing I don't like is that it's heavy. It also does not stand upright by itself. It must be leaned against something. The attachments are very useful, but the vacuum doesn't have anywhere to hold the pieces. I will be keeping this product because the suction is good for both hardwood and rug. I have medium sized dog.

title: Great Value + Highly Satisfactory Stick Vacuum
body: I have only used this vacuum once- based on the first use I am very happy with this vacuum (vertex duo clean). Now, it is true that you have to lean it against something when you use it and store it. I’ve dealt with that before and it’s not a dealbreaker for me, but someone else may find that highly inconvenient. Also, I found that because of the power of the vacuum it feels like the vacuum is getting away from me- I’m just not used to it yet and I will absolutely take it for the sake of a powerful vacuum and a lightweight one at that- these are two things that I absolutely wanted and I got them. The other heavy vacuum I have was too hard on my shoulders and I don’t have this issue now, so for me this is a win. The self cleaning roll is also something I wanted, and having the cord I do not have to fret about it losing power before I’m done or fading out near the end. For a medium priced stick vacuum I would rank this as highly satisfactory, just consider what your personal priorities are and it meets mine! Happy to have it.

title: Top tier power, small capacity not an issue
body: Everything I was looking for in a compact vacuum! I have a kitty living with me and have been lint-rolling everything to remove fur... this bad boy makes all of my upholstry look brand new! I suggest pairing it with Ms. Myers Pet Spray, everything is fresh and super clean! The corded power is so much better than the corded ones and the cord is long enough that I can strategically plug it in and access my apartment from just two places. It is super powerful and while not large in capacity, I prefer that as it keeps me cleaning it more regularly. The capacity was my main concern when deciding between this price point of vacuum so I have to mention that I have no regrets getting the smaller one! It was super easy to empty and to switch between the full vacuum and the handheld upholstery brush features. It is a little heavier than I expected after using my cordless candy, but I think that comes from the quality of materials Shark uses to build its products. I am a DIE HARD Shark fan!

title: 100% Yes on this vacuum
body: Have a dog and live in a smaller home. I needed something that wasn’t too big and would get up all the dog hair, sand, dirt, beach, and frankly my long hair too and this did it! Great product especially for the price!

title: Great suction and versitile use.
body: I have been impressed with this vacuum since I received it. Great suction and versatility. That it can turn into a hand vac is even more awesome. I have low and medium pile rugs and it does great. I would argue at the moment it works better than my regular vacuum. If I was going to recommend a change, I would like the vacuum canister/motor to at least turn sideways so yo can get under the bed easier. The height of the canister prevents from flattening enough to reach all the way under my bed. I so pleased with all its use and efficacy, I am still very happy with it.

title: Powerful corded vacuum
body: I purchased this to vacuum my stairs. It is heavier than I anticipated, but I was still able to use it to clean the stairs. The suction and airflow are outstanding. I have an upright Shark and also a Dyson. This could replace those.

title: La mejor!!
body: La mejor aspiradora que he tenido, después de ensayar con varias marcas definitivamente esta es la mejor, funciona tanto para pisos duros como para alfombras, tiene un gran poder de absorción, tengo mascotas en mi casa y es perfecta porque recoge el pelo y la arena si mucho esfuerzo! Recomendada al 100%

title: Great vacuum? Yes. Replaces your upright? No.
body: Original Review (UPDATE AT BOTTOM): I bought this hoping to replace my current Dyson DC33 vacuum with a vacuum that's more portable and convenient. I have multiple dogs in my house that shed hair like crazy and I vacuum very frequently to keep everything clean. The box advertises that it cleans better than an upright Dyson but after thoroughly testing it out on the different flooring and different rooms in my house, unfortunately I feel it didn't work well enough to replace my Dyson. Don't get me wrong, the Shark Rocket did outperform the Dyson by a long shot on different flooring and I am keeping it because of that. The following are the tests I performed (note I went two weeks without vacuuming prior to this test and I cleaned both vacuums out between tests): After unboxing it, I tried vacuuming one of my carpeted hallways. I have regular short carpeting and I noticed that the shark kept pulling away from me the whole time and kept skipping across the surface. I could tell the vacuum is too light to get a good deep clean. I tried holding it at an angle and putting a bit of pressure down on it and that seemed to help a lot, it was just awkward and uncomfortable to hold and maneuver like this. The shark picked up a lot of hair and dust and I had a full canister at the end. I then used my Dyson over the same carpet I just cleaned with the shark and noticed the difference. The Dyson filled up almost a quarter of its full size canister with hair and dust that the Shark missed. Next I moved one of our rooms that has hard wood flooring. I ran the shark with its included hard wood floor tool and was amazed by how well it cleaned the floors. The white micro fiber cloth was dirty afterwards and the floor felt much cleaner than it did with my Dyson. I also was impressed with how easy it was to use to clean under the bed and desk in that room. After using the Shark I went over the floors like I normally do with the Dyson and the Dyson picked up nothing. To make sure that I wasn't being bias I cleaned out the two vacuums, went to the other room I have with hard wood and tried using the Dyson first. I then went over the floors with the Shark and again it out performed the Dyson. The Microfiber pad that the Shark has cleans the hardwood floors significantly better than the Dyson could and the Shark gets under beds and desks much better than my Dyson. Next I tried using the shark in one of my bathrooms with bathroom tile. I had the same outcome as I did with the hardwood floors. I started with the Shark, and then went over the floors with the Dyson. The Shark's canister was about halfway full and the Dyson picked up nothing. I cleaned them out and moved to my other bathroom with tile in it and tried using the Dyson first. The Dyson picked up quite a bit but again the Shark outperformed the Dyson. Finally I have a large area rug in my living room and I used the Dyson first on one half and then went over it with that same half with the Shark. The Dyson got most of the hair and dust out of it but I noticed that the Shark picked up about a quarter of its small canister that the Dyson missed. I believe it's from the edges of the rug, the Dyson's suction always pulls up the edges of the rug and is too difficult to vacuum close to the edges. The shark on it's lower setting cleaned the outer edges of the rug without having this problem. Next I cleaned out both vacuums and used the Shark first on the other half of the area rug. It performed very well and filled its little canister up with hair pretty quick. I went over that half with the Dyson and it did pick up a little bit (barely noticeable amount) that the Shark missed but in my opinion, the hassle of the Dyson pulling up the edges of the rug isn't worth it, the Shark was much easier to use and cleaned the rug very well. Overall the Shark Rocket outperforms my Dyson DC33 upright on hardwood, tile, and area rugs but the Shark just doesn't work well enough on carpet to completely replace my upright. I'm impressed enough with the performance of the Shark that I am keeping it to use on all my flooring except for carpet. The only other thing I noticed is that my hand and arm did get tired from holding up the Shark the whole time cleaning and the Shark won't stand upright on its own, you either have to hold it the whole time, or lay it on the floor between cleanings. If you are looking for a good and convenient vacuum for hardwood, tile, or area rugs, I would highly recommend this vacuum. If you are looking for a vacuum to replace an old upright and plan to use it on carpeting, buy another upright, not this. This a great vacuum to use to clean quick messes on carpeting but I don't feel it cleans carpet well enough to fully replace an upright. UPDATE: I've had the vacuum for a few weeks now and after frequently using it, I still feel the same as my initial review above, this is a great vacuum but I don't feel it's good enough to fully replace an upright with. Yesterday I decided to try using the vacuum to clean out the inside of my car and I was impressed with how well the micro cleaning kit (included in HV302)cleaned all of the usually hard places to clean. I used the micro cleaning kit to vacuum out the vents, cup holders, dash board, and other places in the car that are too difficult to get with a rag and it worked great. I also used the regular accessories to vacuum my cloth seats which worked very well and they are noticeably more clean. I started using the vacuum on the floors of my car but I quickly changed my mind after it sucked up a few small pebbles which immediately started bashing around the inside of the canister which I feel would have caused damage to the vacuum if I kept going. As far as this vacuum as a car cleaner, I would suggest using a shop vac on the floors of the car (if you have a gravel driveway like me) and then using this vacuum to clean your seats, vents, and other hard to clean places. If you plan on using this vacuum to clean your car, I would HIGHLY recommend getting the micro cleaning kit, it made cleaning my car that much easier.

Then for whatever reason I decided to go over the carpet again to see if it would suck up anymore after already using this and it did! So I decided to repeat and vacuumed my living room and bedroom 10 times dumping after each vacuum because I kept seeing if it could suck up more after dumping the collection chamber until it finally didn’t suck anything else up! It also sucked up a broken sewing needle to save my feet and my dogs paws! No idea where it sucked the needle up from. It collected dust! Hair! Looked like powder stuff so I’m guessing someone sprinkled the carpet refreshers in the past on the carpets. I cleaned the roller 2 times because it collected longer hair around it. Also has guides for your scissors to help you clip the hair away from it! I will be recommending this vacuum to anyone with carpet. I did use the duster attachment to clean my ceiling fan and that worked great! No dust on me or the floor. The only con I would say is that the motor smells funny and it does get warm where the “exhaust” would be which I’ve never had with any other vacuums. Other Positives; I wish I had this when I moved into the new place and had time to use this before furniture got placed in my living room. Feeling safer now that I have this for my dog to lay on the carpet. I prefer to not have carpet but wasn’t an option with this rental. Will be using this before carpet cleaning. Also a huge plus, it is effortless to remove the sections of the tube! My other stick vacuum that is wireless is a huge pain to remove the sections. I prefer wireless vacuums for the convenience but the cord on this vacuum is nice and long, easy to wind up. Over all I highly recommend this vacuum! Definitely disgusting to see how much is trapped inside carpets when you have an incredible vacuum! Also it’s not overly loud, my dog stayed on the couch with this vacuum verse my cordless vacuum she would follow me around at our last house vacuuming the wood floors.

title: Don't buy a cordless stick vacuum — buy this instead!
body: I purchased this Shark Rocket corded stick vacuum after purchasing a cordless vacuum from another brand — and this was the best decision I could have made. The issue with cordless stick vacuums are that the batteries simply just never last long enough. The battery on cordless vacuums typically drain faster, which means you go to through more battery cycles and therefore the faster the battery would need to be replaced. This is not the case with this Shark stick vacuum — because the unit is corded. While you trade off some of the convenience and ease of mobility you get with cordless models, despite the cord, this unit is still light enough to easily get around a home. The Shark corded stick vacuum is powerful enough to suck up whatever mess you throw at it and the HEPA filtration ensures that the air is kept as clean as possible. Once your done vacuuming, with just one press, the dust container opens up to toss the dust away. To store the device, simply mount the vacuum head to the base and the unit can sit upright and stored virtually anywhere. I almost forgot — Shark Rocket comes with some other handy tools such as the crevice tool, the upholstery tool, and the dusting brush. I personally used the crevice tool to get into those hard to reach areas and the dusting brush to clean window blinds. Both worked great in my use. Now here are the downsides. While the Shark Rocket stick vacuum is lighter compared to other traditional vacuums, the actual head unit is top heavy, meaning you can't prop the unit to stand upright if you want to take a break. Additionally pushing the unit will require a little bit more strength to push around since the top part weighs more than the base. Furthermore, while this vacuum worked great on hardwood and tiles, it did not work the best on low pile carpet and rugs, despite advertised as working on these types of material. Don't get me wrong, it will clean your basic low pile rugs but if you intend to use this vacuum on medium to high pile carpet, you're going to be let down. My last gripe is, that with all the tools that this unit comes with, it does not come with a wall mount to place everything on. All in all, if you're looking for a lightweight vacuum to clean hardwood, tiled flooring and occasionally some low pile rugs, this is the best vacuum for the job — without having to deal with the battery woes of cordless models. However, if you expect this vacuum to clean various level of medium to high pile carpet, your best off looking elsewhere.

title: Checked all my boxes
body: I wanted a vacuum that was lightweight, could function as an upright as well as a more portable vacuum, and with attachments that were easy to switch out. My other vacuum is a 13-year-old Dyson Animal – I like it, but it’s heavy at 19 lbs., hard to lug up and downstairs, and requires a lot of thumb pressure to remove attachments. I wanted high quality but didn’t want to spend what I did on the Dyson. The Shark Rocket TruePet Ultralight Vacuum checked all my boxes, and then some. 1. The “rocket” handheld part is only 4 lbs. Perfect for when I constantly need to suck up ladybugs that have squeezed their way inside in the autumn. Or for many other quick vacuum needs. When paired with the long wand and rotating floor brush it’s still only about 8 pounds. 2. Attachments easily click in, and easily detach with a rocker switch. 3. After I received the TruePet, I carefully vacuumed a couple rooms first with the Dyson, and then followed with the Shark. It picked up a little more dust than the Dyson. 4. Less than half the price of the Dyson! 5. The LED lights are awesome. They are on both the rocket and the rotating floor brush, and highlight stuff you wouldn’t otherwise see. 6. The TruePet Motorized Brush is why I sought out this particular model. Shark has several models in the HV320 series. Their website isn’t good at showing how they differ. I think they all have the same rocket, but are accessorized differently. And including the motorized brush makes this a good deal because it’s the same price as the others in the series. This thing has really good power. I have a similar accessory on my Dyson, but it is big and clunky and will fall off the hose if you don’t hold onto it. Shark’s brush clicks in securely so you don’t have to worry about it. 7. Flexible hose. It’s only about 12 inches or so, but it’s a handy extra to have when you need extra reach to get into smaller spaces or just need the flexibility. Kudos to Amazon for being the only online retailer that I could find that even mentions this accessory. Even the box doesn’t tell you everything that is included, until you open the box and see the list on the inside flaps. That was frustrating, because I bought a different model in the HV320 series first only to find it didn’t come with what I wanted. Kudos also to the reviewer(s) who posted photos of the box contents. That really helped! 8. The dust bin. This holds plenty for its size, and is easy to remove and empty without making a big mess. 9. Pushing this as an upright is a breeze. I do have low-pile carpeting, but it feels like it’s self-propelled. I can feel the resistance when I pull back, so I know the suction is good. 10. Loved that Amazon’s packaging came with not only a bigger Amazon box to hide the contents, but the original box was snugly inside another plain box from the manufacturer. Well protected and nobody had to know what had been delivered. 11. Some comment that it doesn't stand upright by itself. Not a big deal to me because it's really easy to detach the rocket and hang it on the wand near the floor. Negatives? Like others have mentioned, it would be nice to have a hard floor brush tool available without having a microfiber cloth. Applications would be basement floor or if it's dirty enough that you'd like to pre-clean before using the tool with the attached cloth. Since the first stroke on a surface isn't always a forward stroke, the microfiber pad would stay cleaner longer if there was suction behind as well as in front of the pad. The wand attached to the hard floor tool (the one with the pad) doesn't lock in and stay upright whether the rocket is hanging on the bottom of the wand for storage or not. It would be nice if the on-board tool clip allowed you to click in the accessories instead of just staying on with friction, because they have a tendency to fall off. But then the accessories meant to go on that clip don't click in to the vacuum either. The rolling floor brush doesn't slide all the way under my coffee table, which has a shelf 3.5" off the floor. It will slide in 8", up to the point where the rolling brush meets the handle. That's still at least 6" further than my Dyson can go, so at least it's an improvement.

title: I'm reviewing a vacuum....
body: We have one very sweet little cat that seems to lose it's weight in hair every month - it's everywhere. Not to mention kitty litter and dried up bits of food that coat the floors in all of the rooms week upon week... I've only ever had $60-80 vacuums and with all of the trouble they have caused with clogged filters, lack of power and loss of suction, I decided to invest in this Shark and I have to say, it's a darn good vacuum. When I'm using this thing, I believe I actually have a look on my face similar to the woman in the pictures - like we're content to vacuum all day long and possibly for a living. It truly is a joy to use - very lightweight but still has some heft in the main motor unit so you can tell it is built well. And it is powerful - I haven't kept up with the technological advances in home vacuums and haven't done the tests with nuts, bolts, marbles or a bowling ball - but it does hurt when you get it stuck to your face - FYI. All of the attachments connect to the unit with a satisfying click and are effortlessly removed. The carpet sweeper unit helps propel itself forward on even the thicker carpets which is a treat because the older cheapo units would get stuck in some areas. Maneuverability and getting under low clearance objects is now done with total ease. The hardwood floor attachment with the terrycloth pad that wipes while moving it across the floor works well too. And though the dual lights on the carpet sweeper and the one on the main unit look really cool (like Audi supplied headlights for this thing), I was surprised to find that they actually light up the carpet/floor and work very well in spotting areas you may have missed. The smaller upholstery sweeper is my favorite attachment and after using it on two of my sofas, I was amazed (and then equally appalled) at how much dirt and hair was deposited into the bin. And the bin is small - like others reviewers stated, I had to empty it 3-4 times after doing the whole place on the first use. However, like a lot of them said, that was just the first time going through what I previously presumed to be my clean apartment. The next week yielded far less and I only had to empty twice (and that's because I leave the bin clean for the next use to gauge how dirty things get over the week). It's a cinch to empty and clean - unlike the last Hoover I owned...I don't want to talk about that. The other truly wonderful thing about this vacuum and my main reason for buying it is it's small footprint. It's not designed to stand upright on it's own but if you live in a 1 bedroom apartment with valuable limited closet space and a girlfriend/wife that wants all that limited space to herself for her "stuff", you don't want a vacuum taking up space where your Taylormade's clearly fit and absolutely belong. A plastic wall/door mount hook comes in the box and I now have it mounted on the wall close to the ceiling inside my precious tool closet where it fits perfectly and is totally out of the way of anything else stuffed in there, the bag of attachments hanging right next to it. The only slightly annoying part is cord management (and I say this coming from a vacuum that had a retractable cord so don't take it too seriously unless you currently have one with that option and have gotten used to the bliss of not having to wrap and then unwrap when you are told you missed an area that needs cleaning). There is a cord hook on the main unit and then a hook on the carpet sweeper and the floor sweeper. If you have the cord wrapped around the hooks on the unit and either of those attachments, you cannot remove that attachment from the extension pole without unwrapping the cord completely. It's a small hassle and easily remedied by just wrapping the cord around the main unit handle and dust bin instead of using the hooks. That way, you can interchange and store the way you want without fussing with the cord first. As you can tell, I'm not getting technical on this review - I don't know much about vacuums because they aren't my thing and it took some deep reasoning and soul searching for me to pull the trigger on a $250 (with tax) dirt sucking machine - I was simultaneously looking at any other FUN electronic item for the same amount before I clicked buy. But, all-in-all, I'm happy with the choice and thanks to all the reviewers who helped me make it. If you're living with someone who has de facto control over all of the storage space in a 1 bedroom apartment with 4 small closets but only 1.5 you can call yours and everything of communal use has to go in your closet exclusively, this is the vacuum for you. If you have more space to work with and call your own, good for you - very happy for you. You will like the vacuum too.

title: It isn't \"Ultra-Light.\"
body: Pros: Powerful vacuum. Very good pick-up; gets under most tight spaces; worked well picking up Border Collie's fur. Has 2 ht .levels for non-carpeted vs. carpeted floors. Needed help from husband to open dirt cup because, he said, "It had a very strong vacuum seal," (also, I have a serious case of "girl hands"). Afterwards, opened up easily. Cord is long for a small space, but I have hardwood floors in every room downstairs (abt 1,600 sq. feet), so I usually need an extension cord if I don't want to keep stopping to relocate the plug (pet peeve) :( I also chose this vac to do my carpeted stairs. My older stick vac is battery powered - even b4 finishing all of my wood floors, the battery dies, and the suction on carpet is puny. I needed a corded vac for power and one I could easily disassemble and use as a hand-held. This one is great for both needs, and picking up pet fur is key. The only real Con I have is that the part you hold, the motor head, is heavier than I thot it would be. After 2 rooms, my hand(s) started to hurt. After 4 rms., (out of 7) arms started hurting. Having said that, my girl hands do lead to girl arms. And I'm approaching 67 yrs old . And I stopped working out 'cus of Covid shutdowns 3 yrs. ago. Don't judge me.;) So the weight of it is subjective. It is reasonable that to get a powerful vac, the motor probably does need to be bigger and I do want the power. Only, I would suggest not calling it "ultra light" but, rather, state how much the motor head weighs in the 1st line of description (admittedly, I didn't actually look at "further details" where a total wt. is probably given, because "ultra light" was in the title.) But , specifically, it's the wt. of the motor head that matters to a weakling like me. :) I removed 1 star due to the "ultra light" description being misleading.

title: High end on a budget!
body: First of all, I will start this for saying, I’m one of those people that are very hard to please when it comes pillows, comforters, and such. I’m basically the princess and the pea lol. I suffer from headaches very bad, especially in the morning time and for years now I’ve been on the hunt for a good pillow and I have yet to find one that doesn’t keep me tossing and turning all night. I’m perimenopausal, so I have very bad night sweats. So I was looking for some thing that would keep me cool. This is probably my third set of pillows from Amazon in the last two years and I have to say I was reluctant but initially I saw some on TikTok and I figured I could probably get these cheaper on Amazon! They are actually on sale for like $26 for two king-size pillows which to me is a great steal! They came packaged very nicely, as you can see in plastic wrap and vacuum sealed. I took them out and allowed them to expand and then I threw them in the dryer to fluff them and sanitize. The color is white on white is very vibrant. The material a soft it is not super sick, but not cheaply made also. I do believe they would hold up well in the wash. The pillows are very comfortable. They have just the right amount of squish. They do not conform to my head shape, but they don’t hold my head up uncomfortably. They are very supportive of my neck and back and I still wake up with headaches, but I think that’s due to other issues I have, but I will say the headaches are not as severe lately since I’ve been using these pillows for a week. I wanted to give myself time using them before I made this review. My significant other also said they were very comfortable that it was like sleeping on a hotel pillow, which is exactly what we were going for! Overall I think these pillows are great. I would definitely recommend them to others. The only reason I didn’t give them five stars is because I have seen better pillows in hotels, but this is very comparable to some and definitely good quality.

title: Will stay in the bottle after all!
body: Update: You actually do have to push these in "too far" if your beverage is carbonated. If you leave them where they're supposed to be, the carbonation will pop the top out, usually within 24 hours. If you push it past that, as far as it will go (almost to the rim) you'll get a seal that will withstand the pressure. Yay! These create a great seal if you twist them down to the exact correct spot. It's easy to push them in too far, past the point of a perfect seal. However, if you use them in a bottle of carbonated beverage - Mexican Coke for example - they will almost always pop off within 12 hours. They don't seal tight enough to withstand the build up of carbonation, which pops them out almost every time. Then the real fun of trying to find it somewhere in your fridge begins. body: Years ago, was gifted a couple of these, by the marketing rep for the Conegliano Valdobiadene prosecco region. They weren't available for purchase in the United States at the time. These have never leaked, never opened inadvertently, have held up to years of professional bar use, on catering events. These Kloveo's are the same as the ones I was gifted years ago. The pictures show the new Kloveo on the left, next to one of my originals, which has been in professional service for almost ten years. Bought the two pack, and the lock cage on one is not set quite straight. Seems to work fine, just not as smooth in use as it could be. Minor thing, I guess. Seals fine. I saw the reviews nothing QC issues. There's going to be manufacturing defects sometimes, with anything. It's frustrating, but these really are the most solid performing sparkling wine cap design I know of, and I've used most of them. My original set have been banged around a lot, and work as well as the day I got them. Occasionally, wine gets through the little vent hole in the silicone seal, and becomes oxidized. It's a pain to address, because there's no good way to rinse it out. My solution is hydrogen peroxide, wooden toothpick, and a pair of rubber or nitrile gloves. Chlorine bleach works too, but can oxidize the rivets on the swivel, and maybe weaken the hard plastic parts. It could also affect the flavor of the wine. Hydrogen peroxide breaks down into oxygen and water, has never caused a problem for me. I've had success with the drugstore hydrogen peroxide. Some non-chlorine bleach is just hydrogen peroxide, water, and citric acid, would also work well. It's basically twice the strength of the drugstore stuff. It's tedious to get the hydrogen peroxide into the silicone nipple, but it does bleach the issue, and you don't have to try to rinse it back out. It won't adversely affect the wine. These sparkling wine stoppers are well worth having. Best you can get, imo.

body: Easy to operate, with no learning curve. UPDATE - LONG VERSION: This is now the second place Wine Saver at www.cooksillustrated.com, as they have found a better one that preserves wine for longer. Here's what they had to say: "For years we’ve preserved open bottles of wine either by using the Vacu Vin Wine Saver, an inexpensive ($9.29) pair of rubber stoppers with a pump that sucks the air out of the bottle, or by pouring leftover wine into a smaller bottle or Mason jar to stave off oxidation. But innovative new gadgets promise to keep wine drinkable longer. We tested six tools, including the Vacu Vin, on half-empty bottles of red and white wine, comparing and evaluating the wines’ flavors and drinkability at various time intervals. ....Our old favorite worked reliably and kept wine drinkable for a week, but two new models bested it. As of press time, these two models had kept wine drinkable for one month. (We’ll continue to taste and report, so check our website for updates.) By inserting one model's sharp, hollow needle through the cork—we never had to uncork the bottle—we could pour just the amount of wine that we wanted while activating a pressurized capsule that simultaneously fed argon (an inert gas) into the bottle to displace the tapped wine. Not even our trained wine expert could say which was fresher: a month-old bottle sealed by this product or a freshly opened bottle of the same vintage. Another, cheaper product is a worthy Best Buy: It forms a barricade against air when its balloon is lowered into the bottle and inflated just above the surface of the leftover wine. On the downside, it’s slightly finicky and can be used on only one bottle at a time." Their new winner, for a short while, was the Coravin Wine Access System, but that was recalled (see www.cooksillustrated.com for more details), and the latest first-place is the Air Cork The Wine Preserver: "Once you get the hang of lowering the food-safe latex balloon into the bottle and inflating it just above the leftover wine’s surface, this budget-friendly device effectively seals off air, preserving wine’s drinkability for at least one month (we are continuing to test). A downside: You can seal only one bottle at a time. Balloons are guaranteed for 80 uses; replacement balloons cost about $4."

title: A reliable necessity for wine lovers
body: I've gone through or tried several vacuum units in the past decade. One, a one-piece unit, worked well but eventually gave up the ghost after many years when the rubber gasket that provides the seal with the bottle shredded - just from a lot of wear; unfortunately this unit was no longer to be found when I finally needed to replace it. Another one piece unit purchased recently through Amazon performed poorly, not making or holding a good seal. I also tried a two piece unit similar to the Vacu Vin, except it also never established a meaningful seal and was a total waste of money. The Vacu Vin, in contrast, is great great great. I've been using it for months now and I am very happy with it; it's consistent in providing a vacuum that lasts at least 2-3 days giving a satisfying resistance and a little pop when I pull the plug. The audible cue for when a vacuum has been achieved is a nice feature, although I must say I found that if I keep going a bit beyond the point where the cue kicks in I seem to establish a better, longer lasting seal, compared to if I stop pumping as soon as the cue kicks in. If a two piece unit works well, as this one does, it is preferable to a one piece for several reasons: First, the sealed bottle is accommodated into cabinets or fridges better, being shorter. Second, you can buy additional vacuum plugs to use with the single vacuum pump, making it easy to replace worn plugs and have more than two bottles "in circulation" at any one time. Third, you don't jeopardize the performance of the pump when you wash the plugs. While I've seen a couple reviews complaining that the pump on this unit can eventually fail after a couple of years' use, to me that is quite acceptable for something that is used every day and extends the lifetime of precious and potentially expensive wine. I would have no problem buying one of these every year if necessary, considering the money I saved by being able to make a bottle retain its quality over several days after openning. Think about it - it's like paying $12 for a year's insurance on hundreds of dollars worth of wine. Update: the seal is unbelievably good. Recently I stored a 25% full bottle for two weeks under the vacuum seal with the Vacu Vin. When I realized how long it had been in the cabinet I decided to toss the contents and when I removed the Vacu Vin plug the bottle was still under vacuum. Amazing. Don't know how good the wine was at this point - I didn't care to test it. But that's not the point. Vacuum is really excellent - at least if you pump somewhat past the audible signal that vacuum has been achieved.

title: Have faith that it works!
body: It is a cheap plastic air pump that seems to remove at least some of the air from half-drunk wine bottles. The rubber corks provided make a little "piff" sucking sound when you remove them after doing the vacuvin pump motion. This suggests there is a bit of a vacuum created in the bottle...so I'd be inclined to think it works as designed. To really know if it works, you'd have to do an experiment with two identical bottles of wine....drink half of each, vacuvin pump one, and compare it to the other that has just had the cork put back into it. If the vacuvin-treated wine tastes better than the other one after a week of storage at room temp, you'd know it works....prevents the wine from getting vinegar-like. I have not done this test yet, but it seems to make sense that removing some of the air (O2) would cut down on oxidation of the CH2OH to CH3COOH. If you really wanted an answer, you'd do a quantitative chemical assay for acetic acid in both bottles. The one that has been "vacuvined" should have less vinegar in it! A better method might be to gas the headspace of the bottle with an inert gas like N2 or Argon...but that could be a bit over the top, unless you are drinking very expensive wine. I'm afraid I'm a bottom shelf kinda guy....so maybe its not even worth saving a partially drunk bottle! Just use it for cooking :)

title: Clicks! (Guideline)

Anyway, I've kinda noticed the pattern till it clicks, so use this as a guideline: If you open a new bottle, pour one glass and cap it, it takes 3-4 pulls to hear the clicks. If your bottle is nearly empty, 10-11 pulls. Simple as that. (Besides, the pump becomes so heavy that it's nearly impossible to pull when it's done, eve if you miss the clicks!) title: Update

So, I replaced the stopper, pumped till it clicked (twice, again...), and even though it stayed in one piece this time, the stopper came out far too easily the next evening, suggesting zero vacuum. I had previously used another brand that really did the job for many years, (till the pump was lost during a move). So, I doubt it's a matter of unrealistic expectations. This bottle of wine is a sacrificial one, tasting like any other 2-3d/o red. It just didn't work. Update - 2 bottles later... This works just fine! The top of the other three stoppers never came off, and the vacuum was maintained overnight. The previous vacuum issue in my case must have been due to a change in elevation and temperature. Something to keep in mind.

But, sometimes, you don't want any more wine. Sometimes, the wine is not really "drinkable" at this time. So, this is a preservative solution! At the very least, I feel good when I hear the "click" of this sealer telling me that my "Walmart" wine or my more expensive wine, is sealed until I choose it again. Beware the obvious. I purchased this for my daughter several years ago. When I asked her "how did this work for you"?, her response was that "we never have a bottle to save"!! So, I would say that there are two things here - the first is that you are trying to save wine for later. The second is that you're trying to pretend that you're not going to drink more in a few minutes!. Whatever, this product seems to do the job and cheaply. I recently ordered 4 more corks as I'm sure that my wife threw away one of the two that comes with it. So, do I divorce my wife or not because she maybe thew away a cork or not? Well, if you like wine, it may be a "tossup". Bottom line, I think this pump has real value, especially if you're not going to drink the whole bottle at one time. It's cheap, and I think it works at removing the air. Now, if there was only a cheap solution to removing someone from your life or buying cheaper alcohol, I'd be the first in line!!

title: Must have for wine drinkers
body: After a wine bottle opener, this is next most important tool for wine drinkers. I often only drink a half a bottle of wine. After getting the Vacu Vin, its night-and-day difference. I've tasted bottles 4-5 days after opening and VacuVin it, and they still taste great. The key to keeping the bottle as fresh as possible is to suck out the air (VacuVin it) as quickly as possible to avoid exposure to oxygen. 1) Open your wine bottle and immediately pour the desired amount (1/3 bottle, 1/2 bottle) into a decanter or glasses. 2) Immediately VacuVin the bottle. Be sure you hear the clicking noise a few times to ensure that most of the air is take out. 3) Store the remaining bottle in a cool dark area (preferably a wine fridge). I didn't have any leaking issues with putting the wine bottle on its side in my wine fridge. Just make sure you really get all the air out (by hearing the clicking noise a few times). Cheers!

As the internal package of stoppers are sealed this was clearly a manufacturing defect so quality control could be improved a bit. Replacement through Amazon was easy, although having to send back the defective product (only to have it discarded by Amazon) is a waste of time and resources.
