title: Comparison HiCoup vs Digision
body: I was looking for a good corkscrew after one that I really liked cracked its handle and started to fail. I saw what was available on Amazon for around $10 and settled on two for a comparison. The two I purchased were the HiCoup and the Digision. This is a side by side review of these two. The general designs are almost identical. Both of these steel corkscrews have wood trim. I picked the rosewood for the Digision (the only choice) and ebony for the HiCoup. Both are lovely with a good finish and operate in the same way, a fold-out foil knife and a two-stage lever to extract the cork (don't ever buy a single stage corkscrew!). Both are similar weight, I haven't weighed them, they feel pretty much the same, but I think the Digision is slightly heavier. Both are efficient and easy to use when you know how to use them (They both have a first-stage lever that you push in toward the bottle top when the corkscrew reaches the proper depth). The differences? Both have a serrated foil blade but the HiCoup has a finer toothed blade (I prefer an un-serrated blade). Also, the ebony handle on the HiCoup looks very attractive but, aside from those advantages, the Digision has a closer fitting two-stage lever made from a slightly heavier stainless steel. Out of the box, the Digision operated more freely than the HiCoup. For example, I had to force the HiCoup lever to its full extent while the Digision moved the same distance with little effort. Finally, if this is a gift, the Digision comes in a nice slide presentation box while the HiCoup comes in a simple card container. One note of interest is that while the Digision has a very nice box, someone at Digision probably has a different job now because, when you open the box, the Digision logo on the corkscrew is not facing the viewer.

title: Not just any old corkscrew
body: Some people don't know that wine corkscrews are not all created equal. They try all sorts of gizmos, most of which I also have tried and rejected. Some wine bottle openers I've used often enough shred the cork, making a mess as I attempt to keep cork crumbs out of the wine. That's sometimes cuz of a too-dry cork or wrong type of corkscrew or dull point on the screw. ISome openers take more effort than I'm willing to offer. Some are not even corkscrews, using some other technique, such as sliding rails into the bottleneck and pulling or twisting the cork out. I have not once succeeded in opening a bottle of wine with that kind of opener (but somehow I've resisted then breaking open the bottle on the edge of a counter (gauche)). Some require more muscles than I own. Some simply don't work for me. The best type of wine bottle opener for me is a "waiter's corkscrew." This has two short levers on hinges ("double-hinged fulcrum") that take turns pushing down upon the bottle's opening lip. The first lever gives enough torque to pull the cork halfway out. Switching to the next pulls it the rest of the way (as 10-speed bicycles have different gears to help create torque). Perhaps my description of the device and usage isn't clear for everyone. if you don't get the image, then go to dinner with a friend and order a bottle wine. Ask the server to show you a corkscrew and how it's used. In particular, the HiCoup corkscrew is, first of all, a beautiful tool. It's not just plastic and metal, but mine has rosewood for the handle (yes plain plastic and steel handles are options). It's so artfully designed that I put it next to the wine bottles so everyone will see it and be envious (no one has admitted envy aloud...yet). The curved handle is more comfortable for me than straight ones. I get more power from my meager musculature. There's a pop-up curved serrated blade with a sharp point that all waiter's corkskscrews have to cut of the bottleneck's foil. This HiCoup corkscrew (yes I've been considering writing a three line, 27 syllable poem about this tool) has a blade slightly curvier than others I've used. Perhaps the blade's angle and how the handle fits my hand allow more pressure at the point so it cuts the foil more cleanly. With others the blade point slips off the foil a lot. I wouldn't have -- actually I never thought -- that such a thing as a corkscrew would be so impressive to me. gg

title: What a little lifesaver. Fast and efficient!
body: I work at a wine bar here in California and the place is always packed to the walls with people. I am constantly busy and we net ~$30,000 a night on weekends just in wine sales. My boss told me I needed to start buying my own wine keys (another name for a corkscrew) so I went online to Amazon. I didn't know if I should take my chances on this corkscrew from HiCoup based on all the 5-star product reviews. How could this simple little tool garnish so many raving reviews? It seemed unreal to me. I also didn't want to drop fifteen dollars on something that I go through so often at my workplace, but I took a chance and bought it anyways. I'm very happy and I do not regret my purchase at all. First day using it was spectacular. The tool itself has the perfect weight. It really feels like you are holding something of quality and craftsmanship. With a nice finish on the wood and a comfortable grip, it works perfectly in a high paced work atmosphere. The double hinge is fast and strong with the first lip usually doing the job if I'm not being lazy. The serrated blade is the best! It cut through even the thickest necks of wine bottles and just *works*. The 'worm' is very cool, with an inline groove running along the corkscrew down to the point. i do not know what this feature is for but it makes my open bottles quickly and efficiently. I would recommend this tool to anyone! I would not spend $35+ on another competitors corkscrew since this one works so well. I plan on owning this for a long time and since the company offers a lifetime warranty on the product, I don't think I'll ever need to replace it. Very happy with my purchase! *TIP* When I first received the item, the hinge between the bottle opener and the handle was very stiff and opening the corkscrew was difficult and annoying. I dabbed a little bit of olive oil onto a rolled paper towel and rubbed some into the two hinges, thus reducing the friction of the metal and fixing my one and only problem. I would recommend doing the same if you're experiencing the same issue.

body: This performs better than most cork screws we have used. Bought one years ago to replace a metal-and-plastic Rialto, which introduced us to the two stage, split lever action that makes it easier to pull stubborn corks. We had seen it used by servers at local vineyards and bought some for ourselves and for gifts for friends. But the plastic on the Rialto eventually breaks after years of use. Several years back, we found the HiCoup on Amazon and ordered one to try. Then went back and ordered more, as our friends' old Rialto's began showing their age. And, now convinced over the years that these are "bullet-proof" durable, finally got around to writing a review after buying another this year! All lever action corkscrews depend upon the mechanical advantage provided by leverage. With a single action lever cork screw, the upward leverage is least at the beginning of the pull, when the cork is being held most tightly in the bottle. At the start of extraction, the lever handle is nearly parallel to the screw in the cork, most of the force is wasted by pulling sideways on the screw, not up. The two stage, split lever action solves this problem by allowing the lever fulcrum to be lower, closer to the rim of the bottle, when the pull starts. The handle then starts out perpendicular to the screw, and all the force on the screw goes into extracting the cork upwards, out of the bottle. One of the "tricks" with this corkscrew is to realize that you want the handle to be perpendicular to the direction of pull, in order to get the best leverage. This means don't screw in the corkscrew all the way at first. We like to leave about half a turn of the "pigtail" still showing outside of the cork for the first pull. Then screw into the cork a bit further before starting moving the fulcrum higher up and starting the second pull. Two easy pulls: out comes the cork!

title: Not a bad wine opener , but not the best !
body: Let me start by saying that I'm a waiter/bartender for more than 13 years now. During this time I used a lot of different products and I worked in a lot of places ; right now I'm on a cruise ship. Anyways , let me get to the point. The good: it's not a bad product.The price is right and I mean it looks good, I can see and feel that they've used good materials and it feel rather good in the hand, that wood being a nice touch. The foil cutter even being so new you can take it out at ease and it helps you cut the top paper of the the wine bottle letting you see the cork.It is probably the second best part of this wine opener. The best part part of this wine opener is that it has nice channels that are helping you when you take the cork out, by not destroying the cork and to leave behind parts of it in the bottle or breaking the cork making it very difficult to take it out.It is probably the best so far I've seen, I mean it does not break the corks, even if I open a $3 wine bottle with a very bad natural cork inside. The bad: This 2 way system of pulling to cork in 2 stages is actually harder to do then it seems. I mean it gives you no problems with plastic corks, but when we talk about wood corks the matter is totally different. Why ? It is simple: when you first try to us the top short part to take out the cork easy, you have to use your own pressure, which looks easy that it seems as you most of the time are in the rush or takes to much time to be done , resulting in applying too much pressure and by this very often you break some of the cork in the first operation of extracting it. Not even when you use the 2-end part to extract the cork is not easy at all. I mean is better than the classical way in one stage, but is not way better than other wine openers.It takes way to much time to adjust and honestly I used just because it does not break the corks, thought I loose time till I get the job done :). Also I was expecting to be thinner , to fit a in a small holster behing my back but it is not :).If this double hinge system was working better, it will get my maxim rating. But like this , it is an ok wine opener. Do not get me wrong, for a house use ,probably is the best. For commercial use that I need where speed is very important, well I found it less use, thought is not a bad product, it gives me too much frustrations till' I get the job done. Conclusion: I'll stick to my Pulltaps same price range like this one for the easy of getting the job done and the slim body that it has. Too bad that this double hinge system is not friendly to use. If it had the Pulltap system will be the best buy.

title: My (new) all-time favorite corkscrew
body: I've been searching for a corkscrew that is both attractive and easy to use. Something that I would not feel cheap pulling out at party or picnic, without sacrificing functionality. The HiCoup Waiter's Corkscrew really hits the mark. I now own SIX of them. To start with, it meets all of my expectations for a top quality corkscrew. The "screw" is of the right diameter and sturdiness. The lever is articulated (hinged) allowing for easy two-stage opening. The foil cutter is sharp. And includes a very functional bottle cap opener. The additional "pros" are all nice-to-haves, but they are what make this item a real treat. Prior to this, my go-to opener was the ScrewPull: https://www.amazon.com/Creuset-WT-110-Screwpull-Waiters-Corkscrew/dp/B000GA311Y/ref=cm_cr-mr-title. Not perfection, but good. The HiCoup is superior in several ways. 1) Attractiveness - All of the variants of this item are nice to look at. My preference is the rosewood, but would be perfectly happy with any of the others. By comparison, my reaction to the ScrewPull is ambivalence, inelegant. 2) Bulkiness - The ScrewPull is bulkier and heavier, making it less convenient to slip into your back pocket. The HiCoup, while less bulky still feels solidly constructed and durable. And, yes, I often have a corkscrew in my back pocket. It's shocking how frequently it comes in handy... 3) Stiffness - My biggest objection with the ScrewPull was that the hinge was very tight and hard to open. The HiCoup does not suffer from this. It's not loose, so it's not opening unintentionally, but it's not hard to open. 4) Price - Despite all the advantages over the ScrewPull, the HiCoup is half the price. This allows me to replace all of my super cheap corkscrew so I never have to deal with them again! Simply put, it is the closest I've come to finding perfection in a corkscrew.

Its importaint to have a double hindge on the wine key to save the precious seconds when it's slammed. Not every double hindge is made the same, I've had them snap right at the connection point as you're trying to open a bottle in front of the costumer, it's just embarrassing. The double hindge that extends all the way to the handle, like the one on this wine key, is the one thing that in my opinion makes the whole difference between a good looking wine key and a good looking wine key that will last. Second most important part of a wine key is the foil cutter, nothing is more annoying when your favorite wine key looses its edge after opening five bottles and now you have to carry a foil cutter or fumble the bottle for two minutes fighting to take the foil off. So far I've opened upwards of a hundred bottles with it and it's still is as sharp as the day I bought it. And finally the cork screw it self, if you buy a Walmart wine key you will know exactly what I mean the cork screw will bend a little every time you open a bottle and by the end of the day you will have something that doesn't even resembles a wine key. No problems with that here either. The bottom line is this is a wine key that performs, and looks great.

title: Rosewood Waiters Corkscrew- an excellent buy!
body: I have had a simple stainless steel waiter's corkscrew similar to the HiCoup Rosewood Waiters Corkscrew for many years and saw this one on Amazon and decided to purchase it based on the reviews as I do for all of my online purchases. It arrived on time and was packages in a nicely designed box, This is a very high quality, well made item.There are no rough edges that would cause injury or damage to clothing if placed in a pocket. The rosewood has a quality, smooth finish that looks very good. The corkscrew works well, grasped the cork easily and with the aid of the fulcrum and lever action lifted the cork out of the bottle with ease. My older corkscrew would tear the cork as I removed it, but this one did not. I did not really need the double-hinged fulcrum as the main one worked very well in pulling the cork almost all the way out of the bottle, but I tried it anyway and it helped to remove the cork completely. I will buy more of these to give as gifts to all my wine drinking friends and relatives. The price is right, the quality outstanding and with the addition to the lifetime guarantee makes it an excellent purchase! Finally, the company seems to have placed a high value on customer satisfaction by sending emails thanking you for your purchase, notifying you of shipment and seeking feedback to ensure you are satisfied with your purchase. They also include two PDF's one for instruction on use of the corkscrew plus an e-book on wine education entitled "The Art of Enjoying Wine" which is very good.

title: Best wine opener I own and I own a lot
body: I work in a wine store and, between opening bottles for tastings, samples for review and the precious few bottles I open purely for pleasure, I pull more than a hundred corks a month. Nothing is easier to use than my HiCoup Waiters Corkscrews. I have one at home, one at work and might buy one to keep in my purse. The two, independent levers, both hinged at the fulcrum, are vastly superior to a single lever hinged in the middle. The shorter, first stage lever is easy to push inward to hit the lip of the bottle and fully springs back out of the way for the final cork removal. The longer, second stage lever is able to apply more force, more evenly because it is directly connected to the single fulcrum rather than being at the end of a double hinge that can flex unpredictably. The worm (the actual screw part) is also better than most. It is thin and slides in without tearing the cork and the groove cut along the entire length provides extra surface area to evenly apply force without any breakage. I have opened bottles as old as 2000 with dangerously brittle corks and had the whole thing smoothly slide out without so much as a crack in the side of the cork. I wouldn't trust a good bottle of wine to any other corkscrew.

The little knife blade was difficult to open and the two stage fulcrum that rests on the lip of the bottle was loose and a bit awkward to use. Daughter loved it so I was satisfied. I decided I wanted one for myself so I took a chance in the HiCoup at half the price of the other. It looked pretty much identical except for those two problems. The knives opened perfectly with just the right resistance and the two stage fulcrum was spring loaded and worked better than any of this type opener I've ever had. You know how these fulcrum a can grate against the bottle lip sometimes even chipping it? Not too good when that happens while you're opening a bottle at the table. Well, not the HiCoup. That spring hinge works like a charm. So I bought a third one to give to my daughter. I'm going to Good Will that first one and probably buy a couple more HiCoups for gifts. Buy this product. body: Years ago a dear friend gave me a Laguiole Corkscrew. It was an important gift. My friend had been told that Laguiole was the best, most sought after corkscrew in the world. I have used the the Laguiole for years. While it is quite handsome — the handle is some kind of highly polished horn — I have never been completely satisfied with it. In fact, in the drawer where we keep it, we also keep an inexpensive, plastic corkscrew as a backup. A couple of days ago my wife could not open a bottle of wine with the Laguiole, so, as she has done many times, she reached for the the plastic corkscrew. Unhappily the cork proved too tough for it and our backup corkscrew broke. This sent me to the internet for a search for corkscrews. That’s where I found the Waiters Corkscrew by HiCoup. The reviews on Amazon seemed too good to be true. But the price was astonishingly inexpensive, so I had nothing to lose by ordering it. The HiCoup came in the afternoon. I found a video on Youtube of how to use it and at 7:45 I went down to the cellar and retrieved the bottle of wine that we had been trying to uncork the week before. One minute later I was a believer. I have used many types of corkscrews over the years — some quite inexpensive, and others outrageously expensive. I have never used a corkscrew that pulled a cork so smoothly and effortlessly as this Waiters HiCoup Corkscrew.

title: Precision tooling, wine opening pleasure!
body: I ordered the Rosewood version of this wine opener and I absolutely love it! Like most people I think I have used a lot of $2-$3 corkscrews over the years and they are flimsy and fall apart. This wine opener feels like a precision tool, something a luxury car mechanic might use. It's solid, strong, no wiggles or rattles, parts that look machined to work together with precision. It unfolds smoothly in a controlled manner, and glides through foam and natural corks with ease. This corkscrew is a pleasure to use and I look forward to it performing exactly as today for many years to come. title: These do Not work!
body: So what is the long sad story on these Vacuvin (VV) « supposed vacuum retaining » bottle stoppers? The short answer is that they have not worked properly since this new generation design of stoppers was created, thereby ending the production of VV’s previous excellently performing loner ribbed stopper of a totally different design that also used a soft rubber-silicone-feeling material that sealed well and maintained the vacuum for days, unlike the current short stopper design that will usually not hold vacuum for even a day. I even bought the old multi-ribbed design that the Chinese tried to copy and that they still sell together with an equally ineffective and badly made pump, but there is, unfortunately, just No substitute for the original VV long ribbed stoppers if you want the VV system to effectively hold vacuum. And by all means, Never buy anything other than an authentic VV pump as only the real VV products even have a chance of working correctly, while the ineffective Chinese “copies” have no chance at all, noting that whether they click or don’t click (like the VV originals) the VV pumps are working as long as you eventually feel pump handle resistance on the upstroke.

So I figured it would be better in bottles that have wider mouthed necks like Patron and Pendleton. The rubber part is still too small for patron, and just barely fits in the Pendleton bottle. The smaller part of the rubber would fit into normal bottles most of the way, but there are a couple of notches at the top that won't fit into the mouth. So...I kept them around as my backup emergency pour spots. However, something about the metal part of the pour spout is very soft and eventually loses shape and constantly falls out of the soft rubber part. I am very disappointed in this purchase. I will stick with Spill Stop.

title: Don't Store Bottles Horizontally
body: To get it out of the way, I really like this stopper. It's a really simple design and super easy to use. That being said... The stopper works by having two rubber discs press against the inside of the bottle's neck. The discs are expanded by a rod that is forced through a hole in the center of the discs. This provides the "seal". That being said, there was a trade-off made between ease-of-use and seal strength. These stoppers are easy to use, but the seal strength suffers as a result. The net result is that I experience a 50% success rate when storing the stopped bottle horizontally. It's never a big mess, maybe a few drops, maybe a small puddle, but it's still a waste of wine and a mess to clean. If you need to store your bottles horizontally, you should probably pass on this stopper. It's a shame, really, as it wouldn't take much of a change to make this stopper work perfectly.

They seal tightly and easily and, very importantly, release easily, too (pull out of the bottle no problem). The other thing that I absolutely LOVE about these is the height. They are flat on the top. Some of the more decorative or fancy wine stoppers are too high and don't fit in the fridge properly because of that. But because these stoppers have a flat top, they fit perfectly into the fridge! I highly recommend. Oh, and it's nice that two come in the pack.

title: Would not seal a Meiomi wine bottle - popped out.

To account for this potential misapplication on my end, I'm leaving 2 stars instead of 1 - perhaps the product itself is fine when used as designers intended.

title: IT DRAMATICALLY STOPPED MY ALLERGY-TYPE SYMPTOMS AND WINE HEADACHES

I have tried to drink more whites (which has helped a little), tried to limit my wine intake (which can be difficult when wine tasting) and tried to drink a glass of water for every glass of wine, but all of these were not giving me the relief I was hoping for. *** After having 2 glasses of Dark Horse Pinot Noir and experiencing another absolutely agonizing night of headache and congestion I finally started researching, found this, read the reviews and ordered it. I used 3 drops in a glass of wine, had 2 glasses of the Dark Horse Pinot Noir and found it REALLY HELPED ME! I had no horrible headache, no itching, very little congestion. Since then I've tried drinking a couple glasses of wine, red and white, without these and every time I have an wine headache and horrible allergy symptoms. Just last night I drank a bottle of Encore 2016 Pinot Noir by myself (don't judge I just wanted to give a visual that I had a decent amount of wine over a few hours); I used 5 drops per glass and only had 1 glass of water to 1 bottle of wine. (note, I drink water before bed every night so I did have a little more water later in the evening but...) *** NO AGONIZING WINE HEADACHE. NO HORRIBLE SINUS PRESSURE OR CONGESTION. A GREAT NIGHT SLEEP!!!! I have also experimented with white wines; they work great for whites too *** As for taste - have not found any real discernible taste difference other than some reds are now smoother. I do occasionally taste the little crystals that are created, but they are not unpleasant and remind me of the texture of sugar. And for some red wines there is a residual left at the bottom of the glass like the picture I've posted from my Dark Horse Pinot Noir, but I just ignore it.

title: No more headaches!
body: I did not know this product existed until recently. I've suffered for years with headaches after drinking as little as one glass of wine, with some wines not being a problem at all and others quite severe - but no way to know in advance. I learned that some people are sensitive to sulfites that are added to almost all wines, but few winemakers tell you how much was added - just put "contains sulfites" on the label. (I've tried wines claimed to be sulfite-free and they were awful.) While shopping for a wine pourer, I saw a link to sulfite-removing wands, but these seemed very pricey per use. Then I noticed a mention of hydrogen peroxide drops and Drop It. Drop It drops have hydrogen peroxide as well as other ingredients to bind sulfites. I've now tried Drop It with four or five different wines, and the headaches are gone! It seems most cost-effective to treat a whole bottle rather than per-glass, but even at the glass-treatment quantity the small bottle lasts a long time. It's also discreet. Possibly the only problem I have with Drop It is that, no matter how gently I squeeze, I tend to get multiple drops (usually after I've done three single drops), a bit of an overage. But I've never detected any change in the taste of the wine.

I did two different bottles of white wine for a dinner party last night and one looked like a snowglobe as soon as I put the drops in and the other barely had any sediment, so it depends. This works the best when you put the drops in an hour or two beforehand, invert the bottle a few times to mix it around, and then let it sit to let the "gunk" settle out at the bottom of the bottle. When you serve it don't pour the whole bottle out or the last person will get all the sludge. Yes, it does slightly change the taste of the wine, you are taking a part of the wine out so yeah the taste is going to change a bit, so probably don't use it on your $100 bottle of wine. But it's definitely not vinegar like some reviews say, not sure if those people used the entire bottle on their glass of wine or what. body: I had cautiously optimistic hopes for this product. I suffer from severe, chronic life-long migraines (I'm 62 and they had started when I was 15). I know so many of you can understand and comprehend the frustration and pain, etc. Now, for the Drop-it Wine Drops. I never heard of these (or the similar ones selling). There are SOME sulphate free wines available, but not that many or by many vineyards. It's a shame. I guess that's why these drops came to fruition, which, if I must be honest, I think is great. If they work for the individual. They aren't for everyone unfortunately. I truly wish they worked for me. I tried the initial drops suggested (per oz per glass)...about 45 minutes later could feel my head really hurting. Not as bad as usual, but it was pounding. I was disappointed (I had NO migraine or headache prior or I certainly wouldn't drink any wine at that time). Next time, I tried a couple more drops. About three more. Stirring as directed. Drank my tasty red wine. Felt nice for about 40 plus mins...then, yes, again my head was starting to pound and got worse over the next couple of hours. I did this "test" about four days (I had to take my rescue medication one day. This just isn't for me. I'm not saying it's not a good product. And it may very well help some individuals who get headaches or migraine. We are all unique and take things differently. I gave this a good rating, despite it not working well for me. After all, I read many positive reviews and this made me give it a try. And I did. A number of times. But while its NOT for me, I say, give it a try at least if you'd like an occasional glass of wine and not have to experience the unpleasant side effects. It may work for you. Good luck and be well all!

I had no problem breathing, I was able to drink it fine, though there were particles in the wine grin the drops that might gross people out but it wasn't really. I still got red cheeks after one glass but I ahead...i hadn't drank wine in over a year, so.. that might have been a individual thing. title: I can drink wine again!
body: This stuff actually works! I have a strong reaction to wine, which has been frustrating because I really like white wine. This stuff eliminates the wine headache! I can usually feel "wine headache" symptoms even before I'm finished drinking a glass. After using this stuff, no symptoms even after two glasses!!! Incredible! [Granted, if you go crazy, it does not eliminate hangover...that will be the next miracle product. :-) ] I found that for a normal glass of white wine, 1 drop does it. If it's a "generous pour" of white wine then 2 drops. I used it for red wine, which normally destroys me with wine headache. It eliminates it! However, I did have a perception that if I used 3 drops it slightly altered the taste of red wine. So, experiment with it and have fun!

title: Great Product for Wine Drinkers

I keep giving it away. I have one at home and one in my purse. I rarely post reviews, but this is totally worth it. Enjoy your WINE!

title: Really works, second purchase

title: It’s a miracle!
body: I cannot believe how well this stuff works! I was at the point where I couldn’t drink any wine at all without a horrible headache that lasted one or two days. Now I can drink 2 or three glasses and I feel completely normal the next day. I also don’t wake up multiple times during the night which usually happens if I drink more than one glass. I highly recommend this! It doesn’t change the flavor of the wine either.

It's pretty much impossible to count the drops, as it seems that at least 3-5 drops come out quickly as soon as you tip the bottle. So not only is it annoying, it also causes me to waste the product because I'm probably using more per glass than I actually need to. But it's worth it & I will continue to use this product.

title: No wine headache

My friends also were impressed with it knowing how just a few sips of wine could give me a migraine. I used 5-6 drops per glass & didn’t drink the bottom where the residue from the drops has settled. title: Protects your wine bottles while traveling
body: I don't usually travel with wine in my suitcase on a plane but I do bring wine with me when I cruise (you're usually allowed to bring 2 bottles of wine in your carry-on and I buy the wine before I board the ship) and that's the main reason I got these. I'm not sure I would use them on a plane where my luggage would be thrown around; and that's why I'm also not sure whether to give these 3 or 4 stars. (I ultimately gave them 4 stars because they are good for the reason I got them). Here are the pros and cons: I like that these protectors are reusable and lay flat when not being used. It makes storage very easy (I have another type of protector that is very bulky and I don't like that). Wrapping the bottle in the protector is also very easy - just insert the bottle into the bubble wrap inside the protector, close it up and you're done (no need to blow up the protector with another device). The zipper part and then the double fold Velcro both add another layer of protection which don't allow the bottle to spill out. The size of the protector also allows for larger wine bottles (or any large bottle of liquid) to be protected. Cons - It was initially confusing about how to use the protector. The outside of the protector says to put the bubble wrap around the bottle and insert it into the outer layer. However, the bubble wrap is already inside the outer layer and attached inside. I went back to the description on Amazon and that said to insert the bottle into the bubble wrap already inside. That made more sense. The bubble wrap is nothing special. It offers regular protection. I think if I were to use these protectors in checked in luggage on a plane I would probably use another layer of bubble wrap that I would get myself. A 750 ml bottle of wine, once inserted into the protector, has room to move around. If one had a larger bottle it would fit the protector better because there wouldn't be as much room to move around. As I stated before, the size can be a plus for many people but it isn't for my needs. One piece that is lacking in this product is an extra layer of absorbency. If the bottle broke, the zipper and double Velcro would prevent spilling but it's not something I want to try out. Overall, I gave this 4 stars because it does fit my specific needs (I need protection in my carry on only). I might have given it 3 stars if I were to use it for travel in luggage that would be thrown around. It might work fine that way, but I don't want to be the one to try that out.

title: COIDEA Travel Protector Wine Bags Set Of 3 - These Reusable Pouches Worked Great For Me!
body: I took the COIDEA Travel Protector bubble wrap wine sleeves to Paris, intending to carry back one or maybe two bottles of Chartreuse in my checked bag. It's an expensive liqueur that's hard to get in the USA, and I had multiple requests for it from people at home, so by the end of my trip, I was lugging around 3 full-sized bottles of the stuff, plus an extra half bottle! This meant my suitcase now weighed a ton and was bursting at the seams. I employed all three of the COIDEA pouches that came in the set (Chartreuse bottles are similar in size and shape to wine bottles, so the fit was pretty good), but the flight back had 3 legs, and I was rightfully worried about my soft-sided luggage being thrown around and crushed. I padded everything with t-shirts and other soft items, and hoped for the best. By the end of the trip I had a groin pull, the telescoping arm on my suitcase was hopelessly broken, and the case itself spent 90 minutes out on the airline's baggage ramp during a thunderstorm, but none of the glass liquor bottles got damaged! I have COIDEA's handy wine protectors to thank for that success (at least partially), and I love it when products work the way they're supposed to, so yes, I would highly recommend this reusable 3-pack to anyone who's going abroad.

body: I'm sad to give a 1-star review, but the ad makes a claim that is not true - this wine bag is NOT leak-proof. I placed 2 cups of water in one of the wine bags, carefully and thoroughly zipped each of the ziploc-like zippers and securely velcro-ed the end up as directed. I then placed it on top of a wide bowl and left it on my countertop. It did not leak immediately, but overnight, drops had seeped out of the corners little by little. I woke up to about 1/3 c. of liquid in the bowl, and a slow but steady drip coming from the edge. Just enough to make a big mess in a suitcase full of my cutest clothes. So the bag may provide a bit of cushion, but not really as there is only 1 layer of bubble wrap inside the clear vinyl sleeve that zips and velcro's. I'm sad because these wine bags are cute and I wanted them to work, but I think putting a bottle into a securely zipped 2-gallon ziploc bag, wrapped with a towel or other soft items would provide better protection.

title: Changed my life for the better
body: Got these to use in the kitchen, and I haven't regretted it for a second. First we used them in our vegetable and olive oil bottles, the ones we keep handy for cooking. Oil pours a little slowly, but steadily, and allows you good control of how much gets wherever you need it (into a measuring spoon, onto the surface of a skillet, into a bottle for mixing dressing or marinade, etc). There's no mess or dripping afterward. But I only have two of those bottles. What about the 10 other spouts that come with it? Turns out, these things are great for pouring spirits (which is of course what they were made to do). I had always poured straightfrom the open bottle into a jigger to measure, but having one of these in the top of the bottle makes for a much smoother pour. If you get good, you get a sense for how much you've poured without using the jigger, just by mentally counting (one one-thousand, two one-thousand). If you're having a party and have quite a few bottles on deck, this makes managing your bar stock much easier. Then I discovered that putting one in the top of an open bottle of wine has the same effect. No more glug glug as you pour, just a nice smooth stream of wine. Keeping the spout in there keeps bugs out as well. More than once in the past I've poured from an open bottle of wine only to discover an earwig had gotten in there. With these pourers in place it doesn't happen any more. Basically any bottle with the right size opening will work well, for very thin liquids like high-proof spirits to relatively viscous liquids like heavy oils. Trust me: you won't regret it.

title: Easy stopper
body: The Cnigrpl wine bottle stopper is a fine stopper for the price and easy to use. Trust me, much easier than trying to jam the original cork back into the bottle. The pump action works smoothly and the amount of pumps needed obviously depends on how much wine is in the bottle. The more wine the fewer pumps required. Wine doesn't usually go to waste around my house and if we open a bottle, we usually finish it. However the two of us don't drink entire Magnums at one sitting anymore. When we buy one and don't finish it, we're stuck hoping its still fresh when we get back to it. Anyhow, I haven't used this type of stopper before and I tested it on a half a bottle of red wine we opened on Saturday night. We each had a glass and then I secured the stopper and let it sit for three days at which point I broke the vacuum seal and poured out half a glass before stopping it again. After three days, the wine tasted very much the same as that first night. After letting it sit for two more days, I tried the wine again and it was no longer as good. It had soured. Clearly this type of stopper works great for a couple or three days on a bottle that is at least half full. Clearly the more air space in the bottle, the less effective it seemed to be, so I wouldn't recommend storing less than half a bottle of wine for more than 3 days. I dinged it the one star only because the Cnigrpl wine bottle stopper suggested it could keep wine fresh for up to two weeks. I just don't see how that would be the case and I have no intention of trying that out. BUT, for my use case of only wanting to keep the bottle for an additional few nights, the Cnigrpl wine bottle stopper worked great, better than using the original cork or screw top.

Which is one reason why I would take this stopper to a restaurant to bring home a partially used bottle and would not do that with the ones I already had. The pump handle on this stopper rotates and has a line that one can line up with numbers on a dial indicating the day of the month. title: Great sealing stopper with 2 big issues
body: This is the best stopper I've ever used for champagne. The longer neck and soft vinyl or silicone white seal stays tight and a bottle kept overnight stays pressurized as if you just opened it. I like the spring action to get the neck of the seal down into the bottle and keep the seal tight against the bottle. UPDATE: After 10 months of use I still like this stopper and it continues to do a superior job of sealing pressurized bottles of champagne. I also use it for wine (which I consume a lot of the alcohol-removed variety). So, no failures at all during this period, except initially. I am careful to rock the stopper, if necessary, gently and not abuse it. I am also using the stopper that I did not file the edges of (see review below) and I am careful about how I handle it. I do not know if the manufacturer has made changes to the product since i purchased it. I recommend you clean the stopper with a damp cloth only, as the circlip and spring in back of it will rust, even though the body of the unit is stainless steel. ISSUE #1: edges are sharp, so sharp they are a safety hazard and must be handled carefully. This can be fixed by filing the edges with a small metal file (and I mean every edge your fingers can touch). I did this on two of the 3 stoppers and I'd really prefer this be done during manufacturing. Filing is tedious. ISSUE #2: read other posts and find it falls apart quickly. It does indeed and I believe the culprit is the circlip in pic1 which sits in a groove in the body. It is meant to keep the seal and spring in the body, but they can slip past the circlip. It is still ductile (circlips are normally hardened steel) and rocking the unit while uncorking it can push the circlip deeply in the groove and bend it and then the black plastic disk on which the white seal is mounted can slip past as in pic3. I tried to capture this in pic2 but it is difficult to see the close tolerance. Pic#4 shows the black disk captive under the circlip (as it should be). So, you can fix the stopper if it comes apart but it will keep happening. The circlip needs to have a smaller inner I.D. to correct this. Due to those 2 issues I cannot recommend this unit. A revised circlip and smooth unit edges are needed and this would be a definite winner! (I'll continue to use mine).

title: It's good, but an either/or solution
body: This product works well to chill a bottle or keep one cold, but I've found that it's really an either/or solution. You can either chill a bottle of warm room temperature wine OR you can keep a pre-chilled bottle cool for quite some time, but not both. Based on my experience, if you use this to chill a bottle, the cooler becomes too warm to keep that bottle chilled for an extended time. This chills to the recommended serving temperatures of most wines, but for those needing the biggest chill (such as dessert wines or Riesling), this doesn't get quite cold enough. I've observed that, once frozen, this can take a bottle of wine from warm room temperature (about 77) down to the low-50s, which is perfect for most white wines. But again, if you're serving a wine that likes to be in the mid- to low-40s (or if you just prefer your wine extra cold), this won't quite cut it. If you're curious, all of my tests/experiences are based on freezing the chiller in a 0 degree F freezer. Your results will obviously vary depending on the starting temperature of your wine and the temperature of your freezer. Overall, I'm quite happy with this product, mostly because it lets me get to my wine faster! Just be aware of this product's limitations and it should meet your needs.

title: Excellent Value, but be careful!
body: Although I own the Le Creuset wine cooler sleeve, I was curious whether this was a good but less expensive alternative. Answer: Yes It does not have the same level of quality of the Le Creuset, but it's less than half the price. The Le Creuset is made from pierce-resistant nylon fabric, whereas the Vacu Vin is some sort of flexible plastic. Nevertheless, the Vacu Vin works equally as well. A design flaw with this product and the Le Creuset model is that the bottom is open. If you lift the bottle by the sleeve, the wet bottle can slip out and break. The advantage that the Vacu Vin model enjoys is that it's not elastic. Therefore, the elastic won't stretch over time and get loose as happens with the Le Creuset. Be careful with either!

title: Smooth and consistent pour
body: I got a 12 pack of these pour spouts, and they were all consistent in size and quality. The rubber part is pliable enough to easily push onto a bottle, and sturdy enough to keep it in place. We enjoy a good cocktail from time-to-time so we have been practicing our bar skills. I saw a showy professional bar tender pour a consistent ounce without using a jigger, so now I want to do that. A consistent pour is essential for me to reach that goal. I can't say these had me doing that, but that says more about my dismal pouring skills than it does about these spouts! In fact, these spouts gave a very consistent pour with no chugging at all. I also made a lot less mess because I had more control pouring into the jigger. The dust cap is a nice addition, but it is only for the short term! I took the spouts off and returned the caps after we were done for the evening. The air return that allows for such a smooth and consistent return also allows air into the bottle when it is just sitting there, so that will eventually spoil the Liquor. Seeing as I live in a hot humid climate that could also mean bugs getting into my expensive liquors. This is NOT a design flaw!!!!! In fact, this is what makes these so good. They were not particularly difficult to clean either. I simply dropped them in some soapy water and then ran the water through them. I left them out overnight on a drying mat, and they were clean, dry and ready to be put away in the morning. I suppose I could have also put them in the dishwasher, but my point is that they were pretty easy to clean. Overall, these are good quality Liquor pour spouts, and I recommend them.

title: Mid-Quality, Unfortunate Poor Shipping Condition, Love that it's Made in the U.S.A
body: Ordered the 20x20x4 sized Merv 13 two-pack for our newly upgraded heat pump/AC air mover. FYI, when purchasing based on nominal size (the main size listed on the packaging/description), always be aware that each filter housing may accept the listed nominal size, but the actual opening is quite likely smaller, sometimes by a fraction of an inch, sometimes by nearly a 1/2-inch, and they may not accept any "20x20x4" filter size. Always be aware of the maximum size your unit can accept, to avoid wasted time and money. This brand, as many others do, clearly states the actual use size, which is quite helpful. Shipping was quick, and while the outer cardboard box that the 2-pack arrived in seemed to be in good condition (no dents or damage), the 2-pack inside showed obvious signs of damage and having been partially squashed, likely prior to shipping. Also, the number of folds in the actual filter material were inconsistent with the photos in the Amazon description (there were fewer folds than pictured). This matters because the total surface area greatly affects the functionality of the product in use. The filter material folds were also poorly glued into the edges of the cardboard frame at numerous spots, and the filter edges had been squished up, kind of like an accordion, causing portions of the filter material to be so closely squished together that it seemed as if it would greatly reduce the actual portion of the filter material that would come in contact with the air movement, potentially reducing its effectiveness overall. There were other sections where it was more stretched out, given that other parts were pushed closer together, resulting in pretty inconsistent baffles/folds in the active filter material. The glue applied to the edges of the filter material, which is encased by a lightweight cardboard box, lock the filter material in place, so there is no way to manually and simply spread out the filter material to be more evenly folded, in an effort to increase effectiveness. I reached out to the manufacturer, and the phone was answered immediately (rare these days) by someone who was kind, very personable, and genuinely seemed like he was interested in trying to help, and to make things right. To their credit, he offered to refund my original purchase AND send me a replacement 2-pack. We discussed the issues described at length, and he honestly acknowledged that they were aware of some of it, and were working to correct and improve their product. You have to respect a company that talks to you like a person, and doesn't try to suggest your concerns are somehow your fault... not all... quite the opposite, actually. So why only 3 stars? After receiving the 2nd shipment, which the gentlemen assured me he was going to go back to their manufacturing area and share my concerns (and multiple photos I'd provided, at his request, comparing his company's product to the OEM product it was time to replace), the next set had exactly the same problems, and actually more damage to the 2-pack inside (again, the outer shipping box appeared fully intact), causing them to be disfigured enough on 1 side that they were unusable in our air mover (it has a very narrow margin for size, and the lightweight, outer cardboard shell of the filter boxes was too crushed to straighten out and still be able to slide easily into the filter housing). I called the customer service gentlemen back, thanked him for his efforts, but sadly advised that I wouldn't be able to use the replacements, given the apparent damage prior to being placed in the very strong shipping box. Honestly, I was very surprised, especially after having called and spoke with him, that their plant would ever send another clearly damaged unit - it was quite noticeable. At the end of the day, credit to BNX for trying to provide decent customer service, but the product manufacturing quality (or lack thereof) made it unable to be used, so I don't have any opinion as to its effectiveness. but if it had been able to be properly installed, it seemed like the quality of the material effectiveness would have been decent otherwise.

title: Fast-Boiling, Sleek Kettle That’s Easy to Clean and Built for Safety
body: I bought the Chefman Electric Kettle (1.8L, 1500W glass model) to replace an aging stovetop kettle that had become a hassle to clean and slow to boil. I make tea, coffee, and instant meals regularly, and I wanted something faster, safer, and easier to maintain. After using this kettle for nearly a month, I’ve been impressed by its speed, safety features, and thoughtful design—especially the removable lid and clear glass body. How I Used It I mainly use the kettle for boiling water in the mornings and throughout the day for herbal teas, French press coffee, and quick ramen. I fill it with tap water, place it on the included base, and hit the power switch. The water usually reaches a full boil in under 5 minutes, depending on the amount. After use, I clean the inside every few days using vinegar and water or a soft sponge, thanks to the wide opening and detachable lid. Pros Fast Boil Time: The 1500W heating element brings 1.5–1.8 liters of water to a full boil quickly—usually in 4 to 5 minutes. It’s significantly faster than a stovetop kettle and perfect for morning routines. Clear Glass Body: The borosilicate glass makes it easy to monitor the water level and boil progress. It looks sleek and modern on the counter, and the blue LED ring adds a cool visual touch while heating. Removable Lid for Easy Cleaning: One of the best features. Unlike many kettles with fixed or flip lids, this one detaches fully, making it easy to reach inside for thorough cleaning or descaling. Built-In Safety Features: It has auto shut-off when the water boils and boil-dry protection if you accidentally turn it on empty. These features give peace of mind, especially if you’re multitasking. Stainless Steel Filter: There’s a small stainless steel filter built into the spout to help reduce particles from entering your cup. It’s not a water purifier, but it’s a nice touch for tea and coffee drinkers. BPA-Free Materials: The parts that contact water (glass, stainless steel, plastic handle) are all BPA-free, which is important to me for health reasons. Large Capacity: At 1.8L, it holds enough hot water for multiple servings—great for families, guests, or prepping a day’s worth of tea or coffee in one go. Cons No Temperature Control: It’s a basic on/off kettle, so it boils to 212°F with no way to select lower temps (like 180°F for green tea). This wasn’t a dealbreaker for me, but it’s something to consider if you brew delicate teas. Handle Can Warm Slightly: The handle stays cool enough to touch, but it does get a little warm after boiling. It’s not dangerous, just something to note if you’re used to insulated handles. Cord Management Is Basic: The base has a place to wrap extra cord underneath, but it’s not especially intuitive or tidy. Still, it works for storage purposes. Comparisons Compared to my old stovetop kettle, this Chefman is faster, easier to clean, and much safer with the auto shut-off. Against the Cosori or Mueller electric kettles, the Chefman holds its own—though those offer models with temperature control and slightly more advanced features. The removable lid sets this one apart from similar kettles in its price range. For those who don’t need preset temps, this is a simpler and more affordable pick. Tips for Buyers Descale Regularly: Use a vinegar-water mix or lemon juice monthly if you have hard water. The wide lid makes cleaning easy, which helps prevent buildup. Don’t Overfill: Stick to the max fill line to avoid overflow when boiling. It boils vigorously, so give it room to breathe. Let It Cool Before Refilling: For best longevity, let the kettle cool slightly between uses if you're boiling back-to-back. Use Filtered Water If Possible: Keeps the glass cleaner and extends the kettle’s life by reducing mineral buildup. Who Should Buy This? This kettle is perfect for tea and coffee drinkers who want a fast-boiling, no-fuss appliance with a modern look and essential safety features. If you don’t need precise temperature control but care about durability, visibility, and ease of cleaning, it’s an excellent choice for daily use in kitchens, offices, or dorms. Overall, the Chefman Electric Kettle has streamlined my morning routine and made boiling water a cleaner, faster, and more reliable process. I love the glass design, appreciate the large capacity, and feel confident using it thanks to its built-in safety. Definitely recommend for anyone looking to upgrade from stovetop or older electric models.

title: boils water fast with virtually no noise at all. Amazingly fast and almost silent!
body: WOW! I buy a lot on Amazon but I don't leave a lot of reviews. This product however, is such an incredible value, and is so very very excellent that I feel obligated to take the time to explain why it is so very very VERY good. I was traveling last week and I needed a teapot in my hotel room, and I went to Walmart and bought a "Chessman" all metal teapot for around $27 plus tax. To my surprise I discovered that it heated water faster than any other teapot I have ever owned, but more important it was nearly silent. (In the past year I have purchased three glass teapots on Amazon, one for around $25 and two more for around $50, and they are all acceptable but when boiling water they make a very loud noise like a rushing waterfall. It is hard to hear the TV or music when it is operating. Just now I boiled three full pots of water in this new Chefman glass teapot. I was absolutely stunned to discover that it makes NO NOISE AT ALL. All you hear is the "click" when it is finished boiling the water. And my subjective view is that it boils at least twice as fast as the previous three glass teapots I had purchased on Amazon. What's more, this Chefman glass teapot only costs around $23 (as of April 11, 2025 with a 15% Amazon discount). Apparently this is a well known brand and has a reputation for fast boiling times. But no review mentioned the noise level. I think it is a very big deal, and if you want to boil. water this is your choice. If you have ever heard a teapot making a noise when operating, you will be amazed the first time you use this teapot. I cannot give it a high enough rating. - followup after one week - it has started making a small amount of noise when boiling - but orders of magnitude less than the other glass teapot I've owned.. I am ordering another one today. a really good product. Hmmm, a further follow up - I just discovered that if you boil white distilled vinegar in your teapot it significantly reduces the noise a teapot makes when water is boiling. I haven't quantified it yet, but objectively it is 1/4th as loud after boiling vinegar. This Chefman is still quieter, but the difference is not as great as I originally thought. The Chefman remains a tremendous value - it is 1/2 the price of some other brands and boils much faster and starts of nearly silently. And now I know I can maintain the sounds of silence with vinegar.

body: The kettle is fine so far, but here are a few things that stick out to me: The removable magnetic cap takes a bit of effort to yank out. You'll get used to it (probably) but it can be a bit jarring. A lot of water tends to adhere to its underside so when you remove the cap that water will splash and drop and trickle everywhere. If it also happens to be boiling hot water... You see what I mean. You may like the removable cap in general or you may not. It won't get in the way of cleaning and filling water, but it's also more effort to remove and find a place to set down. The underside of the lid also has holdover notches for tea/coffee attachments from Chefman's other products I assume, but this product doesn't come with any of them. The spout pours well. My last brand (Cosori) would splatter everywhere but this one has a nice predictable concentrated flow, even though it still has that mesh filter grate behind the spout. Unfortunately, that grate also sits higher than the spout, so you can't actually pour 100% of the water out of the kettle! Unless you do something extreme like turn the kettle upside down, a small -percentage- of water always gets stuck in the kettle. The charging stand is very lightweight. Even more lightweight than its heavy duty power cable, so it actually feels kinda flimsy or wobbly on its own. It shouldn't be a problem if you're on a typical flat surface but it's a noticeably imbalanced experience where depending on how your power cable is sitting the stand itself might be lifting itself off the table (unless your kettle is sitting on it). It's not a serious problem, not a hazard or anything, just a flimsy vibe. I also like that this is 1.8L instead of the 1.7L. For me personally 1.7 was always just a tiny bit too little. This kettle is also short and stout compared to my old one. I kinda like it. It looks nice enough and there's nothing wrong with its form factor, might even prefer it aesthetically. body: I recently purchased the Chefman Electric Kettle, 1.8L, 1500W and it has exceeded my expectations! Here’s my review of this great product: Pros: Fast Boiling: The 1500W power of this kettle ensures that water boils very quickly. Whether I’m making tea, coffee, or just need hot water for cooking, it’s ready in no time, which is a huge convenience. Good Size: The 1.8L capacity is perfect for boiling enough water for multiple cups of tea or coffee at once. It’s ideal for small to medium-sized families or for anyone who entertains guests often. Great Quality Construction: The combination of borosilicate glass and stainless steel gives it a sleek, modern look while ensuring durability. It feels sturdy and built to last, and I appreciate that it's BPA-free and safe for everyday use. Removable Lid for Easy Cleaning: One of my favorite features is the removable lid, which makes it super easy to clean the inside of the kettle. No awkward angles or hard-to-reach spots—it’s very user-friendly. Auto Shut-Off & Boil-Dry Protection: These safety features are a big plus. The kettle automatically shuts off once the water boils, and it has boil-dry protection to ensure it won’t overheat if there's no water inside. This adds peace of mind when I’m distracted or forget to turn it off. Great Price for the Quality: The kettle offers excellent quality at a reasonable price point. For the features and performance, it’s a great value compared to other electric kettles on the market. Stylish Design: The clear borosilicate glass with the stainless steel accents looks sleek and modern, and it’s fun to watch the water come to a boil. It adds a nice touch to my kitchen counter! Cons: A Bit Noisy When Boiling: It’s not overly loud, but the kettle does make a noticeable sound while boiling. It’s not a deal-breaker, but worth mentioning if you’re sensitive to noise in the kitchen. Final Thoughts: The Chefman Electric Kettle is an excellent product that combines quality, speed, and safety features at an affordable price. title: Boils COLD water in 4 minutes. Metallic spout strainer...not plastic.
body: October 30, 2023 update: As mentioned in previous update, I used my older boiler for the toilet. Do NOT put boiling water in your toilet. HOT water is good, but not boiling water. It was raining in my basement, and I had to replace the wax ring in my commode. The boiling water melted my wax ring. This is not a review, but I had to warn others that it is NOT a good idea to pour boiling water in your pipes, after writing my previous update. Also, if you have a clog and that boiling water sits in one spot, it can mess up your plumbing. If you have a clog, use Dawn and WARM water. AND Do NOT use a kitchen boiler to pour water in your toilet; bacteria will splash up into the pot and can infect your family. Buy a separate pot to use for household purposes only, Now I can sleep at night. October 16, 2023 Update: My water boiler is still running strong. Unfortunately, my toilet isn’t. I found out that an hour of Dawn in the commode followed by a bunch of boiling water is the best way to remove a clog (you’re welcomed). So, like most oldsters who have had a strong and loyal career, it was demoted as toilet boiler, while the more youthful water boiler takes the coveted place on the kitchen counter…looking cocky and proud. I felt it had to be done this way, because I also have a microscope and have proven to myself that a heavy dumping of boiling water into the commode can and will result in backsplash landing on and inside the water boiler. Yes, the commode water is probably clean…especially after dumping a small bottle of dawn in the toilet water, but this is one time I don’t want to take any chances. So until it takes it’s last current of electricity, this big guy will be the household toilet boiler. The button is still a bit difficult to push, but it still works. Thank you, water boiler, for taking one for the team and being a sport about it! May 2, 2023 Update: My pot stopped working again. When this happens, I try to push down the button, but the button flips back up again. But this time, I was able to turn it on, but it turned off before the water reached boiling. I figured this behavior meant the pot had finally reached retirement age. So I decided to open the other pot (same model, not been used). I reached over to unplug the cord, and the plug and about 2-3 inches of the cord was very very hot. So I unplugged the cord, and waited until the cord cooled. In the meantime, I discovered that I had my instant pot sitting on the cord, by accident. I’m not sure if this was why my cord turned hot (I’m not an electrician), but I freed the cord from the ruthless instant pot (sometimes appliances don’t get along in my kitchen). When the cord was finally cool, I plugged it back in and it worked like a charm! Now, I’m not sure if an overheated plug was why my pot had stopped working in the past (I mentioned this behavior further down, and blamed it on a wet or overheated plate), but now I’m wondering if the cause of the pot going on a workpot’s strike, was because the cord was too hot. Either way, if it stops working, feel the plug. If it feels warm or hot to the touch, simply unplug it and wait until the cord cools. Thank you, Water Heater People, for saving me from burning down my own kitchen. ❤️ February 4, 2023 Update: I made the mistake of leaving my water pot’s lid open when I turned it on. I got distracted and it boiled dry. Apparently the automatic shut-off mechanism is in the lid. When the lid is opened, the pot will not shut off automatically. So, I went out to pour my water and there wasn’t any. However, the good news is my house is still standing and this pot STILL WORKS! I assume the pot clicked off while water was still in the pot, and then, the rest evaporated. If it had boiled completely dry, the elements would’ve burned out, I’m sure. The second pot I purchased is still in its box waiting to be used. As for this original pot, I now make sure to tap on the lit before turning it on, just to make sure the lid is closed. It’s become a ritual. 🙂 November 2022 Update: I still haven’t used my second pot, yet. The first pot is still going strong. Occasionally, the lid gets sticky, and is difficult to open, but it’s an occasional issue. My water heater blew a few days before Thanksgiving, and this little fella picked up the slack! It heated water for dishes, and made Thanksgiving bearable. April 2022 Update: After almost a year of using the pot, it became difficult to switch on. I immediately bought a duplicate; because, dang it! I love this pot! After I put in the order, I was demonstrating to my husband how it doesn’t turn on, and it turned on! My only explanation of what was happening was that something got wet and it hadn’t dried out yet. I do tend to shoot the water from the tap across the counter into the pot...just to make housework more fun. Maybe I should stop doing that, because water can get into the handle. If your pot suddenly stops working, my suggestion is to unplug it and briefly take a blow dryer to the electric base and the pot’s base. If you have time, forget the blow dryer, and just set it aside to dry naturally. Many of my appliances, when over heated or wet, will cut off and become unusable until it cools or dries out. At least I have another pot. If this gets wet again, I can replace it with the new pot until this one dries out. I’m thinking of buying another pot just for the purpose of boiling eggs. That way, I won’t have to worry about bacteria getting in the coffee. July 2021 update...so, yes, just like others have reported, about a month or so after using it, it suddenly wouldn't turn on. No light, no heat. But I'm not one to sit idly by, and accept a setback as my new reality. No, Sirree! If I'm going to throw something out, I'm going to figure out the cause of the setback so I can repair it. In this case, the first ring around the protruding pin at the center of the bottom of the carafe became rusted. The rust blocks a current between the base and the carafe, preventing the unit from working effectively. If you place the pot at a different angle (place the pot with your alternate hand, for instance), it may work. At any rate, I simply used a fine-grade sand sponge and sanded off the rust. Steel wool may work, also; but it is a very precise and microscopic job, either way. After I sanded off the rust, I blew off the rust residue and added a thin coat of coconut oil to prevent further rusting. So far, so good. I added pictures to point out the rust. As for the white spots inside the pot, that's going to happen if you have hard water. Hey, you didn't hear about people in the 16th century complaining about spots in their water boiler, did you? Of course not! Those lucky people didn't have to deal with water spots, because they carried their water in from the creek and poured it in an iron kettle. I'm sure you can find an iron kettle on Amazon. I'm not sure where your closest creek is. Maybe Google Maps can show you...OR...you can buy white vinegar or just pretend the spots aren't there. Mild update: Since I'm correcting typos that I failed to catch earlier, I will say as of today, June 14, 2021 the coconut oil appears to be holding its own. I added a wee bit more, but the kettle hasn't stopped or failed to start since I applied the first thin coat. 🙂 Older review: I love it! My last water boiler almost caught my house on fire, leaked and the water sloshed out of the spout. This water boiler pours very smoothly and boils 1 liter of COLD water in four minutes. I haven't timed warm water, but I will confirm it's going to be less than four minutes. The blue light is ok; not as spectacular as I thought it would be. But I didn't buy this for entertainment. The spout strainer pulls forward, covering the spout when you close the lid. When you open the lid, it has a spring that allows the strainer to be moved down for filling water. It doesn't stay down, but it won't snap off when you're trying to fill the carafe, which was its intended purpose, I believe. It IS made of metal, so you don't have to worry about poisoning your family with seeping plastic chemicals. In fact, nothing on or in this pot that comes in contact with liquid is made of plastic. The handle and outside of the lid are plastic for the purpose of insulating you from burns. I have on occasion been forced to use a silicone potholder to support the base while pouring, but I wouldn't remove points for that. It does NOT have a temp control...but you CAN watch it boil and could probably judge from the water's action and reaction when it's the temperature for you. Over time, you be a pro and figuring the proper tea temp. I really do like this pot, and would recommend it for my own grandmother, if she was alive to use it. The price is good for the product. I'd buy it if I were you. You don't know when the price will rise. I have a heat streak. So if something does go wrong with the pot after posting this review, I will be sure to return to post the issues. For now, it's working great!

title: Completely Changed My Tea Game!
body: I got this for myself as a present for my birthday, two years ago. It's my favorite thing I purchased that year! The box is well padded - it can be kept and travel safely well. The buttons are clearly labeled and easy to push. It has a secure handle that is safe from the heat of the glass/water. I enjoy and appreciate the base - a good plastic that is well insulated. If you lift up the kettle at any time during heating, it turns off. It truly will keep your water at the temp you set it to for up to 30 mins (great if you want tea ready after a shower or as you wind down for the night). It has some beeps but they aren't shrill, nor are they too loud. Not too quiet either - I think they found right range for it. The boiling can sound a little loud - you notice it when it approaches a low-rolling boil up to a full rolling boil, but you can still hear the beep over that and not be startled. It cleans easily - it comes with instructions on how to descale it, and it is simply wiped out with a soft, non-scratching sponge. One star has been taken off because the "screen" on the spout doesn't stop large bugs at all. I get box elder bugs every winter and spring, and I had to invent a cover to keep the bugs out of my kettle. I don't know what the purpose of it is; it's too high from the glass to filter anything and it doesn't block things from crawling right in. I know that's a gross thought (and gross experience), but it can cleaned very easily. I also don't enjoy how quickly the plate on the bottom/inside looks like it's oxidizing. I don't think it is - no look or taste of rust - but these small marks show up where the bubbles form as it heats and they just kinda stay there regardless of washing or descaling. Although I don't think it's the perfect product, I am grateful I have given it a chance (and put it through its paces)! I would buy it again if mine broke down and I would advise others to get it if they have any concern for tea or handmade coffee - things that require specific temperature ranges to properly bring out flavor! This completely changed my tea game! Now I can't fathom trying to brew tea well at home without it!

I love that there is a light indicator letting you know it’s on warm, I don’t think it’s needed when boiling because when it’s in a boiling state, you know… but it does make it pretty! I love that it does boil water very, very quickly all the way up for seven cups. We usually do 3-4 cups for tea. However, I’ve also been using it when I need to have boiled water for cooking. If I get working late and my son’s getting out of practice for one of his sports, I know if it was a pasta night that I can have enough boiled water without having to wait for it to heat up and boil on the stove. I put the pasta into the pot, pour the water in, and turn on the heat to keep the water going while the pasta cooks. Much faster! It has several settings, though I really only use the “boil” because we use herbal tea, which I’ve read is better to have steeped in the 210 degrees. It has a setting for coffee, which my son loves coffee and has asked for a French press coffee maker; I know nothing about coffee but I assume that French press doesn’t boil its own water so this kettle is, again, perfect. I do have some green tea, and there’s a setting for that but haven’t used it yet, and we don’t need the other settings but if you have white tea, etc. there’s settings for those. This kettle has been a lifesaver for tea and dinners! We have hard water so it does get build up even when washed but water with a little vinegar works perfectly!! Definitely a great purchase and highly recommend.

It boiled 2 cups in just about 3 min. but at full capacity it would hold just over 4 cups. It's much faster than using a pot on a stovetop and definitely more convenient (and faster) than boiling water in the microwave oven. For anything larger than 4 cups (ex., 6 cups needed to cook pasta), it's easy to empty and quickly boil another 2 cups to add to the pot. The top opens wide enough to fill in my refrigerator door dispenser and the handle doesn't heat up so it's very easy to dispense. I opted for the glass pitcher as I like to see the water inside. There are times for certain teas when I might want to stop it early so glass is much more convenient for me vs. stainless steel. The pitcher automatically turns off when done boiling and also there is a very visible blue light that stays on only while heating. Another safety feature is the auto-off when empty. Within seconds of turning the pitcher on with no water inside, it automatically shut off. For those not familiar with electric kettles, even immediately after heating water to boiling temperature, the base isn't hot (or even warm). So there's no danger when using the pitcher of you, or a child, accidentally getting burned by touching the base. So far this has been a great purchase for a great price!

title: Nice Quality Kettle
body: This review is for Amazon Basics Electric Glass and Steel Hot Tea Water Kettle, 1.7-Liter, Black and Silver. I got this to replace a stainless steel Ascot electric kettle which worked wonderfully for about 3 years and before that an Ovente cordless glass kettle which also worked for 3 years. I know it was 3 years because I am diligent with recording all my purchases and they all seem to die by the 3 year mark. I’m not sure if this is planned obsolescence but this has been my personal experience. I thought about getting another Ascot again but it’s expensive and if I’m only going to get 3 years out of it, why spend any more than what I have to for an electric kettle? Don’t do what I did thinking a more expensive one will last any longer! I went with this one because my parents have it so I know it works and it works well for them. Why not go with something I know works? I like it a lot and it boils water pretty fast. I like electric kettles for the convenience of being able to boil water and walk away knowing it would turn off once ready. Gone are the days of waiting patiently for the whistling of the kettle so that I can shut off the stove! Who has time anymore? I only use filtered water to make my coffee and tea and I normally check the temperature of the water before I use it depending on whether I'm making tea or coffee. Some things that I've observed, and others have pointed out, is that the water boils at 7 minutes and 30 seconds for me with 1.7L (Max) of filtered Brita water (whether refrigerated or room temperature). Obviously, the less water, the quicker the kettle comes to a boil (3 minutes for 1.0L). The kettle will automatically shut off when it hits about 210-212°F (based on the 3-4 readings that I've taken). This is a little bit too hot for my coffee and tea so I usually wait a bit for it to cool down to between 195-205°F for coffee and between 160-180°F for my tea. There are kettles out there where one can set the desired temperatures, but for the price and quality of this kettle I think it's working out fine for me. I like the wide opening because it’s easy to fill and also easy to stick my hands inside to clean with a sponge. I couldn’t do this with my last kettle and that was so annoying! Pro Tip: In my experience, if the kettle doesn’t turn on or seems dead, descaling the pot will often restore it back to normal. This was the case with my Ascot where once I descaled it, it worked again for several more months. I had to do this 3-4 times during those 3 years before it died completely. Also, if it doesn’t turn on after cleaning, try spinning the kettle to different contact points on the base. This too was the case with my old kettles. I had to slowly spin the kettle on the base to get it to light up and run. Eventually this didn’t work either so here I am once again looking for a new kettle! Overall, I'm pleased with this Amazon Basics kettle. I like the size, quality, design, features, and boil speed. I would still recommend it and I give it a 5.0/5.0. - 06/15/2024.
