title: Pretty much exactly what you would expect from the listing
body: So far I love it but I've only used it once to see how long it took and make sure the light and automatic shut-off was working properly. Both worked wonderfully, lights up while it's on and shuts off when it's done. At max capacity with cold tap water it took approximately 10 minutes to boil. This is not maintaining a bubbling, rolling, overflowing boil, in case someone for some reason expects that, but it is and it's perfect for my uses(reg and loose leaf tea and the occasional instant soup). To clarify it does bubble up for those of you who may not know how these kettles work that is what triggers the shut-off so it then goes back to its resting state. The handle remains cool enough so no danger there, the body of it is decently hot though as is to be expected. Currently it has been shut off for 14 minutes and is still steaming. The way I drink tea I could easily drink a cup and still have enough hot water for another which is kind of awesome. Cons: The plastic is obviously a little cheap feeling as a few others have mentioned. This is really inconsequential to me as the price is low enough I would expect Something to be on the cheaper and I'd rather it be that than say the heating element. It's still decently think and so far appears to distribute or not distribute heat as it should, so not a big deal. As a side note is also still looks fairly nice. Cleaning. Okay so these things are kind of always a bitch to clean. For this one the mouth is fairly small so it was a bit difficult to get my hand down in it to wipe it out(and I am a fairly small woman). Again, a lot of these electric kettles have this issue so to be expected. The kettle cannot be submerged so the outside just needs to be wiped down with a damp cloth or sponge and if any soap is used make sure the soap is cleaned off and it's completely dry before use. Now for the little filter. None of my old kettles have this so it's a new, kind of cool little feature for me. There's nothing really telling you how to remove it or replace it so I had to mess with it a little to figure it out and with the cheap plastic I was a little scared to do so. Was also kind of annoying with the small opening trying to see and feel but it slides out with a little pressure and then you slide it in and pop it back into place so pretty simple once I figured it out. The chord. So the chord is reallyy short. Like you should probably just put it right in front of the plug in. This is probably the most annoying con for me cause the spot I had is really right next to the plug in but still far enough away that it barely reached and my kettle is practically against the next item on my counter. I did plan on getting a strip for that outlet so I'll make it work but was still a bit frustrating. So prepare to have it directly in front of a plug in if you keep it on your counter. Packaging. Okay so I noticed others mention this in reviews and was worried about it but mine showed up all in one piece undamaged. BUT I can see where the concern comes from. It is packaged in a plastic bag inside a box inside your standard Amazon so no not a lot of cushion going on if the handlers were too rough I could easily see it showing up damaged. Side-note: now at nearly 30 minutes and still steaming so that's pretty awesome for a ten minute heating time. Otherwise everything looks good I'm giving 5 stars as none of my cons are more than minor inconveniences I mostly expected and don't really differ from anything in the listing. Great bang for your buck, I'm super excited about it and can't wait for the much needed tea-time it will bring me! 😁

body: I purchased one for myself and one for my mother after our trip to Samoa. Lots of places there do not have hot tap water. We utilized their water pots to heat up water to take the edge off the freezing spring water showers/baths but we also used it for the instant coffee that is everywhere there as coffee beans aren’t as prevalent & of course for tea. We were so impressed with the kettles and wondered why we never had one at home. We both have the stove kettles- while functional, they take forever to heat up & don’t have an automatic shut off like this thing does. It heats up so fast it feels luxurious to use! This particular model had lots of great reviews and the price that I got both of ours for was exceptionally great. I ordered them as we were waiting to board the plane home & they were waiting on us when we got back! I use mine at least every other day for tea but what I also like to use it for is my mop water or any time I need really hot water FAST !! I never knew what I was missing. My mother called me about a week after we got back and said she loves hers. You can heat up enough for a cup of tea or the whole pot. It’s very user friendly {off/on}, it lights up when heating, dings & shuts off once it reaches boiling. So far this kettle works perfectly. The handle & pop top do not heat up at all, handling it is nice & comfortable. I was worried about getting splash back but the pour spout design is fantastic. The only reason I gave it 4 stars is because the cord/plug is heavier than the base. So when you lift the kettle off the base shifts. It’s not a deal breaker but it would be nice if the base were a little heavier. I like the lightweight of the kettle but not the base. This one is simplistic, lightweight, fast and budget friendly. If you’re looking for that, then you will love this kettle. If you’re look for something substantial and top of the line, this one will feel cheap because it’s so lightweight and mostly made of plastic. For me, it’s perfect because I only need it to heat up fast! It’s also not loud which is great in early morning brain fog.

title: Very good filter but my current one only lasted 3 weeks before the Red Replace Filter Light came on
body: TLDR: this filter actually does a very good job, BUT If you replace it as often as Levoit wants you to, then you could easily end up replacing them every single month to the tune of $400+ per year. But if you take it out and dust it off at least once a month, you’ll probably be able to get 3-6 months out of the filer before needing to replace it. After seeing the Red Replace Filter light come on my 3-week old filter, I was dismayed because I don’t recall my previous ones going “bad” quite that fast and I started to write a 2-star review. But before I posted this I took i tout and found it did indeed have a light coating of dust on it, so I just dusted it off, leaving it looking nice and clean. I'll try cleaning it at least one or two more times before I replace the filter again. To be fair these filters have historically done a very good job for me, and I’d give them a 4 or even a 5 star rating for their overall effectiveness. But I discovered they actually function just fine much longer than that Red Replace Filter light would have you believe. Maybe they consume more power when it’d dustier though. It just seems weird that the Red Replace Filter light would go on again just 3 weeks after I last replaced the filter. It feels like that makes no sense because: (a) I’ve actually been vacuuming more than usual rather than less than usual lately (b) I recently replaced my Merv-12 Nordic Pure furnace filter which does a great job of filtering the air (c) there hasn’t been much as much dust coming in from outdoors lately since it’s the cool rainy season here in LA — I live at the foot of the Hollywood Hills and there’s more dust here in the Summer when so many plants dry up. (d) Since the main source of dust in here comes from the fan I keep in the big window, I bought some cheap new semi-sheer white curtains 4 weeks ago and make sure the fan blows in fresh air through the curtains so that air gets filtered — but that curtain does not look dirty yet. And it’s white so it will be easy to tell. So the only reasons I can think of why this filter might have gotten full of dust so quickly are: I’ve been dusting and cleaning in here more than usual (but I use damp paper towels to do it so I’m not seeing a bunch of dust go in the air when I do it) so more dust got into the filter than usual. I just got a brand new 4x6 rug a few days ago (but it’s very thin and super clean) OR Maybe this filter isn’t up to the usual quality The Machine isn’t performing as well as it used to (but it seems fine) The Machine is just VERY sensitive to dust on the filter and I forgot how sensitive it is. I think the Machine identifies the fact that its motor has to work harder to keep the air speed up once it gets a light coating of dust on it, so that automatically triggers the Replace Filter light regardless of whether or not the filter is cleanable or not, because they’d rather you spend $35 a month on new filters than clean them off and buy them less often. Anyway, I can definitely recommend the C-300 Pet model overall. I bought mine during the Pandemic and noticed that I actually slept a little better if it was in my bedroom, but it did a better job of keeping the overall air quality clean if I kept it in the main room of my condo. So I finally got around to buying their little Mini for my bedroom and we’ll see how that one does.

title: The Filters Are Fine…What's With The 50% Price Hike In 1-Year?
body: These filters are effective for the Levoit Core 300 Air Purifier. When I purchased this unit, these filters cost $20 a piece, but now they're $30, which is a pretty outrageous price increase. I've not tried the alternative filter brands yet. Some of them have mixed reviews, with customers complaining that they don't fit or are short-lived. In some cases though, the alternative brands are reviewed very well (nearly as well as the originals), with customers reporting that they're indistinguishable from the originals at a fraction of the price. As far as I can tell, the primary difference may be in the pre-filter. The Levoit filters are finely-stitched, but based on the pictures I’ve seen, some of the “knockoffs,” may not be as finely-stitched (the gaps appear to be bigger), which could allow more particles to enter the HEPA filter and lead to a shorter life span (which has been reported by some reviewers). Shorter lifespan or not, If Levoit insists on punishing their loyal customers by gouging us for filters, we'll simply start buying non-name brand filters and then when it comes time to buying a new air purifier, we'll look elsewhere. While I'm a fan of the Core 300, it's still a small unit that only does 140 CFM on max fan speed. There’s simply no justification for paying big money on replacement filters for a purifier that moves relatively little air. If the price for these filters ever surpasses $30, there’s no doubt in my mind that I’ll start buying non-Levoit filters, which can be found here on Amazon for as cheap as $12.99 per filter.

title: Worse than previous model in one key way
body: Overall, these electric kettles are great. They are inexpensive, heat fast, look great, and are fairly reliable. I had a previous model that lasted nearly 10 years before the sensor gave out suddenly. The one key difference is this - the previous Chefman electric kettle I had would automatically shut off after bringing the water to a boil despite the temperature not reaching 212F/100C. I live at 6,800 feet / 2,000m in Colorado, and water boils at around 204F degrees here. This model does not shut off when the water boils at a temp lower than the textbook boiling point of water at sea level. So whereas before, I could press the button and walk away, and come back in a few minutes ready to brew my tea, now I have to hang around. Furthermore, the old model had more choices for temperature settings (as low as 105F) and after I brewed my tea I could set it at a lower temp to keep it warm. Rufus assured me it could, even saying, "The kettle has a keep warm function that activates automatically and can keep water warm for approximately 30 minutes.." So, hubby and I agreed it was a good purchase. I just tried out the kettle for the first time. It has some nice features. It heats quickly and I like the included infuser. It's nice to be able to pour from the kettle without having an attached cord. The kettle looks nice on the counter. But the low water mark is .5 liter, which is 2.2 cups, and it turns off automatically; it does not turn down to a keep warm function. These were important enough for me to inquire about prior to purchase, so the fact that it doesn't heat just one cup or have a keep warm feature is a game changer. I am not a coffee connoisseur, so I don't mind instant coffee, and this electric kettle does just what I need. And the water is a lot hotter than the Keurig ever was. My coffee has a better taste. Plus, I use it to heat water to make instant potatoes, instant oatmeal, or instant grits. During the winter, making hot cocoa is easier with the hot water from this kettle. title: Strange fact about the auto shutoff for the highest temperaure setting
body: This is a great upgrade from my previous model, which, after a lot of years, was leaking where the glass met the top. The auto shutoff at various temperatures is a big improvement. There is one strange problem, though. The auto shutoff for the highest temp (212F) doesn't work. My old model would shut off near this temp, when the water was at a rolling boil. I tested the four other auto shutoff temps on the new model, and they worked fine. I also tested the "boil dry" shutoff, and it worked. I suspect the problem is my elevation of 3200ft above sea level. A calculator I found online said water should boil at 206F with my current pressure and elevation. I measured the temperature of the boiling water in the unit and got 208F. Pretty close considering I used a meat thermometer. I am guessing that because the water didn't reach 212, the auto shutoff for this temp was never reached. Since the "boil dry" worked ok, I think the unit is fine. With the old one, I had to guess when to turn it off so I didn't have to wait for the tea to cool down enough to drink. I would absolutely recommend this product, but just be aware of the possible problem with the highest temperature auto shutoff. By the way, I worked in the weather business for 13 years, so I know a bit about temperature and pressure measurements and effects.

title: Decent inexpensive kettle
body: I got this kettle to replace a much more expensive one that kept failing. I wanted on with the electronics in the kettle itself so that sensors etc. would not be affected by corrosion of the contacts on the bottom of the kettle to the base. I will have to say this kettle feels pretty cheap. As others have commented the infuser is held in by three little tabs and I'm sure they will break off in the future since they are subject to the stress of holding the infuser and the thermal stress in the kettle. Upon unboxing the instructions said to run a MAX load of water through the kettle for a complete boiling cycle. I did this and it worked perfectly. Now it was time for some tea. I have been bringing my tea to a boil and let this kettle run it's default cycle which is to boil and stop as soon as it reaches boiling. It foamed up and spilled a good deal of tea all over the counter. I was making several batches (I make up 4 gallon jugs each week) so I reduced the amount of water in the next one to prevent boil over. No such luck, although it did spill less tea. Third batch I'm down to 1/2 and the infuser is mostly above the water. Still boiled over. The last batch I'm getting close to the minimum level and it STILL boiled over. So for this weeks batch I decided to run the next lower cycle, which is to get it to 200 degrees F and shut down. This worked and I will continue to use it this way as I can put more water in it to further saturate the infuser. Plus: It heats fairly quickly. The controls are intuitive to use, and the ring of LEDs under the base of the glass pot change color to confirm your selection of heat cycle. The opening is large enough to easily get my large hands inside for cleaning. The only contacts in the bottom of the kettle to the base are for 110 volt connections. Minus: The kettle feels like it's price, kind of cheaply made. The base is so light I expect it to lift with the kettle. And I have mentioned the infuser. I don't know why it boiled over with the tea inside. I don't live at a high altitude, 900 feet, so that shouldn't be the cause. But if you can live with a 200 degree F cycle or lower this kettle should do the job and that's all I can ask of any appliance especially these days.

title: Brilliantly and Beautifully Designed, Engineered, and Manufactured. Belongs in the MOMA Collection
body: I'm a bit of an appliance nerd who is discriminating in my purchases, and fixes broken appliances for friends and myself. (My kitchen appliances are over 30 years old and work fine.) I was looking for a temperature controlled water kettle because how coffee is ground and also the temperature of the brewing water greatly affect the taste of the coffee. I did look at Target for a kettle, but was disappointed in the selection; 4 different brands under $30 without temperature control--including Chefman but all with about the same features--and a Cuisinart model for $100. This is not a $100 use case problem! I ordered this Chefman model based on the feature descriptions, and I'm more than pleased with my choice. Aesthetically and functionally it's an amazing set of features at a value price point. I'm never sure how detailed I should get in my reviews because if they are too long, I know they will not get read. So, you can stop reading with this paragraph. There are so many carefully thought out features in this product that I can't describe them all, but I feel compelled to address one brilliant solution to a common problem in appliance design to which I often see astoundingly stupid tradeoff that I think border on fraud. Condensing water vapor--commonly known as steam--is highly destructive to seals and unprotected electrical components. This is why I would never buy a dishwasher with the "hidden" controls on the top edge of the door. What are they thinking! In response to consumers wanting a more uncluttered look in their kitchens manufacturers place the control buttons and electronics on the top edge of the dishwasher door, and then in order to give process feedback to the operator (consumer), end up putting a display on the door front anyway. The problem is that hot water vapor finds its way into the control electronics and damages the connections requiring an expensive repair. Instead of design following function, this is design follows superficial marketing feature with the resultant compromise on the underlying functions resilience and reliability. The same water vapor problem exists for small appliances such as a water kettle, but with the additional constraint of a very limited surface area on which to place control buttons and feedback displays such as status lights. The design solution for this product is to move the simple 2-button controls conveniently to the handle--isolated from the potential damage of water vapor--and then provide a simplified and intuitive user interface using the physical characteristics of the glass container to provide feedback information easily read from across a room as to the water temperature selected, and then after an audible beep, confirmation that the heating is complete (see attached photo). This system, combined with the idea that the default mode of heating is to boil the water with a single button push, becomes intuitive after a single use. This is just a single feature of this brilliantly designed product. I don't know who the industrial designer is for this water kettle, but I believe it belongs in the Metropolitan Museum of Modern Art.

title: WOW factor. Many great features!
body: I have used an electric kettle for decades. I have seen them evolve, but I don't update unless my existing one stops working....except for now. Even though I have had the last kettle more than 10 years and it works well, its unattractive and basic. When I saw the beauty and the temperature control feature of this kettle, I really wanted it! I drink many different teas that steep best at different temps. This one even has a removable mesh for steeping tea right in the kettle. Colored lights let you know which temp you chose. A beep confirms that it is placed correctly on the heating element. Another beep confirms your temperature selection and lights the LEDs which verify the temp you selected. One last beep (plus the lights turning off) confirm that your water has reached the selected temp. I checked it with a digital thermometer and the temps were within 2 degrees of selected temp. I was concerned about breaking a glass spout so looked for a kettle with a plastic or metal spout. Check! I was concerned about lids that do not open enough to reach in and clean. This lid removes completely. Check! I was concerned about steeping tea in the kettle as none I have ever owned recommends it. But this one does. Check! I was concerned about style and appearance. This kettle is beautiful. Check! Lastly there is a stay-warm feature. How convenient! Check! The operating capacity is 0.5 to 1.8 liters of water which is roughly a pint to 2 quarts. From cold tap water at *maximum fill* it reached full boil in 11:28 minutes. It is easy to use, ergonomic to hold and sits securely on the base without any wobbling. The cord is short so you must locate it near an outlet. There is a fine mesh filter just inside the spout to reduce particles in your cup. The outer glass surface does get hot, so be careful! Auto shut-off ensures safety. Considering all of the fine features this electric kettle has, the price is excellent compared to other brands with similar features. I HIGHLY recommend this kettle.

body: This product works well. I'm using it to brew loose green tea. Spooning the tea into the center steeper cylinder is not tricky, but just not as easy as a larger basket would be. I had a tea maker that had a large basket once, and that was easier to fill. I ended up making a funnel out of a piece of printer paper, and that helped a lot. Getting the strainer/cylinder off of the top lid was tricky at first, but has become easy now. Not really a problem, but read the directions on the underside of the lid. Filling it with water is easy. there are markings on the side for 1 liter and 1.8 liter. It's easy to judge other amounts. Put the top/cylinder in place, and plug it in. Set the temp with the right button. For me, it's 175 degrees, and the bottom lights up green. My tea is supposed to be brewed at 180 degrees, but that is not available. Choices are 175 (green), 185 (blue), and two more higher levels, plus full blast. Not a big problem. When the tea is done, the unit beeps, and the light on the bottom goes off. Unfortunately, it doesn't keep the tea at the desired temperature. If you want that, you need to click the right button again, and go through the green light heating cycle. I would have preferred it to keep the tea at the desired temperature. When done, remove the top and rinse the glass contained. Remove the strainer/cylinder and empty the tea. This is where it's not as easy as I would like. Because of the narrowness of the cylinder, the used tea doesn't just fall out. I need to scrape it out with a spoon, at least most of it. The tea that remains in the cylinder needs to be rinsed out, but it's a bit non-intuitve. The pic shows the end of the strainer/cylinder, which is a thin metal material with many small holes. If you try to rinse it out like a drinking glass, water just leaks through. It seems like the easiest way to rinse it out is to direct water from a faucet on the outside of the cylinder, not the inside. That gets most of the remaining tea out. Continue rinsing inside and outside until it is empty. That's about it. I works well. It's not perfect, but then nothing seems to be. I would recommend this product for making lose tea.

title: Absolute MUST-HAVE upgrade for at-home coffee and tea enthusiasts
body: I don't know what 195 degrees Fahrenheit looks like, let alone the subtle difference between that and 200, 205, 212 etc. Consistency has always been the greatest enemy when it comes to following recipes, especially when you're still mastering the craft. Controlling for the temperature variable is arguably the most important contributing factor to making consistent, delicious coffee/teas of varying varieties. After all, it's not ideal to brew green tea at hard boiling temperature, nor would you want to boil light roast coffee at lower temperatures. This kettle beautifully solves those issues! The functions are located on the thick handle and are super easy to use. The color LED gives you a visual indicator of what temperature the water is programmed to heat up toward. After a short while using it I've already got the colors and their corresponding temperatures (referenced on the handle) memorized. The borosilicate glass is a huge plus because it is far more durable to wild temperature changes (e.g. refilling the kettle with cold water after finishing a hot brew) than regular glass. Not that you may want to make it a regular habit, but it's nice to know there's some extra durability. The spout is Perfect, and it's even outfitted with an additional mesh filter, in case the loose leaf tea infuser doesn't catch all of the smaller particles, and it truly pours without drizzle which is a pet peeve of mine when trying to pour hot liquid from any kettle. The instructions state to clean the kettle by boiling a full pitcher of water. Don't quote me but I believe it took me about 8-10 minutes to reach the full 212 degree Fahrenheit boil as directed. This heats up water so fast I'm so happy! 5-star review, hands-down. If anything happens I'll be sure to update this. But I'm very satisfied with the build quality so far, so I don't expect any issues anytime soon. Keep their quick guide and care instructions handy! Proper maintenance is key with anything.

title: Handy, efficient water kettle!
body: GREAT for heating water for French press, pour-over coffee, tea!! Heats quickly, very quiet (compare to a screaming tea kettle at 5:00 a.m.? No thanks) Re: lead warning on the box. There is NO lead component in ANY stainless steel, not even poor quality stainless. The lead will likely be in the soldering in the hot plate underneath. It NEVER touches the water or inside of kettle. It's a mandatory warning. Doesn't worry me 1 iota and I'm particular/ vigilant about my family's health. City water, well water, ANY water will leave a white-ish film inside kettle, as well as spots along the bottom. This is not stainless "corroding," simply non-soluble minerals (mostly calcium carbonate) that are left after boiling. Even distilled water, if exposed to air long enough, can leave a non-soluble film. After a few uses, I wipe out kettle bottom w. a paper towel soaked in white vinegar, rinse, dry. No spots! Or soak in 1/2" of white vinegar if spots are particularly difficult to remove. Our hard well water leaves hefty mineral deposits even after just 1 use so I clean our kettle frequently. I'd love if it had a light along the water level for better visual (not enough of an issue to deduct ratings) This will be great for heating water when canning green beans, etc., over the summer, too! Hoping it's durable over time because so far, LOVING it! Will update if anything changes.

Features: The automatic shut-off and boil-dry protection give me peace of mind, especially when multitasking in the kitchen. The spout pours smoothly with no drips or spills, and the lid opens wide enough for easy filling and cleaning. The water level indicator is clear and easy to read, so I can always measure the exact amount I need. Value: For the quality and features, this kettle is an excellent value. I’ve used it daily for months now, and it performs as perfectly as the day I bought it. It’s also energy-efficient, using less power than boiling water on the stove. Overall: If you’re looking for a durable, efficient, and stylish electric kettle, this one is a no-brainer. It’s a must-have for tea lovers, coffee enthusiasts, or anyone who needs hot water quickly. title: Excellent replacement and watch for price drops
body: Last year, I threw away my Honeywell Air Genius 5. As much as I liked it, it was frustrating to maintain and it had a mind of its own. I trust Peer Guardian products. I've had numerous humidifiers made by them so I bought the Germ Guardian AC 4825 to replace the Air Genius. Out of nowhere, about 6 months after buying it, it started flashing a red light to change the filter. Air Genius had a permanent filter. But don't fooled by the permanent filters, it's one of the reasons I got away from the Air Genius, the filter wouldn't clean properly. So, I knew the Germ Guardian had to have replacement filters but I hadn't bought any. I bought one of the generic versions here from Amazon and it's good but when I turn my purifier on, I love the fresh smell, it's probably not even noticeable to most people. The generic replacement filter never gave me the fresh air smell but it was doing a good job on everything else and at the time it was eighteen dollars less than the name brand, about a sixty percent difference in price. I need that fresh smell. I have a puppy that stays in my office and he's a little guy and he stinks. He can't help it. I give him baths but I think it's because he's so short, his belly hits the ground. I'm picking on the puppy. He has hair that sheds and sucks up any moisture so he don't really stink but he has his own unique smell. The name brand filters help with that and give me a more fresh smell in my office. This upgraded version is a perfect fit and it comes with an attached carbon prefilter. It goes right in, no problems and it brought the fresh air back. Simple, easy, change and I caught these on what I assume was a sale for right at twenty dollars, so I bought 2 of them. They are usually around thirty. I also recommend this purifier even over the bigger version and the other brands. I run it on the medium speed from the time I walk into the office until I leave the office. It's like flipping a light switch on. The room it's in is roughly 15 x 17 and it also keeps the air fresh in the 8 x 10 bathroom that's connected to the office. Not the funnest present to buy yourself but if you're like me, your nose and sinuses and stinky puppy will thank you!

title: Freshens Stale Stinky Air
body: I have a multiple cat household--to say the least. Although I have done all those expected things to reduce the odor of litter pans and pets, the air sometimes just needs to be refreshed. I've accumulated three Germ Guardian air purifiers over time. One or all of them are always on. Two are on timers, the big one near the litter pans runs on lowest setting 24/7. The one in the bedroom is on a timer because I forget to turn it on when I go to bed. I'm certain a percentage of it is the white noise, but physically, my eyes often feel sticky to actually a little crusty, and during spring and summer, my throat can be itchy when I wake up. Also, when I switched to an alleged "low-dust" plant-based litter, the dust was absolutely unbearable. A fine layer of powder settled everywhere in my house. I was miserable and ready to go back to a clay litter. The two filters in the main part of the house go a long way in reducing the dust in the air and on my furniture and floors, the reason why one runs 24/7 near the pans. However, in the years since I bought my first purifier, I have seen the charcoal layer of the filters get thinner--don't know if it changes the performance of the filter. I don't believe the white folded portion of the filters have changed much, but the charcoal layer has thinned considerably. I know this because I found an older filter that fell behind some cabinets in my garage and only recently pulled it out to use it and noticed how much thicker the charcoal layer is. Overall, I still recommend the filters and the purifiers for the longevity and effectiveness. I have all of the sizes on a six month subscription so when the new one comes in I just change them.

title: Great value and customer service
body: This is our favorite tea kettle that we've tried so far. Easy to clean: It has a wide mouth that you can fit your hand inside easily for cleaning. Vinegar and water works really well removing any water stains/buildup if done on regular basis. The interior of the kettle is all glass with the exception of the metal heating plate and the plastic lid. Plastic handle is quite sturdy for easy grip. The mesh/plastic filter pops off for you to clean that as well. FYI: The filter screen rarely lasts as long as the lifespan of the kettle. Once you see any signs of damage, remove it and throw it away. Otherwise once it is compromised, the mesh filter degrades/erodes really fast (and you will notice tiny flecks of it in the water). So just ditch it once you see an signs of tearing/damage. The glass DOES get hot. So be mindful of where you place it if you have small children. Excess cord can be neatly wound around the underside of power base. The kettle lights up when you press the power button located on handle, and the light goes off when it's done boiling. Makes it super easy to know when it's on or off. The unit comes with a replacement warranty of 2 years. I have utilized the warranty and the process was easy. My last unit died within 6 mos of purchase (wouldn't power on). As of Sept 2023...To qualify for replacement you need to: #1 do NOT throw the kettle or base out until you get the replacement unit or part in your hands. Go to the Ovente website and click on "contact us" then select "warranty claim" under the How Can We Help tab. Fill out the form and attach copy of receipt. Wait for response with instructions. In my case, the unit just died for no reason/wouldn't power on, so they responded asking me to provide the following via email: 1. A picture showing the 4-digit code located on the silver sticker attached to the bottom of the kettle or base; 2. A picture and/or short video clip (less than 20MB file size) showing the issue/problem; 3. Your mailing address They then reviewed the claim and in a few days emailed back with: We have received instruction from our supervisor that we don't need the item back. All we ask is that you cut the cord at the very end of its cord close to the plug of the rubber stopper. Once cut, kindly send us a picture so we can process the replacement as soon as possible. (whew! Good thing I didn't assume it was safe to throw it away!). I submitted the Pic of the cord cut... And received my replacement kettle about a week later week/free shipping. Very pleased with the return process!

title: LOOKS GREAT BUT CAUTION
body: Update: July 28th 2015. Six months after my purchase and the kettle is no longer useable. I clean this kettle daily and it still looks brand new and we use bottled water only so it's not the water or or a build up of minerals inside the kettle. When it's heating up there is a super strong odour of something burning and that odour is coming directly "inside" the glass kettle. My advise for health and safety reasons is to avoid this kettle. I have owned at least a dozen electric kettles during my lifetime ( age 68 ) and I have never ever encounter such a problem. LOOKS GREAT BUT CAUTION. The best looking kettle we have ever owned is now in the garbage. UPDATE March 15th, 2015: After 2 months of Use: Well here we are two months after my purchase date and I now have to give this item 4.5 stars instead of my original 4 stars. It still looks as good as the 1st day I received it. Like any glass kettle you may want to clean the insides every day with 1/2 cup of pure white vinegar and an equal amount of water. I like things looking there very best at all times so regardless if it was plastic or glass it would still be cleaned daily anyways. The outside plastic is just as easy to clean as the glass. My initial report stated I thought the plastic was cheap but after 2 months of use its actually very durable and easy to maintain and has no discolouration to date. The cord is just the right length and the kettle attaches to the base thoughtlessly like a magnet. The handle design and balance of this kettle is far better than first reported. It's very well balanced when pouring out the water and the lid opener button and on and off switch work flawlessly. It takes the normal amount of time to boil water but its very quiet in the process. I wish the tiny filter screen at the front was detachable and that would make it just a little easier for cleaning when I put my hand inside the kettle to clean it. The screen is not in the way, it simply would just make things easier with a dish rag in your hand. The boiled water tastes great, and there is no plastic taste that I can detect. For the small price that these kettles are selling for on Amazon I strongly recommend that you don't miss out on a great product and try one. Many of the negative comments listed about this product are just not founded. My review stems from a confirmed buy, and after 2 months of use I personally wanted you all to know I now give this product the 4.5 Stars it truly deserves. John Turcotte Ontario Canada. My Original Review: Looks and works great but in truth this is not a 5 star quality product, but is far better than most other kettles for the price paid. To start with, all the plastic feels cheap especially the base. The base really sounds cheap every time you place the pot on it. A thicker and smoother type of plastic should have been used and this is why I only gave this product 4 stars. The power cord is heavy duty gauge coated in nice rubber and it's long enough for most counters. You receive instructions to boil water at least 4 times to remove any odours or unwanted tastes and I did this procedure 6 times and I did not notice any foreign tastes or smells. The handle is much larger than required and is not the greatest of designs and feels slightly off balance when you pick the pot up half full of water. My old kettle was all plastic with a flat stainless steel burner plate in the bottom. Excessive mineral consumption causes a lot of the reflux and digestive problems that many individuals worldwide endure daily. I did know our town water had some minerals and that surprised me because it's chlorinated. I had to boil a cup of vinegar inside a pot full of water once every two weeks to remove the build up of white scale that would accumulate on the stainless steel heating element constantly. So if your water contains a lot of minerals be prepared for a shock, because all glass kettles will instantly reveal the amount of minerals in your water. The minerals float on top and instantly start to appear when the water starts boiling and these tiny white micro flakes look like hell through the walls of the glass kettle. So if you want to own a glass kettle you better get use to the fact that you will likely be washing the kettle out after every use. We use to just leave the water in the kettle after it was done boiling and just add more water to the kettle as needed. Once you view whats in the water after its boiled, you will never leave any water in any kettle ever again. You all know the old saying " What You Don't See Won't Kill You " . Well unfortunately when you use a glass kettle " You will see it ". I'm going to try distilled water to see if the water remains clear after boiling. I can just get my normal size adult male hand inside the glass pot to wash it after every use and its easy to clean right now. The pot being clear glass it will not take very long for the white scale to really be visible and build up on the inside of the glass walls. I wish the little hanging filter screen was removable when you go to wash the pot, but I can't see anyway to unhook it from the lid. There was no indication the screen is removable on the directions / instructions that you receive. The lid and power on buttons and the automatic off feature all work very well. The blue Led Lights are absolutely beautiful and the kettle lights up the entire kitchen when you have no other lights on. The pot is much fatter than you think from the photos that are posted. This 1.5 L is only 1 inch shorter than the Ovente 1.7 L model. So that should give you a pretty good reference on how tall the 1.5L really is and its true size over all. Four cups of water ( 1 L ) brings the level of water exactly to the half way mark etched on the side of the glass pot. Its quiet when boiling and boil's water at about the same speed as most kettles. As previously stated this glass kettle looks and works great but is just slightly lacking that 5 Star quality. In all fairness though, this is a solid 4 star product and for the price paid you will simply not go wrong. I recommend this " Ovente " product to all. I hope my review is helpful.

title: SAFE & much FASTER for me
body: 4.5 stars: I DID NOT get a discount for my review. The first thing you will see in the box is a big red stop sign cutout advising you to: wash the item before use, and within 30 days register your product online for the 1-year warranty. They also provide a toll-free telephone number with operation hours. The website address for registration they gave is wrong, it is Ovente.com/register. You need your Amazon order number, the product number from the name of product, and date of purchase. The website does not give you any feedback after you submit your registration, but later on an email will come with a copy of it. The instruction booklet is sufficiently comprehensive and easy to understand. The 30" cord coils around inside the base so a minimum amount is visible. (My white kettle has white cord which I really like.) You do not have to push a release to pour, liquid just comes out. Nice, substantial somewhat ergonomic thick plastic handle and housing for the heating element. 1st iffy: The smaller opening of the top, and the angle at which the lid fixes open. It took a little maneuvering to get my large lady hand in there with sponge to clean, plus it is a little awkward getting it under my faucet to fill. Your hands or faucet may be different. The top DOES NOT come off to make it easier. 2nd iffy: The "filter" attached to the lid that (when closed) sits in front of the pour spout. I am not sure what it is intended to filter - I do not have any chunks of things in my water, and it is not a tight enough fit against spout to filter out say, tea leaves as you pour. It in fact allows water/tea leaves to flow out UNDERNEATH the filter so it certainly is not going to trap particulates, ala Brita. This uselessness, to me, somewhat cheapens kettle. 3rd iffy: The pot stopped automatically when the water reached a rolling boil. It took me about 30-45 seconds to grab a temp gauge and insert, to find it read 182 degrees F and descending (water boils at 212 right?). If having very hot water and keeping it warm is important, I saw on the Ovente website some glass tea kettles with infusers and warmers. As to metal & plastic touching the water: The glass (to me) seems thicker than a regular coffee maker pot. That said, upon visual and tactile inspection I do NOT think this glass carafe allows the underlying metal or rubber or plastic to touch the water inside of it. It appears that the bottom of this carafe is indeed glass. Underneath on the OUTSIDE of the carafe is the heating element. This element seems to be a metal plate with hard rubber (?) ring around it - this is the part that plugs into the base and it is all on the underside, outside of the glass carafe. This all sits sunken into the thick, colored plastic housing which holds the lights, carafe and its attached heating element. This entire unit is what you pickup off the base to pour. The timed boil test: I decided to compare to my old stainless steel stove top kettle rather than other reviews. I used the same amount in both kettles - halfway between this kettle's minimum of .05 L and the 1.0 L line (about .75 L). NOTE that I prefer my tea water to be just starting to boil (small bubbles on the bottom and sides). This kettle was ready in 2 min 20 sec, the stove top was just over 6 minutes.

title: Decent, But Could Be Better
body: I've been using the OVENTE Glass Electric Kettle for about three months now, and it's proven to be a fairly average appliance. It boils water quickly, as advertised, and the borosilicate glass looks nice on my countertop. However, there are a couple of significant drawbacks that prevent me from giving it a higher rating. My biggest gripe is the lid. The opening only allows access to roughly 66% of the kettle's interior. This makes filling it with water a frustratingly awkward task. A wider opening would make a world of difference in terms of usability. Another issue I've encountered is with the stainless steel base. Within the first few uses, it started to develop stains, and these stains have unfortunately worsened over time. While I understand that this is a budget-friendly kettle, I still expected a bit more durability in this area. Ultimately, you get what you pay for. It does boil water fast, and the glass is a nice touch. However, the limited lid opening and the staining on the base are significant flaws. I wish OVENTE would address these issues in future models. A thicker base and better opening would greatly improve the product. If you're looking for a basic, affordable electric kettle and can tolerate these issues, it might be a suitable option. But if you prioritize ease of use and long-term appearance, you might want to consider investing in a higher-quality model.

title: It's OK, but stopped working after 6 months.
body: I bought this in August 2014. We are constantly using it to boil water for tea and coffee. I would say we use it to heat water at least 5 or 6 times a day. After 6 months and hundreds of uses, it still smells like hot plastic when water is at a full boil and it has just turned off. Additionally, some of the plastic has warped on the lid near the pour spout. Also part of the plastic on the handle has begun to warp. I was also under the impression that the entire container was glass, but the bottom is metal. After about 3 months it began to get tiny rust spots, which were able to be removed with a scrubby, but I was a little disappointed by this fact. This has happened again and again. Not a deal breaker, but I'm not impressed. The handle is comfortable. It does overflow the pour spout and make a mess if you pour too quickly. I previously had a stainless steel electric kettle with a less acute pour spout and it poured wonderfully. Overall, I have been happy with the speed with which it boils the water, and the blue lights are neat. It has never failed to turn off when done boiling. However, this week, after having had the item for only 6 months, it stopped working. I don't know if it's the switch itself that has failed, or some other component. Regardless, with as many good reviews as this item has and having paid more to buy the one with a glass container rather than the less expensive plastic ones, I'm pretty disappointed. It says in the product description that it has a 1-year manufacturer warranty, and I will try to contact Ovente to see if they can replace my kettle. If I do not have a good experience with their warranty department, I will come back and change this review from 3 stars to 1. If I have a good experience with them, I'll still leave it at 3 stars. It's OK, but not great. If it didn't smell like plastic after all this time, and if some of the plastic hadn't warped, I'd give it a better rating. Update (3/9/15): As seen below, a customer service rep from Ovente responded the same day I left this review. I had also emailed them that day. When I called the following morning, the customer service rep said she was just creating a shipping label for my replacement and was just about to call me to request a copy of my receipt/invoice from my purchase so she could verify I was still in the warranty period. She was very friendly, very helpful. My new kettle shipped out that day and in less than a week, I had my replacement. Also, regarding the replacement kettle. It seems to have some newer/different pieces than my 1st one. The power button and button to open the lid are white instead of black. Also some of the plastic detailing was a different color. I don't care about these slight variations, but what I did notice was that after boiling water in it only once, it no longer smelled bad like my other one did the whole time. So I'm changing by review to 4 stars instead of 3. We'll see if this one lasts. I hope it will because I do like it.

title: Failed after 20 months. Was a fairly good buy, while it lasted.
body: I bought this electric kettle because our old one spontaneously died and this was the only model I could find that fulfilled my requirements for a new one: a concealed heating element, automatic shut-off, and a mouth wide enough for me to reach inside with my hand for scrubbing. Beyond that, it's a nice looking counter appliance. It's neat being able to watch the water boil through the glass, and the blue LED indicators are a nice touch. It gives it a friendly, futuristic feel. It boils nice and quickly, too. The only con, and this is minor, is that the black Ovente logo smudges and smears if you touch it or wipe it down while the unit is still warm. It makes for an ugly spot on what is otherwise an attractive piece. Also note: The "max" line is for real. If you fill it even a little bit beyond that line, it will spill onto the counter when it boils. UPDATE: After a few months of ownership and daily use, I have another "con" I need to list; once it has boiled once, it will not turn on again for several minutes, presumably because its thermostat thinks it is still at boiling temperature. I find this unfortunate, and my previous kettles with automatic shut-offs did not exhibit this behavior. Use case: When I want to make a pitcher of hot tea, my tea pitcher is a half gallon. This thing only holds 1.5L, which is just over 3 quarts. With previous electric kettles, I used to be able to boil a full pot, start the tea steeping, and then quickly boil another quart to top it off while the infusion was still taking place. With this new kettle, that is no longer possible, as it takes several minutes for the kettle to become usable a second time, and by then it is too late. While disappointing, this use case failure is not going to be a deal-breaker for everyone. One wonders, though, why this thermostat detects so much residual heat after a boil, even after cold water has been poured in, so as to prevent consecutive boils. Perhaps they could get the design team to correct this in future revisions. UPDATE 2: This just died today, 12/20/2016. It was purchased in April 2015. So it only lasted a disappointing ~20 months of daily use. I guess the next pertinent question is, "Knowing this, would you lease an electric kettle for ~$10 per year?". I suppose I would, but, really there is no excuse for these things not lasting longer. They aren't like brake pads, which, by design, get progressively worn out as part of their normal use; Electric appliances should not need to be so frequently replaced. Unfortunately, all electric kettles seem to be rife with reviews that tell of early failure. So, perhaps this is one of those "they don't make things like they used to" rants. Obviously I need a way to boil water. Microwaving is out of the question, and a traditional stovetop kettle would use more electricity and boils more slowly. So... I either buy another one of these, or play roulette with another brand. Such is 21st century consumerism.

The filter feature was in the way when filling with water. I learned that when the kettle when used at or close to the max fill line it would make a plastic smell likely from this plastic feature. I never used tap water and only used bottled water and R/O water from my water store and did not have a problem with scale. It looked good on my white counter top, and sadly I can not find another white kettle with no plastic touching the boiling water in any nearby stores. Because of the short life and because the pan I have been using on the stove until I find something else, boils water faster- I truly do not know if I would buy this again. .................................................................................................................................. The Unit is not all glass, the bottom of the carafe is stainless and the glass and the bottom are sealed together with something that looks like it does come in contact with the water. I'm wondering what that sealing substance is and if their is any health concerns?? 2 stars for function and a 3rd star for good looks. I may as well use a saucepan on the stove for how looong this thing takes After the 1st boil there is visible moisture trapped behind the glass and inside where the lighting is and I'm wondering how long 'till that causes problems. After the 1st boil the heating element is already stained. Other than coolness factor the light seems useless and may cause problems as moisture is already inside there after the first 8 1/2 min almost boil. The Instructions said to boil 4 times before using. At max fill line 1.5L: using my cell phone timer 1st "boil" after 8 and 1/2minutes the unit had not shut off yet or even produced steam, I was able to pass my fingers through the water(quickly)without burning. 3rd boil while unit was already warmed up took 9min 2 sec to get to a full boil. 4th boil while unit was already warmed up took longer 9min 14 sec to get to a full boil hmmm? The stiff round white 5/16 inch thick 3 pronged cord needs to be wound internally inside the base and come out a notch in order for the base to lay flat reducing the cord to 15 inches of usable cord length photo attached. It was really stiff and bent the opposite way, I did not wish to risk forcing a made in china cord through the notch without winding to get the full cord length. The stiffness of the cord prevents the unit from being pushed back to the wall. I've owned an all stainless Aroma and have used it daily for 4 years it is still going strong and looks shiny inside and out.1.5 L. The Ovante seems to take a long time and the water does not get as hot compared to my Aroma kettle. With the Aroma after 3min 50 sec it produces steam and 4min 10 sec for full boil shut off. The only drawback of the aroma is that I just found that there is plastic inside at the bottom where the boiling hot water comes in contact. I purchased the Ovente to avoid consuming hot plastic water. I am not sure about the sealant in the Ovante and it takes a looong time compared to what I have become accustom to for boiling water, The Ovente is like going back to 3g after using 4g. The Ovente is also not as easy to line up on the base. I do have to say the main reason for purchase is health reasons and price, however it does look good, I bought the white one it looks very current. I have to turn on another light source to put water in the kettle anyway so the fun blue lights are in my opinion an impractical thing that could go wrong. Overall I will be on the look out for something better and likely spending more. I may even send it back because of the moisture leak. Hope this helps your decision making.

Also my favorite part is that it lights up when it’s on. Such a simple thing but, I never seem to forget about it anymore because the light is more noticeable to me in the morning. I’ve seen other comments about the kettle forming rust or having issues with water quality and the auto shutoff malfunctioning. I have never found any of this to be an issue. I have seen some build up at the bottom of the kettle that looks like rust but, I just give it a good scrub and it and it always cleans up fine. I never have issues with it doing anything to my water however, I do always use filtered water so not sure if something may happen with water from straight out of the tap. As for the auto shutoff I can say after over 2 years it’s never failed me. I’ve liked it so much I just purchased a second one for my mom and that’s what lead me to write a review about it. Just a note to some. Make sure you don’t place this kettle, or any that I’ve seen, under a cabinet or in close quarters to anything. It will give off a lot of steam from the top and if something is just above it, it will melt, warp, or just smoker style BBQ whatever it is. I had a friends destroy his cabinet with a different electric kettle because he had it jammed at the corner of his counter and close to the cabinet above. This thing needs just a little room to breathe. That’s just my two cents take it as you will. If you do care it boils a max amount of 1.5L in 8min and 30sec thought someone out there may want to know. Pros: - Still solid after 2 years. No loose parts and I have no worry about using it every day. - Boils water quickly, several minutes at most for a large cup or to go mug of coffee in the morning. - Easy to see blue light that lets you know when the kettle is on or off. - Thick power cable that can be tucked into the base to adjust length. - Being able to watch the water boil through the glass, stupid but awesome and a pro to me. After trying several tips with no relative success I tried the following routine and now it's clean as a whistle. Here's what I did: I used about 3/4 cup of white vinegar. I stood by while it cycled one time. I let sit for a hour and switched on again. I did that twice again - every hour; It was looking better. Then I rinsed out the vinegar. Next with a tablespoon of hot water in the pot, I used a synthetic wet sink sponge covered in 1 teaspoon of baking soda. I proceeded to clean off the stubborn scum on bottom, using the rough side of sponge with a little elbow grease, then I cleaned the inside and outer glass with more baking soda: this is not easy, as you have to gently get your whole hand in there and turn pot as you work. Also worked the spout and filter. Lastly I rinsed and boiled 16 oz water, Swished and drained. Looks new! Going forward I'm gonna try maintenance every month on a less vigorous routine. I have love hate relationships with my 10 or so Roomba purchases over the years... the newer self-cleaning one is least frustrating one, but the Brava which I held off buying for a long time has been one of the best purchases. And these replacement pads are far better than the one batch of less expensive ones I did try. Here's a little something I do.... one, I pre-moisten the whole length of the pad, so the edges start gathering up the sticky dirt the Roombas can't remove, faster than it would take for the Brava sprayed liquid to be reabsorbed in the center of the pad and move to the edges..... two, I usually get 3 or even 4 uses out of each pad - making it less expensive than any cheap alternative. As soon as the Brava stops, I take the pad, and just hold it at an almost 70 degrees under a faucet with a spray option so the gathered dirt literally washes off and I do not let the blue backing cardboard that clicks into the Brava underside get wet. The pad rinses back to almost 90% new, and it can be done a few times before the cardboard connector may not get recognized by the Brava. Plus, the idea is to avoid wastage, not to get married to one pad forever. :) These pads work much better than even the original washable reusable iRobot one. Hope this helps you get the best bang for the buck while staying with the original brand. Mind you, this is not advice, but my experience. Use your own discretion and common sense.

title: Simplifies making tea, but should be unplugged between uses
body: This makes pretty good iced tea. I have been using loose leaf tea and a tea pot with infuser to brew the tea. I've done this for many years and easily adapted my method for this tea maker. I make sweet tea daily using these steps: * Add 2 heaping tablespoons of Twinnings English breakfast and spread over the bottom. * Add 1/2 cup of sugar in the filter (no coffee filters used). I don't spread it out, just pile it in the center. * Add water to the pitcher up to the water line and pour into the tea maker * Add 3 'scoops' of ice to the pitcher. Then add water to the water line. This should be just enough to float the ice. If the ice doesn't float, remove some of the ice until it floats and the water is at the water line. This ensures the same amount of water in the pitcher every time. You don't need the ice at all, but I prefer it so the tea is cool and I can put it directly into the refrigerator. Plus, we have an automatic ice maker and this helps keep the ice fresh. * Place the empty pitcher in the machine, set the strength to 4 and start. Play around with the strength, sugar, and tea as needed for your own taste. This isn't true southern sweet tea as it only uses about half the sugar my grandma used. I like this method because I don't have to deal with tea bags. I get loose leaf Twinnings tea on Amazon and use about one tin a month, which means it's about $6/month for the tea. Much cheaper than buying soda or flavored waters. And fewer additives. This makes enough for the pitcher we use in the refrigerator plus about another glass full. Adjustments are easily made to make less. Cleaning is easy. I take out the basket and turn upside down on a paper towel, then add it to the compost bin. Rinse out the basket after each use by running water backwards through the filter (i.e. from the bottom) until the basket doesn't have any tea left in it, being sure to tilt to get the sides. Every few uses, also rinse out the larger basket the filter sits in with hot water, depressing the mechanism so water drains through the hole in the bottom. The only caveat I've found is that the start button is not an on/off switch. If you press it while the machine is plugged in and is empty, it will start to smoke. There is no way to shut it off unless one unplugs the pitcher or adds water. The instructions are very clear about this, please read them. They specifically state to unplug the machine between uses, which I find to be a bit inconvenient. Still better than my old method, but it shouldn't be necessary. If they manufacturer provided a better mechanism for turning this on and off, I'd give it a 5.

title: Perfectly adequate - it does the job
body: I make a LOT of iced tea at home. I don't do carbonation, caffeine, refined sugar, nor artificial sweeteners, so I pretty much have to make all my beverages myself if I want anything other than water. I grow my own plants for tea so I need something that works with both fresh and dried leaves and flowers. I've used both the Oster and the Mr. Tea makers and they eventually failed because they were too complicated. Hidden water reserves you can't reach into to descale and springs with pressure-sensitive, filtered reservoirs which get clogged with tea residue and eventually fail to dispense the tea properly. This machine has none of that. You just fill up the water container, put the plastic tea basket on the plastic pitcher, pop on the lid and slide it under the water container's output nozzle. Super easy to clean and get all the gunk out. I don't love the plastic pitcher instead of glass, but since I put the tea into glass containers for storage in the fridge the plastic pitcher isn't a real problem. I use a VERY fine strainer in a large metal funnel, so no leaves, etc. get into the tea. I miss the ability to pull out the pitcher to empty as it fills, but at least there's no springs/whatever to go wrong and not function properly. Both the Oster and the Mr. Tea lost the "auto stop when pitcher is pulled out" function months before the machines gave up the ghost entirely. Having to wait for the auto shut off when the pitcher is full is a small price for being able to make a full gallon of tea in just two runs of the machine. I don't use any ice, so it's easy to top off the water reservoir as It empties with a total two quarts of water for each run. I empty the two runs into a gallon jug, mix in whatever else I want in the brew (lemon or other fruit juice, etc.) mix it up and put it into the pitchers in the fridge. It can be served over ice or just stored in the fridge until cold, which is the way I like it. Bottom line: It does the job, it's not ugly on the counter, and it was a very good price.

title: More like a large coffee maker than a typical tea brewer

Where my old one would perculate hot water over the tea and it would sit there until so much water filled up to a drip hole at the top of the tea bag holder that it would then drip into the pitcher, this one is more like those hotel coffee makers. There is an internal water arm that swings over the tea bag area. It does spray out in multiple streams and not just one place, but then the tea immediately goes into the pitcher instead of steeping for any time. Having said all of that, it does brew okay. I find that I put 3 large tea bags in, fill the water to the top of the window (above the max line), then when it is done, I fill it up again to at least the max line and brew it again. My biggest issue with this unit is actually the pitcher itself. The lid doesn't fit very tight and the pouring slots in it are small, so the when I'm pouring, I have to hold the lid or it will come out. Had it happen twice before I realized what was happening. I'm use to just tipping the pitcher with the liquid stopped by the lid and pouring through the spout, here you almost have to just tilt it just enough for the tea to go to the slots and no more than that. Any back pressure on the lid and it pops out. I'm just used to filling up a glass of tea one handed (cup in one, pitcher in the other), and keeping the lid on takes too long, so I've actually just transferred the tea to my old pitcher and I don't even use this one to store tea.

This makes it ideal for double brewing to get a stronger tea. The downside to this model is the flimsy plastic lid. The heat from the steam causes it to warp and not lay flat. I have to manually bend the lid back into shape after each brew. My recipe for a strong, refreshing not-so-sweet tea below: Fill with filtered water to slightly above the Max line (don't worry, she can take it!), put a couple ounces of water into the pitcher (no idea if this is necessary to prevent pitcher from cracking from thermal shock, but the manual recommends it). Fill basket with unbleached basket style coffee filter, 3 tablespoons loose mint tea leaves, 4 tablespoons loose black tea leaves. Set brew strength slider to Max (who doesn't do this?) Brew. Leave basket alone, refill water again, brew again. Remove basket and discard contents, add 1/2 cup of sugar to tea. Add enough filtered water to tea to make it 3 Qt. In my experience it's more important to make sure the ratio of sugar to water is correct.

title: Beautiful and functional electric kettle
body: I had purchased online three other, different brands, electric kettles and they ALL LEAKED. (Fortunately, I was able to send them all back for a refund.) Skeptical of buying any other electric kettle online no matter what bran, this one caught my attention because of the choice of colors and its elegant design; I had been looking for an aqua color to match my newly painted turquoise cabinets. And now, I am so glad the others didn't work out because this one is perfect! First, it does NOT leak! And the best quality is that it heats up quickly with a bonus of watching a boiling water performance through the clear glass illuminated by a beautiful blue light. The light shuts off when the water is boiled, so I don't care about it not having a "beep" when it's done. Although the container and lid are hot to the touch, the sturdy, functional handle stays cool - just don't touch the hot parts as you would not touch a boiling tea kettle on the stove - duh! I have been using this kettle for two months now and really enjoy its presence in my kitchen, the bright colors and its quickly-produced hot water is a happy wake-up note on any early morning, so I do hope it lasts a long time. Photos show the kettle: 1) full roll boiling, 2) boiling done and auto turned off, and 3) just set to boil (the light comes on as soon as you press the "on" button).

title: Truly speed boiling!
body: This electric kettle has completely upgraded my daily routine, it’s fast, sleek, and incredibly user-friendly. The 1500W power boils a full pot of water in just a few minutes, and the blue LED light adds a surprisingly nice touch that makes it feel high-end. I love the clear glass design because it’s easy to monitor water levels and feels more durable than I expected. The wide opening makes cleaning a breeze with no awkward scrubbing angles. The auto shut-off and boil dry protection give me peace of mind, and the 360° swivel base makes it super convenient to lift and place from any direction. For the price, this kettle packs premium features and style, and it’s become an essential part of my kitchen setup.

title: Fast, Simple, and Reliable—This Glass Kettle is a Kitchen Must-Have!
body: I bought the Offacy Electric Kettle mainly because I wanted something simple, fast, and reliable for everyday tea or quick meals—and this kettle nails it. It boils water surprisingly quickly, probably faster than my old stove kettle. The glass body is nice because you can easily see when it’s ready, and the blue LED lighting when boiling is a fun touch. The kettle sits neatly on a small base, so you don't have to drag a cord around when pouring, and the auto shut-off is great for peace of mind. One thing I noticed is the lid doesn’t fully detach—it just pops open. This can make cleaning inside a bit tricky, especially if you have big hands or prefer to wipe it down after use to avoid water spots. But honestly, it hasn’t been a huge deal for me. There's also a handy little mesh strainer built into the spout, so you won't accidentally pour out any tea leaves if you brew directly in the kettle, which I do a lot at work. Pros: - Fast Boiling: Heats water quickly, ideal for morning tea or fast meal prep. - Glass Design: Easy to see water level, plus it looks great in the kitchen or office. - Auto Shut-Off: Turns itself off automatically after boiling, giving some peace of mind. - Built-in Mesh Strainer: Prevents tea leaves or small particles from ending up in your cup. Cons: - Lid Doesn’t Fully Remove: Can be tough to clean the inside thoroughly, especially if you’re picky about water spots. - Glass Body Requires Extra Care: Looks great, but you’ll want to be careful not to bang or drop it, as it could crack or break. Overall, it's a solid little kettle, especially at this price point. It’s been reliable, boils fast, and looks good sitting out on my counter. Definitely worth getting if you want a simple, efficient kettle that gets the job done!

title: Functional, easy to use and clean, looks beautiful
body: I love this Peach Street kettle! It's so easy to use, just fill with water and push the lever down, that’s located under the handle. I wanted a glass kettle. Once I received this kettle I immediately donated my stove top kettle. This one works fast. The instructions say to fill it up to the max line which is clearly marked. I turned it on and timed it to see how long it takes to boil 1.7 liters of water, it took exactly 6 minutes. I did this twice per instructions. I like the built-in mesh filter that lets you put tea bags or fruit in the water with just the water passing through. This makes it easy to boil water fast for tea, instant coffee or for hot cereal. The only thing that gets really hot to the touch is the glass, but not any part of the metal or handle. It automatically turns off once it comes to a rolling boil. I also love the blue color when I turn it on, it looks so cool. The top pops open at the touch of a button. It has a wide mouth makes it easy to fill and to clean. The base has a 360° rotating base making it easy to access the kettle from any side. My son loves that because he's left handed so it makes it easier for him. Beneath the base I can also store the cord in a specially designed storage slot. There is also a notch under the base to put the cord through so the base does not wobble when it’s plugged. I highly recommend this item, It is well worth the price.

body:

LOVE, LOVE, LOVE this electric kettle!!! You will too! The blue LED light is so fun and shines through the bubbly, boiling water. How cool is that? Brings joy to my day :) Thoughts and User Error (my fault): First of all, do not hand wash this electric kettle when it arrives. I always wash everything and did not read the directions first. Instead, boil two pots of water as per the manufacturer’s directions to clean the inside of the electric kettle. (You can clean the outside when necessary with a lightly damp cloth as per the directions). Since I hand washed my kettle as soon as it arrived, I somehow got water where it wasn’t supposed to be and so the kettle worked for one second and then shut off. Great safety feature! Excitement gone. I saw the pretty blue lights and then nothing. My heart sank. Then I read the directions. I realized my error that I was to not wash the kettle. I immediately tried to shake any water out of the bottom side of the kettle and then set the kettle aside to dry out for several days. Fingers crossed. Then several days later, I tested it again and low and behold, it worked! (I had only washed the inside of the kettle but I must’ve dripped water somewhere I shouldn’t have during the process. Also, it was a little difficult to wash inside the kettle (tight opening for a hand to fit) so that probably should have been my first clue). This electric kettle is so stylish and functional at the same time. I highly recommend the white color. It really looks clean on the counter and the blue light really pops with the white and stainless. I contemplated getting a fun color like pink, but am happy I chose white. I almost immediately ordered a second kettle after I thought I broke this one as even in that first glimpse, I knew it was cool and I’d really enjoy it each day! Heats extremely fast and is just SO fun to watch! I think it is a good value too. I researched numerous brands and stores and this one had the features I was looking for. Simple, clean design, not a ton of buttons, I can see the water level, easy pouring, heats quickly, I can turn it off if I want just hot water rather than boiling because I can see what stage it is at, and as a bonus, it has the fun blue light! Thanks, Peach Street!!

title: So handy! And FAST!
body: I don't really use it for coffee or tea, but that's mostly because it's hotter than blue blazes in Florida this time of year and I don't want to drink anything hot. Instead, I bought it to boil tap water. I'm really happy with it so far. This thing is so easy to use! The carafe sits on the base with the handle in any direction you want, so no fiddling to get it on just right. Just stick it on there, flip the switch down to turn it on, and it lights up with a fun blue color and starts heating, just like that. It's at a rapid boil within just a few minutes, then I can just let it sit a while and start to cool before I put the water in my pitcher and stick it in the fridge. So much better than continuing to buy water filters. My well water is okay, but I like the peace of mind that boiling or filters give me. The kettle fits my needs perfectly. It looks good, works well and is a convenient little appliance. I'll worry about a reverse osmosis system next year. Edit 1/26/24: I know I like to see updates on reviews when people have had time with their product, so I thought I would leave an update on this kettle after several months of use. STILL loving this! It's been holding up under multiple uses per day, every day since I got it. Also, when tragedy struck and my Keurig broke, I was without a way to get coffee going for iced coffees. I discovered I have a unrepentant love of instant coffee (judge me, I don't care, it's yummy). Who knew? Anyway, I have been using it even more often for a while, and for more than just boiling tap water. On (rare) cooler days, I can have hot coffee that I enjoy every bit as much as from the K machine. And I can quickly get coffee made and cooling for iced coffee on hot days. Either way, the kettle remains super easy to use, and it still looks good. I love it. So yes, this remains one of my better purchases in a long time.

title: Swift and Stylish: Speed-Boil Electric Kettle Delivers Excellence!
body: The Speed-Boil Electric Kettle has been a game-changer in my daily routine, making my morning coffee and tea rituals faster, more efficient, and stylish. This 1.7L water boiler boasts a powerful 1500W heating element, utilizing borosilicate glass for a delightful brewing experience. The first thing that caught my eye was the sleek design of the kettle. The borosilicate glass not only adds a touch of modern elegance to my kitchen but also allows for a clear view of the water boiling process. Watching the water come to a rolling boil through the illuminated LED light is oddly satisfying and provides a visual cue that the kettle is ready for use. The speed at which this electric kettle boils water is truly impressive. The 1500W heating element ensures a rapid boil, saving me valuable time during busy mornings. Whether it's for a quick cup of coffee or a soothing cup of tea, the Speed-Boil Electric Kettle consistently delivers hot water in a matter of minutes. The user-friendly design is evident in the easy-to-read water level indicator, allowing me to fill the kettle with just the right amount of water for my needs. The 360-degree swivel base adds convenience, making it a breeze to lift and pour from any angle. The ergonomic handle stays cool to the touch, ensuring a comfortable grip during use. Cleaning this electric kettle is a straightforward task. The wide opening and removable lid enable easy access for thorough cleaning. The borosilicate glass material is resistant to stains and odors, maintaining the purity of the water and the integrity of the kettle over time. Safety features are another noteworthy aspect of the Speed-Boil Electric Kettle. The automatic shut-off function and boil-dry protection offer peace of mind, preventing accidents and extending the life of the appliance. In conclusion, the Speed-Boil Electric Kettle is a stellar addition to any kitchen, providing not only functionality but also a touch of sophistication. Its rapid boiling, user-friendly design, and safety features make it a standout choice for coffee and tea enthusiasts. I highly recommend this electric kettle for its efficiency, durability, and aesthetic appeal – a must-have for those who appreciate both form and function in their kitchen appliances.
