title: Just get it
body: I picked up a Thermos Brand Bluey cup at Target at random. Ok, so it was on an end cap and my son wanted it so I said ok. I liked it so much I bought this one here. First of all, before I was using other brands for his water bottle at school. Sippy cups, NUK brand, that one made from recycled plastic, anything. Usually plastic and typically see through. That stops NOW (for him taking to school, I'm not throwing the others out---yet). First of all, I forgot what made a Thermos great: the insulation. This kid will have his water bottle with ice full at night, and still have ice in the morning. I know when he goes to school his water will stay COLD (it isn't for hot drinks). Second of all, it is durable. Toddler durable. Toddler winging it across a parking lot as they are swinging around telling you a story about Paw-Patrol durable. Sure there may be some surface scrapes, but deep down it's ok. And so are you. This thing is so easy to clean in a dishwasher or by hand. Some sippy cups it feels like you are a EOD expert taking apart and assembling the pieces. Not this guy, pop off the lid, pop off the straw, pop off the mouth piece and clean. Leak proof? Pretty much so, unless you don't screw it on properly. If the lid/mouthpiece is open, yea it leaks, but so do most things when the lids are open. Am I worried about lingering odors? My kid loves water. Like, legit, it's his favorite. We only use this for water so there are no odors. Am I worried about his orthodontic growth due to the impact sippy cups have on his forming teeth? No, is this a new thing? I just want my kid hydrated and not chugging sugar all day. Does it hurt when you drop it on your toe? Oh, you betcha. Will I be buying more? Yes, he has already stated he wanted a space one.

title: A Good Electric Kettle, But Needs Improvements
body: I bought this electric kettle to be able to make several cups of tea at a time. For the first two weeks, this kettle was flawless. It doesn't take long for water to start boiling, and the automatic shutdown makes it easy to use. It only has one on/off switch. One you put water and tea in the stainless steel filter, just turn it on and wait for it to turn off automatically. That's it. Why three starts only? It would be 5 if it weren't for two defects: - The blue LEDs didn't last long. First, one side would not turn on, then the second would turn on every once in a while. Now there is no LED lights. - Water accumulates at the base, where the heating element and wires are. This happens when cleaning the carafe. I started noticing this when pouring the tea and saw water coming out of the base of the carafe. I first thought tea was leaking into the base. Then, I figured out that it was during washing that water got in. There is nothing to prevent water from going in, or at least draining properly. This will eventually damage the electrical parts. Other than those to issue, with the second being the most serious, this electric kettle is very convenient. If you get one, make sure the base is well drained after washing. The LEDs may last longer if carefully draining the base.

title: Boils over, water/tea everywhere, (when filled well below the \"max\" line)
body: This regards the 1.0L model. ***THERE IS A WORKAROUND: Boil your water first, without the infuser installed, and turn off the kettle as soon as the water starts to boil, (so that it does not spill over the top), and THEN insert the infuser. This is unfortunate, because it is not a "set it and forget it" operation. But it works this way. Fortunately, it does not take long at all for the water to boil.*** Even when filled well below the "max" line, the water -- or tea -- boils over and erupts from the spout and spills all over the desk, under the base, between the base and the kettle, etc. The spillover also gets between the glass part of the kettle and the heating element that is built onto the bottom of the glass part of the kettle. There is about a 3mm space there, with vents, (presumably so it does not pressurize and crack). Every time the water overflows, (i.e., every time the kettle is used), the water gets between that crack. What that means is AFTER you clean up all the mess, then go to pour the remaining contents in a mug, the water spills from the bottom of the kettle and all over everything again. As far as the look, appearance, etc., I mean, yes, it works, and it does boil water fast. For under $20, if it didn't overflow, it WOULD HAVE BEEN a GREAT value. It's just the particular design of this one that makes usability suffer so badly that I am now looking at another tea kettle that costs three times as much. Good concept, and even good manufacturing for the price. But the mess it makes is truly a shame. For the nay-sayers... This is the 1.0L model. I do not live in any climate extreme. I'm at 400' above sea level, and barometric pressure is typically higher than US average. Yes, when there is tea in the steeper, the overboiling is quite more excessive than when there is not tea, but the effluent over-boil occurs even when it's just clean water. I've tried both tap water, (chlorinated, fluorinated, and 240 grains hard), as well as distilled water, and both give the same result. It's not me, not the water, not the atmosphere. It's the design.

title: 6 weeks in and going strong. Easy to use and accurate
body:
The media could not be loaded.

As a long-time coffee enthusiast, I decided to take my home-brewing game to a new level a couple of months ago. The three cornerstones of quality home-brewing are: 1) a good grinder, 2) a precise scale, preferably one with a built-in timer, and 3) an efficient and reliable device to heat water. Our focus here is on the third element. After six weeks of rigorous daily use, brewing 2-3 cups of coffee each day, my electric coffee kettle has been performing pretty dang well. I felt compelled to write this review after reading some concerns about temperature accuracy. Naturally, I decided to put my kettle to the test. Using a high-end meat thermometer (which need to be accurate as people rely on them to prevent foodborne illnesses) I tested the temperature distribution of 500mL of water, freshly beeped from the kettle. This volume reflects my typical usage: I brew somewhere between one to two cups at a time, using 50mL to pre-rinse the filter and the rest for brewing. The results were impressive. The thermometer registered 204.3F at the top of the water and 205.2F at the bottom, indicating less than half a percent of error across the volume at the time of the beep. Importantly, the kettle pours from the bottom, where the temperature was virtually spot-on. These findings contradict some reviews I've seen. If your kettle isn't delivering the same performance, I'd advise contacting the company about a possible replacement. Remember, maintaining accurate temperatures is crucial for serious coffee brewing. Keep in mind, though, the kettle's maximum stated capacity is 800mL. Attempting to heat more than this could lead to a drop in temperature accuracy. This kettle marks my first 'serious' foray into coffee brewing, as opposed to boiling water in a stovetop saucepan. I appreciated its well-thought-out safety features. The bottom is exceptionally well-insulated and remains cool to the touch after brewing, eliminating any concern about damaging your countertop. However, the sides do heat up, which is to be expected. On top of that, it's very easy to use. Turn it on, choose a temp, and before it reaches temp, hit the Hold button to have it hold temp for up to an hour if you need to multitask. The pouring action is smooth and predictable, without any after-pour dripping from the spout. About the only other thing I'd want would be some kind of real-time temperature monitor (whether analog or digital) on the kettle itself to verify its ability to reach and hold temp over time. Considering the $70 price tag, I believe this kettle delivers 95-98% of the performance you'd get from considerably more expensive models. While I can see the appeal of the additional features offered by higher-end kettles as I continue to refine my coffee-brewing skills, I'm currently satisfied with the simplicity and functionality of this Cosori model.

title: Best Buy
body: Fast and accurate water heater. A best buy. I press Start, Coffee, and Hold to get 96C water in minutes. Seems silly to spend three times the cost of my Hario Switch but accurate temp is important. Worst is 3C low as it's designed to race to 3 degrees under target and then coast to finish. $10 more for Fabuletta allows exact temp (currently unavailable). Fellow Stagg at $170 is a bit more accurate (stopping 5 degrees under and slowly approaching finish). But water cools far more during the pour over. Need Hold for the 90 seconds until final pour. Don't forget the pre-rinse to warm the brewer and filter (and not to clean the filter as many suggest). It never boils because it never gets to 212F (100C). So, no spitting or whistling. The kettle is made with food-grade 304 stainless steel, ensuring no plastic taste in your water and no rusting. The 360-degree swivel base makes it easy to place and lift the kettle from any angle, and the LED display adds a high-tech touch. The digital interface is intuitive, with pre-set temperature options for different beverages. It also features a keep-warm function, which maintains the desired temperature for an extended period, so you don’t have to reheat your water repeatedly. Ease of Use & Safety The one-touch controls make it simple to adjust settings, and the automatic shut-off and boil-dry protection provide peace of mind. The BPA-free interior (if applicable) ensures no plastic comes in contact with boiling water, maintaining purity and taste. Pros & Cons ✅ Pros: Precise temperature control for different beverages Fast heating and efficient performance Keep-warm function for convenience Sleek, durable design Safety features like auto shut-off and boil-dry protection ❌ Cons: Slightly more expensive than basic kettles Some models may have a shorter cord or require frequent descaling Final Verdict The Cosori Electric Kettle is an excellent choice for anyone who values precision, speed, and convenience. Whether you’re a coffee aficionado or a tea connoisseur, this kettle’s temperature control and high-quality build make it a worthy investment. Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)

title: Really Works Well
body: The true test, of course, is whether it's still working well in a year. But a few weeks in, I'll say I really like it. It's definitely small capacity. I bought it for pour-over coffee, and I get one cup of coffee out of it. Ok by me, but it's something to be aware of if you're buying this for a large capacity french press or something. Check the stated capacity of this kettle compared to your brewing vessel. What I really like is the very, very easy and intuitive temperature control system, the fact that the beeps are not very loud, and can be turned off completely, and how quiet it is as it heats. Most kettles get so loud as they heat that I can't hear anything else. Might have something to do with the small capacity, but still, I'm glad it's quiet. I like it. It's not as nice looking as the Stagg, which is what I wanted for years, with it's wood handle and lid knob. But based on reviews, that wood lid knob regularly cracks wide open, and the cheap plastic display stops working. There were a few too many Stagg reviews with the exact same problems...enough of them that I couldn't justify the price. This was the next-coolest-looking, for less money and with better reviews. We'll see how things go over time. ONE YEAR REVIEW Still going strong. Pros: pretty much all the above is still true. Personally I've had none of the issues I see in the 3-and-less-star reviews. Yet. Cons: It did finally get noisy. Maybe as everything broke in it loosened up a little? Not sure, but now it's the typical, loud kettle. It does leak a little around the base, only sometimes. The max fill line is really hard to see. After a while you get a sense of how full is too full, but if you have to rely on seeing the max fill line, it's not easy to make out. It's started making some loud popping noises when it first starts heating up, and I get the sense it's not just water vaporizing in the base, but larger problems looming. When it makes a loud pop, the typically heating sound goes away for a few seconds, then starts again. So I'm guessing the popping is something starting to go faulty with the heating element. As some other reviews mention, the buttons don't work when wet. So what. It's an electric base. We should all be trying hard to avoid getting it wet. It works again as soon as it dries. I see a lot of similar kettles are on the market now. Might be worth exploring other options. But as a lot of us have probably noticed, there's not a huge difference from one to the other. Often, they're made in the same factory in China, with a different name stamped on them, and maybe a couple slight differences in design. But basically the same kettle. I think people's positive and negative experiences come down more to luck of the draw on how well their individual kettle was assembled, how well the circuit board was soldered, etc. 2 YEAR REVIEW Still going strong. Popping noise I mentioned hasn't gotten worse, and I'm starting to think there's a connection between that noise and how much mineral build-up is on the inside. Seems to be worse when there's build-up. Sometimes, for months at a time, it doesn't happen. The "leaking at the base" I mentioned in the one-year review might actually just be steam coming up through the top vents and the edge of the lid, running down to the base. Anyway it hasn't gotten any worse over 2 years. Aside from being noisier than when I first bought it, it still works like brand new.

title: Better Than The Expensive Gooseneck Kettle
body: I bought this as a replacement for a Stagg EKG kettle my roommate is taking with him when he moves out, and was pleasantly surprised to discover that I like it better than its predecessor. I wanted a kettle that would heat water to 205 degrees F, with no plastic touching the water, and no loud beeping. The Cosori pours much better than the Stagg. It is more comfortable to hold and pours well from a lower, more comfortable angle. It's also not as painfully slow to pour from as the Stagg, which a comparison video I watched found was the by far slowest pouring gooseneck kettle available. It used to take me 12 seconds to fill my mug with water for tea using the Stagg, and sometimes I would get impatient and angle it a little higher, and hot water would dribble down the side of the kettle, threatening my toes. I don't have that problem with the Cosori, which pours efficiently and whose lid fits snugly. I chose the stainless steel finish because the paint on the black Stagg is starting to chip off after a year of use; I expect this finish will be more durable. To test the heating, I poured 1 cup of tap water into the kettle, and pressed the button to bring it up to 205F. It took 1 minute and 22 seconds. According to my thermometer, which is accurate to within half a degree, the water was at 202F. I tried again later with more water, and again it was at 202F at the end of the heating cycle after pressing the 205F button. That's close enough for me. Pros: - Very comfortable to hold - Pours quickly - Low price compared to kettles with similar features - Very quiet beep is not annoying, won't wake anyone up, and can be turned off - Stainless steel finish won't chip, unlike black paint - The presets coincide with the temperatures I like to use - Feels sturdy and well made - Has not dripped or leaked with normal use - Comes with a 2 year warranty Cons: - The "buttons" don't move when you press them. They are just touch sensors. In my experience with other appliances, this kind of button is likely to be finicky and eventually stop working. - The inside of the spout and lid is not smooth stainless steel; it has an odd texture. According to the company, the inside is stainless steel and it's not lined with anything, so presumably it is just textured stainless, but it still seems odd to me. It's clearly not a non-stick coating as one reviewer thought, but I don't get why they would give the inside this rough texture. - The temperature options are limited to certain pre-sets, which work for me, but you can't dial in any temperature you want and they are not perfectly accurate. They get within about 3 degrees of the temperature indicated. Update: I've been using this every day for a year and a half now and it's still going strong.

title: Poor design choices all around
body: I just received my new Cosori kettle. I haven't even turned it on yet and I'm already having regrets. There are poor design decisions all around on this model. FIRST, THE LID: The lid had to be pressed firmly in place. There's no hinge, and you can't easily lift it without also holding the kettle itself (and not just the handle, unless you want to risk the hot lid also flinging up at your hand). Why is this a problem? Well, the capacity is severely lacking. This kettle barely heats enough water for 2 cups of tea or coffee, less if you use larger mugs like I do. That means if you're a heavy tea or coffee drinker, and you need to refill this frequently, you have to wait for it to cool before you can get that tight lid off and add more water. After just removing and replacing the lid about a half dozen times, I'm also hearing a slight crackling sound in the plastic of the lid's handle. It's not inspiring confidence in this kettle's longevity. CONTROLS AND SETTINGS: The control design is also not great -- on the kettle base, haven't tried the app yet. Cosori's fallen into one of the worst trends in electric kettles these days by offering presets and no manual on-board temperature controls. These are rarely accurate or adequate. This model, for example, starts at 180F, which is a bit high if you drink more delicate teas. Sure, there's the app. But why should customers be wed to yet another tool that can become buggy or introduce changed features without our knowledge or consent at the time of purchase? Kettles should be designed to last. Apps often are not. So if something happens to the app's development, or to the company itself, you might suddenly lose the extra control you're paying for when you buy this kettle. It's one more potential fail point. Fine for convenience. But granular temperature control shouldn't be limited to that. An LED screen to show the current temp and simple up & down buttons should be a priority over separate buttons for each manufacturer-chosen preset. A decent design would have fewer buttons with more customer control. This might not seem like a big deal if you only plan to use those presets. But I've used several electric kettles, and I can tell you they're very rarely accurate. Even when they're accurate at the point of the temperature sensor, that's not the same temperature of water elsewhere inside the kettle. And when you use electric kettles to brew pour-over, French press, or AeroPress coffee like I do, you'll want a very precise temperature. You can't rely on presets. You learn about variations in your kettle, then you tweak the temperature manually to account for any differences between kettle and cup. OUTER FINISH: The outer finish is another poor design choice. It came already scratched, and there's no way to fix that with this kind of finish. More, if it scratches deep enough to the stainless steel below the outer finish, you'll see it clearly due to the color contrast because this is so dark. The scratches on my lid are like this, and it doesn't seem to require a particularly deep scratch for it to be blatantly visible. THE OPENING: The opening is also less than ideal. You're unlikely to fit your hand in there for cleaning, and even a dish wand or bottle brush would be awkward given the curve of the wall. And I'm not sure why they have a rough texture to the inside of the lid unlike the more polished-looking stainless steel in the body. But the inner lid, while metal (which is good), also seemed to come coated with a dusting of some light kind of powder. The lid in general is a real disappointment. SUMMARY: Look. I have no doubt this little kettle will heat water just fine. But whereas this seems to be Cosori's "top of the line" electric kettle, it feels more like a "lite" version of what a proper kettle should be. If you're a light or casual tea drinker who doesn't mind the pre-sets and/or doesn't mind literally watching your water boil on an app, this might be great. But if you drink more than a cup or two of tea a day, drink tea or coffee quickly enough that you might have to refill this before it fully cools (so you can safely remove the lid), want real control of your kettle ON your kettle and not through a separate app, and don't just want something that will look pretty on your counter, you can find better. This does have potential to be improved. But that would require at a bare minimum a more reasonable capacity (which would also solve the narrow opening issue potentially), a better lid design, and better manual on-board controls. Still not sure if I'll even fire this up given how many problems there are after just unboxing and inspecting it. Given how long I searched for a new kettle, I'm beyond disappointed at the prospect of having to return this and start my search over from scratch. This brand came recommended, so I had much higher hopes for Cosori.

body: I purchased this Oct 2 2022 and received it 2-3 days later. I bought it specifically to heat water for tea, primarily black tea, but also oolong, green and white. title: 3 years later…
body: Three years later and she’s still going strong. I can confidently say I love this kettle. I keep seeing other more expensive and “high end” kettles and think about replacing it but I just can’t. She’s been so good to me. Even after someone accidentally spilled some water on the buttons, she still works great. Here are a few tips that I recommend to take care of your kettle: 1) descale your product every 6 months or so. Especially if you live somewhere with hard water. I am lucky to have access to drinkable water but I still run it through a filter before putting it in my kettle. I have noticed when I use water that has sat out in a pitcher overnight I have to descale my product less. You don’t need a fancy solution, just Google a vinegar solution. Tbh, I would recommend this will all products that you run or heat water through to prevent the lime scale/ water mark build up. I think doing this has kept the temperature accurate. I have read that having lime scale and affect the accuracy of the temp read on gadgets. 2) don’t let water sit in it. I know it’s easy to forget or not want to refill the kettle all the time but I use it so much that I have trained myself to empty it like clock work. 3) this goes along with 2 but don’t keep the lid on. I usually empty my kettle and then put the lid next to it to let it air out. I started doing this about 6 months ago and I haven’t had to descale my kettle yet. It’s kept clean and it gives my kettle an opportunity to air out. 4) make sure you don’t spill water on the outside of the kettle when filling it. This one is kind of a no brainer but if you get water on the hot rings, it might stop it from working. Only takes 5 seconds to grab a dish towel and dry the exterior before putting it on the burner. 5) DO NOT PUT ANYTHING IN HERE BUT WATER. I don’t think I need to elaborate on this one. That’s about all I have for now. You take care of her and she will take care of you! I always get compliments on this kettle. She’s sleek, reliable, and fairly priced compared to other “fancier” kettles. Video is me boiling water to 180 and taking a temp read right after. Still works!

title: COSORI GOOSENECK KETTLE WITH FIVE HEAT PRESENTS IS SIMPLY ONE OF THE BEST PRODUCTS I'VE EVER OWNED!
body: I have never written a review of any kind before, but this kettle has inspired me to tell the world how great it is! The Cosori Gooseneck Kettle with Five Variable Presets is simply one of the best products I have ever owned! I have now bought seven of them because I love it so much, I want everyone I care about to have one too. I bought my first one in December of 2020 for myself. I loved it so much, I immediately bought two more for my daughters. Since then, I've bought one for a dear friend, one for my daughter-in-law, one to replace the one my daughter accidentally set on a hot burner of her stove, and now one to keep at work for all my coworkers to enjoy along with me. What's so great about it? First of all, if you've never tried pour-over coffee, you're missing out. I had an electric kettle before this one to boil water for tea, and it worked fine but all it did was boil water. When I started using the pour-over coffee method, I found out how good coffee could be, and I wanted a kettle that would get the water just right. When I found this one, with heat settings for not only coffee, but various teas and a boil setting, I decided to try it despite a number of reviews that complained of rust inside the kettle. Psssh! Just take care of your stuff, people! This thing works flawlessly, gets the temperature just right for whatever hot beverage you're making for the absolute best flavor, and cleans up like nothing I've ever seen. (I will never again have a nasty drip coffeemaker sitting on my countertop!) And it's beautiful! As I mentioned earlier, I bought my first one in December of 2020, so I've had it long enough for any potential problems to come to light. You can see in my photos that it is still in perfect condition. These are photos of the one I've owned for over a year - I'll be taking it into work on Monday to share with my coworkers. Here's my whole routine: 1. Heat the water according to whatever hot beverage I'm making (usually coffee), pour any excess water out of the kettle, and put it back on the base WITHOUT THE LID. The kettle and lid dry quickly, and I've never seen any trace of rust. 2. I have hard city water so when I start to see white spots in the bottom of the kettle (believe me, you will), I just pour in some white vinegar and let it sit for 10-20 minutes, then rinse until I don't smell vinegar anymore. Look again at the photos of the inside of my 14-month old kettle and its lid - no rust or no lime deposits - every part of it still looks brand new! Just don't set it on a hot stove burner like my daughter did. The bottom of the kettle is plastic and will melt!

title: Great!
body: Great kettle, no issues, worked for many years before I bought it as a gift for a friend. Worth the price!

title: Great while it lasted
body: Great electric kettle in every respect, except it died after 3 years. To be fair, that is still longer than our previous kettles from other manufacturers.

title: Ready when you are.
body: Great tea kettle. Turn on from bed and have water ready when arrive to kitchen is a real plus.

title: Surprisingly Good
body: This kettle is ideal for single pour coffee, which is what I do. Keeps water at an ideal temp while I complete my pour, about 3 minutes. Controls are easy to use. Saw alternatives with some squirrelly dial. Don't need that. All the common-sense settings are represented by buttons. Takes longer than my old kettle. I can live with that. Holds what appears to be 2 large cups or in my case a 16 oz. cup comfortably. Will need to be refilled for larger pours (in a large Chemex or like). Draws a lot of current. Tends to trip my breakers (in a new house) now and again. One time, the electronics got messed up requiring an unplug, much like a computer screen freeze. In general, this is a notable step up from my old unit (analogue only) which lasted 4 years of daily use and is no longer available. Quite pleased with the replacement kettle.

title: Great
body: This is great! Perfect for maté because of the ‘memory’ function. Also I love it being analog and not having any digital screens - all the temps are presented at once and immediately accessible. The only thing keeping it from being a 5 star is I wish it had a lower temp - a 150 or 160. 195 and 205 aren’t uniquely helpful but a lower temp (to make tepid water to proof yeasts or warm bottles) would be.

title: Great Kettle & Settings
body: I absolutely love this kettle! The settings alone are worth the purchase. All stainless steel interior. Great gooseneck for pour overs. Does come out a little fast but just takes some getting used to. For the price, this is perfect! Very pleased & made the perfect cup of coffee today! Highly recommend!

title: Great little kettle at a really good price
body: I wanted a gooseneck kettle to make pour-over coffee and this quickly heats just enough for 1 or 2 cups of coffee or tea. I like that I can set different temperatures for different kinds of tea as well as coffee. The temps are accurate per my instant read thermometer and the button to hold the temperature is handy for making a second cup. The price is great compared to other highly rated goosenecks. The only thing I would change is to make the beep that tells you it's reached the right temperature louder. I can only hear it if I'm really close to the kettle and wish I could hear it if I'm farther away in the kitchen or dining room.

title: Heats fast, very accurate, AND energy efficient!
body: Absolutely best thing for tea since the days of Bodhidharma! It heats a cup of water before a microwave could do it, and then it can optionally hold the temp for the duration. Pours perfectly and balance is ideal. It even has an "oolong" or "green" button. LOL....No more interruptions going to the microwave or worrying about right temp for tea. Very accurate. And the black color is great for gong fu zen tea ceremony! No plastic parts etc. Water tastes great! I would disregard that one old review complaining of rust and scale. Those problems he had years ago must be some kind of local water quality issues. IMHO as someone who professionally advised folks about their water quality problems I admit there is an outside chance he had a kettle with a problem but 99.9% sure it is the water that goes in the pot causing the issues. I use filtered water that is no too hard. If you have hard iron water and want good tea you don't need the Dragon Well in your back yard but a good filtration system! After using my kettle 2 liters a day for 2 years I have had zero problems with scale, rust or leaks and still give a 5 star rating. Six if I could. Every now and then I add a little white vinegar and carefully scour around with a non abrasive blue scotch pad and like NEW! Update 5/5/2022 Out of the five of these excellent kettles I have purchased for family and friends one had a fading of brightness on the "Hold" button which I depend on for my longer tea ceremonies. Within 24 hours the Cosori customer service had replied to my email warranty claim request using email found on the Cosori website, and they immediately and generously sent me a replacement even though my warranty was days from expiring. That is what you call 5 star service. A great company and product! Now, I wish I had not filed a claim because if one is handy the fix for the faded light was easy. First, the kettle still worked with the "Hold" feature even with the dim light so no action was necessary as long. Just press the button and it still works. If it turns off after it comes to temperature then you know you missed the button or hit it twice. The interesting thing about the faded light is that it created an opportunity for a DIY person to replace the little 4 cent LED bulb, and I happily did the unsoldering of the old and soldered in the new after removing the screws and carefully opening the plastic case with a very small screwdriver. The great thing was that I wanted to add a personal touch so i used a RED bulb since it has an image of a fire on it. JOLLY ! Now I smile each time I use the kettle! There are two screws with a triangle shaped head for safety, but I found a $5 bit set that had one that fit. So the old kettle is good to go indefinitely now, and Cosori sent me a replacement that I feel I should send back to them now as it is unneeded. For all you tea lovers out there... I highly recommend this kettle and this company! Happy Cha Dao to you!

title: Love this electric kettle!
body:

We absolutely love this electric kettle! We got it while we were renovating our kitchen and didn’t have a stove. It was so helpful to have a plug in way to heat water for coffee, tea, oatmeal whatever. We use it daily for our pour over coffee. The gooseneck is perfect for a slow pour to let the grinds bloom. I love the multiple settings for types of tea or to hold the heat. It’s super fast on the heating up. We’ve had it for over a year and it’s still performing very well. It’s shuts off automatically so I don’t worry about it being a fire hazard. Great product!

title: My dream kettle has come home!
body: I have had the same kettle for almost 5 years and have been wanting a newer one. After looking around for months, I finally got this one and it's perfect! As an avid tea drinker, this makes it so easy to make the perfect cup every time. And it matched the product pictures perfectly!

title: What a Pleasant Surprise!
body: After twice living with disappointment with two higher priced electric kettles, I was both relieved and surprised to finally get my hands on one that actually works. I didn't expect the Cosori to heat to an accurate temperature, but manual measurements over the course of a month verified that it does just that. It has been accurate to within 3 degrees at all coffee brewing temps. The hold temp feature was also accurate. The only other question remaining is how long will the unit work, and only time is going to tell me that. Its build quality appears to be quite high, and I'm expecting it to hold up. If I'm wrong, I'll modify this review. There is nothing cheap looking about it. There are a lot of electric kettles out there, and it's a difficult choice to make. That is especially true when considering an unknown brand. All I can tell you is that I've had no complaints with this one.

title: Rust and pour over coffee are not a nice combination.
body: I loved this little pour over kettle for the first month of use. I bought it at the end of January (just over two months ago) and have used it daily for my poor over coffee. I wish I could give it a five-star review, but it has rust inside of the kettle. I'm so disappointed because I like everything else about it. I've never had this kind of issue with any other kettles and I haven't experienced my local water as being hard. It's really disappointing. Needless to say, I have used sos pads to remove the rust, and followed other recommendations to clean out the pot. I have dried it thoroughly and left the lid off between uses and still the rust persists. I see faint spots reappear and have to be attentive to the crease between the wall of the tea kettle and the base. It is tedious to have to wipe out the inside and all the crevices after each use to avoid the rust growing. If you choose to get this kettle, be sure to allow it to dry out completely or take the time to dry it out completely after each use from the first use. Best of luck.

title: Worked Great Until
body: After using this kettle for one year, the base after being turned off and unplugged remained extremely hot. I discovered it yesterday as I picked it up to move it, and the base was way too hot. I'm not going to continue to use it due to this, for fear it could cause a fire. Being unplugged, I wouldn't think the base unit would retain this much heat. I'm wanting to know why this happened and how can the base remain extremely hot when unplugged. Seems like this is a serious design flaw. Now I'm hunting for a different brand and hope my next kettle will last a lot longer than one year.

title: Excellent quality and works well to brew tea exactly as nature and Cosori intended.
body: Saw this at a relatives house as they served us tea and had to have it. Looks cool and made of really high quality materials including the skinny spout that works really well. Most importantly we learned that you can now you can select the optimal water temp for different types of teas. No longer are we using a one size fits all team kettle. We are now brewing herbal, black, green and various other teas at the exact temperature that nature and Cosori intended them to be brewed at.

title: Excellent
body: We purchased this several months ago and use it daily. We use it for coffee, tea, more coffee, more tea at various times throughout the day. We use it wayyyy more than we anticipated. We havn't had it long enough to see how it holds up long term but for as much as we use it it has been working great! We got it on sale and the price was fair. It looks nice and heats water up much quicker than our stove kettle. I also feel safer using this instead of constantly turning on the stove burner. My only complaint is that I wish the water reservoir was a tad larger but I knew what I was getting when I purchased it. I keep saying that this is one of my top favorite purchases of 2024. I hope it holds up well long term because we absolutely love this thing!

title: Don’t last long!
body: Not durable! It started leaking after 3 years! It was good when it was working. We used it only once a week. But then it started leaking this June 2025. These COSORI products only last for 3 years. I had a COSORI air fryer, again only lasted for 3 years.

title: Best kettle at this price point and even higher
body: I love this kettle. The goose neck works so well, and it feels really natural and clean to pour. It’s very durable, and everything works well The only change I’d make is that I’m not in love with the touch keys. Sometimes if my hands are just wet enough, it won’t register, but it’s not big enough issue, nor worth removing a star. No leaking at this point. The heating element turns off once it’s reach temp. From my experience, comparable kettles are double the price you pay for this. Cosori has been a solid brand.

title: Great kettle!
body: Got this for the wife for xmas - it was on her list. We used our old kettle daily and it interestingly died a few days before xmas and this one was already sitting in the present stash so out it came. The different settings are nice. It is fast and doesnt push out a lot of steam. It's also much quieter than our old one (the glass style large pitcher). The bluettooth is completely unnecessary and we haven't used it once - maybe if you are a hipster doing precision poor over coffee you might need that app to control water temp :)

title: Works well for a little over a year, then starts to leak and stop beeping
body: I’ve had this kettle since November 2023. During that time, it’s done little buggy things like refusing to turn off or change settings. Unplugging the machine fixes this… but right now the plug is very hard to reach AND I’m 9 months pregnant, so this bug becomes a little annoying, not something I’d expect for a $70 kettle. Earlier this week, it just stopped beeping when it reaches temperature. Again, I haven’t had this kettle for too long and it’s not cheap, so what gives? Unplugging did not resolve this new issue. Later in the week, it started beeping again. Now it just beeps when it feels like it. Lastly, the kettle leaks a considerable amount right at the base of the gooseneck, so be careful. This happens more the more full it is - so the first cup poured will leak, but the second is usually fine. The fill line is hard to see. It’s not in a great position for visibility - they should have put it on the opposite wall of the vessel, but this is just nitpicking at this point. Once you fill it up a few times, you get a sense of how full it should be. Despite its flaws, it’s not the worst kettle. It still heats up quick and I appreciate all of quick settings. Just beware that it will start to fall apart after a year. Worth noting as well: I do not use this kettle every day! I’m a fall/winter tea drinker, so this kettle did not get heavy use for half of the length of time I owned it.

title: Great product
body: Best one I've gotten even over the 200.00 ones. Heats fast and will hold for an hour. Nice led light buttons. The pour is perfect.

title: Exactly as described
body: This is my first electric kettle. I wanted something that worked well and looked good sitting on the counter. I liked the chubby kettles but wanted a smaller size. I was a little reluctant to go for the long spout and the black or stainless, but the reviews on this one were the best I saw. Liked the smaller size and it boils enough water for 1-1/3 cups in 2 minutes. It has multiple temp settings and is simple to use. I add water just before use and when it's done I leave the lid off and it dries quickly, so hopefully there won't be issues with corrosion or rust. I do wish it came in white or other colors but thus far that's the only con I've found.

title: Cosori Electric Kettle
body: So nice. Super fast on heating water for my coffee. Love it.

title: Nontoxic but beeping no longer works after 2 weeks
body: After using it for 2 weeks, the alert that it's done boiling no longer works. I wish it also flashed or did something to let me know when it was done other than the little beep. I was usually not in the room to hear it, so it would have been nice to know it was in fact done. What I like about it is that it doesn't have any plastic and so is very nontoxic.

title: Good Quality and Heats Up Fast
body: I purchased this kettle to use during power outages when I can't use my stove. I quickly came to like it for it's easy settings, ability to hold the desired temperature, and how quickly the water heats up to the desired temperature. It has become a part of my daily routine and I am very happy to have found it. The only thing that is annoying is where they placed the water fill line. It is not clearly marked and is located inside the kettle on the handle side. So cannot be easily seen when filling the pot.

title: This product just did not last..and doesn't keep temperatures at the desired settings
body: I thought I had reviewed this product, but it must have been the previous electric kettle I purchased. I bought this originally in 2020. I used it for about one year because I bought a second electric kettle. I recently took this off the shelf when a friend started staying with me. Our coffee mugs are glass mugs that hold 22 ounces, so the one kettle I had been using wasn't enough. It only holds about 28 ounces, so not enough for two cups of coffee. Within a couple of months this Cosori stopped heating. So, I got a bit more than one year of use out of it. It's out of warranty so I'm stuck. But, I had taken temperature readings on all settings, and then checked the temperature when I used the "Hold" button to see if the kettle would maintain the right temperatures. The digital thermometer I used was a $99 Thermopen which is among top of the line used by chefs. None of the settings except for boiling ever hit the mark. All were off at least +/- two degrees, and more of a temp difference when I used the "Hold" button. I'm not sure if that temperature difference really makes a noticeable taste difference when making white or green tea, but this product doesn't really meet up to its advertised settings. What I found most annoying is that there is a "Max" fill line which is inside the kettle, but it's in the back of the kettle, so when you're pouring water, you have to actually turn the kettle almost all the way around to see make sure you haven't gone past the maximum fill. It is important to pay attention to that, btw, because if you fill over that, you can easily spill boiling water on yourself. I know because it happened to me when my friend filled it too high. I wrote to Cosori, but there's nothing they're going to do with the pot out of warranty. But even so, think about this...even if I HAD not put the kettle on the shelf for two years, the useful life was less than 4 years. Planned obsolescence? My sister-in-law had an electric kettle (different brand) and hers also lasted less than 4 years before the heating element burned out. I doubt these are made for long-term use. I need another kettle, with a larger capacity that also has variable settings since besides my beloved coffee in the morning, I enjoy a wide variety of green, white, black, and herbal teas which all need to be seeped at different temperatures. But, lesson learned on this brand! I won't buy it again, and all I can do is give you my experience.

title: Best affordable kettle so far
body: If you are looking for a kettle to prep your baby’s formula this is the one. Through Bluetooth you can set your own temperature under my brew from 104º F and up. With out having to use your phone every time you want to warm up water to a temperature that is not on the 4 settings. Not even a month in an the automatic setting on “my brew” did not stay at 104 it went up to the 200’s

title: Not a durable product
body: I bought my item around 2 years ago. Unfortunately it deteriorated faster than I expected and developed a fishy smell lately. I tried to descale and get rid of the smell but it did not work. Now I have to throw it away. Given the price of item, this is a quality problem.

title: Simple and effective
body: Excellent little thing

title: Elegant and functional oolala!
body: Summary- Very elegant and highly functional. Pros-- 1. It's heats up quickly without making too much noise. 2. The buttons have this light futuristic touch- not like a touchscreen but not like a button either. It's fun to use. 3. The goose neck spout looks cool and really helps aim. Cons-- 1. I don't know yet how I will clean the spout.

title: Multiple heat settings
body: My wife loves it. I like the multiple heat settings.

title: Love this little kettle!
body: So far this kettle is really great!! I had a nice electric kettle that sadly I broke, so I began a quest to find a new one. And when I say quest, yes it’s been a journey. Looked at MANY brands and read TONS of reviews and there’s a lot of crap out there. Ordered another brand and it wobbled on the base … back it went. Found in reading reviews that many different brands have “wobblers”. Finally decided to try this Cosori bc I bought their air fryer and it works quite well. This kettle has five heat settings for various types of tea, coffee and the highest being “full boil” for black tea or instant soups and cereals, plus a Hold Temp button which holds the temp for an hour. I mostly use the Full Boil selection but have also used the one for green tea, and use the Hold Temp button as well. All have worked beautifully. As for cleaning, I use it almost nightly so I haven’t really had to clean it per se. I use filtered water in it and leave the unused water in the pot. Here’s the CONS … as others have said the timer bell needs to be louder. You can only hear it if you’re standing in the same room which defeats the purpose of having it chime lol. But I will say it boils pretty darn fast … like in just over TWO minutes so I usually just putter in my kitchen and wait. The other cons which are not deal breakers for me are that 1) It only boils about 3 1/2 cups of water so if you have a large family using the kettle this one won’t be for you. 2) It’s wide in terms of how it’s constructed. I included a pic so you can see that from the farthest part of the spout to the farthest part of the handle it’s almost 10 1/2 inches wide. So it’s not going to tuck into a corner of your kitchen. I love the look of the design and it works in my kitchen but I did have to move a couple things around to find the right spot for it. But it works great and I really love it!! Oh and NO it doesn’t wobble!!!

title: PERFECT IN EVERY WAY
body: RE: COSORI Electric Gooseneck Kettle (matte black) UPDATE: This kettle was thoroughly design carefully! Areas where hands and fingers would normally go are cool to the touch, unlike others. Impressive. I finally got myself a gooseneck kettle in place of a regular spouted kettle. [Why did I wait so long?] This works lovely and is the perfect size. It's VERY easy to use and NOT complicated. I was happy to find that the kettle lid 'handle' didn't get NOT, like some other brands do. It comes with directions and a user manual.

title: 5 YEARS GOING ON STRONG
body: I can’t believe I never thought to write this review before, because this kettle has been awesome for the past 5 years! I originally got this August 2019 for my college dorm, and it endured daily use for a couple years no problem. Here we are in December 2024, and it still heats up water incredibly fast, and very accurately to the temperature control. All the features still work good as new. The paint looks great, and the condition of all the coatings, components, and electrical features are pristine. A simple descaling (instructions in the booklet) would have this machine looking and preforming completely brand-new. The only issue I had is the handle becoming slightly loose over time. I contacted the Cosori team (again, 5 years after I got it) for advice and they promptly sent me an entire VIDEO showing me how to re-tighten the handle. Good as new! I highly recommend this kettle and thank the Corosi team for their support!

title: Great Goose Neck Kettle
body: First I really like the look and feel as you pour from this kettle. It heats quickly and will hold that temperature for one hour. For making tea that is a great feature. This kettle is very well made and I expect will keep performing well for a long time to come. Don’ t know that of course since I haven’t used it that long. For pour over coffee it works great. Very good balance while pouring and easy to control the stream. I love all the features it has too. I would recommend this kettle.

title: Fuss-free kettle
body: It's been working great for 2 months! Easy to use and I don't see any plastic components inside the container. Will update with 5* if it lasts a long time with no issues.

title: Loving the Black
body: It is a beautiful teapot. Hoping for many years of use.

title: SPEEDY,, FAST RAPIDO
body: I debated about purchasing this for a while because I already had an electric kettle, but I was gifted an Amazon gift card for my birthday, so the guilt factor about spending the money was removed. I wanted it mostly because of the design. It is just CUTE. And I know and trust the Cosori brand. As I discovered, besides being cute, it is also FAST. I have never had water heat up so quickly by any other method. I make pour over coffee and this little kettle heats the water to the right temp almost before I can get the grounds ready for it. I love this darling kettle and do not regret making the switch from the old one.

title: Hot to the touch
body: I really wanted a teapot that was not hot to the touch but every time I ordered one from Amazon the order would be canceled because they say it was out of stock. This was my second choice. The design is beautiful. The presets are very nice. It heats very quickly. But it's still very hot to the touch if you are not careful.

title: Perfect Office Addition
body: Perfect addition for your office space and kitchen if you don’t like a stovetop kettle. I purchased two one for myself and my daughter-she loves it! Heats up quickly and auto shuts off as well. Durable, water capacity is perfect and it’s pretty.

title: Works. Mostly.
body: I bought this kettle as a replacement for one that was almost identical, same brand, but without the Bluetooth option. Somebody put my old one on the stove and melted the bottom so I had to replace it. So far it seems to be fine, the Bluetooth hooked up really good. It’s convenient that I can set a timer, but I would very much like it if I could just set a time and have that be a recurring thing rather than just setting a timer every night. Also the molding on the handle is a bit rough on this one where it was perfectly smooth on the first older one. Not sure if that’s design or what but it was not great , I know for a fact this thing works great so I’m still giving a five stars but a little bit of work on the app and maybe a little bit of quality control on the factory for the handle and this thing would be even better.

title: Excellent kettle
body: Quality of material is very good Like automatic shut off and hold feature. Heats quickly Would like to know how to turn bell on signaling temperature reached

title: Great for anything other than boiling
body: Writing a review after having it for 2 years. This is a great kettle for the money for anything other than boiling. All of the temperatures on it are quite accurate and it does a nice job maintaining those temperatures if you use the hold setting - settings aren't always exact, but within a few degrees. It's also held up great over two years, working as well as when new and looking just as good. Where I removed a star was the boiling. It is a very weak boil, it just doesn't leave the element on long enough after it thinks it's boiling. The "hold temp" function when boiling is pretty useless as well. The sensor is inside the kettle on the bottom, right next to the heating ring(based on where bubbles first form). So it registers a boil before the full volume of water is ~100c/212f. If you're a few thousand feet above sea level, I bet it works pretty well. However, in my case I find the actual temperature in the kettle when it goes off is closer to 206F, at ~650 ft elevation. It has just started to bubble near the element, but isn't a rolling boil yet. The hold temp feature at boil is worse, get's down a couple more degrees before turning the element back on and doesn't stay on long enough. I've tested a few minutes after "boil" along with leaving it on for a while, results are the same. If you need it for anything other than a boil or you are at a higher elevation, this gooseneck is a fantastic value. If you need something to boil, and stay boiling, then you probably need to look elsewhere. I've started doing more espresso(with a flair) and lighter roasts in filter coffee, so I want water that has just been boiling. This unit just doesn't cut it for me anymore.

title: High-Quality Electric Kettle
body: It heats water quickly, has a functional spout for precise pouring, and is easy to operate. However, the lid may need to be adjusted to stop leaks—this is normal and noted in the manual.

I wanted an electric kettle as my stovetop kettle took so long to heat water. But I also wanted an electric kettle that had zero plastic coming in contact with the water. The Cosori electric kettle meets this requirement and looks and performs great. I’ve had it for a a couple of weeks now and it’s performing perfectly.

title: Stylish and functional!
body: The Cosori gooseneck is as stylish as it is functional. It boils water super fast, pours easily and precisely—with no dripping—and is just the right size for a couple—enough for two large mugs or three cups. It’s isn’t as heavy or as bulky as 1.5L or 1.7L electric kettles (although the graceful pouring spout protrudes several inches from the body of the kettle, which requires more counter room). The three “ready” beeps are loud enough to be heard without being annoying. I like that the lid is removable; it makes cleaning the interior much easier. The auto shut-off is a great feature. I looked long and hard for a new electric kettle before purchasing this one.

title: perfect for my baking
body: The Rubbermaid Brilliance 12-Cup Airtight Food Storage Container is a game-changer in my kitchen, especially for storing pantry staples like flour. What makes this container stand out is its impeccable design and functionality. The Brilliance series from Rubbermaid is known for its crystal-clear Tritan plastic that not only looks elegant but also allows me to see exactly what's inside without needing to open it. This is particularly useful when quickly checking how much flour I have left before starting a baking session. The airtight seal is another highlight of this container. It locks in freshness and keeps pantry items like flour free from moisture and pests, ensuring they stay dry and retain their quality over time. This is crucial for maintaining the freshness and texture of flour, especially in a humid environment. I appreciate the versatility of the container. It holds up to 12 cups of flour, making it perfect for storing larger quantities without taking up too much space in my pantry. The modular design also allows for easy stacking, maximizing storage efficiency. Durability is key with the Rubbermaid Brilliance container. It is made from BPA-free Tritan plastic, which is shatter-resistant and dishwasher-safe for easy cleaning. This reassures me that it will withstand frequent use and maintain its pristine appearance for years to come. While the Brilliance container excels in storing flour and other dry goods, the lid can be a bit tight to open initially. However, this tight seal ensures the contents remain fresh and secure, so it's a minor trade-off for the overall quality and effectiveness of the product. Overall, the Rubbermaid Brilliance 12-Cup Airtight Food Storage Container has become an essential part of my kitchen organization. I definitely feel like it'll be a point of failure, but hopefully it'll break in with more use. The opening is pretty small, I much preferred Oxo's version with a lever action opening that was almost the entire lid. It also feels like a soft plastic, so not sure how well it seals, would have preferred a rubber or silicone, similar to the gasket on the main lid. title: Great Electric Percolator!
body: I’ve been using drip type coffee makers for years and have even tried a couple of K cup coffee makers. But, with all the news around plastics in our food and drinking water, I wanted to make the change to stainless steel. I have a stove top percolator that I love, but it takes me close to 30 minutes to prep, brew and clean up. I was looking for something that would give me the flavor of percolated coffee, but not require all of the monitoring of the brewing process for a stove top percolator. After researching all of the electric percolators on the market, I decided to go with the Farberware 8 cup for my morning brew. After two brews, I think I made the right choice. The Farberware 8 cup percolator is simple to use and brewed the perfect cup of coffee for me. The design is straightforward and setup is easy. Just add the desired amount of coffee into the basket, fill the percolator with water, place the basket and tube into the percolator, place the lid on top and plug it in. In under 10 minutes, I had a perfect cup of coffee. I know that some reviews complained that it produced a weak cup of coffee. Not so in my case. The coffee was strong and flavorful. Adding more or less coffee grounds to the basket is what adjusts the strength. Some reviews complained that the cord is short. With the electric outlet at the back of the counter, I am able to place the percolator all the way to the edge of the countertop without any concern about the length of the cord. Some complaints were about not seeing the progress of the brewing process as it doesn’t have a glass top. As this machine is all automatic and brews quickly, there really is no need for the sight glass. Just listen to the sound and you will know when the brewing process has completed. I’ve left the percolator plugged in for up to two hours and the coffee stayed nice and hot. If you’re in the market for a simple and affordable electric percolator, this machine will be a great choice for you!

title: FINALLY- A SAFE OPTION!!!
body: Finally found a percolator that is totally stainless steel and no plastic finial! Trying to find a coffee maker with no microplastics and aluminum has been a challenge, but this is the one to definitely buy! The percolator well has no aluminum nut in the bottom of the pot and there is no plastic finial on the lid as some other brands have. The only plastic is the knob on top, bottom, and the handle. Percolates quickly, a full pot in approx. 10 minutes. HACK- we are used to a automatic drip with a timer, so we plugged the percolator into an automatic timer! Now we have the coffee ready when we get up still!!!

title: Percolated coffee tastes so much better!

Less plastic waste and less expensive as well! The flat disk paper filters work well if brewing an espresso grind ((like Bustello). Thinking the K-cup machine turns into a specialty device for a custom flavored option when company comes over and this one is the real go-to device.

title: SEE UPDATES!! Terrible CS and product
body: IMPORTANT…. Update: see below, dated 4/24 & 5/24. I really wanted to like this being a percolator user for decades. I order a used 'like new' one, but it arrived more broken than 'like new' so I returned to get another new one. It does the job and makes a nice, hot, flavorful cup of coffee. It is easy to clean, although you end up cleaning it earlier than you think (see below). My problems with may just be my personal issues, idk. 1. There is no light. I knew this. But it sure would be nice to have especially when brewing process stops and then later when you glance from across the room and ask yourself, 'Did I unplug that thing?' 2. Getting the top off is not easy and hence I am afraid, in the not too distant future, the black knob will snap off. That's how hard it is to remove. There is no screw, it is welded on, so if it breaks, there is not solution other than to somehow buy another whole top, or pry it open with a tool. Neither solution is great. 3. Because the inner part of the spout is so close to the top , you really do have to remove all baskets before you start pouring. Otherwise you will be refiltering/brewing some of your coffee. The baskets are hot, drippy and before having a first cup of coffee I find myself swearing a lot early in the morning. Plus, being slightly OCD, I then find myself cleaning the whole drip system before I even pour myself a cup of coffee. Maddening! These issues could just be me being a cantankerous old man who wants an easy cup of morning jo. It does make a nice hot cup of your favorite flavorful coffee. I will use this until it breaks, but still looking for my go to percolator. UPDATE 4/24 6 months in pot was working ok until we went to plug it in and the wire attached to pot sparked. Luckily my wife was not holding the pot anywhere near that area. Smell of burning rubber, a dark burn mark on my counter and a very frightened wife. The cord had just snapped in one section exposing a bare wire. (See pic) We have a coffee bar and are careful with our coffee pots. This was not user neglect or us ‘slicing’ the cord by mistake. We don’t prepare food by coffee bar. Wrote to Faber customer service but have yet to hear from them adding to disappointment. This is very dangerous . Someone could have been shocked, the counter could have had permanent damage or if left on counter in ‘keep warm’ mode, who knows what could have happened! Very scary. And no response from CS is a big red flag! Avoid!!! Final Update 5/24: After not hearing from Farberware CS i purchases a compatible cord. It was a better cord since the wires were one piece and was actually molded into the plug. All worked well for about 3 weeks until the percolator stopped working altogether. There was a burning smell and then it stopped functioning. Between the original cord being downright dangerous, customer service being terrible, and now the product not working at all after a mere 8 months. I double down on my DO NOT BUY! AVOID AT YOUR OWN PERIL!

title: Just did not work for me
body: This did brew coffee and my issues with it may not be anything to a regular percolator owner/user, but here goes. My experience with one is from my childhood when an aunt had one. Best coffee I ever tasted. I remember the bubbling in the glass knob at the top and when it stopped bubbling at the top it was ready. When it was done, just pour and serve. GREAT! So, that is my limited experience. I bought this pot on the good reviews here and online. Maybe picky, but here are my issues with it: This one is a total feeling, but the handle shape is strange to my hand when you fill it with the max water. The handle feels flimsy and out of balance. I saw a few reviews online where the handles had just come apart and with the weight of the water and how the pot is balanced when picking up, I could see a potential for stress breaks. Now this is just a feeling, but when I filled it or carried it I always felt like I had to support the bottom to stop the handle being stressed. Maybe there are plenty out there that have gone years with no problem in daily use, but did not feel correct to me. Instructions say to remove the internals, once it is done brewing, before serving. This is fun. First, lid is tight (that's a good thing), but the knob feels flimsy on the top so I always felt like I had to be very careful is gently pressuring the lid off. The plastic knob, I assume, is screwed onto a threaded post that is affixed to the top of the metal lid. There is no attaching hardware visible from under the lid. If the knob were to snap off then hopefully the mount would stay on and you could either get a replacement or something else that would thread on. Perhaps you can ignore the instruction to remove the internals, but then the pour spout is right at the top so everything you are getting is coming out right at the filter area. Not ideal to me so I feel you have to follow the instruction. Of course, removing the internals before serving requires removing a super hot dripping mess. As such I felt I needed to do this by the sink. So, unplug, towels or pot holders out, hold the hot pot in place, wiggle lid off so as not to stress knob, take towel/paper towel/pot holder etc. and grab the stem on top of the internals, lift out and into the sink, prop so it does not fall over and dump wet grounds everywhere and then put lid to pot back on. Just me, but then I feel I need to go ahead and clean everything before relaxing and enjoying my coffee. The cord is SHORT. The actual wire between connectors measures approx. 22.5 inches long. This is basically just enough to plug it on the counter right in front of the plug area at my house. My plug is under the upper cabinet in my kitchen and approx. 9 inches up off the counter to the first plug inlet. Most of the cord length is taken up bridging this gap from plug height to bottom of pot to plug in. To keep it plugged in for the warm function and then actually pick it up and pour coffees is cumbersome. So, we unplug it. Maybe the warm function would kick in if you plug it back in (perhaps it would sense the liquid is already warm) or perhaps it would start a perk function again. Not tested as to have the plug in with that short cord does not work for me. I unplug it and just leave it sit on the counter to pour additional coffees. Perception here, but the cord also seems lower grade. Sure it looks like a thick, three wire, heavy-duty cord, but it is not like the shiny black, heavy-duty cords I have on other appliances. If I take a thumbnail and gently push on the side of those cords it does not really make a mark and they feel more substantial (electric kettle I have). This cord is dull black and will easily indent with a soft push of my nail. It springs back, but just makes me feel that the plastic is softer and perhaps more inclined to damage or separate. I actually found where others have had the cord break and had to replace it, but did not see those reviews until after seeing how this cord was on the one I bought. Spout. My purchase decision was actually swayed towards this pot because it had the short pour spout at the top and I thought it would be easier to clean. Now I'm less enamored with it. The spout is a simple U shape metal "funnel" at the top of the pot. The coffee actually comes out of the side of the pot through a small, round, hole that is raised within this U shape. The design allows a bit of coffee to pool in the bottom of the spout and sit there. Now, maybe the other pots with a lower hole and long spout from towards the bottom of the pot may work exactly the same and you just don't see any pooling in the spout area, but as I can see this at the top, it bothers me. Seems like a spot to keep dabbing dry each pour and/or a spot where you could get a buildup of dirt/whatever if not regularly cared for. Sure you clean the pot after each use, but still seems like a residue collector. I have a tough time knowing when the coffee is done. I knew there was no light to indicate it was done and no clear knob to see the thing actually perking (or not), but I guess I sort of expected the same obvious perk sound that I remember from the old glass knob one my aunt had. This pot does not make the same sort of sound and it is not obvious to me when it is actually done. Especially if we have some low AM music going. I've yet to catch an obvious "brewing off" type sound in going about my daily AM routine. So, I find myself guessing, putting my ear by the pot and wondering if the sound is it still working or that is a keep warm type sound. I now look over at the clock when I plug it in, wait around 15 min (12 cup make) to hopefully be sure it is done and go from there. Maybe these are all non-issues for everyone, but they are issues for me in my beginning adventure into perk coffee again. I guess I should have bought an old style percolator with the glass knob you could see the perk water bubbling up in or at the very least, one that has a light that either comes on or goes out when the perk is done. I'm going to start researching those and also paying close attention to the cord lengths.

title: Second Time Is A Charm!
body: Update 4.13.23 I returned a very good I got in poor condition from Amazon Warehouse, first time this has happened, so I decided to give it another go. I ordered this one like new, I have not used it yet, but as I previously stated I own one that is easily two decades old and like it so much I want another for work/secondary residence (gf's house). This time Amazon delivered a like new item - as advertised. Again the only improvement to this work horse and major player in the coffee game would for it to completely shut off about an hour after it is initially plugged in to prevent scorching the stem and the bottom of the pot should all the coffee evaporate. The coffee maker goes into a stay warm mode once the coffee is made. On my older model I have literally written "unplug me" with a picture of an electrical plug on the top in permanent marker to remind my self to unplug it once the coffee is made. I've forgotten to unplug it twice, first time I majorly scorched the bottom in the hole where the stem sits and the stem. I had to use steel wool & scouring powder to get the char off, second time (a few days ago) it was minor and used a blue scrubbing pad. Some char remains but it does not affect the taste of the coffee. Four stars, great product highly recommend especially if you can get it in good condition at a discounted price. Initial Review: I inherited a coffee pot like this from my Father he used to drink a lot of coffee and it was definitely used. First off, let me say this is a GREAT coffee maker. I got tired of buying k-cups and brought the heavy artillery back out. I thought this coffee pot is so good I'll buy another one and take it to work or my girlfriend's house. Ordered this (first) one USED VERY GOOD. I have not bought anything directly from Amazon Warehouse that was listed in very good/like new condition that was not in excellent shape, very little to no visible signs of use. Until now, the box was new and it has been refurbished with a three prong female in the pot itself and a new detachable cord, unlike mine (2 prong) which is 20 to 30 years old or more. When I took it out of the box I was immediately disappointed on inspection this coffee pot probably works but is in FAIR condition at best, heavily used with a major crack in the base and a rusty screw on the bottom. The lettering on the sticker is worn (mine isn't). I tried to reason it out but then I saw the screw on the bottom was rusted. Yard sale/thrift shop condition with a refurbished cord. Almost immediately I put it back in the box to return it. The condition was unacceptable for VERY GOOD. However, I thought enough of this product overall to buy a second one (that I don't really need) at a discounted price. I wish it had an auto shut off after an hour. I try to unplug it as soon as the coffee is made as the warmer will stay on and scorch the pot if you forget to unplug it, I've done this once and had to scrub the pot out and the tube with steel wool to get rid of the char which will ruin the taste of your coffee.

Fill marks: instructions tell you where they are and max fill (HINT: the bottom of the pump tube spring). The fill markings are on both the inside and outside. title: Non-toxic, delicious cup of coffee
body: I bought this percolator after learning about microplastics and how they leach toxic chemicals into water, food, and air, especially when in contact with hot liquid. The hot water comes in contact with the metal only, making it safe and delicious cup of coffee. The percolator makes a smooth, delicious cup of coffee. Far superior to a standard coffee pot or K-Cup coffee maker. Additionally, it's easy to use. Assembly is a snap, and it takes approximately 5 minutes to percolate. Once it's done, it switches to a warm setting, keeping the coffee hot as long as you need. Clean up takes about 4-5 minutes, and I let it air dry on our drying mat. The marks for the number of cups are on the inside, which are easy to see. I read a few reviews complaining about this feature, but it's plainly visible inside the pot as you fill it with water. I also read a few critiques about the pot not signaling when it's done brewing, but you can hear it switch from percolating to warming. One important feature to note, the coffee comes out very hot. Hotter than a standard coffee pot, so I pour a full cup immediately after percolation is complete and let it sit for 3-4 minutes to cool a bit. This coffee pot is one of the best I've used, and it's toxin-free! The price is comparable to a good, standard coffee pot, and I highly recommend it for a smooth, delicious, toxin-free cup of coffee.
