body: Seems high quality. Like the stainless steel parts (not a fan of plastic). The coffee is HOT, so be prepared. Have always used drip so took a bit of getting used to and tweaking the water to grounds ration. I am happy with the product.

title: Bought 2x, won't buy again
body: I bought one a few years ago and used it like crazy for 4 years when it went belly up and suddenly stopped heating. My coworker gifted me with the second one and it lasted almost a year before it stopped making hot coffee versus warm coffee. When it worked great, it was incredible and the coffee was smooth with a rough grind from fresh Aldi coffee beans but I'm so disappointed and this one dying in under a year that I have switched to a different brand coffee maker altogether.

title: 10 Stars! And, Update
body: I have been concerned about running hot water through a plastic drip machine for some time. So, I ordered our new Faberware stainless steel coffeepot yesterday morning and it was on our porch before 10:00 p.m. All parts are very sturdy and look like they will last a very long time but that is not the best part. I never write a review this early on but the coffee was so good, I was excited to share! This morning I had the best cup of coffee I have ever had - Starbucks included - it was rich and full bodied but not bitter and the perfect temperature right out of the pot - hot. I hesitated to follow the directions (which said 2T is the unit of measure, meaning per cup) but it was really good using regular Folgers. I added my usual anti-inflammatory mixture of Turmeric, Cinnamon, Ginger, and black pepper and heavy cream - delicious!! (Spice recipe if you are interested = 1t Turmeric, 1t cinnamon, 1/2t Ginger, 1/2t black pepper then add 1/2t of mixture to hot coffee.). Update 2 weeks later: After blasting through a Costco size container of coffee, I started using 1T per cup instead of 2T and it's just as good. That is also what Mr. Google recommends for a percolator.

title: Disappointing, don’t buy.
body: Purchased 10/24. Stopped perculating the water through the basket 3/25. So disappointed in the product. TAKE BACK MY FIRST REVIEW. I found my error in cleaning the spring on my percolator. It works fine. Phew! Still an expensive pot but I love the traditional Farberware products.

title: Great coffee maker
body: Love this. It’s perfect for our camper coffee stays hot and does not take up much room. Will buy another for our home.

title: Awesome, Thank you
body: Beautiful!!!

title: Great Perculator
body: I just ordered another Farberware Percolator which will be my 2nd one in 43 years. The first one I had lasted about 15 years that I got back in 1982. Then when I wanted to replace it the prices were too high and I ended up getting a Kenmore perc from Sears which was also a good pot that lasted maybe only 13 years. When it went out I found another Farberware on sale so I bought it because it is my preferred coffee maker. It lasted about 13 years and we noticed that the heating element had melted parts of the bottom part of the percolator. Instead of replacing it we decided to just order a new pot because the plastic had 3 holes melted into it on the sides of the black bottom part of the pot. I love this coffee pot for the taste of the coffee because it's much better and has a richer taste to me than drip coffee and the speed at percolating which is about a minute per cup is also good. The ONLY thing I don't like about the pot is that it doesn't keep the coffee as hot as when it's first finished brewing but maybe that's a safety feature, I don't know. But, if I let my coffee sit too long in the cup and add to it from the pot I still have to heat it up in the microwave because what I'm pouring from the pot isn't as hot. I ordered it and am getting same day delivery which is great because now I don't have to go without coffee tomorrow morning like I did this morning.

title: trips your breaker... (good coffee if it works!)
body: This made GREAT coffee...for about 2-3 months. (We took very good care of this guy too! Washed daily by hand...) Then, suddenly, when we would make coffee our circuit breaker would turn off. I would try plugging it into a different outlet - sometimes it worked...sometimes it tripped the breaker... We live in an apartment. We had them come in and change out the breaker. The first coffee we brewed after the breaker changed...yep, tripped the breaker. It was PERFECT and FLAWLESS for about 2 months. Then...every once in awhile the breaker would flip...then, eventually it was every time...and all outlets... I even resorted to brewing my coffee out in the apartment hallway because that seemed to work. But our maintenance crew said it seems to be a problem with the percolator. Now - I loved not having toxic plastic in my coffee maker - and, this coffee tasted GREAT! So... I am going to spend another $100 and buy this percolator again and see what happens. (I did read the reviews and it seems this might be an inherent issue with this percolator...) We shall see...

title: Loud clicking
body: I used it once. I would love to say it made a great cup of coffee. However, it makes a continuous loud clicking and whirling sound while it's plugged in, even after the coffee is completely finished brewing.

title: Love it!
body: Works great! Nice to have a hot cup of coffee and tastes great. Definitely recommend!

title: I really wanted to love it, but--
body: I really wanted to love this percolator. It makes great hot and perfect coffee. It has no aluminum or plastic that touches the interior. However the lid is so tight you are asking for an accident by trying to pry it off. This is a BIG hazard. Also I really would love a glass knob to see the color of the coffee. Lastly, it does not have an automatic shut off – not that any percolator does – but some do have a stay warm option which would at least help keep your house from going up in flames when you forgot to turn it off. Just kidding about that, I think. But having made the transition from a coffee maker where your water to be brewed sits in plastic, I am trained for the four hour automatic shut off and now that I've had this unit a few days and have woken up to scorched innards, I would say I'm past the point of retraining myself.

title: Great coffee pot but inner basket lid has sharp edge
body: This coffee pot is wonderful and should have 5 stars, but when washing the lid of the inner basket, I’ve gotten cut and also my husband. It’s still a fantastic coffee pot, but this is a design flaw that needs to be corrected.

title: Perfect
body: Outstanding!!

title: Sturdy, easy to use & great coffee!
body: We needed a smaller coffee maker for our RV. There's not a lot of counter space and every square inch is needed to cook. I thought about a percolator because it is much smaller than a drip coffee maker. This was so easy to set up and use! Within minutes of opening it I had hot coffee. I just followed instructions to clean first and set up, plugged it in and that was it. The coffee doesn't take any longer than a drip coffee maker to make coffee. The coffee is rich and flavorful. It also stays hot for quite awhile even unplugged. The pot and parts seem heavy duty. I am very happy with this percolator. I actually went online and read many reviews before ordering. This one was the highest rated of all of them in every report I read. The only disappointment is that this one doesn't have the clear glass top so you can see the coffee perking. Just a nostalgic touch that would be cool.

title: Most durable lasting coffee pot that you will ever need!
body: These coffee pots are from our parents/ grandparents generation and still they make the best coffee. Yes we have all this new technology that can make a single cup at a time or can pour into a regular cheep coffee pot. But this 1 right here this farberware coffeemaker will last for years. This 1 I actually bought for my grandmother who needed a new 1. The 1 she had prior to this 1 was the exact same and lasted her over 30 years at least. It is very durable and very easy to clean. Yes they cost more money than a regular coffee pot you get at a store or online but those one have to be replaced every few years... Or you get a coffeepot that makes a single cup at a time where people don't realize when that coffee is going through the cheap plastic lines in the machine to then go out and in the cup that all kinds of bacteria gets in it. Yes you can clean it obviously but even still do you really think it get it all if you use it every day? Not a chance. But now a coffee pot like this is basically what you see in the commercials where you can smell the aroma of the coffee beans itself. Which that's a fact I've noticed over the years from when she has her coffee during the day. Also its only a couple peices that can go in the dishwasher and really get cleaned where you don't have too worry about bacteria or anything like that. So next time you think about buying a coffee pot I really do recommend this faberware pot. They make smaller 1s and bigger 1 depending on how many cups you want it too make but you should definitely go with this brand. They have a few other older brands 1s like this 1 as well which I can't tell you how they are but I can tell you most of them are made the same with durable pots and not some cheaply made plastic pot. Now yea you might be reading this review and thinking it's just a coffee pot but than you start to think about what I said how it will last literally for years and years and you don't have too worry about bacteria building up in it either. Really think about that because with all the recalls that have been on tv with food lettuce etc that all has too do with bacteria. So now thinking yea 1 less thing too worry about in general by buying a coffee pot like this is actually really worth it and you don't have too worry about the bottom of the pot getting burnt or anything like that with this and if you buy 1 it will literally be the last coffeemaker that you will ever need to buy... So that's my review on this and honestly I barley give reviews unless its something that will save people money in the long run and will be better too NOT worry about any other bacteria like with all the recalls either food that's been going on the news lately...

title: Great coffee pot
body: Use this coffee pot every day, great pot, makes great coffee. Love that I can make 8 cups or 2 depending on how much coffee is needed that morning.

title: Strange handle but nice coffee maker
body: Have used this coffee pot since January 6,2025. It is an 8 cup but available in a 12 cup. I really like this coffee maker. It perks to a nice HOT cup of coffee. Yes I like my coffee really hot and this does the trick. I do have to blow on the first few sips to cool it. Second cup just as hot. The handle is a bit strange to start with. Only second pot of coffee but i like it. The only real drawback is there isn’t any visual indication when the perking is complete. Without my hearing aids I don’t hear it perk so a visual would be nice. The handle feels strange but very comfortable to pour. No drips. Perks hot and keeps coffee hot. I am not a Luke warm coffee drinker. Price good for a 10 cup maker. In the last 3 years I have gone through 3 coffee pots of same manufacturer. It’s like they had a one year use timer on them before it self destructs. Hopefully this one will last longer.

title: There is no plastic inside this pot!
body: This pot isn't fancy. There's no cute little light to tell you when it's ready, but you'll know when that time is at hand, because the kitchen will get much quieter. There's also no clear knob that allows you to watch your coffee perk. That's OK too. This pot may be utilitarian, but it's simple and effective. I wanted a coffee maker that didn't have any plastic parts inside, and this is it. I looked at lots of options, and for the money, an electric percolator seemed like the best choice for making many cups of coffee at once. However, not all percolators could claim that the inside construction was ALL stainless steel. Some models relied on plastic (?) rubber (?) silicon (?) seals where parts fit together, e.g., the center of some pots where the heating element connected to the pot, or a gasket around the knob on the lid. Some models with clear, hollow knobs where the coffee could be seen percolating into them were made of plastic, as well. Let me say this again. This percolator has nothing but stainless steel inside. To me, that's more important than extra features. The coffee from this pot is just as good as my old plastic drip machine made, but this one makes it much hotter! It'll take the fur right off your tongue if you don't let it cool a little before that first sip. That'll work great for anyone who lives where it's cold in the winter. Cold cups out of a cold cupboard will quickly moderate the coffee's temperature. But I digress. I found that for about the same strength coffee, I had to use about a half-scoop more grounds than I used to use with the drip maker. Cleanup is a couple more steps, but really isn't too big a hassle. Bang the grounds out of the basket in the garbage, wipe what remains out with a paper towel, and rinse out what is still clinging. If you live in an old house like I do, consider giving your plumbing as light a load of oily coffee grounds as possible, thus the extra step with the paper towel.

title: Best Value for the Money
body: I wont say that I am a coffee snob, but I cant stand anything other then a truly brewed cup of coffee. Those water rinse drip machines seem to only produce flavorless brown water. This is the next best thing to that great cup of coffee that you make on a camping trip with those little aluminum coffee pots that go on the campfire. Great quality as always Farberware!

title: Better than expected
body: Bought this coffee maker at little more than half price it was a resale was thrilled when I got it and it was as if it was brand new love it

title: Percolates but not long enough for a strong brew.
body: This unit brews fast….but that’s the problem. It’s TOO fast and then kicks off into warming mode. Getting a good strong coffee doesn’t really happen with this. There’s no way to increase the time it brews so you get what you get. Unfortunately, I failed to return it in time so now, it’s just a mediocre machine that works…..kinda. I bought another Cuisinart percolator and it seems to do better and percolates a little more aggressively for longer.

title: Too hot coffee!
body: The coffee is too hot. I can't seem to get a flavorful cup of coffee, even adjusting amount of coffee. My previous percolator was a 12 cup and made good coffee til heating unit died. Expensive enough for a forgettable cup of coffee.

title: Disappointed
body: I am disappointed in this percolator because: -- It makes weak and watery coffee if you use the recommended amounts from the enclosed manual. -- Any amount of coffee and water less than the 6 cup max makes tasteless brown water. -- There is no on/off switch so you have to plug/unplug it "hot" which causes a spark gap which can wear out your wall plug (I was warned about this by an electrician). So I had to buy a separate extension with an on/off switch. In summary, it only seems to be good for 6 cups at twice the recommended coffee quantity. So I only use it for guests. For myself, I bought a steel cone filter for making my 2 cups in the morning. I guess Faberware is not what as it used to be.

title: Quality coffee maker
body: Excellent quality works as good as the old ones from back in the day

title: I was interested is avoiding plastic in our coffee.
body: I like this coffee maker. It's the same kind my parents and grandparents used. The only thing I would change is having a light on it to let you see that it's still plugged in. And maybe an external glass tube to show the coffee level. I bought it to avoid the hot coffee coming in contact with the plastic in our Mr. Coffee during the brewing process.

title: No filters
body: Brews quickly

title: Simple to use, and NO plastic parts...
body: I ordered this perc coffee maker to rid myself of all the PLASTIC parts of my Mr. Coffee drip maker. (Heat and plastic is a lethal combination!) I am really enjoying this stainless steel coffee maker. Funny thing is, there's NO buttons and NO lights to break, and instead, just a simple-to-use machine that makes delicious coffee. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!

title: no water line to measure
body: What I Like. This pot makes a pretty good cup of coffee, and it makes a piping hot cup of coffee. the thing I don't like about it is when I fill the pot with water it would be nice to be able to see where the cup spots are measured. you can't tell where to fill the water up to. I only make 4 to 8 cups of coffee in the morning The marks are on the inside of the pot and it's in the metal color, so it blends in. They should make it so you can see the marks on the inside

title: It is Impossible For Me To Get The Lid Off
body: I have a small coffee pot that is the same brand. It is easy to get the lid off. I know how to do it. I can't get the lid off on this one. My grandson got it off for me. I am planning to give this one away. I like the coffee pot but I can't use it.

title: A Wedding Gift for my Best Friend
body: I ordered this percolator for my best friend‘s nuclear I bought this as her daughter-in-law brought a percolator maker on a trip and she loved the percolator coffee.. Friend of mine suggested this brand. So far so good. She hasn’t mentioned anything negative.

title: Wheezing/squealing noise!
body: Love a good percolator - and normally like Farberware. But this one has started to have a high pitched ‘wheezing/squealing’ sound after it finishes brewing and continues as long as it is heated. If we unplug it, it will eventually fade and stop but as soon as it heats up again it starts. Makes coffee ok but the sound is really annoying snd makes me wonder if its defective or might short out. Of course, we’ve had less than a week buy discarded the box since it was recycling day yesterday.

title: Handle wears out quickly
body: It was great until yesterday. The lid has always been tight and the only way to get it off is to tug hard on the plastic knob. It takes a good pull to get it off. After 6 months of doing that, it is now leaking out the top when it percolates. I haven't been able to find another electric percolator that meets my standards of no plastic touching the coffee and all stainless steel inside including the basket (no aluminum). I would love an electric percolator just like this but with a glass knob. The one I found has plastic in the bottom. In the interest of needing my coffee daily, I may have to get another one like this.

title: Maybe I Just Don't GetIt
body: I thought brewing coffee via percolator would be interesting and eco friendly. But, having this reminds me of how good we have it with automatic brewing machines, like those of Mr Coffe, Bunn, etc. Most baffling is the 1970s safety feature of plug it in and it's on because switches are for wusses. There's not even a light to indicate what's going on in the pot, nor any option to switch off after X amount of time has elapsed. I don't know what kind of grind to use, but you'll probably need filters if you use mass produced, pre-ground coffee. When your coffee is done, I don't if I should just start pouring or empty the grounds out first since it looks like the brewed coffee might commingle with the grounds before exiting. If you do opt to remove the innards before pouring your first cup of joe, be careful, because they're metal and freaking hot, and tough to grab. So, get some tongs if you don't have any. That said, if you look past the gripes and know what you're getting into this is probably a solid product, which is why I gave it four stars.

title: No longer drinking plastic from POD coffee maker.
body: I'm using this aluminum coffee pot & gave away my coffee POD machine. I no longer wanted to use plastic with hot water for my coffee. Counter space about the same as POD machine, but shorter, nicer looking. Cheaper to use ground coffee instead of the PODs. Brews several cups at one time. I then put brewed coffee in a thermos & unplug the coffee maker. I like the taste better than the PODs & can adjust the strength easily just by adding more or less ground coffee.

title: Simple to use.
body: This unit works well and I like that the basket does not have small holes that coffee collects in and closes. This basket has many small slots that the coffee drips through that do not clog. I wish it had a light to indicate that the perking is done but you can hear when it stops and don't forget to pull the plug out after use. I also fill to 12 cups and re-perk the next day to make a stronger cup of coffee. I call their 12 cup more like 3 or 4 of my idea of a cup of coffee. Easy cleaning is also an attribute of this unit.

title: I WISH IT HAD AUTO-SHUT OFF
body: THE ONLY COMPLAINT IS THERE IS NO AUTO SHUT-OFF. THIS WAS PURCHASED AS AN ALTERNATIVE TO USING A REGULAR COFFEE POT WITH PLASTIC. THE COFFEE TASTES FRESHER AND CLEANER BUT I REALLY THINK AN AUTO SHUT-OFF SHOULD BE MANDATORY.

title: Pot
body: No light to show done brewing Feels thin & " cheap"

title: No auto shutoff
body: Ok, it's a good coffee maker, I bought it because I wanted to get away from my old coffee maker that has plastics in it. I wanted a complete stainless steel coffee maker, and I thought this would be a good choice. It is all stainless steel, it does make good coffee, easy to clean, keeps the coffee hot .....But as I learned a lesson today, there's no automatic shut off. So if you forget to unplug it the pot keeps staying hot, which is ok if your at home, and want another cup of hot coffee an hour or two later. But if you go out somewhere and forget to unplug it, you could have a problem, even fire. So listen up Farberware, install auto shut off switch to be safe. I'll use it until I can find a stainless steel replacement with auto shut off. That's why 3 stars.

title: Meh
body: I had a Faberware 12 cup perc years ago that made wonderful coffee. (I also have a 48 cup Faberware coffee urn that makes the most delicious coffee ever.) Since I no longer have the 12 cup, I purchased the 8 cup in hopes of having the same euphoric experience but it was not to be. Very disappointed. Coffee was too strong/bitter and pretty much undrinkable. Could be the quality of coffee these days, too. Seems all we get are varying degrees of blah, and left with memories of what was. In any case, Faberware (made in China) is extremely over priced, and leaves me sadly disappointed and unimpressed. Back to my Keurig. Sigh.

title: Great coffee maker
body: Love this device love that it is all Steele

title: Check the plastic for defects
body: Love my Farberware coffee pot. But as I looked at it closer the plastic on the bottom rim where the Farberware brand is it's not smooth. Will probably have to return it

title: Disappointed!
body: I bought this Farberware 12 cup coffeemaker in November 2024. I wanted to love it, but it’s finicky. Some days it perks well and I see steam coming out of the spout. Other days it doesn’t and the coffee tastes watered-down, even though I measure the same amount of water, 4 cups, and 4 scoops of coffee using a coffee scoop. It uses twice as much coffee as my old drip maker used. Therefore, I am going through a 45 oz. container of coffee in no time. I wouldn’t mind if it was consistently good, but it isn’t. Has anyone had a similar problem?

title: Good percolator
body: We love this percolator works well don't need filters coffee taste good automatic shut off in about 5 minutes the only thing is the cord is to short all in all very good buy thank you

title: Makes great coffee, but maybe too hot
body: This percolator design is great! The lid for the basket stays secure during brewing so that coffee grounds don't float out of the top like some other brands. However, it gets 4 stars because I've noticed that it seems like the pot keeps the coffee so hot that it simmers or boils after the brewing process, which really isn't ideal for maintaining the quality of the coffee. That being said, if you unplug it quickly after percolating process is done, it stays warm for a long while and won't do as much simmering.

title: Still the best!
body: I had a farberware percolator for 20 plus years then it quit working so when I looked into getting another I was like "ouch" on the price so I bought a different one... suffered with that for a year (using a net strainer to pour each cup because of the amount of coffee grains). 😕 Finally went back to Farberware and it doesn't have the glass top to see the perc or the long cord like my last one but still it makes the hottest, richest, smoothest pot of coffee with no floating grounds!(Put away the strainer for good) Honestly Farberware is the best brand for coffee percolators! Enjoying a cup right now!😋☕

title: Use with Caution
body: Be very careful when you remove the lid off the pot to remove the coffee grounds basket after percolating. The lid is very difficult to open. I did scald myself when I tried to open it the first time, and I had burns that I had to treat for a couple weeks on my arm and chest. The lid is set onto the pot so tightly that as you use force to remove it the pot jolts and the coffee splashes back. I have managed to hold the pot handle tight enough and keep the pot far enough away from me to allow any splash-back to be away from my body. I have not been able to eliminate it completely when opening the lid. Operation: You have to listen for the pot to know perking is complete as there is not a light indication. I believe there is a beep, but you have to be near the pot it to hear the it. It makes good coffee in a timely manner. I use a strainer when I pour the coffee to catch excess grounds but there are few. I love the 8-cup size that is difficult to find. Overall, I can't recommend this coffee pot because I feel there is a safety danger when removing the lid. If not for that, I'd give it Four Stars, taking one off for no light indicating the coffee is ready. I would return the item, but I didn't expect a problem from a Faberware product and discarded the box.

title: Love everything but the handle
body: This percolator pot makes great coffee. My only dissatisfaction is the handle. It is thin, and when the pot is full at 12 cups, it is hard to hold on with one hand. Would like a wider handle for gripping.

title: Gourmet Coffee Every Time
body: I bought the 12-cup Coffee pot, although I only make coffee for myself. The attractiveness of the 12 cup impressed me. I make only 6 cups of coffee by filling with water to the 6 cup line. The lines are on the backside, or the handle side on the interior, and are hard to read. Put six Tablespoons of coffee in the basket (3 coffee measures.) Plug it in and in a very few moments, some of the best coffee I have ever tasted. For me, the 12 cup pot is heavy to lift but I’m an advanced-aged, small woman. The cord is very short, no on-off switch. Love this percolator.

title: Great coffee maker
body: We have been using the percolator for almost a month and we love it. The coffee tastes so much better than our old drip coffee maker. Percolators take up less counter space. I also like have a detachable cord. Very happy with this purchase.

title: A classic
body: Nice percolator! It is old school, so I had to get used to unplugging it when the coffee was gone, but even then, after forgetting a few times, it still worked great. It's space saving, made without any plastic on the inside, and looks lovely sitting on my countertop!

title: Fits all needs, whether in the sink or on a mat!
body: This drain fit my needs perfectly. From either sitting on a drying mat with the spout going over the sink or to sitting inside the right tub of my split sink, which fits perfectly by the way. The water drains great out of the drip pan. There may be a slight issue with the notches cut in the utensil attachment which causes draining issues, but other than that, it works like a charm.

title: Glasses and dishes drying rack
body: I like this because it has a drain that if you put the rack close to your sink it will drain most of the water out but not all so I have to lift up the rack after all my dishes have been in there for a while and the water will completely come out of the bottom because you don't want water sitting in the bottom of your dish rack, I think it would have been a superior wreck had they made this to where it was higher on one side and lower on the other to where all the water drained out so you didn't have to lift up the wreck other than that I think it's okay but not great

title: Sink Buddy

title: Think about the size

title: Best in sink rack that I found and reasonably priced.

title: I hate messy kitchens

title: Overall a great rack that’s minimal
body: I recently got this dish rack, and I’ve got to say, it’s a solid addition to my kitchen! The sizing is a bit small, but honestly, it’s perfect for minimizing the number of dirty dishes piling up in the sink. It encourages me to wash up right away instead of letting things stack up. As for assembly, it was super easy—no complicated steps or tools required! I also love the little drain spout underneath; it really does a great job of draining water away, keeping everything nice and tidy. One tip: I recommend putting some type of resistant material underneath the rack to prevent it from sliding around. It helps keep everything in place while I’m loading and unloading. Overall, I definitely recommend this dish rack if you're looking for something compact and efficient!

title: Efficient drying
body: This drying rack is sleek, modern, and easy to use. The adjustable arms keep it in place over the sink or you can put it on top of the plastic base to use beside your sink. I love that the solid plastic rack has a movable spout to drain excess water into the sink. And the silverware holder on the main rack is removable if you need extra drying space. The one thing I would change would be to have built in rubber feet on the base of the plastic rack. They tend to fall off when moving the rack, which means they are easy to lose.

title: Nice, but a few flaws...
body: Am (mostly) happy with this; it's aesthetically pleasing. A bit small, but functional. My 2 concerns: The bottom mat should be angled slightly towards the drain, it's not entirely efficient. And, sadly, the drain holes on the silverware tray are only on one side. I have the tray set on the other side of the rack, so that it tilts away from those holes... and no water drains. Every few days, I remove the silverware tray and drain it manually. Otherwise, it's good enough.

title: Slides but nice
body: 4 rather than 5 stars only because the 4 feet don’t have any rubber so as to “stick” to the counter. It slides. If that’s what you want, then good for you, you’ll like it!

title: Decent
body: Great dish drying rack. Good size for a small area like an apartment counter. I think the drain mechanism could be a bit better ( my counter gets wet) but otherwise its a good product.

title: Better quality than what ive seen in stores lately
body: Nice black color, appears to be made well, and does exactly what is described. Only downside is its a little smaller than I had in mind...this is likely my own fault for not paying attention to the dimensions listed.

title: Perfect in Every Way!
body: Excellent dishrack at a good price. I live in a log home and it fits right in like it belongs. No issues whatsoever.

title: The best one to get

title: Great for Small Kitchens, But Check the Size First
body: This dish rack is a great space-saving solution for smaller kitchens, offering a sturdy and well-designed structure that holds dishes securely. The rust-resistant stainless steel construction ensures durability, while the silicone feet provide excellent stability to prevent slipping. The drainage system is efficient, directing water straight into the sink, which helps keep countertops dry. The detachable cutlery holder is a useful feature, making it easy to organize utensils, and the overall sleek black design blends seamlessly with most kitchen aesthetics. Despite its durability and smart design, the capacity might be a drawback for larger households. While it comfortably holds standard plates and a few cups, bigger cookware like woks or pasta plates may not fit as easily. The drainage spout is a nice touch, but some users might find it a bit short, requiring strategic placement near the sink. Additionally, while assembly is effortless, the lack of snap-on features for the cutlery holder and main rack means it doesn’t store as compactly when not in use. For those needing a compact and sturdy dish rack with efficient drainage, this is a solid option. It holds up well over time, resists rust, and remains stable on the counter. However, if you frequently wash large dishes or need more drying space, a bigger model might be a better fit. Overall, it delivers excellent value for the price and is a practical choice for smaller kitchens or those looking to keep their counters clutter-free.

body: There are many other great reviews but I just wanted to add my take on just a few of it’s greatest features (comparing to numerous other coffee warmers in the past years—all of which I got frustrated with). First, it has a glass resting plate! With a little wipe it goes back to perfectly new looking-all my others were tacky looking in a month. The hottest setting really does reheat—not instantly but in about 10 minutes. The timer to turn off actually does work!! It is easy to turn on but does not turn on just with a little bump/touch like some—I almost had a fire with one coffee warmer because a cloth napkin was laying partially on the warmerand thus turned it on. If you want to heat up a cup that is cooled off, put it at 167° or 185°--in just a couple of minutes, it will be very hot again. body: Tired of nuking my mugs of coffee 2 times before finishing, I purchased a mug that keeps your coffee temperature consistent from the first to last sip. It was amazing… for 3 months. Back to the big box store with their unbeatable return policy. Now spoiled, I started looking for an alternative. I’ve always thought coffee warmers were gimmicky. I saw the KitchekShop reviews and number 1 best seller spot and thought I would give it a try. It actually works very well. You do, however need a flat-bottomed mug, that’s not double insulated. They’re not that easy to find. I wish they would charge $5 more and include a basic mug. I currently see they have “bundles” but the mugs aren’t for me as I am not the “best grandpa ever.” As for the warmer itself, it’s good. The only drawback is that it’s not really portable. If you move around a lot, you might end up back at the microwave. If you drink your coffee in one spot, like your desk, it’s perfect. It gets pretty hot so beware of accidently burning yourself, pets, children, etc. If you’re a hoarder don’t buy it (or, probably anything else)! I read lots of reviews on this warmer before purchasing and a lot of people are having problems with these melting and burning their desk , tables..etc. Watch my included video. I have had a few Mug Warmers and not one really kept my coffee very warm or hot. I really liked the look of this one and the fact that it could go up to 185 Degrees. One of the things I loved when buying this was that it showed a very large and vibrant digital read out. Well, that was my first disappointment. The digital read out is very small compared to the photo and nowhere near as bright as in the photo. I will say I do love that this can keep my coffee extremely hot. I have decided on the 145 Degree setting as my default. It keeps my coffee in my mug very hot. The 167 and 185 Degree settings make it to hot. That being said the plastic shell or this warmer gets extremely hot and the bottom gets scary hot. I can see why many reviewers burned their desk top. This is also probably the reason for many saying the warmer did not last long before it would no longer get hot. I put a silicone trivet under it and that helped with the heat transfer to the desk top. But, I was still worried about how hot the warmer itself was getting. I purchase some rubber feet here on Amazon. They are 1/2" Diameter and 1/4" Tall. I stuck them to the bottom of the existing mug warmer feet. Now between those rubber feet and the silicone trivet my desk top only gets slightly warm. The heat build up on the unit is now less also. That extra 1/4" really helps with the heat. I went to the web site listed in the instructions on my PC and registered for the 2 year warranty. I will update my review if I have any problems. I know I should not have to modify or adapt a product to work properly and obviously they are having some issues with these. But ,if the small modifications make this unit last then it is well worth it for the hottest mug warmer I have ever had. I would have given it 5 Stars if it had the large digital read out as pictured.

title: Works great! No disappointment here!
body: Well, I've only had this thing for one day but I just had to go ahead and write a review. Most people think that I like my hot beverages way too hot. Most people tell me they'd have to wait for their hot beverage to cool down before they could even try to drink it if it were the temperature I like to drink my hot drinks at. That being the case, I was concerned that this mug warmer would not be able to actually deliver the $185° temperature it advertises and keep my drink as hot as I like it for hours. I was wrong! I sat for over an hour with my beverage on the warmer taking a sip every once in a while intentionally dragging out finishing the drink. From the first sip, which I waited for 15 minutes after setting it on the hot plate to take, down to the last bit in the bottom of the mug, my drink was hot, hot, hot! Every bit of the temperature I wished for it to be from top to bottom. I did not expect it to actually perform that well. The unit is extremely easy to use. Plugged it in, turned it on, selected the highest heat setting and set my freshly poured hot cup of tea on the hot plate. As soon as I was done with my cup I pressed the power button again and turned it off. Obviously, it's going to take a while for it to cool down and so if you plan to take this out to use it and then put it back or store it in something after you're done, you're going to need to allow for time to let it cool. But anyone who sees that as a drawback doesn't know how the world works. I bought this on Prime Day so it was about half price or at least that's what they claimed. But buying it at less than $20, if it doesn't crap out on me anytime soon, is an absolute amazing deal! I will come back and edit my review if it doesn't last long because I can imagine that would be one of the only or likely the only thing I'd have to complain about. But if it continues on like this I will have become a very happy customer!

Looks decent and I'm happy with them. I did add some screws today just for a little warm and fuzzy added comfort. The base is designed to resist coming loose with downward pressure but if you push "up" they will pop free at the back end with very little effort if they are mounted vertically (hanging). That will depend a bit on the surface it's applied to of course. Not made to do chin ups on but adding screws makes them that much more secure and not sure how they will behave mounted to a wall. Using as a dish towel holder you're going to be banging it and bumping it regularly so I would highly recommend securing it with screws if that's how you're going to use it. They give you anchor screws and two extra adhesive pads so you can move them around a few times or take them with you if you move. One thing to note is the post may not be perfectly parallel/square to the base so if you do mount them like I did it may standout and drive the perfectionist in you bonkers. You get what you pay for. Unlike the original Miele bags, the generic version doesn't have the same self-sealing mechanism, which means dust and debris tend to spill out when I try to dispose of it. title: Miele rocks
body: I've owned a Miele for a few years, and while it sounds crazy to sing the praises of a vacuum cleaner, I must. I originally got it because I was sick of the jet-engine, ear-piercing sound of cheaper canister vacs - I love how quiet it is. Over the years I am continually amazed at how stuffed the bag can get with no reduction in suction - believe it or not (because I've never had the bag-change warning light go off either), I get reminded to change the bag because I sense the vacuum is heavier than normal ! When I do, the bag is always so stuffed it is hard to remove - yet it can be removed without emitting any dust or debris,or tearing, like paper bags. AND, as I said, it still has great suction in such a state. All in all, just a fantastic piece of engineering - albeit a pricey one. I bought a Miele dishwasher because I was so impressed with the vacuum, and that has been a joy as well. Essentially silent, and cleans everything much better than its predecessors - I never even knew how much cleaner and spot-free things could be (I'm in NYC with great water supply - no need to use its built-in salt water softening feature). And it's an 18" model, to fit my apartment. Holds an amazing amount.

title: Love the Bottle, Not the Lid
body: I bought the 32 oz black water bottle, and it shipped quickly, which was great. But less than two weeks in, the lid snapped. My husband was working in the kitchen, went to take a sip, and the lid (with the straw) just broke off. That alone tells me this thing isn’t the most durable. I reached out to support to ask if I could buy a replacement lid. To their credit, support was super fast, I appreciated that. What bugged me, though, was it felt like they were trying to find a reason not to help. They asked if we had dropped it, if we’d damaged it, and even pointed out that there was dust on the bottle and asked if it had been taken to work or used in a similar environment. Like… it’s a water bottle. It’s supposed to go places. And no, we hadn’t taken it to work, it was dusty because it was the weekend and we were polishing new countertops. lol Anyway, despite all of that, they did let me know that they would send a replacement lid, which I appreciated, especially since I’d barely had the bottle. They even followed up with a picture showing the delivery date. I actually got it a day later than estimated, no big deal, and surprise, instead of just a lid, they sent me a whole new bottle (a size smaller, but still). Outside of the lid breaking, the bottle itself is great. It keeps water cold all day and does its job well. Just hoping the replacement holds up a little better.

title: Love exists - and it's in this water bottle
body: This bottle is PERFECT. The 26oz size is like Goldilocks' chair - not too big, not too small; It fits snug in my backpack side pocket, and the cupholder in my car. I also love the option of the straw and spout; for the price-point this was the perfect bottle, not many others I found had both options and were as well-reviewed. And the handle? Don't even get me started, it's perfect. I hate those bottles that have the fixed plastic handle, they always cramps my fingers - this one is a rubbery, ergonomic blessing. Although, the size of this bottle also fits perfectly in my hand, so I probably wouldn't even need it anyway. The outside material is also very nice, not slippery like some of my hydroflasks. The pink is also sooo pretty! I also always test the efficacy of insulated bottles, and this one passed with flying colors; I filled it up with ice cubes and water and forgot about it on my nightstand, two days later I go to dump it out, and (almost) ALL the ice cubes were still in-tact. I'm sure if I kept it in the refrigerator, it would've been days until they completely melted. To test the heat retention, I put some tea in it, and it stayed the SAME TEMP for the hours it took me to drink it! The only drawback I might think of would be ease of cleaning for the underside of the cap, since there are a few nooks and crannies I couldn't get with my scrubber, but I'm sure a good soak, rinse, and dry will be just fine for prevention of bacteria buildup. It's also hand-wash only, but I prefer that for product longevity. The bottle also comes with a lifetime warranty (at least at the time of my purchase) TL;DR, super impressed by this bottle for the $13 I paid for it. Keeps cold drinks cold, keeps hot drinks hot. Fits in the cupholder, slim profile, comfy handle, great spout and straw option.

title: A must-have when your dryer is poorly designed and clogs itself
body: My terrible LG dryer that came with the house requires a vac attachment like this, because it is terribly designed (like many other LG products I've dealt with over the years), and at least ten percent of the lint goes past the filter and into the tight spaces of the dryer. This attachment gets where it needs to go, and pulls out the mess for me with limited effort. I often find other clean-up jobs where this attachment saves me a lot of hassle as well. I actually purchased this to replace one from the same manufacturer that I bought years ago but ended up breaking. I'm not going to blame the manufacturer for that old one breaking, as I used it for more than the intended purpose and definitely stepped on it and did other things that damaged it. This new one seems a bit more flexible than the old one and actually fits better inside my dryer's lint trap area. The rubber "adapter" on this is also better for my Shark rocket than the old one was. I can simply put a "crevice tool" on the end of the Shark and put it into the adapter, instead of having to attach a round-ended hose to the Shark in order to get it to attach.

title: Deep Cleaning Removal of Lint From Gas or Electric Clothes Dryers
body: This vacuum attachment works very well to get the lint out of my gas dryer. The attachment wand allows the suction to reach the bottom of the vent system where the extraction motor is located. It was a yearly job to take the front lower panel off the gas dryer and remove the front of the extraction motor inlet housing to get the lint out. Now I can do deep cleaning after every load. An electric dryer would benefit even more from deep cleaning removal of lint.

title: good for corded vacuums
body: I have an Amana brand washer and dryer (side note: they suck, don’t ever buy Amana). I always clean the vent after each time of using the dryer, but lint falls down into the deep deeeeeeep crevices that are impossible to clean or reach without some type of extender. I got this because the lint build up was finally getting to the point of needing to be cleaned out. I have 2 vacuums to start. I typically using my cordless vacuum as it’s just easier to get around, so I tried that first. Bad idea. The hose fit on easily but it turned my vacuum into a tornado, or so it sounded. I have no idea why but it made my cordless vacuum go nuts. It sounded like it was going to catch on fire, its suctioning volume was insanely loud. So I wouldn’t recommend using it on a cordless vacuum. I tried it on my older corded vacuum, I’m lucky I kept that thing now. Worked perfect, 10/10. The hose fit on it great, and it got about 90% of the lint out of the deep crevices.

title: Good cleaning accessory

It could go inside the vent without any difficulty and I was able to connect it to the suction unit without any issue. I regularly clean the vent filter after every load. However this tubing made it easy to clean further. The brush is additional help to loose the lint sticking to the sides and bottom of the vent. Overall, it is a good buy. title: Kind of useless

Maybe it’s the design of my dryer, but all I could get to was the area that the lint screen fits into. I could see into that recess where it exited to go to the internal port of the dryer and then out to the vent, but it was a hard 90° at the bottom corner of said very narrow slot. There was no way to get the brush or vacuum nozzle to make that turn, so all I could clean was the lint screen’s “home”. title: Why did I wait so long? This thing works!
body: I love this thing! Who knew? And I got it for less than $10 - worth every penny plus more. I have had this in my shopping list for months and months. It went on sale so I decided to order it, not expecting much. And really, when you open the package, it doesn't look like much, just some rubber or plastic looking parts and a big long brush. I thought, meh, I'm underwhelmed. But boy does it do the job! I was impressed. The brush, I am not sure about as much - it does loosen things but dust becomes stuck to the bristles and is difficult to clean and it just now occurs to me that I could have vacuumed it! ha! But the vacuum part is awesome. I attached it to the tube of my old upright vacuum that has a lot of power behind it - easy to do. First you attach the two (or three) rubber/plastic parts together, and then push the bigger end onto the vacuum tube - give it a little force if you have too, it'll be fine. I stuck it down the vent trap and up came all this fuzz. Now, I clean out my trap every single load of laundry no matter how small: every.single.time. And still this pulled up so much lint! Dang! I then took it outside and suctioned out the outside vent - lots came out of that too. Take a look inside your vacuum and see what has been hanging out in your dryer vent - lots of lint - and for me, lots of lint from many years of never vacuuming it out. Dang! Note that if the suction isn't as powerful to check to be sure there isn't some lint clogging the rubber/plastic tube-it'll clear out easily. Also note that according to how powerful your vacuum is, that will determine of course the power of the suction, but once it is concentrated in that tube, it creates a big suction. I used a power cord vacuum as those are usually more powerful than the rechargeable ones. The amount of lint that came of of that was eye-opening. I had no idea. I found other uses for it - I vacuumed out my old baseboard heating vents that I usually have to clean with a rag and it was always a pain - this fit in there easily and went to town. I also stuck it under my washer, dryer, refrigerator, and stove and moved it all around to vacuum up whatever may be under there - dust bunnies or when I drop dog food or nuts or something and it rolls under the fridge. The flat part is flat enough and flexible enough to get under there whereas the vacuum attachment was not. This would vacuum tight areas/corners or baseboards or between furniture cushions. Maybe my wood blinds. I am so pleased with this I only wish I'd ordered it sooner!

title: The Best Cheap Gooseneck You'll Find
body: I purchased this kettle to use primarily as a "gets the job done" kettle for my office coffee setup. I am serious about my coffee and have used more premium kettles such as the Hario gooseneck and the Fellow Stagg EKG. The Fellow is my go-to at home, but I didn't want to spend $150 again, so I purchased this Bodum kettle. My review of this product is at least somewhat informed by comparing its performance to more expensive products like the Fellow Stagg EKG. First, I want to address the leaking/steam valve issue that many other reviewers have complained of. In some photos I saw of this product before purchasing it, there was a plastic cap on the steam valve, but there was no plastic cap on mine. Bodum seems to have updated that part to a metal thingy that is, I hope, a lot more literal-fool-proof than whatever plastic piece they were using before. I took some pictures and added them to this review. To clarify: this kettle does not leak if you do not overfill it. If you fill it up to the fill line like a sane person, you will have a problem-free water boiling experience. Its design is in no way defective, and I have been using it several times per day for a few weeks now with absolutely zero leaking issues. It would probably leak if I filled it way past the line, but any kettle-- including the Stagg and other pricier options, as I've witnessed firsthand-- will leak through the lid holes if overfilled. Pour rate and quality: Before getting to the Bodum, I want to mention the speed of the pour for the other kettles I've owned. The Fellow Stagg EKG pours at a rate that I can only describe as glacially slow-- water comes out of it in a very slow and controlled drip, which is nice for pour-over coffee but feels ridiculous when pouring a lot of water at once, such as for French press or tea. On the other hand, my Hario kettle pours much faster, but it still allows for some control. So, if those are the ends of the spectrum, then this kettle from Bodum kettle pours quickly, at a rate that is most like the Hario and is honestly more pleasurable to use than the Stagg. I suspect it agitated the coffee bed more, even if the stream doesn't feel as delicate or controlled as the Stagg. The water stream produced by the Bodum is steady and does not break up or dribble, even when pouring from a height of several inches. Really, by all objective measures such as this, the Bodum's performance rivals that of any higher-end offerings. When filled to capacity with room temperature water, it boils in about 5 and a half minutes. Really, my only qualms with this kettle are with the cork on the lid and handle. They feel expectedly flimsy, but as other reviewers have said, I'm optimistic that they could be replaced with a drawer knob or something when-- definitely when, not if-- they break. When I'm buying in this price range, it's definitely not something I can really fault Bodum for. This kettle also does feel a bit wobbly on the base, but only in the way of a table with a slightly short leg. The base is plastic and feels sort of cheap, because it is. Does that matter? Again, in this price range, I don't think it does. In all the ways that count, this kettle functions identically to higher-end, pricier kettles. It's annoying to clean and has flimsy handles. The cord is short. It doesn't heat up with turbo speed or hold a ton of water. But so what? For less than $30, nothing will give you a good and controlled pour, a quick boil, and neat design. UPDATE (April 2023): I've had this kettle for over a year now, and I'm still immensely pleased with it. The cork on the lid and handle is still holding up well-- honestly, it's still like new-- after daily use. It hasn't started to rust on the inside or anything. It's still in perfect shape; I'm honestly impressed. I have experienced the issue where water leaks out of the bottom a handful of times, but I think I've discovered what causes this: the mechanism that automatically turns off the kettle once it starts to boil is seemingly triggered by steam, and if I attempt to turn it back on to maintain boiling or if I reheat more water a few times in a row, the steam causes enough condensation buildup around the switch that some of the droplets come out. I don't think this is "leaking" at all; if anything, this is really my fault for trying to push the kettle beyond the scope of what the manufacturer intended.

body: When it came down to Fellow's Stagg or Bodum, I went with Bodum because I didn't need Precise Temperature Control. Using it 2 times a day for a week now, heats up within 2-3 minutes, very happy with the purchase.

title: Beautiful!
body: Not only is this kettle beautiful in person but it gets hot very fast and it's not too big. I'm very pleased with this purchase!

title: Second Updated Review after less than a year of use. Not Happy! >: (
body: My Mom has this electric water kettle in black and I was very impressed with it so I decided to get one for my kitchen. I got mine in chrome. It heats up water super quick so no need to use the stove top or microwave to heat up water for my hot chocolate/tea. It's very well designed and looks great on the counter. The only "criticism" I have is that the electric cord is kind of thick and stiff, but I suppose that is for safety reasons. There is a MAX line inside the kettle so don't fill water beyond that. If you need more water, just heat up some more. It really doesn't take that long. I read a couple reviews about concerns with the cork details but so far I have not had any issues with it. UPDATED REVIEW - November 20, 2024 I have owned this electric kettle for less than a year and already it is broken. VERY, VERY disappointed since I really loved its ease of use. I don't use this kettle a lot since it's mostly for heating up water for hot chocolate in the colder months. Well, I just started using it consistently again and the little pop-up button no longer pops up to stop the water from boiling. I thought it was just a fluke so the next day I used it again and the same thing happened. The water continues to boil since the button does not pop up. Grrr! And to top things off, now the kettle is leaking water from the bottom! (And no, I did not overfill the kettle). This kettle has gone from a great product to a huge disappointment and a potential safety hazard. I am way past the return window so the money I spend on this kettle is now down the drain. I am going to see if I can contact the seller but I am not holding out any hope. I have changed my star rating to 2 Stars. If I can contact the seller and get a satisfactory solution, I will change my star rating. For now I am a VERY upset and disappointed customer!! SECOND UPDATED REVIEW - November 22, 2024 I was unable to contact Bodum on my own since there was not a "Contact Seller" option on the Amazon product description. I decided to chat with an Amazon Cust Service rep. I explained the problem with the kettle hoping for a replacement. The rep gave me the phone # and website for Bodum to get help with the kettle replacement since it is still under warranty. I called Bodum but no one was answering the phone, so I emailed them a detailed description of the kettle's malfunction. I NEVER heard back from Bodum. Not even an acknowledgement that they received my email. Today, I decided to contact Amazon Cust Service again to see if they could reach out to Bodum on my behalf. The first rep did not offer to do that for me. He transferred me to another dept. The next two reps that I chatted with abruptly left the chat due to "technical difficulties." The fourth and last rep I chatted with finally offered to issue me a refund/return. I really just wanted a replacement kettle but that was not an option. The rep sent me an email with the UPS QR code that stated the amount of my refund. Only after I gave the kettle to UPS to send back to Amazon, did I receive another email stating that there would be an $8 restock fee!!!!!! This was not mentioned to me by the Amazon Rep!!! My question is, why am I being charged a restock fee for an item that is clearly damaged and will not be restocked??? It is going into the landfill. I am very disappointed in Amazon for not making this fee clear, and thus reducing my refund amount. I have changed my star review from 5 stars to 1 star. Very disappointed in Bodum, and now Amazon Customer Service for not disclosing the restock fee.

title: Start of Day, evening comfort
body: Love, very nice for a breakfast nook or neeakfast bar. Use almost daily.

title: Amazing product for an amazing price!
body: Great design. Works well; it boils water quickly. Very easy to pour from because of the gooseneck spout design. Amazing price compared to others. It is a little hard to clean because the opening is so small but since I only ever use it to boil water, it doesn’t really need that much cleaning.

title: No nonsense, just works as advertised
body: I bought this kettle 4 years ago and have used it almost everyday once or twice. To begin with the good part, the kettle is very easy to use and just works. It boils the water quickly and cuts off. The lid is insulated enough to hold the water warm for up to 30 minutes. The neck and the handle gives enough balance to control the pour, which is perfect for brewing coffee. Now, coming to the bad, the kettle's switch just broke off today for no apparent reason. However, given that it is after 4 years, I am willing to give it a pass. While, the kettle's neck has a slow pour which is desirable for brewing coffee, while emptying the kettle, it takes a longer time. I wish that there was some way to empty the kettle more easily. Cleaning the lime build on the inside with a brush is also easy. Overall, a decent purchase if you just a need a kettle that works for a few years.

title: A terrific kettle at a great price
body: I love this kettle, and IMHO it is by far the best thing at this price point, and also better than some considerably more expensive models. I actually bought another, more expensive one that had temp control to compare the two, and I ended up sending the other one back. This little gem looks better, heats up just as quickly, and my blind tasting of coffee brewed at the two different temps (ie. boiling for this one, and 203 for the other one) yielded no difference whatsoever. It's simple, petite, and holds enough water to make coffee for two, or possibly three if you're doing smaller cups. Although I was initially enticed by features that veri-temp models offer (like holding the temperature, etc), I realized that in reality I don't actually need any of those. I mean really, why do I want to keep my water at a certain temperature for an extended period of time when it takes only moments to reheat anyway? Also I really like the simplicity and elegance of the aesthetic. The only thing I'd love more is if it came in some fun colors.

title: Precise, fast, and perfect for real coffee — even at work
body: I use the Bodum 27oz Bistro Gooseneck Electric Kettle in my office setup alongside a ZERO JAPAN ceramic dripper and a MAXUS digital scale, because average coffee just isn't acceptable — even during work hours. This kettle heats up fast, holds a steady pour, and feels balanced in the hand, which makes a huge difference when you’re aiming for a proper pour-over and not just dumping water on beans. Clean, simple, and reliable — exactly what I need to keep standards high even when everything else is chaotic.

title: Cute, compact, fast, great
body: Great overall. I searched for an electrice kettle that had no major plastic components other than the base. Only docking a star because the lid handle is a little less sturdy than I'd like. I can see it breaking eventually. The handle angle was a little weird, so I carefully bent it downward a bit -- do so at your own risk. Worth the purchase.

title: A Tea Lovers Kettle!
body: The Bodum 27oz Bistro Gooseneck Electric Water Kettle, Pour Over Coffee & Tea, Stainless Steel, Matte Black kettle is the best little water kettle we have found. The water is heated to 200 degrees Fahrenheit in just a minute or so. The Gooseneck pours the water out very well and is perfect for covering Tea in a defuser to steep in your cup. The most impressive thing is that the kettle is warm on the sides while the water temperature is Hot but the base is cool to the touch. You can set it on a table or counter without any damage to the surface. It is a great value and serves our needs quite well. The Black color goes well with our other appliances in our kitchen.

title: This is the second one we bought....
body: We got one as a gift for someone last year. We went to their house and they made us tea. This kettle heats water so fast and pours amazingly well. It's so cute, and doesn't take up room on the stove. Very easy to use. PROS: Excellent pour, heats up really fast, easy to use, very easy to clean, very pretty statement piece. CONS: there is no SOUND to indicate your tea water is ready. The on tab just "clicks" off. Also the light is not on the tab its located around the side, which is a little confusing as you can't tell right away it's on/off, started/done. On a redesign I would change it to have a little bell indicator or something and ensure the light is where you would expect it to be. Overall it's great, a good price, and gorgeous, works well.

title: Elegant, great price, easy care.
body: Elegant, fast and ergonomic. Glass kettles tend to break. This one is fantastic! Looks elegant at my home coffee station. The finish is oh so stylish and it heats water in a snap. I would say that if you're kind of a messy, carefree type this might not be the product for you. The handles are cork so if you tend to handle your kettle with dirty hands it might not be practical. If you have a stylish set up and are a regular hand washer or just generally a very neat person, this is the product for you. Looks great alongside Alessi, or other high end appliances. Can be minimal, modernist, midcentury, Japandi or eclectic. Elegant enough to serve in.

body: Heats water quickly. Fits nicely in my countertop.
