body: I don't know if the inside of this product is actually Stainless Steel because there is a familiar odor, that isn't present with stainless, but with other metals. I do like that it heats to boiling quickly, then shuts off. It is not silent, but it does the job as intended

title: Works as it should
body: We use this for pour-over coffee when traveling in our travel trailer. It heats water quickly and fits pretty much anywhere we have put it and looks nice when we leave it out. I took a star off (would be half a star off if I knew how to do that) due to the fact that it is not the easiest to clean but that could be due to the fact that none of us in this family have dainty hands. I use a bottle brush to clean but it still has spots that look like they are growing something. I do not think it is mold or rust but it has spots nonetheless. I have used vinegar and clean it often enough that I am not super concerned about it but others might be so I thought I’d add that part.

title: Quick heating and elegant design
body: I was very pleased with this kettle. I used it at least once a day for appx 1.5 years, until it developed a crack just below the spout, so I deducted a star. That said, I probably used it as much as an average coffee drinker would in 4 years.

title: One cup at a time perfection
body: I love this little thing for several reasons. First, and obviously, for making pour over coffee, yes, you can pour a big kettle slowly, but this makes it way easier to get an even pour. Get the bloom, then try to match the stream going in with the one going out of the funnel pour over thingy. Now for the extra bonus, it's quiet! I make a little cup every morning when my wife and children are asleep, this doesn't make a loud boiling sound, or a loud "click" or a beep like many kettles. Use it daily and love it!

title: Stopped working after 6 months.
body: I really like the size and function of this kettle. But I purchased it on November 28, 2024. It has stopped working today on 5/30/2025. I press the button and the kettle does not turn on to heat the water. I will contact Bodum support to get some assistance.

title: Bodum Gooseneck Electric Kettle: Enhancing Your Pour-Over Experienceour Pour-Over Experience
body: Let me introduce you to the Bodum Gooseneck Electric Kettle – the unsung hero of my morning routine. This sleek and efficient kettle has become an essential part of my coffee-making ritual, thanks to its ease of use and compatibility with my Bodum pour-over coffee maker. First and foremost, let's talk about simplicity. The Bodum Gooseneck Electric Kettle couldn't be easier to use. With just the flick of a switch, it quickly and efficiently boils water to the perfect temperature for brewing coffee or tea. The gooseneck spout allows for precise pouring, giving me complete control over the water flow as I saturate the coffee grounds in my pour-over cone. Speaking of pour-over coffee, this kettle is a match made in heaven for the Bodum pour-over coffee maker. The gooseneck spout provides the ideal flow rate for evenly saturating the coffee grounds, ensuring a consistent and flavorful brew every time. Whether I'm making a single cup or a full pot of coffee, the Bodum Gooseneck Electric Kettle delivers flawless results with minimal effort. However, if there's one flaw to note, it would be the size of the kettle. While it's perfectly adequate for everyday use, I sometimes find myself wishing it had a larger capacity to accommodate more water. This would be especially convenient when brewing multiple cups of coffee or when entertaining guests. Despite this minor drawback, the Bodum Gooseneck Electric Kettle remains a staple in my kitchen arsenal. Its ease of use, precise pouring capabilities, and compatibility with the Bodum pour-over coffee maker make it an indispensable tool for any coffee lover. Say goodbye to uneven pours and hello to perfectly brewed coffee with the Bodum Gooseneck Electric Kettle by your side.

title: Hot water leaking
body: I ordered this on April 29th and already hot water comes out the bottom all around the sides when I pour it into my coffee grounds. It hasn't even been a month yet. :(

title: PERFECT for 1 or 2!
body: FINALLY! I have tried and mostly burnt every type of whistling tea kettle out there. Every type! Every one! Although before I bought the last wonderful whistling tea kettle (stove-top) that I killed, I looked at electric tea kettles, but nothing struck me. Too large; Too much of an odor with others; Too fragile with others. I decided to look up electric kettles again and found this absolutely beautiful (IMO) item from Bodum -- a brand I know and trust. Their materials are exceptionally high quality for all of the things they produce. This is certainly no exception. It's solid and well constructed. It was packed beautifully -- cardboard mostly and it was neatly disassembled by me -- hardly any waste. I appreciate that. Then that first use: OMG I'm in love! It takes no time at all (5 minutes for a full kettle = 2 cups of tea easily), it is extremely quiet, and the turn on/off switch is simple. But you'd better listen for it to "pop" up or you'll have to reheat again, which will happen very quickly. The whole thing is no fuss/no muss. It pours beautifully. Every other kettle made me lift my elbow so high it was uncomfortable. Or the angle made it very awkward to pour the water. This one is PERFECT. I LOVE IT. So much. It's made making a second cup of tea so easy. This is the best thing since sliced bread, as they say. The black matte finish is gorgeous, wipes down easily, and has a lovely graceful low profile. I can't say how much I love everything! Except -- well, I'm going to call Bodum for some hints -- but I'm not sure how to "wipe the inside with a cloth" when I can't get my hand in; but I did push the towel in with a wooden spoon to make sure it was clean. It's been used SO MANY TIMES in these just 2 days but I still can't see any discoloration or mineral deposits yet. I'm not worried about cleaning it. This kettle is exactly what I've been looking for for years but didn't know it! So glad I found this Bodum product.

title: Wonderful kettle but it does leak
body: Love this kettle. It’s adorable and heats water quickly! But after a couple weeks water is now leaking out of the bottom. Not sure why. I have emailed the company just waiting on response.

title: 5 years later.....
body: I've been using this kettle several times a day for almost 5 years. It heats quickly and reliably. The cork handle is in very good condition. The cork on the lid is showing signs of wear but is still intact and complete. Paint is starting to chip or wear in a few places but not terribly considering it's age and constant use. It functions perfectly like new. I love that it is light weight and easy for me to handle with arthritic hands. I purchased a new glass kettle once just for the flashy looks and lights but ended up giving it away because of the heavy weight. Couldn't be happier with this kettle and will likely replace it with the same model when the time comes.

title: Just ok - be cautious!
body: I had for this for a few weeks and used it without issue. Recently it’s been leaking hot water from the bottom every once in a while after being heated. I always only heat enough water for one cup of coffee, so I don’t know what’s making it leak. Also be careful because if something even subtly brushes agains the little button that you press down to turn it on can easily accidentally be triggered. It’s happened more than once now that it heated up empty.

title: It's just right
body: I just got this, so I can't tell you how long it will last. It does have a 2 year warranty (you have to register for it). It has very clear and complete instructions, can't be put in the dishwasher or submerged in a sink full of water, etc. It holds a liter of water and has a "MAX" fill indicator inside the pot. It heats the water and automatically shuts off with a click (as opposed to my stove-top tea kettle's loud whistle). I made my pot of pour over coffee and it came out great! It fits nicely in the coffee corner of my kitchen and looks stylish. I like it!

title: ALMOST an awesome electric kettle
body: I’ll start with what I really liked: - simple, modern, clean design - heated VERY fast - good weight distribution; easy to pour fast or slow; comfortable handle Here’s what I didn’t love: - yes, it dribbles a few drops of water from the base - no, it didn’t pour water all over the place; anyone who says it did either received a defective unit, removed the plastic piece (that kinda seems like it’s for shipping and should be removed BUT DEFINITELY SHOULD NOT), or most likely, overfilled it - material was thin, would be easy to dent, felt cheaper than it looks (but to be fair it’s pretty light, made of stainless and still inexpensive so what can one expect?) - the screw from the lid to the cork top was tiny and flexed the very thin metal top - the most obvious physical weakness. A wider screw and a metal washer would’ve at least braced the weak point better - overall I didn’t think it would last forever, and eventually the black paint seemed like it might scratch away, but for the price, it seemed pretty good The dealbreaker: - the smell. It came with a not untypical, chemical smell once unboxed. I washed the insides with dish soap and gave it a good rinse. - first use: smelled terrible! Kinda like solvent / glue / plastic / bleach. Smelled inside the hot kettle = more concentrated than the bad smell in my kitchen. - boiled a mild citric acid solution, several times, then washed again. A little better, but not gone. - used for another week; still there, still an off flavor in my drinks - boiled white vinegar, several times, soap and water inside again. Still there. - gave it another week to off-has whatever it was. - not getting any better at this point, after using 3 times a day for 3 weeks. Sending back for a refund. Final take: From reading a bunch of reviews, most people had no problem with any off smells. Mine was pretty intense, something I would imagine most people couldn’t live with. So my guess is that the occasional unit is shipped with this issue. I would’ve just returned for a replacement, and hoped the next one wasn’t smelly. For the money, it works well, looks cool, and heats up super fast. But I found a crazy good price on a much more expensive adjustable temp gooseneck kettle and pulled the trigger on that instead. If you’re still reading this I’d recommend going for it - unless you’re ready to shell out considerably more for something nicer. My $.03

title: Exterior Not Heat Resistant Like Stainless Steel
body: Bodum kettle is decent. The description says made of attractive durable stainless steel, but that is partially misleading as the exterior is not heat resistant, and for that reason it may not be a good item to stock in an air b&b.

title: Kettle
body: Works great

title: Just about perfect for tea and pour over coffee
body: I've long been a fan of Bodum and their double wall glasses and coffee and tea gear. When our glass water kettle broke and we needed a new one, I saw that they had this lovely design in a long spout kettle. Be aware that it is kind of on the small side, it's only about a liter whereas our other one was close to 2 l. However that's just fine as it's a perfect size for doing a pour over where you don't want a big heavy kettle. Having the long goose deck spout really is better for pour over coffee. The cork handles are very nice touch. It's very simple you just push down a little mechanical lever to start it. Our other electronic kennel did have various settings for lower temperatures and this one does not have that, just "boil". I find that dark roast coffee likes a lower temperature water, so that is one slight drawback to this simple kettle.

title: Great kettle!
body: Love this! Use it daily, easy-fast-pours well. No worries about leaving it on. Holding up to daily use pretty well!

title: Decent, attractive, gooseneck kettle but absolutely NOT 1500 Watts
body: It's an electric kettle, there isn't a whole lot to say - it boils water. I was looking for a gooseneck design because it allows much more precise pouring for coffee or tea, liked the stainless steel, and the price was right so I gave it a shot. I found it very difficult to locate the wattage in the product info on the listing, which was frustrating since that's kind of the most important spec for an electric kettle I can think of... Only in Amazon's similar product comparisons is the wattage listed where it shows 1500 watts. A few days after ordering, open up the package and sure enough the product sticker and all included literature clearly show 1000 watts. I tested with a power meter and same result, 1000 watts. So this product is FALSELY advertising itself as 50% more powerful than it actually is. Buyer beware. Additional note of caution: because the body is uninsulated stainless steel, it gets extremely hot after a cycle, if you touch the metal cap while trying to remove it, you will burn yourself. Wait for it to cool down before attempting to take off the cap to clean out or dump the water. At the end of the day, am I pissed I was lied to in the listing? Absolutely. However, I think I paid around $30 and it still boils water, albeit slowly. So I'll accept its mediocre performance and try to focus on the fact that it looks great on my countertop. I'm writing this review to hopefully warn others of the wattage issue since I did not see anyone else mentioning it at all, which is very odd...

title: Yep, it leaks!
body: I love this black gooseneck because it is so elegant and I enjoy using it. Many other reviewers commented about how it leaks, which did not dissuade me from buying it, and after a few weeks I see that mine now does. Specifically, it leaks from the part of the kettle near where the gooseneck attaches, so when you go to pour it water comes out of both the spout and from near the base of the gooseneck. This is not a problem for me because when I do my pour-over coffee, I always use it over the kitchen sink. For others, it might be a problem. Since I wrote this review I have realized that the reason the water appears to leak from near the bottom of the gooseneck is because I am tipping the pot down on that side to pour the water and that is the lowest point. Who knows where the source of the leak actually is because I am just seeing the result.

title: Beautiful and Functional Countertop Piece
body: I recently upgraded my tea-making routine with Bodum’s Melior Gooseneck Electric Tea Kettle, and I'm thrilled with the results. This kettle combines precision and convenience in a sleek, modern design that has become an indispensable part of my daily life. The standout feature of this kettle is its precision pour. The gooseneck spout offers a controlled, steady flow of hot water, which is perfect for brewing a variety of teas, from delicate greens to robust black teas. It's a game-changer for tea enthusiasts who value the exact water temperature and brewing time. The convenience factor cannot be overstated. It is a time-saver and ensures that my tea is brewed to perfection every time. The kettle is durable, easy to clean, and the matte black finish adds a touch of elegance to my kitchen countertop. In addition to its tea-making capabilities, I've found this kettle to be versatile for other hot water needs, such as pour-over coffee, instant oatmeal, or even preparing hot water for cooking. It's a versatile kitchen appliance that serves multiple purposes. Overall, the Electric Gooseneck Tea Kettle has elevated my tea-drinking experience and simplified my daily routines. It's a reliable, well-designed addition to any kitchen, and I highly recommend it to fellow tea and coffee lovers who appreciate precision and convenience in their brewing process.

title: One year later..
body: It has been one full year since I purchased and began using this product. I am pleased to report that it is still in perfect, like-new condition. I de-lime it every couple weeks with just white vinegar and it shines inside again like new. The at first, worrisome cork cap is still fine and has not come off or deteriorated. I have used this kettle daily and am still very pleased with my purchase.

title: Exactly what I wanted
body: This electric kettle is replacing a Hot Shot hot water dispenser I've used religiously for more than 30 years. The Hot Shot was inexpensive, simple, and fast. Unfortunately, it's also now been discontinued. Although I was skeptical of the Bodum kettle after making tea the same way for decades, I have to admit it won me over very quickly. Just like with the Hot Shot, I pour in the exact amount of cold water I need (7 oz for a perfect cup of tea), it boils in just a couple minutes, and I pour the entire contents into my tea cup. Or if you drink multiple cups and/or have tea with guests you could just fill completely and dispense the hot water as needed as you would with a traditional teakettle. Simple, just like the trusty Hot Shot.

title: Is a 2 year life span ok?
body: Kettle was used daily, but after 2 years it stopped turning on. I would have liked a longer lifespan but perhaps at this price point this is as good as it gets?

title: Insights from 5 months of use
body: I have used this kettle twice daily since purchasing it late December 2021. It heats water quickly, in my subjective opinion. (I never use the microwave to heat water.) I did time the kettle once out of curiosity but, frankly, it seemed pointless. If life has reached down-to-the-minute timing, coffee or tea probably is not the wisest choice in a busy schedule. :) The kettle is solidly built. That said, I never lift the kettle by the goose-neck spout as that would weaken it over time, in my view. The cork handle stays cool and is durable (I had wondered about durability before the purchase.) When heating water for a pour-over coffee, I can tell by sound when the water is just before a boil. The sound of the water increases as it heats up, and then as it approaches boiling it begins to quiet down. For tea, I bring water to full boil and therefore appreciate the automatic shut-off with the kettle. It is also lovely that using the kettle does not heat up my kitchen in warmer weather like when I use a stove-top kettle. Before buying the kettle, I noticed all the kerfuffle in a number of reviews with concerns or questions about the small plastic piece placed over a metal tube inside the kettle. I am guessing the metal tube is a safety feature of some sort. Yes, it seems an odd choice for Bodum to have chosen a plastic piece inside a metal kettle. However, as you can see from the photo I attached, that piece is well above the "max" fill line (a metal tab). The plastic piece is not in contact with the water at any time. Overall, I am highly satisfied with the electric kettle and would recommend it to friends.

title: EZ To Use
body: Pretty simple in terms of a "how-to". Fill lines on the inside for those who can't measure properly. Theres a nifty safety feature that turns the boiling off when your water is ready to go - unlike other boilers that just make a scorched mess in your kitchen. The goose neck design offers consistent airflow for pour overs. The matte finish of the kettle itself ensures ease of cleaning. Overall pretty high quality.

title: There are better choices
body: Bought so that we could upgrade our pour-overs. The most bothersome aspect is that the cap on the kettle is cork and is very wiggly. It’s attached to the cap with a small screw that’s almost impossible to tighten. So, every morning is an exercise in frustration getting the cap on and off.

title: Had this thing for 4 years
body: Heats up super quick, shuts itself off automatically, no metallic taste which speaks to good quality, and the light isn't too bright at all.

title: Would buy again.
body: Best kettle I've purchased. all stainless steel and boils water very quickly. Best price I've seen the kettle. and holds about 2-3 thermos' full of water.

title: Great product!
body: I typically use a traditional teapot to make my hot water. My boyfriend has this electric tea pot and I loved it so much that I bought my own. I highly recommend. Pros- it heats up in about 90-120 seconds. It’s smaller than a normal tea pot, so it takes up less space. It’s also sleek looking and very quiet. Cons- Since it’s smaller, it only holds enough water for about two cups of tea.

title: Buenisimo
body: Muy hermoso y eficiente, caliente el agua súper rápido

title: Wonderful kettle
body: This was a terrific purchase. It is aesthetically pleasing. It boils quickly and silently. The spout design is the best part of the kettle. It is precise and even. I make loose tea in a pot and it makes for even pouring over the leaves. The lid and on/off button feel a little weak - could be sturdier but I am mindful not to jam these. Overall I recommend. I got the matte black and in my all stainless kitchen it fits in and balances the look

title: Great Electric Kettle that is Stylish
body: This electric tea kettle heats water up fast and even looks great left out on the counter. It's easy to use - just fill it up with water and push the switch down. It will boil the water and automatically shut off once done. Water pours out of the spout nice and evenly, and since the spout is a gooseneck and long and skinny, the water goes right where you need it - no need to worry about it splashing elsewhere. The handle is comfortable and placed in such a way that makes the kettle feel balanced when your are pouring water out.

title: Think no further, purchase!
body: It's the perfect kettle for frequent tea drinkers. I use it at least 6-7 times a day, its quick, light and convenient and it sits on my shelf at all times since it looks so beautiful! I live in a city with hard water so I boil a mix of water and vinegar every now and then but so far works like a charm! The only think is that I think the cork on the top is hanging by a thread and I might damage it if I'm not being careful. But definitely a must purchase!! It makes boiling water a very pleasant experience.

I bought this 15 months ago and used it maybe 20 times. It was great at heating up quickly but it did on many occasions leak. Now it’s broken. The switch no longer works. Not a good value for the money.

title: Kettle Perfection
body: I love my new kettle. The design is elegant, the size perfect for 1-2 people , and the water heats quickly. I bought it to replace my Bodum Bistro Kettle, which I have had for many years. Unfortunately, it met its end after falling to the floor and and losing a small but essential piece of plastic.

title: Quick and Quiet
body: This is a beautiful kettle. The mat black finish is really classy looking. It is a smaller kettle (two 12 oz mugs), but I like that it has a smaller footprint on the counter than many. The cork accents are attractive. It boils water quickly and is much quieter than my previous kettle (Breville).

title: Leakage hack
body: I've owned two of this kettle and both ended up leaking in about a year. This kettle has been otherwise fine - good design without ugly logo, simple and easy use, water boils quickly, and affordable. So I was trying to find ways to deal with the annoying leakage and I think I found how. The leakage seems to happen as soon as the water gets in, and not as a result of boiling. Check the leakage right after pouring water in: pour water into the kettle over the sink, see if it leaks, and if so, let the leak dripple into the sink, then boil the water. I've been testing this hack for about a week and there hasn't been any more leakage after boiling, once the initial leak check was done.

title: Not the best, but still good
body: It's functional, but the handle feels flimsy. I also don't like how the lid feels when you pull it off and put it on. Kind of like scratching a chalk board. Also, doesn't have temperature settings and the water cools down quickly if you don't pour it immediately after its heated.

title: Great product! Heats water so quickly!
body: This heats up water in under 30 seconds for about 2 cups. The matte black looks very nice and the value is great! It’s easy to open and fill and the water tastes great so I know that the kettle doesn’t give it a bad taste. I highly recommend this kettle!

title: Very fast water boiling
body: We got this to heat water for our pour over coffee and it works very well. The water boils very fast and since we have an electric stove it is much faster than heating water on the stove. I also use it to get hot water for cooking when I am rushed. Automatic shutoff is great. There is an indicator light and it is designed to shut off so it cannot get dry and burn. Beautiful on my counter.

title: Great quality, style and heats up quickly
body: I love this added to my little coffee station. It’s perfect for all the different ways to make and try out coffee. I’m new to coffee so I have been experimenting with different brew methods and this was exactly what I needed. The button is a simple click, the auto shut off works great, it doesn’t make any noises apart from the water boiling inside. The water gets HOTTT like, really hot. I even use this to make ramen, oatmeal, tea, etc. The size is perfect. I leave remaining water in it and just fill as I need to. No weird metal taste. And the style is very neutral and works well with any theme.

title: Bodum Melior Gooseneck Electric Water Kettle easy to use and you get what you pay for
body: I recently bought the Bodum Melior Gooseneck Electric Water Kettle and have been using it for a few days now. So far it has been a pleasant experience and I am enjoying the gooseneck design more than traditional kettles. Honestly its kind of fun just pouring water out of it. The kettle I received came perfectly fine no dings or scratches anywhere, and its kind of small though I wouldn't say smaller than advertised(27 ounces is less than a liter of water). It only has the one button but that's all I need it for and for the price I am thoroughly satisfied.

title: Love that spout!
body: I really like the snakey spout. It shuts off quickly once it reaches a boil. My old kettle would boil for too long. It also seems like it produce too much steam, which is necessary because I keep it under my cabinets on the countertop and excess steam will cause bad things to happen. Lastly, it is really sharp-looking in my green and white kitchen!

title: The ultimate value kettle
body: This kettle will boil water and deliver it unto a coffee bed with relative speed and comfort. There are kettles that offer more control over temperature. There are kettles that offer a more perpendicular pour, providing a theoretically more even extraction. There are prettier kettles. There are much nicer coffee focused kettles on the market, but a kettle won’t make or break your pour over. Save your money and put it towards a capable grinder and get this kettle. It is cheap, it is fast, it looks sleek enough, and it works. This kettle will not connect to your phone via Bluetooth, as it unconcerned with trivial complications to your coffee routine. It’s job is to heat water and pour it nicely. It does this at a better value than most every kettle on the market. I have upgraded basically every aspect of my coffee bar besides this kettle because there is simply no need to. Bodum is a brand that is very inconsistent in its quality not only within its product lineup, but within units themselves. I lucked out and my unit hasn’t let me down. Don’t be afraid to replace it if it is leaking or is faulty. It’s worth it to get one that works at this price. 8/10, points docked for no temperature control and an angled pour that takes some time to adjust to.

title: Don’t over fill, but good kettle
body: Leaks a little bit if slightly over the fill line. Besides that issue I love this kettle, sleek and clean design and I love the cork

title: A Household Staple
body: Possibly one of the best electric kettles to ever own. No glass or plastic to deal with, and it looks absolutely gorgeous. It works extremely efficiently and has never let me down. They last forever, and for the price you can’t get anything better imo.

title: Love it !!
body: I love this kettle. First of all I have purchased numerous electric kettles lately in this price range, from borosilicate glass to "full" stainless steel. The all had plastic somewhere in either the water container itself or where the steam would drip back into the water. The inside of the lids were plastic, etc. I returned so many that I was going to give up and just use my glass kettle over the gas stove. Then I found this one! It is so stylish with the matte black and best of all no plastic. The cap on the tube inside is metal now. I was still wary, was it too good to be true? So I boiled some water to taste to see if it tasted like metal and it didn't. I like the size as I have limited counter space and I love the curved thin spout which makes it easy to pour into a smallish container without splashing over. It looks "European" and ergonomic and with the assets I mentioned above, it is perfect!

title: Cheap Chinese crap
body: Why did you pick this product vs others?: Bought it lil over a month ago already peeling and falling apart, the design is trying to copy fellow but you can tell it's just a "pain job"... I finally pulled the trigger and bought fellow, buy once cry once I guess

title: First use so far its looking good
body: Takes about 5 minutes to boil water. Looking at steam cap it looks different from the models from the previous year, in the old ones it looks like a silicone or plastic cap is on it but this one is metal. Steam goes out from the bottom on slots on the bottom of the kettle. Unlike kettles of lower quality the first boil does not smell bad which is great. Kettle is harder to clean. They say to wipe it down but people with small heads will have a hard time wiping it down like the guide says. I'd suggest using a twisted paper towel and maybe long cooking chopsticks to absorb the majority of it while leaving a paper towel along the edge of the inside to absorb any remaining liquid. Because of the steam spout cleaning it with soap and water will be pretty much out of the question and using water and vinegar is pretty much the only choice. Will provide an update on this kettle after further use.

title: Drink more tea now.
body: Drink lots of tea now. This has made it super easy. Highly recommend. I read some issues about spout leaking, but I have not had that issue

title: This is a great kettle for the money!
body: I recently purchased this kettle to replace my old, modern-styled one, and I couldn’t be happier with the upgrade. The heating element is cleverly positioned in the middle of the kettle’s interior, ensuring quick and even heating, which is a noticeable improvement over models with the element at the base. The satin black finish is not only sleek but also durable—no scratches or scuffs so far. The well-designed gooseneck spout allows for precise pouring without any splashes or messes. Overall, this kettle is an all-around winner, and I highly recommend it!

title: Spills
body: Somehow, after one use…… water condenses outside of the pot in a ringed crevice near the base, where the heating elements are. When I heat & pour a second pot of hot water, the water in the crevice spills all over the place.

title: Works great
body: I bought this for my coffee and tea station, it has worked great si far and I use it EVERY DAY! I really like it. I let it air after using it, to avoid any mold or mildew.

title: Easy to Use but Hard to Clean
body: I've had this kettle for a month now and it has been really great purchase. The looks are good, it holds plenty of water for my needs, and heats up quickly. Gets to a nice boil and turns itself off like it should so I don't feel any risk setting it and forgetting it. Also its cork handles ensure I don't have to touch hot metal at all, while the gooseneck stout is quite nice for accurate easy pouring. I am docking one star because it is a little difficult to clean with inside (though I've had no issues with lingering water or rust) and that it does seem to not hold temperature exceptionally well. The top opening is very hard, to near impossible to fit a hand in to clean so you'll need a scrubber. I've found having it upside down over a cloth or drying mat is best after use. As for holding temperature, it is all metal and clearly not double walled. You'll feel the heat if you touch the metal. But because of that too it will also seep heat so if you set it and don't go back to it when done it can cool off. It's quick to heat back up and its accurate thermometer only heats it as long as it needs, but when there is no audible alert when it comes to temperature, you may do it a few times.

title: Great gooseneck kettle, but I miss variable temps
body: I love this little dude! It's incredibly reliable and holds up to multiple per-day uses, as it is my daily driver for making coffee at the office. I've had it for roughly a year, and have made coffee with it at least once per day since the initial purchase. Usually, for specialty coffee anyway, Bonavita is considered the hallmark of a good, relatively affordable gooseneck kettle, but I honestly feel that this kettle's neck and body are shaped in a way that makes pouring much easier without too much separation caused by surface tension of the water. My one gripe (though I recognize it's not a given with every kettle) is the lack of variable temperatures. Even having the option to go to 200 F or 205 F instead of straight to boiling would be nice, though I realize that would likely add some cost to an otherwise excellent value proposition. Highly recommended!

title: Works as intended, leaks at bottom seam after a few months
body: Works as intended, leaks at bottom seam after a few months. Boils water in 2-3 minutes

title: Best Electric Kettle there is
body: My roommate had one and I missed immediately when I got my own apartment. Highly recommend, boils water in under 2 minutes

title: Does Not Last Long - Water Leaks
body: This water kettle is very aesthetically pleasing, feels nice to hold, and works fantastically to make pour-over coffee. I had no issues for the first 4-5 months. Unfortunately, it then started leaking water from the base. This made pouring the hot water over ground coffee dangerous and I almost burned myself a few times. I reached out to the manufacturer to see if anything could be done but did not get a response. Other reviews stated similar things, with minimal support from the manufacturer. Given the relatively high price of this kettle, I am disappointed.

title: The jury is out -
body: My Keurig from years and years finally died. So, I started to look for options. Found the pour over method, and bought this to go along. I have been holding my review, because spots that form at the bottom of the kettle. I am worried that is mold? I am going to try a method suggested by another reviewer and see if that takes care of the spots. I have not had any leaks yet, but I have no used it that often, as the spots concerned me. They do not look like water spots. At the bottom where it meets the wall, you can see a different color, like it is beginning to rust? I cannot take good pictures to try to amplify and see if it is rust? Many reviews said that it heats up water quickly, to me this is a bit slower than an old machine that held more water. From pushing the lever to auto-shut off takes 4 min and 27 seconds in my unit. It does not hold the heat that long. So, you come back for a second cup, and now the water is not hot. You have to cycle again. It is better than a stove top, because there is no risk that you left the stop on! – that I have done at the start of my pour over experiments. It looks good on your counter. At the end I ended up buying a Keurig in a blue big box place, that have the simplest one for half the price of any other places. Does it talk to me? No, but I can get coffee quickly!

title: Works fast
body: It heats up really fast but has no temperature control at all. Poke in the dark. Also, not sure how to clean it since hands will not fit into the opening. But so far so good. I think I would be happier with a more techie one with dials, etc.

title: Works perfectly
body: Works exactly as advertised. Handy to have in the kitchen

title: Works great for CHEMEX. High Power usage. No measuring fill lines.
body: There’s so much to like and a few negatives depending on your usage (potential dealbreakers). First, it boils water FAST. At full, it boiled in a little over 3 minutes (see timer photo). It’s very attractive and easy to handle. I really like the matte black. Very simplistic in a good way. The gooseneck spout makes pouring extremely accurate (I use mine for making coffee in a CHEMEX). Have not had any of the issues others have complained about, just leave the plastic piece inside in place, it’s not intended to be removed (these people need to read the instructions!). One concern, depending on your situation is power consumption. It uses a 1000W of power. To put that in perspective my microwave uses 1200W. So if your in an RV or Tiny Home, you’ll obviously need a solid inverter if your off the grid. And my personal MAJOR gripe and why I gave this 3 stars is the lack of measurement indicators inside the kettle. This I just don’t understand AT ALL. There is only one, the Max Fill Line. Maybe I’m just blind and don’t see it, but I have looked everywhere inside and out and nothing. But the instructions say it’s there so maybe I got a flawed one. I guess If you don’t care how much water your boiling it doesn’t matter, but if your someone that is water conscious (like an RV’er) or want to boil exactly 3 cups of water, this will be a pain. You’ll need a measuring cup handy at all times. I’ve since confirmed from other buyers it does not have fill lines. If you use it in the kitchen for preparing recipes, keep a measuring cup handy. What a colossal oversight. Still, even with that flaw, I really like everything else about it and don’t mind the extra step of measuring the water (besides it’s too much of a pain to return it.).

body: It’s a cool design. The knob on top, it’s so wiggly it’s hard to get it open. Not sure if all are like this. I’ve tried tightening it.

title: Great until it leaked
body: This was super cute, but not sure it is going to last. I got it Nov 30 and all of a sudden today Feb 6 it is leaking from the bottom.

title: attractive and works well
body: I encountered this hot water heater in our room at Sun Mountain lodge in eastern Washington. I was delighted as I like to make a cup of tea first thing in the morning. I was impressed how attractive it was and how fast the water heated. I then ordered three of them, two for home and one for a gift. I really like it.

title: It’s so quiet!
body: This is the quietest kettle I’ve ever heard! And surprisingly fast boil as well. It’s unreal. I like the light weight of it, but it’s also firmly constructed. It’s perfect for 1 or 2 cups. I Love it.

body: Update: Ok, I still love it, however, I did realize that I wasn't paying attention to the maximum fill line. It is lower than I would have anticipated. WHILE OVERFILLING, I did experience some leaking. SINCE NOT OVERFILLING, I have zero leakage :) It is still perfect for me needs! Where do I start? This product is PERFECT for my needs and I don't know why I didn't order it years ago! I needed a fast heating option for just a couple cups. My gas stove kettle seemed to take 15 or 20 minutes to come to a boil, then it was tricky to pour it in the pour over without dripping it on the counter. This one, even at full capacity, takes less than 5 minutes to bring to 'just below' boiling temp. I don't think it rolls to a full boil. That's totally ok for my need. Within minutes I have a neat and tidy no spill pour for my tea, or my pour-over. I love it! It is a little difficult to clean because of the piece that comes up the center, but that is a small price to pay for the quick timing of getting hot water! OH!, and it's pretty, too! :)

That's all! The cork as a lid was also an odd choice (that's what I actually expected to break first). Anyway, trying my luck with a non-gooseneck one from a different brand. We've purchased half a dozen other Bodum tea and coffee related things besides the kettles over the past few years, and have found that they are high on style, but not sturdy and often not well thought out.

body: I grossly underestimated how much I would use this kettle. If you cook alot or are a big coffee or tea drinker, this kettle is your champion. I probably heat up at least 6 kettles of water a day, 10+ on weekends. It's super fast, attractive, and I shudder to think how hot my kitchen would get in the summer trying to do something as foolish as turning on a big stove eye to heat up a small volume of water (most of the hear just goes to fight against your AC). With this kettle, all of the heat goes to the water and your kitchen stays cool. +++++

body: Great product

body: Love the look and the thin spout. Wish it were faster to heat (microwave is fast for hot water for french press) and had some kind of an audio alert when heating was complete.

From what I can tell, as long as you carefully read the instructions as you should and use it properly, you shouldn’t have any issues. It reaches a boil in under 3 minutes every time even when I fill it to the max line. I’d be careful with the steam holes! Be sure you put the lid on where the steam holes face away from the handle. The plate that heats it cools down so fast too! I have yet to burn myself with this product and I am very pleased with the convenience this has to offer on time and easy management. The only thing I can think someone might pass it up is theres no temperature gage. Though they don’t cost much if you need it. I never did! I hope you buy this boiler over others. I haven’t written a review before but I wanted my first to be positive and this was one!

title: The BEST basic kettle that's not a Stagg imitation.
body: If I could afford it, I would get get a Stagg Kettle. But since I can't, this is the best basic kettle with its own unique design, and not one of the hundreds of blatant Stagg ripoffs. I'll be using it for pour over coffee, but I'm not obsessive about the details. This kettle heats the water and looks great, and that's about it. If you need timers, temperature settings and Bluetooth, this isn't the kettle for you. But if you just want something basic, dependable and good looking, this is the best kettle for the money. Even if it craps out after 3 years (which seems to happen to all kettles in this price range), it will have been worth it and I'd buy another.

title: Great product for 1.5 years now, using it daily.
body: Some may think it leaks and I did to at one time but it does not leak. You either spill water down the sides while filling kettle or when you remove the lid you will have condensation spill off on to the side of kettle. It happens all the time but it does not leak from the construction of the product.

body: This is a great starter gooseneck for anyone wanting to get into coffee or even tea. Doesn't have advanced temperature control, but if you use mostly light roast I think this does a fine job. Boils fast and is solidly built at a reasonable price. A laser thermometer can give you a good idea of how long it takes in your particular home for the freshly boiled water to cool to your desired brew temperature.

body: There must be a zillion electric kettles on the market, but I feel that I found the one for me. If you want one that heats a large volume of water, can be set for specific temperatures, or has a keep warm option or electronic noises to indicate operational status, the Bodum Melior gooseneck is NOT for you. Keep shopping. I wanted a kettle to quietly, quickly bring a cup or two of water to a boil, then turn off automatically. Appearance and ease of handling were also important. The Bodum fulfills all my requirements beautifully.... and frugally to boot. I can't address long-term durability yet, but everything feels sturdy and looks well-designed. The precision -pouring is pleasant whatever your hot beverage of choice.

My husband picked it up to pour out the hot water and it just broke off in his hand. He wasn’t using it in any strange way, just lifting it up to pour. I’m so bummed because we loved ihownit looked and had literally barely used it.

body: I just found my instruction booklet and receipt for this which I bought in November of 2014. It's now July of 2025. I am amazed that I have used this "kettle" for over 10 years!! It works as well as it did in the first year! I love the fact that it has six different temperature settings. I can fix a cup of tea and drink it right away.
