title: Good Kettle but Has Some Issues
body: The Cuisinart 1.7-Liter Electric Kettle is a good kettle with some solid features, like the 6 preset temperatures, which make it perfect for different types of tea and coffee. The stainless steel design is sleek and looks great on the countertop. It boils water quickly, and the cordless feature is really convenient. However, there are a few downsides. The lid is a bit tricky to open sometimes, and I noticed that the kettle can get a little noisy when boiling. Additionally, the temperature control buttons could be more responsive. Overall, it’s a solid product but not without its flaws.

title: Not accurate enough for science experiments, but makes a great cup of tea! ;)
body: Love this kettle. I understand from other reviewers that I should expect the writing on the buttons to wear off sooner than I would like, but I am willing to live with that for the plus of having multiple buttons preset for my teas and the stainless steel "innards". As to that, the interior is nearly 100% stainless steel. The only places that are not are the area around the little hole near the bottom that lets water into the window area so you can tell how full the pot is, the underside of the lid, and the tab that holds the filter screen. The water-level window is BPA free per the manufacturer, but it is nice to know that most of my water is not touching it as it boils away. As to the lid and the screen tab, these only touch the steam in the kettle, not the water. Granted the steam can condense and fall back into the pot, but this does not seem to cause an off-flavor that I can identify. As to accuracy, I'd say it is good enough. I have tested it at full boil and at the Green Tea setting of 175 degrees. I'm at 5600 feet, so full boil here is 204 degrees not 212. The pot is clearly confused by this and wants to keep working to get the temperature up. However, it shuts itself off after a minute, then a minute later it tries again, boiling the water away. Since it has an automatic "boil dry" shutoff, I am not worried about this issue, but I will keep and eye on it when it is set at the Black Tea (boil) setting. When tested at the green tea setting, I noticed the water was always heated about three to five degrees past the set temperature (it took 1.7 liters of 67 degree water to 178 degrees in 6 minutes, and 7 minutes to get to full boil). When the water cools to one degree below its set point, it turns on the heat again and heats the water up to 178 again. In two cases, it went up to 180 degrees. I don't find this a problem though, because as soon as you pour the water into a cup, even a pre-heated cup (using the hot water in t he pot), it always cools down three to five degrees (I tested this too!). So, it is the perfect temperature IF it is overheated in the pot. Finally, the beep. It beeps when it reaches temperature, but it is a very soft beep.... kind of like hearing a truck back up way down the street from you when you have all your windows closed. Easy not to notice if you are in another room. I'm good with that too, as I have excellent hearing, and if I miss the cue it automatically keeps the water warm for 30 minutes anyway. Highly recommended.

title: Love This Kettle!
body: First , let me say I've used Russell Hobbs kettles for many years, as they lasted for many years and were known as an excellent product. However, my latest RH Kettle died after about 18 months of use for no apparent reason. It just never turned on again. After reading other reviews it seems the general opinion is that they were once great but not any more. Which sent me on a search through kettles reading numerous reviews. (thank you, all reviewers!) So far the kettle is great! Some things I love: a) The lid opens with a push button so it is no longer a two hand job to fill the kettle. b) There are various settings for different kinds of tea! how great is that! These settings include temps for white and green tea, french press coffee and plain old boil. :) c) There's an optional "keep warm" button which will keep the water at your selected temperature for 30 minutes and then turn off. I especially love this as I would leave the room, do something while waiting for the water, it would take longer than expected and I'd always be reheating the water.... (maybe why Russell Hobbs broke??) d) It beeps when ready! Why don't they all? It's not a loud, annoying beep but if you're listening for it you will hear it. e) The window reservoir window clearly shows (and measures) how much water you've got in the pot' f) Yes, it heats quickly. I rarely fill the kettle to the top and the half kettle that I'm heating seems to take only a minute or two. What I don't love and why I didn't give this 5 stars: a) There;s nothing exceptional about the appearance of the kettle. Nothing awful, but i could have enjoyed a style with a little pizzazz. b) Not sure if the cord is really going to wind up in the base as tight as I would like (haven't gotten to this yet). The kettle arrived within 48 hours of being ordered. I rinsed it out, plugged it in and had tea within minutes. Such a relief to have a HOT cup of tea as I've been using a keurig which doesn't have a real hot setting. I'm pleased with my selection and would encourage others to buy this kettle. It's not a cheap kettle but the features are great and I'm hoping it will last like the old Russell Hobbs used to.

title: Beautiful, convenient, and functional!
body: Idk how it started, but I seem to have a "thing" for kettles, and have more than I'd care to admit. As each of my kids leaves home, the first thing they'd take was one of my kettles. They use them to make coffee, tea, mashed potatoes, and ramen noodles in their dorm. I love cooking and canning, and have found so many uses for this kettle. It's nice to look at, easy to use....even in the dark, and cuts time and valuable prep space when canning. Also great at sterilizing utensils and jars. I like the weight of it....doesn't feel flimsy or will easily tip over like other kettles when the cord gets bent/twisted. The "keep warm" feature is convenient too. Bottom line, this is my new favorite kettle due to it's size and different temp settings for making various tea blends. If you're on a budget and only need it to boil water, this would be an overkill, IMO. Lots of much cheaper alternatives on here for that. However, if you find the temp and keep warm options helpful, this is a solid piece of equipment I highly recommend.

title: Awesome Tea Kettle!
body:
The media could not be loaded.

Love this! I was on the fence between a standard tea kettle vs electric. I reviewed a bunch before deciding on this. Works as claimed and my jasmine and green teas are so much better! I also drink lots of herbal teas. This heats water very fast! The temp control is fabulous. I knew temps should be lower for my teas, but was too impatient to let the boiling water cool for long and grew accustomed to bitter green teas. No more! Huge difference if you are a tea lover like me. The water gauge and swivel are also very nice features. While the “stay warm” feature holds temp for only 30-minutes, I have found the water stays hot for a good long time. If you have to reheat at all, only takes a few seconds. I don’t understand complaints about noise. It only makes noise when it is really close to temp—the sound of steam building in the kettle—not the actual device. Not a big deal at all and short-lived. I also don’t understand cleaning complaints. If I end up with hard water deposits, vinegar and a brush will work. I use filtered RO water for my tea, so shouldn’t be an issue. These are not designed to cook tea—and why would you? Tea (even black) is not meant to be boiled and cooked. A tea “pot” is for steeping. A tea “kettle” is for heating water. I would never do both in the same vessel. The “filter” is in case you have sediment in your water—not intended for actually brewing tea—although it looks like some people do. I have a separate glass teapot I use for actual brewing, so this is perfect. This is a little heavy when filled to max, but not unmanageable. I only fill to 1.5L (shoulder issue) rather than max and it is plenty of water and easy to handle. Love it! Hopefully, it lasts. If I have any issues, I will amend my review. I will add, I have a Cuisinart steam/bake toaster oven and also love that. Have had for a couple years now, use it a lot and NO issues. I sent another brand back that was inferior. So I am thinking this is a high-quality product. If it goes bad out of warranty, I will happily purchase another as I appreciate a good quality product and have used the heck out of it.

title: Love my Perfec Temp - (Edit: slightly less than my initial review due to a couple problems)
body: I love this Cuisinart Perfec Temp Kettle. Only wish it was came in a 2 liter model as I typically make 2 quarts of ice tea at a time. Only 1 very slight design flaw... when pouring the last cup from the kettle, the water comes from the lip of the spout (where it should) and also from the upper edge of the hole in the kettle where the spout is located. It all goes in the cup, so no problem. But if I were working on the next improved model, there are a couple easy ways to fix this... lower the top edge of the spout hole or put a baffle inside the unit to prevent water from getting to the top of the unit when tipped to get the last cup. June 2017 edit: My initial review was 5 stars. I've lowered it to 4. I was going to lower it to 3, as I was having an issue with my new one, but I begrudgingly give it a 4 as the problem seems to be getting better with time. So, I'm on my 2nd CPK-17 now. My first CPK-17 developed a leak at the bottom of the handle. And, leaving it filled overnight resulted in a small puddle of water below the base in the morning. I really liked my first kettle, so I purchased another. Unfortunately, I'm having a problem that others have mentioned in having difficulty opening the lid. While my 1st kettle only rarely did not open on the 1st press, it always opened on the 2nd. My new kettle has not been as cooperative. And *one* time I had to SHAKE it while half full about 10 times while holding the button, before the lid finally popped open. I've only had this new one a couple weeks now and, so far, that has only happened once, but it frequently takes more that one press of the button before the lid will open. This problem is improving with use so I'm hoping the lid will loosen up further over time. 2nd edit: So it's been over a week now since my previous edit and it looks like the lid has loosened. I've been using my 2nd CPK-17 two times a day and the problem experienced with the lid failing to open hasn't occurred once since my previous edit.

Husband still bought another. We'll start using that after determining if using a lower preset temp is a good solution.

title: Flawed by poor implementation.
body: Overall this kettle is well made and sturdy. I paid a premium for this thing because I want it to last for years, which to be fair I expect it to. So why only three stars? Because it's SOOO frustrating. It has multiple settings for different temperatures of water. Handy, right? Making green tea? Use that setting. Set it to boil, and it will boil like a champ. Until it randomly forgets what setting you set it to, and Cuisinart inexplicably made the default setting 160f (the coldest possible). Why not set boiling as the default when that's what 99.9% of the time most users will want? The other setting is "Keep Warm", or as I call it "Poltergeist Mode". It just keeps turning itself on to keep the water at temperature, which is a colossal waste of energy. And again, the default setting for this mostly useless and electricity-hogging feature is ON instead of OFF. The upshot is that three or four times a week the damn thing's goldfish memory strikes and I have to reset it to boil and non-haunted mode. It might not sound like much, but it gets really old, really fast. And all this user frustration could have been easily avoided by sensible design choices. Avoid.

title: Pretty Good, But Not Perfect
body: We’ve been using Cuisinart Electric kettles for years and have found them reliable and overall quite satisfactory. What attracted me to this model is the ability to specify the water temperature. I wanted to have more control of the temperature at which I brew my coffee. This kettle works fine. I have no idea how it will hold up. Water heating is fine. Controls are overly fussy. It doesn’t just turn on and off, but stays warm, has a sleep mode and is more complicated than I need.. Why the temperature setting aren’t enough and they add the type of tea that temperature is best for seems like overkill. If we’re smart enough to know that a kettle that heats to different temperatures makes sense, don’t you think we’d know what temperature works for different types of teas? Besides, I mainly drink coffee. Base of unit is much lighter and less stable than past models. Kettle is heavier than our past ones. My wife doesn’t like it as much as the simpler older ones. I agree. Can’t these manufacturers leave well enough alone if they have a good product and only add really needed improvements, while not making the operation more complicated?

title: Died after 30 months / Clunky to use
body: Purchased this March 2022. In September 2024, the sensor that detects when the pot is boiling started failing, and twice we caught it boiled dry and had to dump it. An expensive purchase for two and a half years of service! During its short life, my wife really appreciated the different temperature settings. However, it had a few nagging issues even when working. The 'keep warm' button is on by default, so the kettle repeatedly heats itself after you've poured your drink. And it defaulted to the lowest heat setting after being off its base for a minute or more. Meaning that I usually had to press three buttons 'Start' 'Boil', and 'Keep Warm' (the latter to turn it off, not to turn it on) just to get a cup of boiling water. Finally, it seemed to have real trouble pouring the last bit of water - would get stuck somehow in the base of the kettle. We're replacing it with something with a more classic and hopefully robust design.

title: Best Kettle Ever
body: I drink a lot of tea and coffee (mostly tea). And my fellow tea drinkers recommended this. After years of a boil only kettle, I sprung for an upgrade. This is the greatest kitchen gadget I've ever purchased in my life. Heats up wicked fast and has a special setting for every kind of tea and coffee (6 in all). Simple to use. Just buy this, you won't be sorry.

title: Designed for my entire tea collection, does the job nicely!
body: This kettle is attractive, with its stainless steel carafe, updated shape, and pretty blue display - it should be, for its price. It's extremely easy to use, as the temperature, start and hold buttons all do exactly what you'd think they would do. And the fact that the kettle itself is cordless (the cord connects to the heating base) optimizes freedom and comfort of use. I have an extensive collection of teas of all types, so the various temperature settings take the guesswork out of heating water in a stovetop kettle. (I regularly use every one of the temperature settings!) Although my ear was becoming fairly well tuned to the sounds of my stovetop kettle, nothing takes the place of absolute certainty! Besides the various temperature settings, I am happy to finally have a kettle with a volume window. Before, if I wanted to use my larger teapot to make a partial (not full) pot of tea, I had to use a measuring cup to ensure the proper amount of water for the quantity of tea leaves I was using - a big pain. Although this is a common feature of electric kettles, I'm happy to have this feature combined with the various temperature settings this kettle offers. I'm not crazy about the way the Cuisinart pours, however. The somewhat irregular flow is probably due to the presence of the removable filter at the inside entry to the spout, but this is no excuse. It could have been better designed. It's especially annoying when I am pouring the last of the water out and, in order to get the last ounce or so to pour, I have to return the kettle to upright and then pour the last bit out. The half hour hold feature is nice, but I'm finding I need a bit more time. An hour would have been better. As it is, I find that many times I need to manually turn the kettle back on, once its passed its half hour hold time, in order to finish up the remainder of the contents. All in all, this product was thoughtfully designed and appears to be the only kettle on the market that truly satisfies the needs of the consummate drinker of a wide variety of teas.

title: Good compromise buy
body: This is a good electric kettle. However, it is not the best-ever electric kettle. I lived in England for a long time so have had several excellent electric kettles. This is also my second model of the Cuisinart CPK-17 PerfecTemp because the first one did stop working within three weeks. However, customer service was good and agreed to send out a replacement which arrived very promptly and has been working every day for over a year. I use mine to make white, green, oolong, black and herbal teas at least twice a day. You do have to read the instructions carefully at the start to figure out how to turn it off/not leave it on the 'warm' function or how to use the temperature memory function, but after you are used to it you don't think twice. Pros: -Looks good, stylish -Love the blue light -Not heavy when full with water -Takes a decent amount of water at a time -Heats the water pretty quickly -Metal not plastic -Enclosed heating element so you do not have to deal with cleaning the element -Heats it to close to the temperature you choose -Great customer service from Cuisinart Cons: -My first unit failed and I had to pay a moderate amount to receive the second replacement unit -The water temperatures listed seem a little high, I have to use "oolong" setting for green tea as the "green tea" setting is a bit too hot. -Somewhat pricey, I really feel it should be cheaper. I have found that the boil function is super-hot. The outside of the unit also remains hot so not suitable for those with young children. As there are not that many models of temperature-selection electric kettles on the US market I still gave this four stars because I use it every day and can adjust the heat of the water better than if I had a regular electric kettle and had to wait for the water to cool down. It dresses up the kitchen and is pretty easy to keep clean and in good condition. I just hope it lasts!

title: So far so Good!!

title: Buy Yourself A New Mug To Go With This Kettle
body: BREAKDOWN: COMFEE' 1.7L Stainless Steel Electric Tea Kettle (BPA-Free, 1500W Fast Boil, Auto Shut-Off with LED Light) IMPRESSIONS: A great modern appliance in line with air fryer, that gets you back to boiling water rather than microwaving it. And you definitely taste the difference in your coffee and tea. Really makes customizing your own drink a better experience both in prep and flavor quality. POSITIVES: Simple and safe to use. A single button press activates it with an led to indicate when it's on. And it shuts itself off after bringing water to a boil, so you never have to worry about over-boiling. There's a thumb lever press to lift the lid for refilling the water. When removed from the base after heating, it's safe to set on down on surfaces. The size is large enough for multiple cups and the mostly steel exterior provides a lot of durability. Plus, it's so easy to keep nearby so you don't have take a trip anywhere to get a fresh cup to drink. THOUGHTS: It took getting shamed by real tea drinkers to make me go back to using a kettle after relying on heated water from fountains or the microwave. And I'm so glad they did because I missed the quality brewed water activates in tea and coffee. Definitely get you one, if you don't it already.

title: Boils water like it's being paid by the hour.
body: 📝 Review: There are few things in life more satisfying than pressing a button and watching water boil while pretending you're conducting a tiny science experiment. The COMFEE’ electric kettle nails that vibe—and looks good doing it. I bought this for tea. I now use it for everything: French press, instant noodles, hot toddies, and on one very dark morning, to defrost my windshield. 🔥 What It Does Well: FAST. 1500 watts of pure hydrating rage. From cold tap to bubbling chaos in under 5 minutes. Honestly? Terrifying in the best way. LED Light Show. Blue glow while boiling = subtle sci-fi kitchen drama. Makes me feel like my water is leveling up before I drink it. Auto Shut-Off + Boil Dry Protection. Important for people like me who wander off mid-boil to watch TikToks or rethink their life. Stainless Steel Interior. No weird plastic taste. No floating mystery bits. Feels clean, solid, and like it belongs in a Bond villain’s lair. 🤏 What Could Be Better: The lid doesn’t open super wide, so if you’re the kind of person who wants to scrub the inside with a sponge (hi, overthinkers), it’s a little tight. No temperature control—just boil. But you know what? title: It gets the job done, i guess...

I kept it rather than returning it b/c despite its issues it gets the job do, and i like not worrying about it being plastic (a lot of electric kettles seem to have plastic parts for some reason!). The size is also nice, and I couldn't find anything better in this price range at the time anyways. Pros: --- it's metal so it's not gonna crack! ---none of the plastic parts on this kettle come in contact with the water (unless you use the weird strainer it comes with which i obviously don't). ---the handle is protected (encased in plastic) so that it doesn't burn you when you pick it up. ---it has an auto shutoff feature that (eventually) shuts it off. There's also a little light on the lever to indicate when it's one (not that you need it). ---the 1.5L size is more than enough to provide 2 large mugs of water. --- the bottom of the base is designed to allow you to easily wrap the cord in to keep it tucked up and out of the way when not in use. CONS: ---this kettle isn't as loud as my microwave but it's definitely not quiet... ---the auto shutoff feature doesn't seem to kick in until after it's been boiling for at least a minute or 3. ---it takes longer than a glass kettle to heat up (difference of 3-5 minutes maybe). ---there's a seam at the top of the handle (near where you press to open the lid) that you can burn yourself on if you're not paying attention when you pick it up. ---sometimes the lid can be difficult to pop up and it also doesn't lift up all the way, which can make it difficult to fill the kettle (i often fill it up by filling a cup and dumping it in from the cup, which i do find kind of annoying).

I don't know why it made a calcium (or whatever white)deposit that stuck to about 1/3 of the bottom, but it doesn't come off. I tried to wipe it out it out but it's there to stay. It hasn't flaked off into subsequent kettles of water I boiled so maybe it's a discoloration and not a deposit. It's too much of a pain to return things so I kept it. The shut off once it starts to boil is slow to happen in my opinion. My mom's kettle shuts off as soon as it boils not after it's boiling and boiling for several seconds. I don't like that. I wouldn't purchase this brand again.

Never sweats the way a glass will when filled with cold liquid, and does not leak. Fantastic for summer use when you need to keep cold drinks cold.

title: Cute, but Overpriced

I own a 40 oz Hydro Flask bottle that I use daily, but it is very large. It's too big to fit in any cup holders. I was wondering if a 32 oz bottle could fit in a cup holder, so I asked Rufus about it on this bottle's listing. Rufus said yes. This bottle went on sale. The other sizes besides the 32 oz were already sold out, so I went ahead and bought it. However, when I received it and was able to see it in person, I realized that it is the same size around as my 40 oz bottle. I feel like buying the 32 oz bottle was kinda pointless, especially at the price. The original price was about $45, whereas the 40 oz bottle (which is not a special print) I have is also $45. The special design on this particular bottle is driving up the price. If I had known the 32 oz was gonna be too big to fit a cup holder, I would not have bought it.
