Now, we both enjoy our beverages at the perfect temp, all the time. And no more wasted coffee.

title: Works well
body: Owning this is how I know I don't have any real problems in my life. I always thought flying cars would be the key indicator, but this item proves that we are now living in the future. Coffee stays as hot as I want it; I don't have to finish it more quickly than I'd like to, or settle for less-than ideal drinking temperature. I will note two minor drawbacks which may impact you more than me, depending on your use case. First, I'm anxious to place the mug on the charging station until I know it's thoroughly dry, but since I only use it on leisurely mornings, not every day, this is no problem. Second, it can form a "skin" over coffee if I use too much milk or cream (which would be too much, anyway). But neither of these issues have managed to ruin the experience for me.

title: Great mug, a LOT expensive, but definately works.
body: The original review was accurate, but now that I've had the mug for 6 months (Originally 3 star), I have to reduce its rating... The mug itself is great, works well, and does what it says. It keeps my drinks at the temperature I set it to. The reason I'm reducing the rating here for 2 reasons. 1) Trying to reach an actual person or something more intelligent than an automated help desk, is seeming to be nearly impossible. - To expand on this: I have been unable to find any contact information to report any issues I do have with the mug or software (I have no issues with the mug so far, but the software annoys me to no end). 2) The software for the mug is so far below par, that they might as well just have a digital display on the side to show the temp and just set it that way. - Let me expand on this: a) If you don't keep your mug paired, ie: carry it with you 100% of the time, anytime it isn't paired, it forgets its pairing, and you have to go through the pairing procedure again to reconnect it. My car is a 2014, and the BlueTooth in it remembers my phone when I start it up, but this mug cannot. b) There's no way to override the heating to ON, if the sensor doesn't trigger to say the mug isn't empty, it won't turn on, even in the software Bluetooth connection. Through some digging, it states that it determines if it's empty by the significant difference in temperature: The mug is cold, pour warm to hot fluid in it, and it detects the temp change and determines it's not empty. I understand this is probably a safety feature to prevent the mug from burning out, but there should be some way to turn it on when you put room temp liquid into a room temp mug. (I usually make a batch of tea, and if I don't finish it all in a day, I use it the next day, I shouldn't have to microwave the first cup just to get it hot enough for the mug to realize it's full.) So in summary: -The mug is absolutely great, so far it's held up fine, with no chips/scratches. Works great to keep temp set. -Software needs a LOT of work. The biggest issue is the Bluetooth connection/protocol. I shouldn't have to re-pair it every day just to connect to the mug to change it from Tea to coffee, or some other temp for a different drink. -Better contact forms, for when you can't resolve the problem via automated help. I'm hoping that by rating this at only 1 star, maybe I'll get a way to contact the company, or at least they'll read this review and take the issues under advisement. Maybe even make a suggestions/complaints form to get these issues noticed so they know what to work on. Until I see a way to contact a live person, even if it's just email, or something simple, I cannot rate this higher than a 1. IF I were having a real issue with this mug (like it not working) I'd be out the money it cost me to buy it. Original Review Below this line: *********************************** Keeps my tea at the temperature I set, making every sip enjoyable. Pros: Heats relatively fast Keeps Temp very well. Con's: It's for Right Handers, if you're left-handed, (or hold the mug in your left hand), the LED is on the back side where you can't see it (less of a problem while you're actually holding it), but if you set it down for grabbing with your left hand you can't see the LED. The software is a little glitchy. I tried setting it to Celsius for a little bit, then when I tried to switch it back to Fahrenheit, it wouldn't switch, I had to reset the app completely to default to get it back to Fahrenheit. Couldn't find a contact form for issues (like the above software glitch), or suggestions.

title: Great Gift for Coffee Lovers
body: I have bought this mug two times as a gift and both recipients love it. It's super easy to set-up and use and it keeps your coffee/tea very hot (sometimes too hot!). I like that it has temperature control, so you can raise and lower the constant temperature of your beverage to fit your liking. I plan on buying one for my work office, since I am always interrupted and never get to finish a hot coffee! Definitely would recommend for any coffee lover or for anyone looking for a unique/quality gift idea.

title: Great Features, but a Bit Pricey for What It Offers
body: The Ember Mug 2 is undeniably a sleek and innovative product, but I can’t help feeling it’s a bit pricey at $120 (or even $100). That said, it does come with some impressive features that make it stand out. The ability to keep my drink at the perfect temperature (between 120°F and 145°F) for up to 80 minutes—or all day on the charging coaster—is a game-changer. Whether I’m working at my desk or enjoying a quiet moment, my coffee or tea stays exactly how I like it. The smart LED indicator is a nice touch, letting me know when my drink is ready to enjoy. I appreciate the option to use the Ember app for precise temperature control and notifications, but I also like that it defaults to 135°F without the app. The auto-sleep and motion detection features are thoughtful additions, ensuring the mug conserves power when not in use. One downside is that it’s hand wash only, though the scratch-resistant coating and IPX7 rating make it easy to clean. Just remember not to put it in the dishwasher! While I love the functionality and design, the price tag feels a bit steep for what it is. If you’re someone who values perfectly tempered drinks and doesn’t mind the investment, it’s worth considering. However, if you’re on a budget, you might find it hard to justify the cost. Pros: - Keeps drinks at the perfect temperature for extended periods - Smart LED indicator for temperature readiness - Auto-sleep and motion detection features - Hand wash safe with scratch-resistant coating Cons: - Expensive for a mug - Hand wash only (no dishwasher) Overall, the Ember Mug 2 is a luxurious and functional product, but the price might not be for everyone.

title: Get one
body: Worth it totally- no worries as I’m a fan and 3rd time buyer and this was a charm!! The color is great - paired, cleans & heats perfectly- charger even renewed my others! I’m ready for anything the day brings knowing my coffee will always be perfect!!! Thanks Amazon & Ember!!

title: Worth it but too tiny
body: This product is quite impressive. While on the charger it will keep your beverage HOT all day. Off of the charger it keeps it HOT for 1 hr. While on the charger, it will heat up your beverage to HOT rather quickly. While off of the charger it takes way too long to do so. The product itself is amazing and I really recommend it for everyone who takes their time drinking and enjoying tea or coffee. I got this for my wife for Christmas because she constantly has to microwave her coffee because we have 5 children … but mainly because the 19 month old is demanding lol. I just regret getting a 10oz. I didn’t realize how tiny 10oz is because I assumed most mugs are 8oz. Wrong! lol. I am exchanging this for the 14oz. With the 10oz, once you put the coffee there’s hardly room for creamer and sugar (when it comes to a real coffee drinker). I gave it 5 stars because the product works excellently. The app is very impressive and fun (to me). I love to watch on the app how the T° of the coffee goes down immediately after pouring in creamer. I love it. You can customize the color code of the light on the mug and name the mug in the app. You can also set the T° you want your beverage to be going forward (set it and forget it). It’s awesome. I watched a YouTube video about the mug and the review said they don’t think it’s worth the $ although the product worked really well. That’s kind of an oxymoron. I think you’re getting what you pay for and in a good way. Your beverage literally stays HOT or (if you want) warm until the very last drop. I don’t often drink coffee or even tea, but when I do it’s Dos Equis lol jk… when’s I do I can’t stand where the last few sips are cold. I want to get one for myself except I hardly drink tea or coffee, just to show you how great the product is. I think the 10oz is too tiny. 10oz might not be as necessary to be in the size of a tech mug since it’s not much to begin with and can be finished rather quickly (although my wife still appreciates it in her lifestyle). For the real tea and coffee drinkers out there I highly recommend this product, but the largest versions.

title: My favorite mug, now
body: Absolutely awesome. I love this more than I thought I would. As a slow drinker, I had no idea how amazing it is to have the last sip be just as hot and delicious as the first sip. I love having a solution to keeping my coffee hot that isn't a thermos or hot plate. People complain about the app, but it's been fine so far. It does forget the phone is paired, which is annoying, but it's quick to re-pair. The app telling me when it's reached the perfect temperature, so not having to keep manually measuring myself is massive. The biggest weakness is the charge. It's slow to charge and quick to drain. For me, I don't care about the charging time, but if it could hold the charge even an hour longer, it would be a perfect product. Even when I pour coffee in that's over the temperature, the battery drains super fast without using the charging coaster. In the future, I am apprehensive about the app not working. As a final thought, I do wish there was a way to set the temperature outside of the app.

title: Two plus years of use. A flawed product, but still something I use everyday and adore.
body: I've used this mug for close to two years now. This is one of those products that starts as a luxury splurge, but a year in you realize just how essential it's become to your routine. It will sneak it's way into your favorite things if you are a regular coffee or tea drinker at all, and it's role becomes undeniable. The thought of no longer having it genuinely makes you feel a tiny bit sad. I could beam all day about how much I love this ridiculous mug. So, instead I'm going to rant about all the dumb things about it that detract from using it. The form factor is good enough, but the handle is poorly designed. The edges are too squared off, the shape isn't made for human hands being so thin, and because the mug is so bottom heavy it takes these minute design flaws and emphasizes them. I've not had any issues with the coating, but I am careful not to use metal utensils to stir things in it. While the bottom looks a bit scuffed up, the coating is just fine. Positively, the outside of the mug does not get hot so you don't need the stupid handle to hold it. Handle is pretty at least. The way the mug charges uses two prongs that connect with a ring on the bottom of the mug. It's not inductive charging and I'm not sure it could be given the threat of liquids. I don't have much of a problem with it being contact based and it nestles nicely into the base. The issue resides in the prongs themselves. They are tiny little spring loaded prongs that are predisposed to break if you do not baby the coaster. Sideways pressure of just putting the mug on the coaster from too flat of an angle over and over can jam the springs or break the prongs. I understand the need to have it be spring loaded to ensure contact, but must the contacts be so small and fragile? It just seems like there's so many better solutions to this problem than small aftermarket parts. Although, it does mean more replacement coasters sold. I gifted my mom one of these for Christmas and she's been through two coasters with broken prongs. The app is modern looking, and is just fine. Just fine like everything else. They want the app to look clean and minimal so instead of just having simple things like an on/off on the app home screen, you have to swipe in an unintuitive way to find that basic function located among temperature favorites instead of on the screen with your base temp and adjustment. There's nothing indicating you can swipe to see a screen of options. Nor can you control the sleep timer on the mug through the app for inactivity. It's just not using the space it has available all that well so everything feels like it has one too many steps involved for basic interaction. Prime example of form over function and the entire thing could use a redesign. If I only have a single mug registered to my device, why make me click the mug to connect and control each time the app starts up. Just default to the one thing it's linked with and auto-connect until more devices are added. And these features would be useful because the mug just doesn't detect empty or almost empty all that well. Many times I've had an empty cup and it just keeps on trucking, burning whatever last remnants have evaporated and been left in the bottom. Most of the time it works as it should, other times, you need to hold the mug completely upside down for a few seconds for the accelerometer inside to figure it there's no possibility there is anything in the cup. If you use cheap flavored creamers you will quickly learn of the burnt smell of sugars. With no control over an inactivity timer it's a bigger problem than I would like. These minor issues all add up, because no part of the product is undeniably extraordinary. The battery has degraded relatively quickly with heavy use and no longer lasts more than 20-30 minutes off of the coaster. It burns things all the time when I've not noticed it hasn't properly triggered the sleep function. With the heater being in the bottom, the temp feels progressively hotter as you drink more and more. And now more recently, the rubber ring on the bottom of mine has deformed under the heat of normal handwashing and no longer can seat properly. It's only a matter of time before repeated washing has done away with all the glue that secures it. It wants to have that marriage of luxury form and function that Apple-like products have, but when the function is so simple, it finds these odd ways to come up short. Like the LED indicator only being on one side of the cup, sorry lefties, or lack of optional auditory cues for the sake of convenience and accessibility. It is still just a mug. It does keep things wonderfully warm. I use it everyday, and often several times. The minuscule comfort of a hot coffee or tea keeping it's temp as I toil away at projects is annoyingly priceless. It has injected an unexpectedly strange joy in my day to day life that makes the absurd price of a cup feel entirely justified. I've not touched another mug in my home since receiving it just about. I just hope the next iteration is a bit smarter and the cost saving measures aren't as apparent.

title: Great concept. Execution and product support . . . not so much.
body: This is a product that is ... frustrating. The concept is fantastic, but the execution doesn't do it justice. It's one of those products that is "pretty good" when it works, but the manufacturer just wasn't able to push it over the edge to being "great." I've had an Ember Mug 2 for almost a year. For the most part it's been fine, although it could use greater battery life when off the charging puck. Lately, however, the mug has been acting up -- turning off randomly, even when sitting on the charging coaster, full of hot coffee; failing to turn itself on when being filled with hot coffee first thing in the morning; and failing to detect that it's been placed on the charging puck, and thus no charging takes place. Unfortunately, customer support via Ember has been, so far, unhelpful. I exchanged a few emails with first-level support ("Make sure it's plugged in," etc., LOL), and after my support inquiry was sent to a "team" at Ember for follow-up...nothing. I think there is a notice on their site that they're very busy, so responses may be delayed, but, well, they need to do better. All in all, a product that's hard to recommend, unfortunately, because when the stars align, it's a pleasure to use. But my mug's lack of reliability is making me start looking elsewhere.

title: Great if you like your coffee black ... BUT
body: OK ... So I waited several months before writing a review. Initial thoughts ... Ember does a Great job keeping your coffee hot! Certainly much better job than some of the inexpensive options (e.g. better than Brookstone per my personal experience). Definitely keeps me from having to reheat coffee in the microwave every 10min ... HOWEVER, the Ember does not solve for one of my key challenges. I tend to drink coffee with Cream & Sugar. And when you re-heat creamy coffee, it tends to burn a layer of milk that sits on the surface (it's terrible ... ruins a good cup of coffee when you drink that muck by accident). And sadly, because the Ember does such a good job keeping coffee hot ... this same phenomenon tends to happen. And more specifically, it tends to happen if you leave those last few sips sit too long (tends to super heat a bit as you get to the bottom of your mug). I'm thinking I could probably try to adjust the Temp setting as I get to the bottom ... but I rarely remember to do that. So all said, Great mug ... but not Perfect. And yes, for the record ... app still kinda stinks. Doesn't happen all the time, but mug often loses Bluetooth sync.

title: It works, just wish it was a little hotter
body: 2nd Edit. I am restoring my original 4-star review (see below for why I dropped it, 1st edit). After using this for several months, even though it doesn’t keep my coffee at a temperature I prefer (much hotter than 145), and I wish it lasted longer than 90 minutes, it has become my go-to mug, especially for morning coffee. The top half of the coffee cools down too fast for me but the bottom half does stay pretty hot, and I like that. I never used to drink a full cup because I hate lukewarm coffee; I just have to drink it a little faster than I want. So back to four stars. Edit: after using the mug for a few weeks, I’ve come back to lower it a star. Really the 145 degrees is just too low as a top temperature and I can’t pop it in the microwave to heat it up because of the components. It takes too long to recharge. I want more than 90 minutes warming time. Taking the base and plugging it in wherever I go isn’t feasible. I really, really want to like this mug and I’ll keep using it (because it was so expensive). I could overlook the other things that bug me if it kept it heated to a much higher temp—160 to 180. This only keeps my coffee at 145 degrees—not hot enough. I noted when the coffee was put in the mug it was 182 degrees (as measured by the blue tooth settings); I wanted it to stay at this temperature, 145 is too low. It only works for 90 minutes. Not long enough for me, I drink my coffee over time. It will stay on longer if you keep it in the charger disk but I don’t have plug ins where I’m normally drinking the brew. So not convenient. Other than that, it does work so I really can’t complain. It meets all the specs it laid out. It was my fault for not realizing 145 degrees isn’t as hot as I’d like it to be. That’s why I give it 4 stars, they didn’t misrepresent at all and it does work. Can’t fault them.

title: It’s ok
body: If your an all day coffee drinker be sure to keep the charging stand close by because it will not stay charged for long. But I love it.

title: 5 Stars ... except for the color red!
body: I bought the red cup for my daughter because she loves the color red. However, she found It's very difficult to see the red/white/green signals on this red cup. I have a black cup like this and the colors show up bright and clear. Otherwise, love these cups. They keep the coffee at a great temperature!

title: Must have for those who like to sip hot coffee
body: Honestly, took me a long time to come around to spending this kind of money on a coffee mug, but Happy Wife Happy Life. It has become a bedtime routine that I make sure this thing is on the charger each night before bed otherwise I know if my wife has to start her day with a "regular" old coffee mug and not one keeping her coffee at the perfect temp, it'll be a rough day. Can't say enough about these guys. We have the travel ones for us both now too.

title: Still my favorite mug, but non-existent customer support.
body: I ended up buying another one of these when the coating wore off on the first one. Probably too expensive, but I tried a different cheaper mug in the interim and did not care for it. As clunky as Ember's app can feel at times, it was infinitely better than that competitor's. Just know that customer service almost never responds, no matter how many times you ping them. Sometimes I wonder if the company is not going to be around much longer, given how absent their customer service seems to be.

title: This is \"That Gift\"!
body: The kids and I gave this to my husband for his birthday and it became a "GOAT" item from the start. The coffee was always hot, no more microwaving it again because I had to take a call or step away for five minutes. I would reccomend that you but the lids that goes with it to make it even last longer. This is one unique item that any coffee drinker or tea drinker MUST have.

title: Totally unnecessary but awesome
body: A totally unnecessary but, at the same time, luxurious amenity. You can set the temperature you want in the app and it will notify you when your beverage has cooled to that temperature and then will keep your beverage at that temperature for over an hour. It may last even longer if you get a lid for it. Would highly recommend this as a gift for a family member or coworker who drinks coffee or tea.

title: Lasted 3 Years, 10 Months
body: Update No. 2:After 3 years and 10 months of about 1000 uses, battery is finally losing ability to charge. time for a new mug. Update: 16 months later I still use the ember mug every day and like it. But something is loose in the charger base. I have to turn it upside down and place the inverted mug underneath it. I guess a wire is loose or something of that sort so electricity only flows with the whole set-up inverted. So I can’t place the mug on the charger to keep my brew hot for a long time. Since I finish off any given dose of Java fairly fast, this is not a problem. I can do at least 2 cups before I have to recharge. I hope the charger doesn’t die completely. Crazy expensive, but Ember uses induction heating to break the 125° barrier. The “hot” plate never gets hot. All the heat goes into the coffee. It holds a healthy 9 oz. Hand wash. Do NOT microwave. I never seriously thought I’d own a Bluetooth coffee mug and be happy I did. The usual run of nearly identical coffee warmers are just miniature hot plates that, for safety reasons, do not dare go over a certain temperature; around 185°. That temperature, transferred to your mug or cup, just can’t keep your coffee more than about 125° tops in a room with normal temperature. That just doesn’t do it for me. I don’t want warm coffee, I want a HOT coffee. In the past – and by the past I mean about a week ago- I would get up literally every three minutes and warm up my cooling coffee in the microwave for 15 seconds. That worked, but it was tedious. With the Ember mug, You download the app, easily pair your mug to the app after pressing the bottom button and set your desired maintenance temperature. In my case that temperature is 145. I would go to 155 if it would let me but 145 is the max and will do. If you’ve poured a cup that is hotter than 145 the temperature will gradually lower, accurately displayed on your phone or tablet screen if you care to look, and when your target temperature is reached you get a little notification and the temperature stays there very reliably. This is so great. No more getting up from the table and doing The microwave thing. You don’t even have to keep it plugged in once it is charged. The ember mug is good for at least a couple of cups of coffee before the battery inside the mug runs out. If you keep it on the little induction plate then there is no limit to the number of times you can refill. You don’t have to drag around a little induction plate with its cord and transformer if you need to switch rooms. Due to its induction style heating, the bottom of the mug does not get hot. The mug knows when liquid has been poured into it and turns on by itself. A neat thing: if you have half an inch of liquid in the mug it somehow knows that the liquid still needs heat. But as soon as the mug is empty, the mug knows the score and turns off. As long as this thing keeps working reliably, as I pray that it will, I will regret the high price less and less as the months go by. So buy buy buy Ember Mug!

title: Proper care to extend the lifespan of your mug
body: For everyone having limited use with this product, you HAVE to first rinse it out, to remove the burnt coffee at the bottom, THEN you need hand dry it with a paper towel, as anything else WILL scratch the base of the mug, causing it more easily (rapidly) burn, limiting it’s productive lifespan. Also the cheapest element is the low-cost, third-rate charging cord. So, if possible, purchase several, as the charging cords WILL rapidly fail, without question.

title: Better than expected.
body: What a great purchase! So far so good. I’m a picky mug drinker- and now I don’t wanna drink from anything else.

title: Great mug and excellent customer service
body: I just love being able to sip my coffee leisurely while this mug keeps it at the perfect temperature. I loved it so much that I bought two more as gifts. I also bought the optional lid to make it easier to carry around and reduce the chances of spilling. The coaster stopped charging the mug after seven months. I emailed Ember and they responded immediately and are sending me a replacement coaster . They were very helpful and made it easy for me. I was very impressed with their customer service.

title: Great mug
body: Ember makes the best mugs and is worth the price over similar brand products..

title: Effective
body: It actually works. It is pricey but highly effective for those of us who sip our coffee and make it last. Coffee stays hot.

title: Great concept with a few limitations - Returned
body: Edited Review: Day 30 I am editing my review after one-month of daily use. My ember mug was buggy. It lost connectivity to my iPhone 15 on ocassion and I had to reset the mug several times. Then the battery life dropped off quite a bit and using it became really frustrating. I tried the trouble-shooting steps recommended by the manufacturer, but nothing seemed to make any difference. I confirmed that the charging base was plugged in and working as the battery displayed in the app as charging. But in the end, I has lucky to get 20 minutes of battery life holding at 142 degrees when not on the charging base. Rather than trying another unit, I decided to return the Mug to Amazon as a defective unit before the return period expired. Original review: I really like the ember Smart Mug. There's really nothing else like it. I enjoy spreading out the pleasure of my first really hot cup of coffee in the morning. There are three flaws that cost two stars in my review. First, the 10oz mug is really too small, and the 14oz mug is too large (particularly since it adds to the weight of the mug). My typical morning brew from an Aeropress is about 9oz, which leave very little room between a dry and wet walk in the dark from my kitchen to my office. Optimally, the mug should be 12oz. YMMV. Second, the Ember App does the job, but is not very flexible. Most importantly, I'd like to be able to add a coffee brew time button with a duration of my choosing. I can set it manually each time, but who wants to do that? The tea timer pre-sets don't work for my brewing process. Also, you can not set the temperature for the mug above 145-F, which is a few degrees below my desired holding temp. Third, and this is the biggest reason for the loss of a star: The price is too darn high. I got mine on sale for $88 ($41 off) during Prime Days in October 2024. A big discount, but frankly I can't justify a price over about $40 for the mug. If you're a coffee or tea geek, then you're probably used to paying high prices for specialized brewing accessories and other coffee/tea kitsch, but this mug is priced only for the most indulgent of coffee/tea enthusiasts. Don't get me wrong, its a nifty thing to have. It's nice looking and functions well (within it's limitations). Battery life appears to be good out of the box - exactly as advertised. I haven't had it long enough to comment on durability, but I'd suggest treating it with kid gloves as much as possible. Hand wash and dry, but be careful not to drop it because I'm pretty sure the handle or cup rim won't survive the fall to a tile or wood floor.

title: Like it
body: Like that it heats to 150. I do have to be watchful, tho, cuz it will turn off easily. Otherwise works very well.

title: Love my hot coffee....but its short lived
body: No doubt about it, I do love my Ember mug. I love how it keeps my coffee hot without having to nuke it or drink from a chunky thermo tumbler. I'll do that for work. But when I'm home relaxing this mug adds a lot of enjoyment to the hot beverage experience. I love being able to set my perfect temperature through the app. Drinks stay hot for a long time, even off the charger. But it does have its downsides. First is the cost. It was a treat for me to purchase this and I thought long and hard about choosing this or a knockoff. I decided to just spend the extra and go with the original. Prices are still pretty high across the board and I think Ember is probably still the choice I'd make, but I'm open to looking at others. As the instructions state, this mug has to be hand washed and don't use metal utensils in it. I do both of these things and after 6 months, its still looking pretty good. I managed to nick the ceramic around the lip when I bumped it with a knife in the sink, but it hasn't effected its use. The biggest disappointment is that the charging coaster stopped working making this a mug that doesn't keep your coffee warm nor can you reheat in it. There are e little spring loaded contacts on the coaster and one of them doesn't spring up anymore. I believe support is going to replace it but if not, its nearly $40 to replace. I'm hoping prices come down on both the set and the charging coasters. They are really a wonderful treat if you've got the budget for it.

title: Works well, if not so overpriced would give a 4.5 star review, I have and have gifted many. SILLY$$$
body: If you have $$$ go for it, aside from price I love it and cant live without the emug. Have tried other brands. This is like a 4 year review have had EMBER 1 2 10oz and 14, and have the new 6 oz ones. Get the 14 10 OZ is silly. Batt life is better in Mug2s PROS: + Works well. indeed holds your drink at a precise temp between 120 and 145 F ( I like 136 for black coffee) +Keeps bev warm to hot for a long time. Time depends on ambient temp. and chosen temp, initial temp of bev (but have not found it to be as long as advertised, and does not stay warm indefinitely on coaster) +Nice quality for the most part +good textable tech support (have had several charge coasters replaced that's a flaw I will mention below) + Nice 'materials, I find the cup easy to clean, I only drink black coffee, so a simple rinse, a sponge bath every so often. +turns of when finished w/ bev. MEH +/- The app is a nice one once you have it paired, you can set your desired temp and charge the color light, and see the current temp, while this is neato, I'd prefer it required no app. Once set up the app isn't required +/-The handle gets the job done, the competitor NEXTMUG has a nicer feel and shape, NEXTMUG is also more aesthetically pleasing IMO and colors and tops DO NOT COST MORE. It doesn't function quite as well as Ember, but its a close runner up that is less, but still IMO too expensive unless you catch it on sale. The cheaper competition I tested THERMACUP was a fail, if redesigned and still offered at 60 dollars, could be a winner. I reviewed this contender as well. +/- Packaging, there is too much of it. NEGATIVES - PRICE -Charge cradle (If liquid gathers causes electrolysis and the charge pins fail) have had to warrantee several cradles) -PRICE AGAIN different colors cost far more, the travel mug is stooopid expensive -overpriced "accesories" again, check out price of 12V car "lighter plug" adapter -The top cost extra way extra -not usb C, yeat another "proprietary" charge block.......I find this particularly annoying. Will update in the future Conclusion: This is a functional product that is marketed as a luxury item such as many apple products. A 60 dollar USB C chargeable with all included would be rad. This is not a tesla. I freaking love it but it is NOT A GOOD VALUE for most. At 120 bucks it should be dishwasher safe. Like I said I'm a black coffee guy. My dad likes lots of milk and drinks slowly, the heated mug curdles it, and becomes hard to clean. Many reviewers have said the coatings aren't durable, I 100% disagree. They are scrubbing or stirring hard. or using one of those frothing wands. That will screw up most cups, be they smart or dumb.

title: Does what it says it does
body: Look if your goal is to have 1 cup of coffee over the span of an hour and keep it nice and hot this is it. The battery really only lasts about an hour and some change. So don't expect back to back cups unless you're going to be resting the mug on its charging dock. If you work from home this is perfect. Personally I just drink a cup in the morning in my living room and it takes me about an hour. I'm okay with the mug being basically dead after one cup cause I'm done by then. If I want multiple cups of tea tho I do have to move the charging dock out to where I am which kinda sucks. Overall I like this mug a lot. 1 knock against it is having to use an app to turn it on and off. Kinda annoying

title: Best mug for people who take a while to finish tea or coffee
body: Works great so far. The size was perfect and my gf loved it as a gift!

title: Just does what it says, barely
body: I had very high hopes for this mug. I almost returned it. Pro:1- It does just what it says, keep the coffee warm for 90 minutes or so. 2-I like the feel of it, I was afraid it would feel like plastic, but it doesn't. Cons: 1-The app is very nice, but won't stay connected. If you do anything else with you phone you not only get disconnected from the mug, you must pair it again! Every time, every day! Quite annoying, makes the app pretty much useless. 2- When using the mug, sitting it on the charging disc keeps it hot, but does not recharge the mug. The mug will only recharge if it's empty. So even if you spend time at your desk with the mug on the charging disk, you only have the 90 minutes of walking around time. I will use it during breakfast, but then there are fewer minutes later to be moving around with hot coffee. The bottom line is it does what it says well, as long as you are aware of the limitations. I took it down one star for the annoying app issues.

title: Keeps hot
body: Great product. Keeps the coffee hot.

title: Charging Coaster Dead, No Support From Ember
body: Ember mugs are great when they work. However, the charging coaster just stopped working for no apparent reason. I contacted support, and they replied asking for more information, which I immediately supplied them. My mug is well within the warranty period. After my reply nothing. They have ghosted me for over a month now, even after more emails from me asking for a reply. They don't have a support phone number listed on their site. These mugs are pricey - what good is a warranty from a company that doesn't respond to customers asking for support?

title: Stylish, Smart, but Needs a Few Tweaks!
body: I bought the 14-ounce rose gold Ember, and I’m loving it! It’s got a sleek design, a satisfying weight, and the customizable LED light is a fun bonus. But a few tweaks could make it even better: First, it really needs a travel lid. The open top drains the battery faster, so including a lid would make a huge difference. Also, the app can be a bit finicky—it sometimes disconnects, even when the cup is right next to my phone. Not a dealbreaker, but still frustrating! On the bright side, the charging base is stylish, but it would be amazing if it held its own charge so I could use it on the go and it honestly doesn’t work keeping the cup on the charging base. It still drains the battery. It doesn’t charge it if it’s on which is a major bummer as it takes 2+ hours to charge the cup again and I like multiple cups of tea, back to back. And Ember, please switch the bulky plug to USB! Not only would that be more portable, but it’d let me plug the charger into my laptop or a charging block for easy charging on the go. Overall, it’s a great product with room for a few small changes that would make it perfect! The battery life is my major issue and it not charging while on, on the charging block.

title: Great to keep coffee hot
body: My husband loves this mug- he can keep his coffee warm all morning. He loves that he can choose the coffee temp in the app. Definitely reccomend for any coffee drinker.

title: I can't imagine going back to drinking my coffee without it!
body: I work from home and can easily get distracted and spend hours sipping on my morning coffee. It's made that SUCH a better experience. The mug itself feels robust, but not too heavy. Absolutely does the job of keeping my drinks at the right temperature. My gripes with it are two minor things. First, the use of an app (I think most would agree) is such an unnecessarily convoluted part of this product. The mug is usable without it, but you are not able to adjust the temperature. These are controls that easily could have been integrated into the mug itself. I can understand wanting to create the simplest/cleanest looking product you can, but it seems far more likely that the push for an app here is motivated by opportunities for marketing and data. I use mine without it with no issues. The second issue I have with it is price. It's worth every penny to me, but realistically, the price is a barrier to me having multiple. Ember is the most tried and true brand and I don't doubt their quality, so I stuck with it, but most other similar cups land at significantly cheaper price points.

title: great gift!
body: Got this for my wife for 7 year anniversary! She loves it! Beautiful design, keeps the coffee at the her preferred temperature, and super easy to use and set up!

title: Great for ones who just want to sip coffee!
body: Purchased this for a family friend who always drinks coffee but it of course gets cold. He liked how high tech it was with the app and how user friendly it is. The cup was easy to clean and it stayed the temperature you set it to. Great gift or having it for yourself!

title: Bluetooth disconnecting
body: I had originally purchase the Next Mug and i was happy with it. However I wanted to be able to fine tune the temperature of the drink. The Next Mug has three settings. So I return the Next Mug decided to try the Ember Mug. I like the fact that the temperature can be customized with the app. Once the temperature is set it remains until you change it. However it you want to change it you need the app. And the app needs to be connected via Bluetooth. And that's the problem. I am constantly reconnecting the mug to Bluetooth. If the mug has disconnected from the app then you don't get a notification of when the temperature has been reached. I will keep the mug because it works but I wish the would fix the disconnection problem. I have read online and I am not the only person with this issue.

title: Keep that morning coffee warm and welcome.
body: I love my ember mug. It works to keep your drink at your preferred temperature. It's easy to clean even with the connecting metal work on the bottom that has to stay capable of handling an electrical flow. Already purchased another for a different location.

title: Great but has flaws
body: I have 2 of these mugs, this one I purchased from Amazon, which is white ceramic. The other from Costco and it's a silver metal. The Costco mug is my fair superior as it recognizes when I'm using it, automatically knows my preferred temp and i rarely need to use the app. The white mug from Costco always needs me to turn it on via the app and the charge does not last very long so I need to use the charge the whole time. Both work, it's just one is better. On another note, I don't think I could go back to regular coffee mugs. I love that my coffee stays as the perfect temperature the entire time I'm drinking it, even if it that takes 2 hours. When I need to replace, I will likely buy from Costco again and choose the metal cup.

title: Lost support
body: I’ve had my 14 oz cup since early 2023. I lost Bluetooth pairing about 4 times. I’ve tried everything to get it back. I’ve written Ember but o answer after a couple weeks. Last year their support was good. I’m afraid they no longer are providing support. I’m ordering another brand that you can set the temp without Bluetooth.

title: Love this thing!
body: I bought this for use at my office, which has a fairly long walk to the closest microwave, so I don't keep having to heat up my coffee. I've had it for about 2 months and it works perfectly. Even though I'm not really a "smart device" person, I set the temperature on the app once and have not had to fuss with that since. The device seems to know whether or not there's liquid in the cup, so it turns on when I pour in my coffee and turns off when I'm done. I keep it on the charging plate pretty much at all times, so I haven't really tested the battery life. The reason I am giving it 4 stars instead of 5 is because of one little design annoyance that the designers didn't quite think through: the plug. I would think a small device like this would have just a regular old plug, but instead the plug is a box that extends 3 inches below where it actually plugs in, much like I would expect from a larger electronic device. Because I'm using this at my desk with a power strip (where my monitor also has a large plug), it prevents me from being able to plug everything in at once. I would suggest updating the design so the plug swings out to the side rather than down.

title: Warm coffee for hours
body: Ordered a used cup, said it was in very good condition. Upon arrival, I smelt a burnt order eminating from the package. In short, the cup did not function at all, it was burned up. But, I requested a replacement and it arrived a few days later. It was in excellant condition and works perfectly, so far. I am very pleased. However, they should check the functionality of their product before shipping it.

title: Decent enough and satisfied
body: I really like this mug. It is sturdy, a good size, easy to hand wash, and easy to use (charger, app, etc are all easy to set up and use regularly). There are a few things I don't love: - the battery life is not great. An hour or so. You almost always have to keep the charger near. - the liquid in the bottom of the cup is always hotter than the top, so the heat isn't super even - the mug disconnects from the app often, so the notifications are not consistent either. - it ain't cheap! I am constantly worried about dropping it or breaking it because it's not like a normal mug. Overall it is a good and I will keep using it daily.

title: Glitchy product. Horrible support. Good concept. Regrets.
body: Great concept. Expensive. Glitchy - sometimes it does not turn on, or does not recognize the cup is empty - or full. I’ve had to delete and reinstall the app several times - then re-pair it. Tiresome. Support is atrocious. They must have recently replaced any people they had with AI-bots, poorly trained ones at that. I emailed them about a problem with their charging plate (they know this is a problem because they list it in their drop-down menu - where the electrode charging prongs get caught/trapped/recessed - and then don’t make contact with the mug - so it can’t charge). After getting an auto-responder email that they got my message, I had to chase them down 8 days later trying to find out why they haven’t done anything. “Sorry, we don’t have any record of your message”. What?? So I forwarded their response back to them - “oh, you must have been affected when we recently switched our service ticketing process”. Their website says they support using Facebook Messenger - so I send them all the information again via that method (picture of the faulty unit; picture of the serial number, proof of purchase/receipt from Amazon). They respond with ‘we need you to email this to us’. F! Then why the H do you say you offer FB Messenger as a support channel? So I email them (again), and their bot - ‘Ellie’ replies “we need your purchase date, receipt, retailer, etc” - which I had already included originally AND in my last email as a PDF and a JPG image. So I sent it all again this morning (July 1, 2025). That’s where this sad story is at as I write… When it works, all is well. So they get 2 stars, not 1. Updates to follow… Buyer beware.

title: Great idea, wish the charge lasted a little longer
body: Works really well but charge doesn't last long.

title: Long Charging time.
body: It takes a long time to charge. the battery start wearing down as soon as as it's off the charger, even when hot liquids are put into the cup. It would last about an hour which is good but it takes longer to charge than the heating time. It's good that it keeps tea or coffee warm at a stated temperature but the mug is not cheap. it takes more than 2 hours to get the battery back to 100%.

title: Hot coffee for hours! But charging coaster only lasted a year.
body: I love this mug! With the ember lid on it keeps my coffee hot for hours - it's a game changer for a busy mom. However the charging coaster stopped working after one year. I contacted Ember and they said it was still under warranty and gave me a code to order a free coaster, which I ordered, but then it was never shipped and they won't reply to my emails! I'm super disappointed with their customer service and now I can't charge my mug unless I buy a new charger....

title: I bought two.
body: Nice to know you can walk away from your cup and know that it will be hot when you get back to it. Just wish it was a bit larger.

title: Great but wore out
body: It worked great for quite a long time but the heater did end up going bad after about a year of my husband yawing it of course when I said use he USED that coffee cup hard.

title: Perfect for me
body: I love these mugs! I like my hot drinks to keep their temperature. Very useful for when you want to slowly enjoy your drink or if you get distracted/interrupted!

title: Save your warrantee and be prepared for pin issues
body: Keep your paperwork! My Mug got harder and harder to charge over time (less than 1 year).. One of the pins on the charger was stuck down and would not pop up. Contacted mfgr - it was still under warrantee. They replaced it but now the new one has done the same thing - but this one out of warrantee period. I'll be trying a different brand next time. too expensive to replace every year.

title: Second Time's a charm
body: I had purchased the original version of the ember back 5 years ago. Unfortunately, after prolonged use, it has lost a lot of its charge, and could only keep the drink hot for barely 30 mins off the charging saucer (it originally could go for more than an hour). So, I decided to bite the bullet and buy this second version. Functionally, it is the same as the first version. Same size, same features, same wonky app (personally, I would recommend just setting the temperature at its highest in the initial app set up, then disconnecting it and never using the app again, for your sanity's sake). The mug seems to have a slightly thicker build than the first version, though I can't tell if that's actually true, or if I had just stripped so much material from washing the original over the course of 5 years that I made it lighter. The battery lasts for about an 1.5 hours, which apparently is 30 mins longer than the first version. If I were to make a recommendation between the two, I'd say to get whichever you can get for cheaper, assuming they are both new out of the box (don't get a used one, since you'll risk it having lost some of its charge). The extra 30 minutes is nice, but like the first version, you can put it on the saucer where it will both heat and charge at the same time, making it a moot point to most people. I'm docking a star because I don't agree with the price. I feel there should have been either a more significant batter charge (up to two hours, or having the ability to charge faster so that you don't have to keep it on the saucer), or some other additional features to warrant keeping it this high. From a functional standpoint however, it works like a charm (outside of the app, of course).

title: fine if you drink plain coffee and don't use the app.
body: Great concept. Would be nearly perfect for people who drink their tea/ coffee plain. If you add milk or sweetener however it will burn and create a film on top of your drink. The Bluetooth connection becomes unrecognized by the app within a week, and the re-pairing process is a headache. There are options to edit the pre-defined temperature settings, but the app forgets your settings after 24hrs and reverts to temps that scald add ins. All in all: it would be fine if you drank your beverage pain and didn't use the app. Do NOT recommend the copper-like one as it has a coating that is nearly impossible to clean. Other colors are fine to clean (we have the copper, sage, and lilac ones)

title: I'm giving up on the Ember Mug
body: After using Ember mugs for a year or two, I'm finally fed up. Here's the letter I wrote to the company. (By the way, their customer support is almost nonexistent.): Dear Ember, I’m fed up with Ember. I’ve bought at least a dozen of your mugs. (Many have been gifts.) And I have several at home. There are two major problems: [1] they keep breaking (i.e. they stop working), and [2] your customer service is the WORST I've ever encountered. Please note the exchange of emails below. I wrote on March 5 and it took until April 29 to get a response from you! It was nice that you ultimately offered me a replacement coaster, but I couldn’t wait fifty days—and didn’t think you’d ever respond—so I had already purchased a new one. Now, my mug won’t heat up properly. (This has happened in the past with other mugs of yours.) Although the app says my coffee is at 144 degrees, I’d guess that it’s more like 125 or 130. I’ve done all the usual troubleshooting many times: delete the Ember app and reinstall it, turn off the mug, delete it from Bluetooth, reconnect, etc. So far no luck. I’ve switched the heating pad, but that doesn’t make any difference, either. In short, the mug no longer works. I’ve loved having the Ember mug (when it works) but the problems are just too great. I don’t even need the app—it’s a nuisance. I ALWAYS want my coffee and tea at 145 degrees. (I’d prefer 150 but you don’t go that high. NextMug does.) Anyway, because my mug isn’t working I’m sending away for overnight delivery of a NextMug. Its reviews on Amazon are just as good as Ember's. Assuming that it works okay, that will become my go-to mug, and it will be the gift I give to friends, and colleagues. I’m a loyal person and rarely switch brands—of anything. Unfortunately, the poor quality of your products and the abysmal service has left me no choice. Sincerely,

title: some like it hot
body: My wife loves her coffee hot. This stops her from going to the microwave to reheat her coffee every few minutes.

title: Best Christmas present!
body: LOVE this mug and use it every morning!! I can set the temp or my coffee and see it steaming for an hour while I sip it and read.

title: Fantastic product
body: The Ember, 14 oz coffee cup is exactly what I was hoping for. I have used it for a week, and it has performed as I would expect. I get roughly 1 1/2 hours of hot coffee in the morning, which fits my life style - I am retired, so I have more leisurely time in morning. I keep the charging base next to the coffee pot and since they are both black, they look great. The design of the coffee mugs is excellent. The fit and feel are just right. The rubberized bottom and the overall weight are matched well with how I like a sturdy, yet thin walled design. The freedom of not having to have the charging base act as a warming plate is joyous. Once I finish, I just rinse, towel dry, and place back on charging station. In the afternoon, I switch to tea, with an occasional single cup of coffee and the EMBER is ready to go. It take’s approximately 2 1/2 hours to recharge and I have not found that to be an issue. The APP is simple and for those who like playing with the temp, is useful. The good news is that if you don’t want to use the APP, the product is completely seamless. The indicator light bar is almost unnoticeable (that is good) and switches from green (charged) to white when in use, to warm red when needing to be recharged. EXCELLENT PRODUCT - worth the money!

title: As described, but...
body: (April 11, 2024) So far so good. Have used most days of the week for the last 2 weeks and it is working exactly as described. Pros: The app is easy to use and has a lot of nice features. I like the customization option for the front light and that it shows the battery life. The cup itself is very easy to clean by hand, no staining at all if it sits unrinsed overnight. It will stay at a default temp of 135 F° if you don't use the app or don't have your phone (which isn't as warm as it sounds depending on the drink, but it is a very intuitive feature). Neutral: The cup will stay charged for 90 minutes without the charging plate which is good for someone who is at a desk, but not practical for on the go. However if you are drinking coffee, the flavor is best within 2 hours of brewing. Con: Only downside is when it's off it's not very self insulating. Your drink goes cold fast like a regular mug. You have to keep it on to keep your beverage warm. Also, the lid was an add on. For the price you'd expect it to include the lid. Overall giving 4 stars right now and will update after longer use. *** (UPDATE July 12, 2024) Took about an hour to get the temperature up to the hottest setting today (the fire symbol). For reference: the battery is at 77% and I always keep it on the charging plate while heating up or until just before it reaches a full charge. I've only had this mug since March and it shouldn't be this fickle after only a few months of use. Will report back here again if anything else changes.

title: Cozy Mornings!
body: I love this mug. I work in a home office and easily get distracted with emails and I love how this mug keeps my coffee the perfect temp even if I get distracted with work. I will say, the battery doesn't last too long if you're not keeping it on the coaster, but since I primarily got this for an office it's not a deal breaker for me. If it's away from the coaster, it may only stay warm for around an hour, which is still a help in my opinion. Connecting the mug with the app every day is slightly annoying but not a big deal. I thought it would just stay connected after the first time but when I don't open the app and pair it every morning it doesn't get hot, only takes like 5 seconds though. Always room for improvement but overall I really like the mug. I've heard mixed reviews on the durability, so I'm curious how it will hold up over time, I also bought the protection plan just in case, but so far so good.

title: Reset it before returning it.
body: My husband and I are a bit fanatical about keeping hot beverages hot. We have a shelf full of thermal mugs that work for about 15 minutes and that's it, then we're off to the microwave. Again and again. We've never spent this kind of money for the "luxury" of heat, but I needed to get my husband something for Valentine's. It worked perfectly out of the box for him and still does. So I had to have one. However, my first mug never held the temperature, especially on the Keurig beverages straight out of the coffeemaker. I returned it and took a chance on a second mug. Same problem. However, this time I remembered the instructions (that always helps!) for resetting the mug: Press on the button on the bottom for a full seven seconds until it changes color. I did that and lo' and behold it works perfectly! I haven't tested the battery life because a) I generally sit in one place while having my coffee next to the charger and b) I only have one cup a day and finish that before the battery ever dies. There are a few things I'd recommend to the manufacturer: The smaller mug says it holds 10 oz, which is true BUT you shouldn't plan on moving it while it's full. It goes almost to the very top. I got the optional lid, which goes down into the liquid when it's full, but does a great job of helping to keep it hot. The button on the bottom is very difficult to push down and could cause a little pain for folks with arthritis. Also, I'd like another five degrees of heat, up to 150, please. Should be an easy software update. Overall, this is what I hoped for.

title: Stays hot coffee
body: Bought as a gift for my mom, who is constantly microwaving her coffee in the morning. She loves it and no longer needs the microwave!

title: Keeps coffee at an ideal temperature for an hour
body: It might seem expensive but since I was previously throwing most coffee away because it became cold in the cup, I think this will pay for itself in a year. But, meanwhile I can enjoy a mug of coffee that maintains its temperature through several sections of the morning newspaper

title: Not good if you use creamer in coffee
body: Does a good job keeping drink at desired temp, so that’s nice. However, unless you’re drinking only black coffee or tea (no cream), it gets kinda gross. I use half & half in my coffee and after a while, there’s a yucky film that builds up on the drink’s surface. Kinda squashes the joy of having a heated mug.

title: Greatest way to keep your coffee hot
body: I purchased this for my husband after I was gifted one. It is great for your morning coffee or when you are leisurely drink coffee or tea. It will keep your beverage hot for a couple of hours.

title: Nice cup
body: I really love this cup. I get busy working and end up sipping on my coffee for a while and I love that it keeps it nice and warm. I took the star off because your coffee does get a film if you don’t have a lid and you use creamer. Also, I have the white one and within the first two weeks it’s stained on the inside. And the battery life could use improvement.

title: A Necessity
body: Before buying the ember mug 2, I didn't even know smart mugs existed, and then I thought it was kind of silly, a frivilous use of money considering the cost. These mugs are expensive! I was even skeptical about having to use an app to operate the mug. I try to keep as many "smart" devices out of my house as possible. But then I started using the Ember mug every morning and it has become a necessity, at least during winter. My "new" house is 130 years old and none of the previous owners added insulation to the attic or exterior walls. They also never installed central heat and air. Until I can get heat installed this winter, we use space heaters. When it's 35 degrees outside, it's 35 degrees inside. But I can sip on my coffee for an hour, even in my cold house, and it stays hot! The ember mug has essentially been a lifesaver for me this winter, which is why I say it's a necessity. And now I can't imagine living without it, except in the summer when it gets really hot here in the south and I'll be making iced coffee. I also bought the recommended lid to help keep the heat in and use less energy. So far, I am loving the Ember mug and having hot coffee to keep me warm during this frigid winter so far!

title: Best purchase in a long time
body: I ordered the Ember and read the reviews after ordering. I was a little hesitant after reading some of the negative stuff in reviews. I don't usually write reviews, but I like this product so much, I thought I'd give my input to help others out. -I work from a home office and found that my coffee tea gets cold before I finish it because I take my time while working. -It is even better than I expected to have drinks stay at the temperature I want. With the app, you can adjust the heat to the way you like it. The last sip is as good as the first. -I didn't have any trouble setting up the cup and app. I followed some guy's advice in the reviews to make sure the cup is fully charged before setting up the app and followed the instructions. That worked great for me. -I haven't had any of the issues some seem to have had with the Bluetooth disconnecting (I use and iPhone mini). It's been very solid. Twice in the first two weeks, it seemed to not be heating though it said it was connected. I simply turned off the heater through the app and turned it on again both times and it worked fine. -There's some talk about not getting the charging stand wet. I am careful with that, making sure that I haven't sloshed and gotten the bottom of the cup wet. Not a big deal at all to pay attention to that. I don't walk around with normal mugs wet on the bottom anyway. -One review I read complained about the length of time the mug holds a charge. I generally, sit it on the charger by my workstation, so it's always charging. If you do that, no problem with charge. A few times I've taken the mug other places in the house. It easily goes 1.5 hours and my guess is it'd approach ~2 hours, maybe a bit more. That's plenty long for me. And I can recharge it and use again later. It's definitely no iPhone in terms of battery life, but works for what I do. If you expect it to keep something warm for 8 hours, I don't think it'll do that. -It's a very solid-feeling mug that's got a really nice feel. Good heft, some sort of traction rubber on the bottom so it stays put where you set it down. -I was hesitant reading some of the negative reviews relative to the price. I am 100% happy with this purchase. One of the best things I've gotten recently and makes a fun difference in my days. Highly recommend it.

title: I hate to love it!
body: I am now on my third Ember 10oz coffee mug over the last six years and getting ready to buy my fourth. I have come to terms that I am going to have to buy this item every couple of years because coffee inevitably get into the base unit causing it to corrode and stop charging the cup. One can replace the base unit for about $30, but the metal on the bottom of the cup corrodes with the base over time. Nonetheless, I LOVE having a cup of coffee at my favorite temperature! Instead of drinking coffee all day like I did in the past, I have two 10oz cups that I can sip on all morning. When this company cracks wireless charging technology for the Ember, it will be a "must have" product in everyone's home.

title: Great buy
body: I'm giving this 4 stars because the battery doesn't last through 2 cups of coffee. Other than that, this is an awesome buy. Can heat my cup up from my phone and heats to the perfect temperature and fast.

title: Just meh
body: I've had this mug for almost a year. I use it almost every day. PROS White is very clean looking, modern Temperature control is awesome CONS App is trash - When I first got the mug I was able to log in and set the temperature. I have never been able to successfully connect to my mug again. Now the temperature is slowly decreasing and my coffee is not as hot as I want. It, can't connect with the mug in the app to change that. 🫩 The white coffee mug is now stained coffee color on the inside, I've tried soaking the inside with hot soapy water and washing it everyday. It's still stained. The saucer looking component has to be plugged in and the plug is rather large, it's awkward on my kitchen counter. Lastly, 10 oz is too small! Overall, I would try a different brand if I bought again.

title: Update: DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY
body: My FIRST mug began failing, so I returned it for a replacement. The replacement worked 3 days past the return window, so I am stuck with a mug that doesn't work, and Ember's customer support is worthless. They simply don't respond. I wonder how many of the other 5 star reviewers have had the same experience as I but didn't bother to update their reviews. I ordered this 14 ounce Ember induction cup believing it would not work as advertised, and I would have to return it. Silly me! After using it the first time, I ordered two more for my son and his wife for Christmas. I like being able to set my own perfect temperature. I pretty much use it at my desk while working in the mornings. When I do take it away from its warmer plate, my coffee stays the perfect temperature for about 80 minutes. I researched these types of cups using online review sites, and every single one of them said that the Ember is by far the best at keeping coffee hot for the longest time. Others were less expensive, but I decided not to waste my money on a cheaper brand that had meh reviews. I was able to get a great deal (40% off) in a Christmas deal, which made the cups somewhat affordable. I highly recommend this Ember cup, especially for coffee lovers!

title: It needs a larger battery, but I like it.
body: I like my coffee hot. I have a mug warmer on my desk that can be set to 131, 149, or 167 degrees, and I find the highest setting to be perfect. I take a while to drink a cup of coffee, and almost never finish a cup (or repeatedly microwave it) because it is gets cold. I hoped this Ember mug might keep the coffee warm for my first couple of cups of the day, when I'm not at my desk using the mug warmer. It doesn't. The highest temperature setting for the Ember mug is 145 degrees; cooler than I prefer but still acceptably hot. But I'm guessing that the 80 minutes they promise is based on a lower temperature setting. The mug shows a white light when your selected temperature is reached. Since the coffee is hotter than 145 degrees when I first fill the cup, it immediately glows white. When the white light starts flashing, that means the Ember mug is warming the coffee to maintain the temperature, and when it turns red, that means the battery has died and it is not warming anything. The light usually goes to red just as I'm finishing my first cup. No doubt it draws a lot of current from a battery to run a heating coil, and more so for a higher temperature. At least for my slow coffee drinking ways, it apparently needs a bigger battery. So why do I still like it? I know that my first cup of coffee for the day will be hot from start to finish, without multiple trips to the microwave.

title: Almost RETURNED it, made 1 change, and now completely WORTH THE PRICE!
body: First, the Ember Smart Mug does exactly what it says it will do. So it would not be fair to give it less than 5 stars. If you set the temp on your app to 145, it will keep your drink at 145. It is easy to use. Once you have paired it to your phone initially, you never have to think about it again. Just hand wash it, put it on the charging coaster, and it will ready the next day. BUT DOES IT SOLVE THE COLD COFFEE PROBLEM? Ember is expensive. For that price, it should ensure I never have cold coffee again. Unfortunately, that is not entirely true. Ember will keep your coffee hot, but only until the battery runs out. For the 14 oz mug, this takes around 1.5 hours when fully charged. Like most coffee drinkers, you might down the first cup in 15 minutes, the second over the next 1/2 hour, but that last cup may sit on your desk for an hour or more while you're busy. Then when you get a moment to take a sip; ugh, cold disgusting coffee. So the WHOLE story is that Ember will keep the first and 2nd cups piping hot, provided you finish them within the 1.5 hour battery life. But honestly, I didn't search for a $120+ coffee cup for the first 2 cups of the day. I searched for a way to keep that 3rd cup hot, for an hour or more if possible. My first attempt to work around the short battery life was to use a standard coffee cup for the first 2 cups, and then use Ember for the 3rd. This did help, and the 3rd cup stayed hot longer. But not long enough for me. And should I really have to jump through extra hoops for a coffee cup that costs over $120?? I didn't think so and had made up my mind to return it. DON'T GIVE UP, THERE IS HOPE! Thankfully, before giving up and sending Ember back, I searched on Ember's website for ways to extend the battery life. And there I found the HOLY GRAIL... EMBER can heat your coffee while sitting on the "newly redesigned charging coaster", WITHOUT using your battery! WHY didn't I find this sooner! All I had to do was move the charging coaster to my desk, instead of next to the coffee pot. Clouds parted, stars aligned, and now my 3rd cup will stay hot all day if I want. And I don't notice any difference with the coaster on my desk. It is so slim and sleek, I don't even notice it sitting in that spot that was reserved for my coffee cup anyway. FINALLY, HOT COFFEE ALL DAY! I would give Ember 6 starts if I could, for finally solving the cold coffee dilemma. Thank you Ember for such an amazing product. Might be worth HIGHLIGHTING the ability to keep your cup hot for hours provided the charging coaster is used.

title: best thing is your last sip is as hot as the first
body: Seven days of use so tentative review but it all works as it's supposed to. The software has not required re-pairing to the Ember. Being able to walk around with the cup and not have it too tethered to a heating coaster is a good feature. The battery charge is enough for leisurely sipping all the way through the mug and a refill. But in my experience the charge always runs out during the third mug, so now I tend to keep the coaster near and use it some of the time. 145 F turns out to be hot enough but just barely. Didn't realize I favoured the hotter temps of coffee drinking but apparently so. If you add cream, you'll find it drops the temp a lot so if your 2nd or 3rd cup is coming out of the pot not as hot as your first, and then you add cream, your temp will be 130F or so. The cup is not designed to heat your coffee from a lower temp. For me it's managed to get a up up from 130F to 145F but slowly, and I've taken to heating water in the kettle to pre-heat the Ember for each cup. It's winter and the house is colder so maybe this will be less necessary in other seasons. The heating function doesn't turn off immediately as soon as it's empty so it does tend to cook some coffee onto the bottom surface after your last sip, but I've found it to be easy to clean. I had sipper mug lids that fit this cup already in my cupboard so you may already have something that fits. A lid does improve the heating efficiency a lot if you're trying to raise the temp after adding cream. So, overall I use this the same way as I used any other cup, still pre-heating with water from the kettle etc., but the difference is the last sip is as hot as the first sip. That alone makes it worth it.

title: Love my Ember cup!!
body: My second cup. I dropped my first one and I missed it so much that I immediately ordered another one ... will not drink out of a regular coffee cup unless it's absolutely necessary! I love it!!!!

title: Battery Operated Coffee Mug
body: OK, so I have tried coffee mug heating plates and since most mugs are concave on the bottom, they don't work very well. I saw an Ember mug add and decided to give it a try. It's way over priced, but I drink coffee every day so I thought I would give it a try. My experience started with having trouble unboxing the mug. The outer cardboard was so tight I had troubles sipping it off to get to the main box to open. The Ember mug does work to keep coffee warm enough. I like that the app let's you select any temperature up to 145F. The mug size is OK, feels solid and like it is made out of ceramic. Size wise it is better than some mugs but could be a couple of ounces bigger. The handle on the Mug is good and is bigger than most, which I hate small handles on most mugs. The sides of the handle are a little sharp. It would be more comfortable if the sides were rounded a little more, minor issue. You can't use the mug unless you have a cell phone with bluetooth. The phone app is terrible, the most disappointing aspect of this mug. The color LED light on the mug is way overly complicated. You can make the color "your" color, but it still uses other colors. When charging or in use it does not use the color you selected, it is either red, green or white. The only time I see my color is when I first pick up the mug. Since I drink coffee all morning, I need the charger at my desk. On the phone app the level of charge should be on the main screen, instead it is hidden in a setup screen that you can only get to from one screen. The app needs all of 1 or 2 screens, instead it has like 8 screens and makes it a hassle to operate. The UI is also not intuitive and I am always having to undo an action because I clicked on something wrong. For the price they should at least include a cover to help reduce heat loss and help with battery life. And you really need a second charger for the kitchen for after I wash the mug and would like to leave it near my coffee maker to recharge. Instead I have to store it in my office to recharge which is inconvenient the next morning. I really like the concept, but based on the price and what you get and the pathetic phone app I am giving this product 3 stars. I would give it 4 stars it the app wasn't so bad. I would give 5 stars if they made the phone app more user friendly, included a cup cover and a second charger for under $100. For now it is an overpriced convenience with hassles.

title: Wonderful mug with room for improvement
body: I love this mug! I use it every day! It’s only gets four stars for three reasons: Issue 1: once your mug shuts off and your coffee gets cold, you are unable to simply place the mug back on the coaster, charge the mug, and warm it up. The mug just doesn’t sense any liquid in it since the liquid inside is the same temp as the mug at this point. To get the mug to then reheat the coffee back up to temp, I have to nuke it in a different mug for 30 secs so once it is poured into the now-charging-on-the-coaster mug it will sense it and begin to get it to your preferred temp. Takeaway lesson from this problem: don’t let your mug run out of battery. If the auto turn off happens while your mug is charging, you just take off the mug, wait a beat, and put it back on and reconnect. Issue 2: the mug doesn’t automatically connect to your phone. It’s silly really, but it makes a difference when all other Bluetooth devices I own are remembered and auto connect when they are turned on and activated. When I forgot to connect my mug I don’t get the notification that it has reached my desired temp and I wait a lot longer than I should before remembering that it wasn’t connected this time. Pulling up the app and connecting and seeing the temp it’s at isn’t hard, but it would be wondering if it connected on its own it would be so much easier and user friendly, especially for people who aren’t as tech savvy who may have received this as a gift. Takeaway: hopefully this is in development for the next iteration of the mug Issue 3: metal utensils will leave little marks on your beautiful white mug. I don’t know if anyone who doesn’t automatically grab a metal teaspoon to stir their coffee/tea with or to hold their teabags down with, but beware that when you stir you’ll leave little marks on the bottom/sides of the mug. Takeaway: you are warned about this due to the mug being ceramic, and I remember the first few days then simply stirred with a spoon the fourth day and thought, “Noooo!!!!” as soon as I remembered, and saw little marks that will just be there forever now. I would love it if ember designed ceramic spoons that could come as a pack and the option to purchase separately that you can use for your mug so it stays white and clean. I have ceramic soup spoons but they are too big and other spoons I see are too tall as well. Otherwise the mug itself cleans out the coffee marks nicely after each time you use it. If you keep these things in mind, and understand that the convenience outweighs these issues, you will love your mug as much as I do! Still, there’s always room for improvement and I look forward to seeing what they add to it next! 👏

title: App is a huge negative.
body: Never had to create an account / sign into an app in order to keep coffee warm before. Was so long between using these cups that the app had updated, demanded my sign in, and completely forgotten both of my cups which have not moved and the app has always been on my same phone without any changes. Just did not exist in the app anymore. I do not think I am even going to re-sync them with the app. They seem to hold the last temperature and personalized LED color they were set with which is all I am probably ever going to use them for anyways. Tired of poor human factors design of apps and devices; no, there is no reason I should need an account and share my info to operate cups. Do the cups work? Yeah, they are fine, they do the job; probably would have gotten the larger ones (14oz) if I had it to do again but also probably would not have gotten any of them if I experienced the app first. If you are going to use them regularly and do not mind creating an account with each new app, it might be more worth it; for me it is just an occasional novelty at this point.

title: Great mug but horrible app
body: So it works as advertised. I ordered this for my office at my job. I tend to pour the tea but then forget about it or i get busy moving across the buidling without my mug with me and thats why I ordered this . But I am even more pleased that this one maintains its pairing. I never did get the first to stay paired once my phone went dark. This one hasn't yet forgotten in three weeks. But all is not perfect.
