title: Won't charge after six months = Useless
body: It turns out this is a really expensive paperweight. Purchased it 6 months ago almost to the day and now it won't charge so keeping my coffee hot on or off the base isn't possible any longer. I'm pretty sure it's because one of the two contact pins in the base no longer springs back up to contact the metal ring on the bottom of the mug. I read up on the mug before buying it and I learned two things. Don't use metal utensils to stir because they scratch the coating inside the mug and cause it to flake off (which you ingest) and don't get anything sticky on the charging base because the pins will get stuck in the down position and won't make contact the mug's surface anymore. I drink my coffee black so no utensils and I always hand wash the mug so no problem with the first one. I've never spilled anything on the base. (I'll attach pictures to show the condition of the mug and base.) I my case the spring which pops one of the pins back up after its been compressed has given up the ghost. I can take the base and slap it lightly on my hand and the pin will come back out but it doesn't stay there. If you look closely at the pictures you can see the left pin is lower than the right one. I didn't read the warranty before buying it and I should have. It's only 30 days and is nothing but one limitation and exclusion after the other making it as difficult as possible to get your money back. I should have suspected something when a product this expensive, and at least on the surface this simple, only has a 30 day warranty. I've had a Zojirushi travel mug for years (20% the cost of the Ember) that keeps my coffee hot ALL day, (that's not an exaggeration), but since I''m retired I thought it would be nice to have a regular mug to drink from but that I didn't have to go to the microwave all the time to keep the contents hot. You can't put this thing in the microwave so I can't even use it as a regular mug, unfortunately I suppose it's going to the landfill. Hope you have better luck than me but beware!

title: Stylish and Functional – A Coffee Game Changer
body: The Ember Mug is both stylish and practical—perfect for keeping your coffee or tea nice and hot for hours. I love the app feature that lets you customize the exact temperature to your liking. It’s such a small luxury that makes a big difference in your daily routine. The color I picked was such a hit that my wife’s office team now wants to order them for their own desks. Definitely worth the investment if you enjoy your hot drinks at the perfect temp!

title: Excellent product
body: Gifted to a friend and she loves it!

title: With an Apple phone. App Works, but, heat is not for more than 1 hour
body: Works well, but not for more than 1 hour , even with full charge. If you have 2 oz or less in the mug, the temperature does not hold, the automatic shut-off kicks in, and your last 2 sips are cold. Easy to set up, charges quickly. The box the mug came in says it’s a 10 oz, to get a 10 oz drink you have to literally fill the mug to the “rim”… ideally you can only get an 8 oz size drink… the manufacturer should not market this as a 10oz mug… DOES NOT WORK IF U HV AN ANDROID PHONE, AS THE APP DOES NOT WORK AND MUG CANT BE USED WITHOUT THE APP. …. This Ember mug versus a Muggo mug : with the Muggo, if used while plugged in maintains the heat for as long as it is plugged in, so literally, my last sip is very hot as the first sip. That plugged in option for use is not available with the Ember mug.

title: Mostly very good if cleaned properly. (version 1)
body: After a year's worth of use was considering a second and thought would share thoughts. In general - a very good purchase, does as promised. After a year I'm not sure the battery is holding up as expected, but that's to be expected as far as battery life goes. The one flaw that annoyed the most - if you don't make sure the bottom of the mug is absolutely dry, the contacts on the charging base will corrode and break. Just a simple patdown isn't enough - the rubber spacers on the bottom of the mug will retain moisture, after several months I noticed the corrosion buildup on the charger base (the small spring that sticks up) and tried to clean it only to have that spring break off completely which of course left it unable to recharge. So if you're used to washing it prior to using then you'll likely end up having to buy a new base within a year. If your habits have you wash after using with a few hours to dry completely before putting it back on the base, then I expect you'll be fine. This was with the original version, I have no idea if the new 2.0 version addresses this situation or not, only that the replacement base had the same weak-looking spring which will likely suffer the same fate over time if the base isn't fully and completely dry after washing, which a simple toweling or wipedown is insufficient due to the rubber spacers retaining moisture.

title: Made for Apple
body: This isn't my first Ember. I had the version 1 travel mug when it first came out (dead now, non-replaceable battery....) many years ago and I loved the idea of maintaining the temperature of my warm drink. A Yeti will keep your drink scalding hot for a long time but when you're sitting at your desk and get lost in something, it's nice to go back to your drink and it be how you want it. With that being said, this isn't made for people that use Android. My partner and I both recently purchased a version 2 mug and are having the same issues with connectivity. She's running a fully updated Pixel 4 and I have tried using both a Pixel 6 Pro & a Samsung Galaxy S22 Ultra. On to the issues: Initial pairing was impossible. These ship with old firmware and we just couldn't get the firmware to fully download and install on any of our Android devices. The only way I was able to update the firmware was by connecting them to an iPad. Once the firmware updated, we could connect the mug to our phones. That was just the firmware. What about day-to-day use? I have to re-pair the mug to my phone every single morning. Sometimes I forget and am forced to hold a hot cup of coffee up so I can hold the button on the bottom of the mug to put it in pairing mode. This usually works. Sometimes it doesn't. I reached out to Ember support and they told me that my phone isn't on the supported device list. To be fair, many, many new phones aren't on the list. I don't think they appreciate the audience they're trying to sell to. There is a pretty good chance that if you're going to spend more than $100 on a mug that has bluetooth, you're probably using a phone from the last couple of years. They also mentioned that the mug still works without the app. This is true but part of the reason someone would buy this is to be able to change the temperature, depending on what you're drinking. So if you have an iPhone, this is probably going to work for you. If you have an Android device, best of luck!

title: Ember Cup

title: Doesn't hold a charge for very long
body: I've now had this product for about 2 months. While it keeps the liquid nice and warm, the charge in the cup has steadily decreased. It started out at 90 minutes but it's already down to an hour and takes several hours to get back up to a full charge. I sure hope the time does not decrease any further. Otherwise I'll go back to my old coffee cup and reheat in the microwave.

title: Does its job
body: This mug works , if you tend to forget you have a drink and find it cold later. It’s a luxury, though , because you may just use a microwave to reward your warm drinks. Works for about an hour , longer if you always put it back in the plate ( charger) . I wash it and put it there right away after every use so it’s always ready . If you are a fast drinker maybe not useful to you. More for people who take sips and do work in between. I paired it with the phone first time I used it, but you don’t need to use the phone, guess has a standard temperature , you really don’t need to program it for it to keep your coffee/ tea warm.

title: cool!
body: got it for my boyfriend and he loves it! he tends to forget about his coffee or take his time to drink it. so it’s really cool for him to be able to keep his coffee at a certain temperature and not have to constantly be microwaving it to reheat. it is a little pricey but i think it’s a great thing to get if you or your friend is a avid coffee drinker!

title: App and pairing is problematic
body: This is my second updated review after using this mug for awhile. The glitchiness of the app is so annoying that I would not buy this again. The added convenience of this product does not warrant its price; battery charge goes down quickly, and the constant fussing with the app and trying to turn the mug off or on is annoying. These are high class problems but this mug is expensive. I love gadgets and love the idea of this mug but wish it worked more reliably with ease. I am updating my review after having the mug for several weeks. Below is my original review. The mug does not need repairing but it needs to be switched on before the phone recognizes it. So the app is not as problematic as it seems at first. I love the mug because it works, but one drawback is that the charge does not last very long. I bought this because I had surgery that has kept me fairly immobilized and I thought this might be helpful to make hot tea without boiling water and to keep coffee and soup hot. It does all of those things, but not for very long. The mug I bought isn’t really big enough for a can of soup and putting a metal spoon in it is not recommended, but you can make do. In summary, great concept, well made (I love my rose gold material and its bottom heavy with nice rubberized thick bottom cover), a bit pricey, and just wish it stayed hot longer. Would buy again. I love the mug when it works, but too often, it takes too many steps to re-pair it and get it functioning. After a time at rest, the app says it is not paired with the mug, and I always have to restart my phone (this is within 16 hours of last use), at which point, I have already had my coffee already cold, and not enjoying it because I am fussing instead of sitting quietly. It is a frustration and a high class problem, but the price of the mug does not justify this type of glitch. It should be easy and reliable for this high price item. I would not recommend it for that reason.

title: Great mug but doesn’t last
body: There is a reason Ember only has a 1yr warranty. I love this mug. I have become dependent on it. I like my coffee hot. Ember has done a great job capitalizing on people like me because I buy a new mug every single year. There is truly nothing on the market better and I have tried them all. I think Ember knows this and has not made any improvements over the years to correct the 2 main issues. I have been through 8 mugs now and they each have had the same issue after about a year 1. The coating starts to wear/chip on the edges and on the bottom interior. Is the coating toxic if ingested? I would rather not chance it. I clean it daily with a paper towel and dawn dish soap so I know I am not abrasive when cleaning. 2. The charging coaster prongs always break. Without fail as soon as the warranty is up. The spring holding the prongs up wear out and they sink in. Once this happens the coaster will no longer charge the mug. You can buy a replacement coaster for $35. For $100-150 a pop I would think Ember would fix the spring issue and find a more durable coating but clearly they choose not to bc people like me keep buying it over and over again.

body: I got this as a gift for my significant other, who loves Marvel and especially Spider-Man. (He also loved stealing my Owala water bottles.) title: Good bottle, but probably not as durable as some options.
body: I've been using Yeti and Stanley bottles for awhile, and one of things that made me look for a new bottle was the Yeti and Stanley straw lids either leak, or they build pressure and expel liquid when opened. The old Yeti straw lid design was leakproof but it built pressure, the new design has a vent so it does not build pressure, but it leaks on it's side. For me I do a lot of traveling that has elevation changes so I was tired of getting baths when opening the straw, or having to rotate the lid loose to release pressure and then tightening it to drink from it. So I tried out the Owala, and it does seem to strike a better balance of not building pressure, but also not leaking on it's side. It's nice to be able to sip from it, or drink from it and I like that it's easy to get the seals out for cleaning, and the sip lid is also designed in a way that's very easy to clean. It's also more capacity than say a Yeti version in the same size, the 24oz Owala is basically the same size as the 18oz Yeti and much smaller than the 26oz Yeti. I suspect this is because the airspace between the walls must be thinner. In theory that might give the edge to Yeti in keeping things cold, but either one will keep iced drinks icy cold all day. It's not perfect though, for one they dent very easily, you can actually squeeze the sides of the Owala and feel it flex in the middle, in comparison to say the Yeti bottles that do not flex and feel much more solid. The 26oz Yeti rambler is 22oz and the 24oz Owala is only 15oz, so the Yeti is likely using much thicker walled steel. Also the lid feels like it's made of a cheaper, more brittle plastic than the Yeti lids, which can take a ton of abuse. I'm also not a fan of the lock/carry loop. It works well for a lock, but it's too narrow/thin to be comfortable carrying it by the loop. It's too small to get 2 fingers in comfortable, and carrying a large water bottle with 1 finger gets old, where the Yeti lid carry handle is much more comfortable. At the end of the day there still seems to be no perfect leakproof straw bottle that does not build pressure. For everyday non-abusive use those the Owala is pretty darn nice, and it's easy to clean, with more capacity in a similar size.

However, for making tea in the morning while doing ten other things, it didn’t work. The volume turned out to be so small that I could only get one mug per boil, and there’s no way to set the timer to get your attention after a certain time, so you have to be paying attention. (Also, there’s no divider between minutes and seconds - it threw me off a few times before I realized that “120” on the timer meant one minute and twenty seconds, rather than one hundred twenty seconds!) While a minor feature, I adore the fact that the little screen tells you the current temperature of the water as well as what it is set to. There is just something fun about knowing the water temperature of the cold water you just poured in. Speaking of cold water, the time it takes to boiling takes a bit longer than my kettle at home, but I believe that's just the water I am using. I don't fault the kettle for that. Cleaning is relatively easy, however, I have not had to worry about limescale removal yet. Limescale is due to minerals in water, and the product came with a slip to explain how limescale affects your kettle and how to fix it. I appreciate that the manufacturer includes this. Lastly, this is my first gooseneck kettle and it's a joy to use to make pourover coffee. the flow rate is great and hope to use this kettle many years into the future.

I wanted one like the original because I used the original one 3 times a day for four years but they don’t sell it anymore. This one looked nice so I picked it up. That was a mistake. But let’s do a pro/con list Pros: - The heating time. It heats water very quickly. It did two 8 ounce cups of water in under two minutes. - The display is clear and easy to see. It has the set temperature and the current temperature. Cons: - While heating the water, I smelled burning that was like burning plastic. I don’t know if it was the smell of something burning off of the inside of the kettle or the base but it was a strong enough smell that it made me nervous and I only ran it once. - This thing is very cheaply built and flimsy. My previous kettle is a similar shape and design but it was sturdy and had substance. This kettle is nothing like that. The base is thin, hollow plastic and the kettle is much thinner. The whole thing feels like a toy. - Even with water in it, the kettle did not sit firmly on the heating base. I had to push down to get it to sit right. - There is a thin ring around the display that’s painted gold and much of it was scratched off. - The plug is not grounded (two prong only). I’ve never seen an electric kettle that didn’t have a grounded plug. I can’t speak about the taste of the water or features like auto shut off because I didn’t use the kettle enough to get to use them. Normally I set up my first cup of water for tea when I get up and then use keep warm to keep the water hot until I am ready to use it. I would not trust this kettle to leave it alone while not in the room. This is already in the box and on the way back to Amazon. It is definitely not worth the asking price.

title: Works but has some important flaws
body: I really wanted to like this because of the features and price point. The basic functionality works correctly and it's nice to hold in hand and use. But I have a few complaints, in descending order of importance: 1. If you happen to live a bit above sea level, where the boiling point of water is below 100C, it will continuously attempt to re-boil the water, never switching off by itself. You'll have to manually lower the set temperature. Since it already has a temperature sensor and a bunch of logic, it should be able to figure out that the temp isn't increasing, and switch off in that case, since that means it's boiling. 2. The beep is really, annoyingly, loud! There appears to be no way to switch it off. I'm trying to make coffee while half the house is still asleep so this is quite important for my usage. So far I'm working around it by manually switching it off just before the set temperature is reached, but it's annoying to have to do that. 3. Some basic design issues: the maximum marker is not very obvious (took me a while to find that it was on the rivet that attaches the handle on the inside); the giant "designed by..." gold lettering on the front of the base is in rather poor taste. I'm probably going to return this one and see if I find something better. I hope some of these problems are fixed by intasting in a future version, because other than these, it's a very nice kettle!

title: Surprisingly good quality
body: First let me say that I ordered mine back in November 2024 and it is now January 2025 and I'm only just starting to use these. If there was any quality change in between those times, I just wanted that understood. Ever since owning a vacuum sealer, usually the FoodSaver brand, I have always bought the FoodSaver Brand rolls. I am a die-hard FoodSaver brand customer. Anytime I strayed, I fully regretted it. I've tried a few different vacuum seal bags that had excellent reviews and all found them desperately wanted. I liked the thickness of the FoodSaver brand bags. I didn't like the price, which is why every once in awhile I would try something else. I would generally use them up, double bagging them until they were gone but a few I actually just threw away. I am explaining this because for my review on these bags, you need to understand my mindset before trying these. After trying a generic vacuum sealer and throwing it away after the second use, I spent $150 on sale for my newest FoodSaver brand vacuum sealer. However I was almost out of bags, and the amount of bags they send with the machines is laughable. I couldn't really afford to buy the vacuum seal bags that I so desperately needed in addition to the machine. So I tried once again to use a generic thinking that even if I had to double bag at least it would last long enough for me to recover in order to buy my normal bags. For the first time I was not disappointed. These had excellent reviews so I figured once more down the rabbit hole. But when I tried them, the first thing I noticed was they are not much thinner than the FoodSaver bags. There is a slight thinning but they are very durable. The second thing I noticed was they didn't have the white stripe for writing the date however, I found the textured side takes the marker just fine. I ordered a pack that had three rolls of 8 in and three rolls of 11 in which are the only things I ever use. I don't like the baggies even though my machine has an attachment for it and I can't afford the containers plus who wants to create storage space for those things. The variety in the box suited me. The storage capacity is based on how much of the bag you cut, just like all the others. I didn't measure them to make sure they were the size they should be but upon use, they seemed exactly what I was already used to. They are a easy to cut, easy to fill. My only problem with these was after filling, the edge curled. If you're using a flat vacuum sealer, that's not going to be an issue for you. However mine is an automatic feed system, and a curled edge caused a problem feeding into my vacuum sealer for sealing. It is remediable. You can pull the two sides together on each end and it helps to curve enough to feed it in. A problem I would definitely not like to have however considering the price difference between these and the FoodSaver brand, I am more than willing to put up with it to save so much money, since I saw no other faults. I will be buying these a second time, to ensure quality control before committing to them completely. For the first buy, I am extremely satisfied. Even with the curling of the bag, considering the price difference, I decided not to even take off a star. I wanted to be able to use my vacuum sealer for more than just separating meat into one time usable quantities. I want to be able to take any prepackaged food and be able to vacuum seal it so we don't get the ice crystals. Basically I wanted to be able to use it as much as I want. With the price of these bags and their quality, I am now able to accomplish just that.

title: Great Kettle - Great Looking - Easy to Use
body: Why did you pick this product vs others?: I chose the Chefman Gooseneck electric kettle because it was in the perfect sweet spot for value for money, looks, and tons of great reviews. I use this to help warm up Distilled Water for my using my Neti Pot. It has made my twice daily task much easier. It is easy to use, very quick to heat up and has a gauge so I can tell how much water is in the kettle. I can heat up as little as one cup or go up to four cups. This one is a keeper and very cute. I have no problem keeping this out on my bathroom counter.

title: Great for pour overs
body: Bought this for coffee pour overs. It is exceptional for this task. The buttons are easy to use for your desired temperature. The only negative, which is not unique to this model, is that if you fill it anywhere near the max level mark and pick the highest temp (full boil), it will boil up the narrow spout and overflow onto your counter. Any similar style pot will have this issue. I usually pick the lower coffee setting, so this is not a problem.

title: This little kettle does it all
body: Such a great purchase. I drink multiple cups of tea a day. Here's why I love this kettle: 1) It doesn't take up much space on my counter, 2) It doesn't have a plastic interior its all metal, 3) It heats up different amounts of water so I can only do a cup at a time or multiple which is handy, 4) It can heat up to different temperatures based on the type of tea (and quickly), 5) Probably my favorite feature It beeps when the water is ready so often with other kettles I would put in water and get distracted doing something that my water would be cold. I absolutely love this kettle.

title: I’d buy again. Wish for louder ready beep.
body: Loved this for my daughter’s tiny New York apt. Fast, easy, love the preset boiling temps and the keep warm setting, which we use often. My only wish is that the water ready indicator might be a bit more prominent, which would be helpful in her bustling home. Over time, we (daughter, toddler and grandmother) find ourselves attuning to the quiet beep and I can see where it would come in handy in some situations. I’m buying one for my home.

title: At last, one that keeps doing its appointed tasks
body: It turns out to be the perfect solution for my needs of easily pourable hot water source to fit comfortably right next to my Flair 58 espresso machine. The first couple of efforts were magical push-button affairs. Which worked for a few weeks before giving up the electronic ghost. You know, temperature control within a single degree, keeping the water hot until... when? The point is, it was all for naught. I didn't need that kind of temp tolerances, certainly couldn't taste the difference. And I hate that a thing integral to using a manual, lever machine ... cannot be depended upon. But this one is reliable, straightforward, holds I believe .8 Liter, has auto-shutoff, is comfortable to hold and pour. Hey, it does what it promises, hopefully for months/years to come. I am a happy espresso drinker.

title: Does the job, looks good doing it
body: If you’re looking for a basic “barista style” gooseneck pour-over kettle, this will do nicely. Pro: Fast. Water for two avg. size mugs (2 cup capacity) with room for milk reaches full boil in about a minute and a half and automatic shutoff at about three minutes and a half. You can begin pouring anytime during that window in my experience. Lined with stainless steel. Black and silver finish blends beautifully with our black granite countertops and the other black appliances. While heating there’s a nice blue LED that lights up on the lever. Nice touch. Con: Outside of kettle is not insulated so it does get hot. You have to train yourself to only use the handle which is durable plastic and does not heat up, but which also feels good solid and balanced in your pouring hand. Totally worth it for the price. Great little kettle that gets the job done fast and looks good doing it. Note: I only use it for boiling water, so cleaning isn’t much of an issue for me. It does have an inside rod along one edge, which does the heating, which would require you to get a behind it with a sponge I guess. (See photo)

title: Nice little kettle, but...
body: After using it for a few months, we like this electric kettle overall. It boils water reasonably fast and is not bigger than it needs to be for us. The grippy rubber feet on the base keeps it from easily sliding around on the countertop and the kettle itself is easily lifted off its base with one hand. Blue LEDs indicate when it is heating. Two nit-picks, though: 1. After the first day of use, some corrosion or oxidation spots appeared inside on the heated metal bottom . We use reverse osmosis filtered water and this surface looks like it is stainless steel so I don't know why spots would appear. So now, after taking the hot water we need, we pour out any remaining water (for plants) and flip the power on for a few seconds to quickly evaporate the film of water left on the bottom. With that routine, the spots have not gotten worse. 2. The plastic mesh across the spout was much too fine. In order to get enough "head" to force water through the mesh, you would have to tip the kettle so far that water would pour out around the lid and make a mess. Not so great design engineering. My solution was to cut away the plastic mesh with a sharp knife. Yes, I would recommend this kettle, assuming that it will keep working well for at least several more years.

title: Essential to prevent costly cabinet repairs.

I have had to completely rip out the interior surface of a cabinet to get rid of sagging, rotted wood, and this mat would have prevented that. The lip is high enough to keep in a fair amount of water before overflowing, but itbis narrow enough to keep under sink storage at a maximum. The material is flexible enough to install in seconds, regardless of pipe layout, and it is affordable enough that I would recommend that everyone have one for their kitchen. title: Basically works, has some issues. (Died 9 wks, 3 days after purchase)
body: Issues: 1. Temperature set control in 5C increments. Want 1 degree (C or F). 2. The coffee presets only go down to 195F in 5F increments. No 185F or 190F. 3. Removing the pot to pour stops the temperature hold. Have to hit the button again to regain temperature. 4. Power down does not retain settings. Have to reset everything from scratch every use. That said, I'm keeping it mainly because it's such a handsome piece and my wife loves the look of it. It works well enough for me. UPDATE: After using it a while, I've gotten it pretty well figured out: 1. Plug it in, turn it on with the power (main) button. 2. Use the dial under the main button to set the temperature ( I set it to 185˚F). 3. When it get to that temperature, it will beep and you can do your pour over. It will NOT hold temperature after the initial boil. If you want to hold the temperature: 1. Press the "Hold" button, with whatever the desired temperature already dialed in. 2. Press the main button again. You'll see a timer and a status bar at the top of the display. 3. It will now hold the temperature for that duration. I'm using a large Aeropress, and I find the hold feature useful as follows: 1. Follow the procedure for the initial boil above (I use 185˚F). 2. Pour into the Aeropress, swirling the spout around to simulate a bloom. 3. Set the hold for the temp (185) for however long you need. 4. After two minutes, press into a large beaker (I use a french press glass.) 5. Let everything sit until ready to pour cups (usually 15 to 20 minutes while I finish breakfast preparations.) The pot will keep the water temperature at the initial boil temperature.) 6. When ready to serve, pour the remaining water into the beaker/carafe. That will warm up the initial shot, nicely. 7. Pour and enjoy! Without the Hold feature, I'd either have to rewarm the remainder, or live with it all cooled down for however long it's been since I did the initial pour. This way, I'm reintroducing water at the original steeping temperature, and it warms things up nicely. Update Jul 13: It died. 9 wks, 3 days after purchase. Display flashes when I plug it in, then goes blank. Can't use it without the display. Too late to return. Junk it and buy something else, I guess. Too bad. I was getting real used to it.

title: Great kettle - easily goes onto its base, heats fast, looks nice
body: One of the reviews I read mentioned that it was difficult to put the kettle on it's base - that has not been not my experience. This kettle works exactly as other similar ones, you just set it over the base and it goes right on easily and with zero problems. One thing that is not too important (for me at least) but FYI - it is not an infinite selection of temperatures. The rotating dial might lead you to think this... The options are (in F°): 104°, 113°, 122°, 131°, 140°, 149°, 158°, 167°, 176°, 185°, 194°, 203°, 212° (using the dial) or 195°, 200°, and 205° using the preset temp button. In practice, here is how I use it: Press power on and the set temperature is always at the default 212°. Press the preset button and then turn the knob to select between 195°, 200°, or 205°. After you have selected one of these three preset temperatures, that is the default preset the next time and every time thereafter that you push this button unless you change it. So, after you have picked your preset temperature, you can just hit power on, hit preset once, then power again to start the kettle and away you go. Cool having the base show both the current temp and the set temp displayed at the same time so you can see status at a glance. There is also a little completion bar along the bottom that grows as it gets closer to full temp. Copper color / buttons are a bit bright/shiny but that is pure personal preference. The lid is plastic (the rest of the kettle is metal except for the handle for insulation) but it looks the same as the kettle and doesn't touch the water other than some condensation so having a plastic lid is definitely not an issue for me. Highly recommend if you are looking for a gooseneck kettle. This pairs perfectly with the insulated stainless steel Mueller French Press Coffee Maker 34oz https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07JGBK6XV which is also a great product.

I made sure to read the manual as people complained before about pots like this one cracking or leaking and it says to always use cold water when operating the pot because it has a timer and the temperature control is only for the safety shut off for dry operation. using already warm or hot water will cause the pot to overheat the water beyond safety limits and could damage the pot. it doesn't matter if the water is cold it still heats it up to drinkable temperature in 2 minutes or less so putting hot water inside doesn't speed up the process so its best to play it safe and use cold. I really have no complaints about this product it's perfect as is and I love it. I will update this rating a year from now to inform you how it holds up. I do use it every single day at least once so it will get its stress testing.

body: I absolutely love this travel kettle. I use it at least 4-5 times a day to prepare tea mostly, but it is super convenient for heating water for oatmeal, instant soups, even hot chocolate! It is so super easy to heat the water, literally just takes a few minutes. The visual display is very easy to read and the timer is very audible and alerts me when ready—-ever-essential to keep me on task—-especially when I have a lot going on. With 4 temperature settings that can be started at a touch of the button…it is perfect for those crazy weekday/workday mornings. My favorite temp for my tea is 140 degrees, as that is the setting I found best to use if I want to drink tea right away. Having 4 different settings means you can find the perfect temperature for what you need…giving you lots of options. I have found I like using the higher temperature settings for when I am making drinks first thing in the morning to bring to work to enjoy HOT throughout the day. It heats up the perfect amount of water to fill up my favorite tumblers in a lightening fast amount of time. Originally when I got this, I was going to bring it to work every day…but I actually have been keeping this at home because I am afraid one day I will forget it at work, and be lost without it! It is the perfect size to bring to the office, or travel with. I also want to take it the next time I travel, because I am not a fan of hotel hot water kettles. This way I can bring my favorite teas with me to enjoy, even when I travel. So convenient! I love that it is made from food grade stainless steel, so I haven’t had any issues with staining, and it is easy to wash and clean. For reference, this has a high quality stainless finish inside the kettle is pretty similar to the highly popular stainless tumblers out there. The best part is that it is SO easy to pour and/or transfer liquids to another container because of its perfect design, size, and user-friendly style, and of course it being pink is just icing on the cake! I definitely recommend this for anyone who wants a high quality user-friendly kettle that heats up quickly, is reliable, and most of all, a timesaver!

title: Seems to work, but what’s with the FCC logo?
body: I like making my own coffee with an aeropress when traveling, but that becomes a challenge if the hotel room doesn’t have a microwave to heat some water. This device seems like it will do the trick. It’s small enough to stuff in a suitcase and it heats water. That said, it’s pretty odd that the box and label on the bottom of the device prominently feature the US Federal Communications Commission logo. I guess this is an attempt to make it look all official or something, but this is a kettle, not a radio. What do they think the FCC is going to regulate on a kettle? Is the little heating element blasting out radio interference? If anything, proudly featuring the FCC logo makes me less confident in the quality of the device, as it kind of screams “sketchy Chinese counterfeit!” Counterfeit of what, I’m not sure. The reason I bought this is because I didn’t find a comparable kettle made by a known manufacturer. So, four stars because it seems reasonably well built and it heats water, but not five because of the sketchy use of the FCC logo.

title: Served its purpose
body: I bought this for a trip. I knew I wouldn’t have access to a decent coffee pot so I bought this to make pour-over coffee. I tested it at home for a few days and it worked perfectly. It does take a little time to heat up to 212 but a good cup of coffee takes time so I don’t mind the wait. Once on my trip, day one it worked as expected. I made 3 cups that day with no problems. On day two it wouldn’t turn on. I had to unplug and replug it in several times before it would light up and respond. Once it did, it worked fine. ( I determined it was definitely the kettle since I tried multiple plugs.) Day three was the same. I did get it to work each time but only after unplugging it and trying again multiple times. Sometimes it would light up on the first plugin but wouldn’t response when I touched the button to get it started. When I got home I tested it again and got the same results. Ultimately, it did serve its purpose and I was able to make several cups of really good coffee on my trip for less than $40. It was frustrating and took a lot longer than it should have but I was overall glad I had this. After using it less than a dozen times, it started acting up so I would not trust it on a second trip. I’m not sure if I have a defective one or it’s just not reliable but I would likely buy a different one next time I travel. I don’t believe this was user error as I read the instructions and did exactly as they said - I know small appliances like this can be dangerous if not used properly so I was very careful. I also never used it back to back either. It was used once, emptied, turned off and unplugged for hours before it was used again.

body: I love this sleek, slim, portable kettle! It was purchased specifically to heat water to 195 degrees for my morning cup of coffee in an AeroPress. It is so simple and easy to use - just fill with water or other liquid, screw on the top, plug it in, press the button to one of the four preset temperatures, and done! It beeps when finished and will hold to temp for up to 12hrs., according to the instructions. (I didn't test this since I use the heated water right away.) The stainless steel inside is easy to clean, although the unit cannot be immersed in water since the detachable cord plugs into it. It holds 380ml of liquid to the max fill line. The instructions say it can be used for heating soups or other liquids but I've only used it for water. It heats the 200ml of water I need for my AeroPress in a few minutes, takes up very little counter space, and is portable for travel. The only improvement would be to add a USB charging option so electricity isn't required when traveling. I can't speak to the durability since I've only been using it for a few weeks, but it has worked great so far. Love this little device!

Although it does not retained heat for long but it served its purpose, I can’t complained about it, has multi-purpose. title: Only tested it but so far, so good.
body: I got this to use while car camping in the colder months. I didn't want to have to get out of my car and get the propane and Coleman stove out for my morning coffee or tea. Figured this would be a nice way to get things going while still in my pajamas. I sleep in an old-timey Ebenezer Scrooge gown and long floppy hat and it's a lot to deal with when I'm still groggy. Haven't used it "in the field" yet but tested it at home with my power banks. Works with my EcoFlow River 2 Pro great. It used about 5% of the battery and the water boiled in about 7 mins. Tried it out with my Jackery 240 even though this kettle is rated for 300W. It actually got the water up to 150 or 160 degrees but would shut off when it got any hotter. That used about 10% of the battery. Probably hot enough for some teas or instant coffee so that's not bad. I just unplugged it from the Jackery and back into the EcoFlow to bring it the rest of the way to a boil just to see how long that would take and it was only a couple of minutes and took another 2% of the battery to do so. I guess this could be useful if I needed to save power on one of the batteries and spread out the usage. Anyways, we'll see how it holds up. Oh, and I filled it just a little below the fill line and didn't have any issues with spillage from boiling.

body: I like the idea behind this but the lid is really tall and it requires a lot of strength to line up the lid with container for twisting on. However, I like that you can adjust the temperature of the water and have used it for making instant coffee as well as herbal tea. You would never be able to drink straight out of this without burning your mouth even though it looks like a thermos, it’s got metal right up to the top where you pour that will conduct heat. The cord does fit inside the container for transport really well, but you will need to bring another container to pour the contents out of this one for drinking.

So this is a nice substitute. I took off a star because I wish it had an off switch. The light stays on after it’s done even after 5-10 minutes. It doesn’t seem to turn itself off unless I unplug it. I don’t like leaving any portable heating appliance on even if it’s not in heat mode so I alway unplug it after every use. It’s a little bulky due to its size but that’s not a problem for car trips. title: great travel kettle

This little kettle is the perfect thermos size that packs into any side area of my carry-on, takes up practically no space, power cord goes inside (along with whatever else I can squeeze in - one one flight, no show socks - don't judge me). It heats water fast! Much faster than the usual in-room coffee maker. Temp is also easy to adjust, although I usually just use the max boil setting. Little reminder when it is done, auto shut off if I forget to shut it off, super easy cleanup, and looks nice. All the buzz points I wanted in a to go kettle, without being the popup kettle type I replaced. I bought the black version so my only minor nit is that it came with a white cord. Other than that, a few months in and most of that time traveling all over, it has been a great sidekick.

title: Revised review: Nice compact size kettle, but not worth $40
body: I bought this compact size kettle for use in the RV, where cupboard real estate is at a premium. First, the pro's: it is nice and small (heats just one cup of water), it is quiet (important since I get up a lot earlier than my husband in the morning), and the water does get up to a boiling temp. Now the Con's: (1) it is hard to tell if it is turned off or on...there is just a power button and I have to watch and see if the temperature displayed is going up to know if it is on; (2) it takes quite a long time for it to heat up, especially considering how little water is in the vessel; (3) there is no pouring spout, so in order to pour out the water, you have to unscrew the cap which is hot and releases hot steam, so I have to use a dishtowel each time and I have still burned myself a couple of times. I've purchased much better electric teakettles for about half what I paid for this one. I wish I could return it, but the window had closed by the time I had a chance to use it. Disappointed in this purchase. UPDATE: The customer service team for this product reached out to me to explain why the water heats slowly and to further explain the power light. I now understand why the product works the way it does...because it is so small. I upgraded my review to 3 stars as a result. I still feel it is a bit overpriced, however.

title: Great kettle, 2 things I'd change
body: Review of: COSORI Electric Kettle, Cool-Touch Double Wall Stainless Steel Insulated, Automatic Shut Off & Boil-Dry Protection, Durable Tea Kettle Boiler & Heater, 1.5L/1500W, Black - It heats up quickly (although I find this statement to be subjective, being based on personal experience and desires). - Holds a ton of water, just over 7 cups. You can make 5 large mugs of tea with that, or 7 small, one cup, cups of tea! - The handle stays cool, even after boiling a full kettle. - The body of the kettle does get hot, but I'm older and have toughened hands, so I can touch it it. - It's heavy when it's full. Might be hard to lift and pour for smaller people, seniors, arthritic hands, or very small hands - Does not dribble, and I find the handle pretty ergonomic. I do have tiny hands, but pouring for me is fine. - Average noise level while in the boiling process. I've had a few brands over the years and none of them are quiet. Cons: - 2 Lid Issues. I would prefer it to pop straight up to a 90 degree angle when I push the button. Instead, this barely opens enough to put new water in. You can force it up to a (almost) 90 degree angle. However, I VERY often need to refill it right after I've used it. The lid get very hot, much hotter than the body does. So I need to fold up a kitchen towel to open the lid to refill it so I don't burn myself. This extra step is a pain. - Ideally, I've realized I'd prefer a removable lid so I could fill it straight on my fridge door. The pop up lid gets in the way. So we do have to fill it using a separate pitcher, which means that sits out on the counter with the kettle and feels cluttered. This wouldn't be an issue for people who just use straight tap water from their faucet. -Color...I also realize I want color in my kitchen. I'm soooo tired of the black and white options. But I'm finding the best products tend to keep their color options to a minimum. And this IS a good product! Just a couple of tweaks I'd make to it :)

title: This is the kettle I was looking for that has no plastic exposed to the water or steam inside.
body: Our previous electric kettle needed to be replaced, and we wanted to get one that does not have any plastic being exposed to the water and steam inside the kettle. We tried a couple out that we though did not have plastic inside, but unfortunately they did. And, pretty much all of them that we have seen online also have what looks like a silicone ring internal around the bottom where the glass meets the bottom heating element plate. This kettle is the only one that I could find that does not have any plastic exposed to the water and steam inside. It is made from double wall stainless steel, and there are level marker on the inside of the kettle. Our previous kettle was 1200 watts, and this one is 1500watts. I do recognize that the water heats up faster with this kettle. I also did a lead swab test on the inside of the kettle and can confirm that there are no traces of lead in the kettle metal. If you are looking for a great kettle that does not have plastic exposed to the inside water and steam, look no further, this is the one.

title: Good but can be better
body: I've had this kettle for about 15 days and used it multiple times a day. I was looking for a kettle in which the only material hot water touches is stainless steel. This model meets that need. First, let me address a few concerns other reviewers posted. 1) The kettle is loud. Yes, it's not the quietest. And it is louder than my last one. But the extra noise didn't bother me. 2) The lid only opens partially after pressing the open button. I actually appreciate this design. I've used kettles whose lid springs open all the way splashing boiling water that accumulated on the underside of the lid. But this feature seems to drive some users insane. 3) Lack of controls other than the on/off switch. I had kettles that offered a dizzying number of settings. After the novelty wore off, I pretty much just used 1 setting. So, having just an on/off switch is fine with me. 4) It stains easily. This seems to be true. After just 15 days of use, I can already see a stain mark beginning to form. I only boiled filtered water in this kettle. So, this does bother me a little. But again, I've seen people posting pictures of their $200 kettle that also stains. So, at this price point, it's acceptable. Plus, I'm sure this also depends on the local water quality. 5) One reviewer finds the circular hole on the inside wall of the kettle "suspicious". Since my requirement was to have hot water touching nothing but stainless steel, I grew suspicious as well. But, this hole is covered by the contour of the lid when closed. So, it didn't bother me too much. Now, on to some of my own observations. 1) The advertisement says the outer body of the kettle is cool to the touch while the water inside is hot. This is only partially true. The area immediately below the lid (1-2in below) is very hot. 2) the water does not pour from the sprout neatly. If I tilt the kettle just a little too much, water can spill from the sides of the sprout. I believe the designer sacrificed functionality for a clean industrial design. I've had kettles that still poured nicely when the kettle is in an almost upside down position. 3) In my opinion, too much vapor/water droplets accumulate while water boils. This makes the top of the lid very wet, and as some reviewer noted, contributing to water damage over time. And lastly, 4) the power cord is too short.

title: Works well but unable to see water level and power cord is short
body: This is a basic electric kettle. There is one button you push with your thumb to lift the kettle lid to add water. There is one button you push to turn on the kettle. I would buy another kettle which shows you the water level. That way, you do not have to open up the kettle every time you want to know how much water is in the kettle. It’s a small detail but very convenient. The power cord is rather short. If you have a big distance between the outlet and where you want to place th kettle, check the length of the power cord before purchasing this item. I have kitchen cabinets above my kitchen counter and must place this kettle in a location where the steam does not directly impact my kitchen cabinets. The power cord is a little short for my use. The lid opens about 45 degrees which is kind of limited. When filling this kettle with water, I have to take a little more time to position the kettle under the sink faucet. I prefer my old kettle with a lid that would open up 90 degrees. This is another small detail, but it can save you time/energy/effort. I have a COSORI air fryer (it was recalled and I received a replacement). I am happy with my COSORI air fryer and that is why I chose COSORI for the kettle as opposed to a different brand. That is not a sophisticated way to choose a brand, but that’s the way that I did it. There are so many options on the market now it can feel a little overwhelming. If you need a super basic water kettle, this is a good option. The price is reasonable. The kettle is insulated which protects you from touching a hot kettle. I imagine this might be good for a household which has children because it reduces the risk that a child will touch the outside of the kettle and get burned. However, I would buy the Hamilton Beach Electric Kettle* ($35) instead of this one. That kettle comes with an easy-to-view water window and the lid opens 90 degrees which I find more convenient than a lid which opens 45 degrees. TIP: for any kettle, do not leave stagnant water in the kettle. I noticed that mold grows on the inside bottom of the kettle. I thought that heating the water in the kettle up to at least 100 degrees would kill any bacteria, but that is not the case. * https://www.amazon.com/Hamilton-Beach-Auto-Shutoff-Protection-41037/dp/B0BRT94C91/ref=sr_1_21?crid=29DF26DUHY724&keywords=cosori%2Btea%2Bkettle&qid=1702155151&sprefix=cosori%2Btea%2Bkettl%2Caps%2C108&sr=8-21&th=1

title: This is the best kettle I've owned.
body: I bought this to replace an old GE kettle that had a similar base plate. The metal contacts on the bottom of the old one became corroded to the point that it wouldn’t power on any more. This has a similar design for the base and contacts, however the new kettle has a concave bottom. The concave bottom of the kettle, compared with the relatively flat bottom of the old one, leads me to think that the contacts won’t be as prone to getting wet if placed on a wet counter. This would be a design improvement, but it will take years to determine that for sure. I definitely have more confidence in the design on this one. I like that the top of the kettle is big enough that I can wash and dry off the inside with a towel when needed. By contrast, my old kettle had a very narrow opening so I’d need to get creative when cleaning it. For reference, I typically wear large gloves and there’s enough room for someone with bigger hands than mine to wipe down the inside. The fill marks are embossed on the inside of the kettle which makes it very easy to see while filling. I really like this design compared to my old kettle, which had a clear fill gauge located on the handle, which was useless. The shape is dead simple, basically a pitcher, no weird bulges or creases, so it’s easy to see whether or not it’s clean. The only spot I’d be concerned with cleaning is the spout, which, because it is welded on, has a crevice along the weld and the side of the pitcher. The spout is big enough to clean by hand though, so it’s a minor concern. Overall it feels sturdy, the walls are thick, it holds temperature well, the safety switch is loud enough to hear clicking, it looks nice, and I’m happy with it. I’d definitely recommend it. Purchased April '24, Edit, January '25, This thing is awesome. I am a klutz, and when I whacked this thing against a cabinet (by accident, because I'm a klutz) it showed no damage. The cabinet didn't either, so that's a plus.

title: Works well and good customer service
body: I bought this kettle because I wanted to stop using the plastic electric kettle that I had. The only plastic on this model is on the outer lid, handle, and separate base. When I first received it, I noticed there are two holes inside the kettle - one near the handle and one on the lid. I was worried that condensation could get inside these holes and cause mold growth. I wrote the company and they said that the holes are to relieve pressure. I make sure to keep the lid open to dry out between uses and I haven’t noticed any issues yet. After pouring, one single drop of water would drip from the spout, but as my last kettle had an issue with spilling unless pouring verrrrrry slowly, this wasn’t a big issue for me. I had an issue with scale forming immediately after the first use. Customer service was very helpful with cleaning tips, but nothing worked so they sent a warranty replacement. I didn’t realize, until after I got the replacement, that there was a slight dent in the spout of the original kettle that was causing the drop of water. The new kettle doesn’t drip at all and I'm very happy with it.

title: Awesome 4 month kettle
body: Dec 3’19 UPDATE: After no luck reaching out for help with troubleshooting.. I gave up and bought another kettle. But as soon as I did this one started working again. No clue, glitch? I did see the lid separate from the lip of the lid, so when the kettle was boiling it didn’t read the temperature right and boils longer than it’s initial boil time and the steam was stronger and coming out of the gap. It got too hot and popped off? I dont know really. Not brand new, got a used one? There was a chip in the top lid where the lid was so maybe it eventually steamed apart. Maybe it was dropped when packaged? If the reviews are for design and functionality, I’d say this is a good enough kettle. But for lack of customer service, I deducted a star ⭐️. Oct 16’19 UPDATE: the Cosori just stopped working. It worked fine 2 days ago. That’s only 4 months! Of course the window for a return in out. June 2019 - This is my 2nd attempt to owning an electric kettle. 1st order was the Amazon brand which I opened and used as soon as I received it and it failed (leaked) in the spout and handle area. So I immediately researched again, read more of its user reviews.. then went back to my list of 3-4 potentials and chose this newer Cosori. For a person who drinks and makes hot tea daily it’s top priority to have clean boiling water. Would I use a simple glass whistle kettle like I had at first again? Only if I can stop accidentally breaking glass, borosilicate glass or not. I took a photo for comparison in height and design between the Amazon one and this Cosori before I returned the other. This Cosori kettle is a nice kettle. Good light weight for its size. I like the color combo, mostly black and sleek. It boiled right at 6 minutes and then turned off immediately. I was hoping the base could act as a warmer (keep warm) base for the kettle but that probably would require more work in the engineering (R&D) department because the kettle automatically turns off when the kettle has reached the correct boiling point. So I dont know how they could have both functions. Maybe some other brand has it and I missed it. To me what’s important is that it works great! It does what it’s suppose to do and that’s to boil water. Clean up is easy. First 1-2 uses you may find water spots after the water is poured out but from what I read it’s from what’s inside the water we use that gets left behind, like minerals. To rid of it I used 1 part vinegar to two parts water and let it sit for a few hours (because I forget about it) and just normal recommended cleaning. 1:2 part ratio is like 1 cup vinegar and 2 cups of water. I use a bottle brush or a used fabric softener (doesn’t scratch and scrubs very well) and Dawn. I have filled the water tank past recommended up to the two holes line in the spout to test if the boiling water leaks or spits/shoots out boiling water if you pour over the tank’s recommended capacity. Result?! Still good!!!!! Although I can only speak from my testing on my kettle.

title: no plastic touches the water - and super fast to heat up

title: Many pluses but two distinct design flaws
body: Critically, this an all steel kettle. No plastic touching the water to be boiled every day for years and the infused water consumed by humans (those little plastic "water level" windows in kettles should be completely done away with). Heats quickly and turns off like clockwork as soon as the water hits boiling. Brings water to a full boil (essential for good brewing). Five stars for all this. This kettle obviously was designed to look sleek and modern - and it does. In the process of that they ruined the spout by not making it deep enough. Obviously didn't want it protruding too much. Now, when you try to make a full pour, boiling water sloshes out the sides of the spout. Putting form over function is so dumb. They should fix this starting tomorrow. Another, though less important, design flaw is that there is no knob on the lid (sleek though). Sometimes you need to open the lid fully just after it's boiled and everything is still hot. The thumbpress on the handle will release the lid but not always open it all the way (it doesn't seem to be meant to) so, absent a knob on the lid, you have to push it fully open by the (often hot) edge of the lid, not terribly inconvenient, but not ideal. This tea kettle would be better for a knob on the lid. I was suspicious about this hole (see pic) in the water cannister, top rear, but hasn't caused any concerns and I've made 4 pots of tea per day with it for months now. I guess it is to allow any water that gets inside the plastic outer shell to get steamed out. Great hot water kettle but could easily be better.

title: More than just good-looking
body: I've had my Cosori Electric Kettle for almost 1 year now (purchased Nov. 2023) and have been very happy with my purchase, not only is it a sleek & modern addition to my countertop, it's quite the reliable appliance to give consistent results, heating up ever so quickly - I'm always amazed at how speedily it comes to a rapid boil, then ever so faithfully automatically shuts off. I also adore the fact that this Kettle retains heat so well, so no need to re-heat for a second cup of coffee. One advice to you, who may re-heat leftover brewed herbal teas, is to keep an eye on the Kettle as some herbal brews can foam up in a closed Kettle, you wanna be close by to do a quick shut-off to prevent an overflow (yes, even a one cup amount can foam up & overflow - good thing I was standing right next to it). Overall, I recommend you purchase this Kettle, so much that it's a guarantee that when this Kettle no longer functions, that I will certainly buy another one as it is good value for money. There is no after taste and the size is impressive - we've never had to fill it all the way, even when making coffee for four guests. Don't hesitate, buy it!

title: first one had a problem, second one is great!
body: It heats quickly and has become our primary way to heat water for tea, french press coffee, ramen, and oatmeal. I wanted one where the water-contact components were all stainless steel. There is some plastic on the 'outside' components but the inside where your water is, is all stainless. The first one I ordered had an issue with turning off when the water was boiled. The problem was that the lid on top needs to be completely closed for the heat detector to work. If I put a small weight on top of the lid, it would work fine. If there was no weight, it wouldn't detect the boil. I returned that one and ordered a second. The second one is working just fine.

title: Zero Internal Plastic, Double-Wall Construction: Perfect Kettle
body: It is nearly impossible to find an electric tea kettle that truly has no plastic parts which come into contact with the water. This is a very rare example of an electric kettle that is 100% smooth stainless steel on the inside, without any plastic components inside. Even the built-in spout filter (an unnecessary component) is 100% steel, and does not have a plastic mount. Even the underside of the lid is smooth steel. The only plastic on this kettle is the parts that appear black on the exterior (such as the handle, and top rim, and bottom, and the illuminated clear plastic on/off switch on the bottom exterior). This is also a rare example of a kettle that is double-wall construction (like a "Thermos") so the exterior does not get hot when the water is boiling. Excellent design. Look no further.
