Was looking for an ALL stainless steel kettle for my family. After researching, I’ve found that pretty much ALL black plastic used in kitchen products were recycled using computer plastic, which contain tons of toxic and potentially carcinogenic chemicals; resulting in us throwing out our current product! After a week of use, the Cosori kettle has performed as expected - excellent! Room temp water(72 degree) boils at around the 6 minute mark. Water also stays warmer longer due to the double walled stainless steel. The 2-level lid opening was a great safety design. It prevents hot water splashing on you, and makes it easy to clean the interior when you open it fully. The blue led was accurate and turns off when the water comes to a boil. Overall it’s a very good value for the money. The only cons is that the external stainless steel metal feels a bit thin. Otherwise we’re happy with our purchase!

title: Easy to clean/de-scale if you have hard water
body: There are no nooks or crannies to collect lime or other mineral deposits if you live in an area with hard water and no water softener. A teaspoon of food-grade citric acid powder (also purchased on Amazon) boiled in an inch of water removes the white lime scale easily. And it doesn't seem to get as much build-up of those white mineral deposits, perhaps because of its smooth, stainless steel interior? Just a little on the bottom. It heats up quickly. However, the only way to control the temperature is to turn it off before it boils, which doesn't bother me since I always want to boil the water. But my daughter uses hot water to defrost little baggies of frozen breastmilk, so if you do that a lot, maybe this isn't for you. My only "complaint" is that it only comes in one large size, and so the kettle is a little heavy for me. If they start making a smaller size, I'd happily buy that too.

title: 2 years and still going strong!
body: This is my first electric kettle, so I have nothing else to compare it to (other than microwaving water or using the stove). But even without other kettles to compare it to, I would still go with this one! The design is simple, just one button to boil and that's it. I've never had any issues with the spout or the water not getting hot enough. It's performed perfectly for 2 whole years. Would it be nice if it had a warming feature to keep the water warm after boiling? Yeahhh. But it comes to a boil so quickly, I don't even mind having to press the button again if I want to make some more hot water. The only flaw I have noticed is that the black coating on the outside did start to come off in one place. I noticed this after moving and this kettle being in a box. I don't know if it happened during that process or before, but it's only a slight cosmetic problem. I honestly don't mind much. I love this kettle! Definitely reccommend.

title: In use multiple times a day
body: My kettle is one of the most used products in my kitchen. I use it multiple times a day. Works well. No complaints.

title: Stainless steel—no plastic
body: This teapot is all stainless steel (except for the handle), which is the main reason I purchased it. There is no plastic on the inside. It’s also cool to the touch after heating the water. I especially like the automatic shut-off. I wish it was a little smaller, but I definitely like the teapot.

title: A bit disappointed in longevity
body: This product has been in my home for less than 2 years. It doesn't get used every day, but it heats quickly when I do use it. I've recently discovered that I have to hold (rather than click) the on switch down several times before it stays on to heat the water. Hard water or not, I expected more longevity and less trouble shooting. Looking for one with a different type of power switch.

title: Does not hold heat
body: Maybe, I misunderstood the description- I thought I was buying a water boiler that would hold the heat after the boil, like a ‘thermos’ would, due to the double wall construction. This water boiler is made with lightweight, easily dented, double walled metal material- I hope it’s stainless steel. It does a reasonable job of getting a liter and a half to a boil. There is no plastic in contact with the water (a good thing, in my book). It does not hold the warmth after the boil. But maybe it is not manufactured to do that, maybe not the manufacturer’s fault. Like I said, maybe I misunderstood the listing. But I am not pleased with how it dented before I even put it to use.

title: WoW-works great!
body: This is the best! Highly recommend.

title: Be aware: only lasts a year
body: I purchased this twice. Each lasted a year. The first one, the button snapped inside (which is made of flimsy plastic) so I had to turn it like a dial to start it otherwise it wouldn't work. The second one, the thermostat broke so it would turn on and off and never got to boiling point. But with that said, it was amazing the whole year. Very quick to boil, easy to clean, and never tasted like plastic. Is it worth $40 to last a year, not really. Would it buy it again? No. I'd rather try my luck with something else.

title: The first one worked and the second one leaked.
body: We have purchased this item twice. The first time it gave good service and finally the kettle switch failed. We use this kettle frequently so I purchased another. This one was defective and leaked water I noticed after a few days after I had gotten rid of the packaging. The container is a solid metal one, the only place to leak would be around the pour spout. I suspect a defective bond with the spout attachment since water runs down the inside of the outer casing and out the bottom.. So order with caution perhaps consider another brand.

title: Beautiful kettle
body: Beautiful kettle. Functions well.

title: Love it.
body: First time electric kettle owner. I used it recently and I've started getting excited to use it. First thing I did was read the manual. It is short and talks about how to use it and has safety instructions. It repeatedly says to not fill the kettle above the "MAX" line (which is shown in measurements inside the kettle). Also while cleaning it, to not submerge the bottom of the kettle and the part that boils the kettle in water as those are electric parts. Unplug the appliance when not in use. It comes with the kettle and the part to boil the kettle. It is also corded, not wireless. For easy of portability and space, the cord is able to be wrapped underneath the part that heats the kettle. It's very easy to use. Plug it in, fill the kettle with water (do not go above "max"), set the kettle on the boiler, then press the clear tab down. It will light up while boiling, then automatically turn itself off when it's finished. Wait 5 minutes before pouring. Also I learned to have the kettle in an open space and not underneath anything because while the water is boiling, the kettle will have hot steam coming out of the spout. I placed it by a window in my kitchen during use as there's an outlet near it. The water is way hotter than the hot water dispenser I have. I am so excited to use it during winter. Also the water still stays hot after an hour. Great for coffee and tea!

title: Excellent Stainless Steel Hot Water Kettle
body: This is a well made Stainless Steel Hot Water Kettle. The water heats to a boil quickly; perfect for hot beverages and foods like pour over coffee, tea, oatmeal, etc, The auto shut off works well and has a light that turns off when the heat cycle stops. The handle is easy to grip and remains cool to touch. The spout does not drip and no water leaks from the kettle. The kettle is light weight.

title: Nice Cuppa Tea
body: I just received my pot today. I preformed the test pot max fill (Brita filtered water), let it boil until it shut off, let it sit for 5 min., then dumped it into dish water. I refilled halfway with my filtered water and turned it on. It took 3 min. to boil before it shut off and the temp of water was 160* I then unplugged my cord and placed my pot on a heat resistant silicone pad. I don't know how long it will retain the temp as this is my first pot and I just wanted a cup of tea. I placed one Red Rose teabag (black tea) in my cup and poured my water over it. I do like that my tea is nice and dark, I prepared it plain so I could taste the water from pot boil and my tea tasted great! No residue or metal taste. My microwave never seemed to get that dark color from my tea bags when cooked for 3 min. in there, then I would place the bag in afterwards. So far so good. Will update if any issues arise. The person who sent me a question to my email (I could not find it on here). Question: Is this stainless steel kettle cordless? I didn't see it mentioned. It looks like it may sit on a separate heating element -- is that correct? Amswer : This Kettle has a separate heating element, and it shuts off when water temp is reached. It doesn't keep temperature after it shuts off...I hope this answers your question.

title: THIS IS REALLY A GREAT KETTLE!!
body: Over the past 2 years, I've tried two other kettles. In both cases, the lid had plastic on the inside and we didn't feel good about that. Also, they were lightweight and didn't feel particularly durable. Conversely....THIS kettle is stainless steel inside and out.....including inside the lid. It has a simple straightforward on/off control. It's super easy to clean due to the higher lid position (which you move it to by hand). Also, it's double-walled, well made and sturdy. It's the quality kettle we were hoping for and have finally found. We really do love it.

title: No plastic! Looks and works great!
body: Love the design. 100% stainless steal inside and love the wide lid! - I can easily fill it up under the fridge’s water dispenser. We had a Hamilton beach kettle prior to this one and the lid broke and the auto shut off stopped working. This kettle is hands down waaaay better. Also love that the outside is not hot to touch due to double wall. Our old one was not like this. Very happy with purchase.

title: Great, but....
body: This is a great electric kettle. It's durable, has auto shut-off, and in general does everything it should and says it does. It's served us well. However, there is a design flaw that makes me questioning whether I would want to get it again should this one ever break: There's a hinge at the top of the kettle where the lid bends. Even with the lid closed, steam pours out of that hinge space, which just happens to be where I used to put my thumb to pour the hot water into my cup. Essentially, every time I'd try to pour the kettle in the beginning, I would burn my thumb on the steam. I had to train myself to grab the kettle differently so I wouldn't keep burning myself. This is something that could easily be fixed with a design revision, a thumb rest with a cover over the vent maybe? Perhaps doing something different with the lid. But having a product burn you because a design wasn't thought-out enough... There's no real excuse for it.

title: Quick & reliable
body: I absolutely love this tea kettle. It heats up in minutes and has an auto shut off so you know when it’s ready. I’ve been using it daily for months with zero issues. I love that the outside is protected from heat so you won’t burn yourself. Great value.

title: Sleek. A bit loud. A bit heavy. Does what it's supposed to.
body: The steam really comes spewing out so don't use under a shelf or cabinet.. Heats quickly. 750 ml capacity.

title: Fantastic plastic-free kettle! Love it!
body: I was not looking for a new kettle, but my cousins showed me their Cosori kettle which they had just gotten as a replacement for their old kettle which had plastic on the underside of the lid… as did mine. One thing I don’t want is plastic encountering anything hot that I will be eating or drinking. I actually bought two of them, because I have an apartment as well as a country house that I rent out some of the time. For the rental house I got the stainless steel model, which I love for its durability, because short term rental guests break things. I love that it is cool to the touch on the outside, and looks great with my other stainless steel appliances. For my apartment I bought the glass model, because it is visually unobtrusive. It really is beautiful. They both work wonderfully. I would highly recommend them even for people who don’t care about hot plastic encountering their food. They are the perfect kettles. I do wish there was a smaller apartment-sized model. I have had several other brands before, and every one of them has a minimum water level, which is more than I want to boil for myself. There must be a reason for this, because they all have it, but it seems wasteful to me. I would like to be able to boil just one 8 ounce cup of water. There doesn’t seem to be an electric kettle that does this. But otherwise, this is absolutely perfect!

title: Love it!!!
body: I was unfamiliar with his brand before I made my purchase. I was searching for a high quality commercial, food-grade stainless steel kettle. This kettle is perfect for us! We do not care about the digital function, and actually prefer the simplicity of this kettle. We use it every single day to make coffee in our French press and to make tea on cold evenings. We couldn’t be happier with this purchase!

title: Great kettle!
body: Excellent kettle! Love large capacity and stainless steel construction. Auto off feature works great!

title: Works great
body: We’ve been using it for about a week. We use it for brewing tea and French press coffee. So far I’m impressed with its ease of use and efficiency. I also like the price, the double lift lid, the small on/off lever, stainless steel liner and relative light weight. We’d purchased two Brevilles. They’re $200 and last 1 1/2 to 2 years (it’s a race to see if the base stops working or the kettle.) no more. Update Feb 27, 2025. Works like a champ. So glad I got this. Heats water in no time, and keeps it hot for a long time.

title: Functional (see new update below)
body: We bought this to replace our VonShef that stopped working after two years. I would have bought the VonShef again, but it is no longer available. After only 3 months with the Corosi it functions well, but I didn't realize how much I would miss the side window. It was extremely useful to be able to see at a glance how much water was in the pot. The Corosi has no viewing window and you must open the lid to see how much water is in it. The sides and handle do stay comfortable to the touch even when heated, unlike our previous VonShef. UPDATED 1/23: Cosori contacted me as a result of this review and said they would send their clear glass model to me. After some back in forth trying to get clarification as to what they would charge, nothing, I said to send the new model. The first attempt failed as they sent the exact same model as I already have. Back to customer service to let them know and request a shipping label. Then we did get the glass model and find that it is a vast improvement. Not that there is a difference in quality, but the fact that we can see how much water is in the pot and see when the water is approaching the boiling point versus active boiling. I would definitely recommend the glass model over the lower end double walled metal model. While I have to give Cosori customer support kudos for seeing my not very stellar review and contacting me a bout a free upgrade, the confusion over their exact offer and then failure to send the correct model initially, shows a lack of coordination between the customer support team and the order/shipping departments. All that said I would highly recommend this model: https://www.amazon.com/COSORI-Electric-Indicator-Protection-Stainless/dp/B07FKN76ZS/ref=pd_rhf_ee_s_bmx_1_9?_encoding=UTF8&pd_rd_i=B07FKN76ZS&pd_rd_r=844b6aed-8add-4ce7-9ca3-b68348b2ccbe&pd_rd_w=DTkvN&pd_rd_wg=8nR13&pf_rd_p=727767e7-d142-40af-a9a8-d3633da31912&pf_rd_r=F7DEAC338Q6EF7SJKVXW&psc=1&refRID=F7DEAC338Q6EF7SJKVXW

title: Big Betty!
body: That’s what I call her - My Big Betty. This electric tea pot is wonderful. I’ve always had stovetop whistling tea pots, but I just remodeled and purchased a new induction stove. I didn’t want a stovetop kettle in my new kitchen. I researched electric kettles and this was a top tier alternative to my usual. It heats up fast and looks great!

title: TEA TIME!
body: Love this classic vintage-look black kettle! I appreciate the simplicity of the design and user-friendliness. If I could change one thing….. I wish it had internal sound-insulation. It definitely lets you know when the water is boiling. This is a minor issue - not even enough to deduct a star.

title: Heats quickly, just wish it had larger capacity
body: I shopped for a while and read reviews on about 10 "finalists" for an electric kettle. My main goal was to find a stainless steel interior with as little contact with plastic as perfect. There are none that are totally plastic free, though many say the boiling water doesn't come into contact with the plastic. This was the best option I found, and I haven't regretted it. It has not bothered me that there is no window to view water levels, it just takes a quick peek by opening the lid to check before you turn it on. I also chose this one because the exterior does stay very cool to touch, so our kids can use two hands to pour it when they use it. The only two drawbacks that keep it from being a five star review are that: 1) the pour spout is poorly designed, and you do have to pour very slowly in order for it not to splash boiling hot water. This poses a danger to kids especially. 2) the capacity at 1.5 liters is a bit low, and the water gets used up quickly. Fortunately, it heats so quickly it hasn't really been a problem, just a minor inconvenience.

title: Great electric kettle. Incredibly energy efficient.
body: The double wall design for this electric kettle is what makes this such a good product. Double wall electric kettles are a must-have if you boil lots of water. Your old single wall electric kettle still wastes a significant amount of energy through the walls, and stove top kettles (on electric coil stoves) are the worst. Since all the heat is contained within the inner vessel, this might as well be one of the most efficient electric devices for boiling water, next to a microwave which is about 60% efficient at boiling water. Insta-pots are also incredibly efficient as well since they also form a vacuum seal between the inner and outer wall. Technically gas stoves/dryers are more "heat efficient" than electric/induction stoves since most electricity used to power the stove tops in the first place come from your local gas-fired or coal-fired power plant (honestly it depends on your energy mix). Accounting for combined-cycle turbine efficiency losses, boiling water with natural gas beats boiling water with electricity in almost all cases. It's just the reality of thermodynamics. The best, most "environmentally friendly" way to boil or heat anything with solar energy is with a glass vacuum heating chamber, but we're just not there yet as a species. Maybe in my lifetime.

title: Great kettle! No plastic touching the water.
body: Love this kettle. Matches my black stainless steel kitchen appliances

title: Almost perfect
body: Overall this kettle has worked very well. It gets water very hot and I really like the wide opening for easy cleaning. The outside finish is a lovely dark stainless steel which looks very sleek and elevated in our kitchen. The only thing I wished it had was adjustable temperature control. Also, if you get impatient while pouring note that the lid WILL leak water in addition to coming out of the spout. Not a problem for us, but just a note that it is not as snug as some other kettles.

title: Not seamless, but works well!
body: My morning ritual consists of waking up, taking the dog out and pouring my morning cup of tea. I have a tea kettle which sits on the stove that I don’t mind using to boil water, but sometimes I forget to take it off the stove while cooking and it quickly becomes covered in food splatter. (Gross, I know.) That’s when my lazy self turns to the microwave to heat my water. I needed a better way, and why not buy an electric kettle! I found this kettle had fantastic reviews and I loved the color options available. However, I’m sad to report this kettle may not be for me and I may end up returning it soon. Here’s why... Pros: - Price point is great! It’s a very nice kettle for the price. - Color selection. - Heats water rapidly! - Easy open top, cool sides while boiling. You won’t easily burn yourself with this kettle. - Super easy to use! Put water in, press down the button, done! It shuts off when it’s ready. Cons: - The size. It’s pretty bulky. I imagine most kettles will be bulky and seeing as this is my first one, I’m unsure what I was envisioning. - The lid- while the lid is super easy to open and close with the touch of a button, it makes it impossible to fill up the kettle using the refrigerator dispenser. - This is not a seamless kettle- I went back and read through the description and it does not mention it’s seamless. (I looked at so many I think they started to blend together.) However, I personally prefer a seamless design. I dumped the water, even wiped out the inside, left the lid open, and a few hours later when I went to check to see if it was dry water seeped out of the seam on the inside. I worry about grime/mildew forming in that area. - I saw a lot of complaints about the inside discoloring. This did happen to mine after two uses despite boiling vinegar and water to clean it as mentioned in the instructions. I’m not going to knock off a point for this as I do think it’s normal seeing as I have very hard water, but it still doesn’t look great. - I also wish it had a warming feature but for the price point, I don’t expect it to. Overall, this is a great kettle. It heats water quickly, it looks pretty nice, but I just don’t think it’s the right one for me.

title: Love that the outside does not get too hot
body: Used electric kettles in Italy and found them so convenient we had to get one when we got home. This model was actually better than several others that I have used both in America and Italy because it has a double wall which acts as an insulator. You are not touching a super hot pot and thus eliminates a possible burn risk. Does get warm on the outside, but it is not in the burn range. Heating is as advertised - at the max fill line it does heat to boiling (and beyond) and turns off at 6 min. This is actually much faster than my gas stove and tea kettle for heating the same amount of water, plus it turns itself off too! I also like that is metal vs glass so less risk of breakage. I would recommend a buy for this model.

title: Cosori Electric Kettle
body: Needed a new electric kettle since my other kettle only lasted 5 years!! I prefer Electric kettles over boiling on a stove. I have had kettles burn up and melt by forgetting them on stove. I find the electric kettle a safer option. Very happy with this electric Kettle. I like the stainless steel and double wall. It is all in one and has an enclosed element so cleaning very easy. With all electric kettles and water there eventually is a scale build up, but again very easy to clean. Lid opens good but does not open fully. You can move lid up to open wider. This kettle boils water very quickly and stays hot for at least 10 minutes which I am satisfied with. Has a nice swivel base and cord is long enough for counter use. I put kettle next to electrical outlet so no issue. It has a switch at the base of kettle that turns blue when on. It has the automatic turn off feature which is a must. It is a solid black and no clear glass (plastic) for viewing water level. As a personal preference I do not find that important since each time I use the kettle I rinse it out. This is a good basic electric kettle that gets the job done. Hope it lasts a long time. Would purchase again.

title: Disappointment out of the box
body: I purchased this kettle a little over a year ago. I had a previous version of this from this company. It was a great kettle worked fine. Had it for about four years and it was getting a little bit used and then I noticed they put out a new model, so I jumped on it. The minute I took it out of the box and held it in my hand. It felt uncomfortable. The changes they made. I don’t think we’re very good. Most of this is subjective but let me continue. The handle design is uncomfortable compared to the previous model. The design of the cover which goes up halfway and then can open actually more is the biggest pain. Opening the thing up, halfway makes it a disaster trying to put water in. It is extremely difficult to then open the cover up all the way. I don’t know what this function does but it’s completely useless. The major issue I now have is that after timing the heating yesterday it now takes six minutes and 33 seconds to bring tap water to a boil. Sometimes change, or “updating features” are just not the way to go. I’m gonna look for something new. And I’ve learned that if I don’t like the handle the minute, I pull it out of the box. I’ll send it back.

title: Big enough to fit my Aeropress and Timemore grinder inside for road trips.
body: I no longer have to be victimized by lousy coffee from the gas station chains, those "fresh ground every cup" abominations that are taking over in place of actual brewed coffee. With some road beans, a hand grinder, an Aeropress and this kettle, I can have seriously good caffeine in any hotel room or anywhere else there's an open electric outlet. And the best part is my grinder fits inside the aeropress which fits inside the water kettle, so the whole thing is way smaller than bringing a good electric percolator on the road. Only complaint I have is that the lid on the kettle won't open up fully when I press the release button. I have to manually wrench the lid fully open. Other than that, does what I want it to.

title: great stainless steel kettle
body: I bought this as I wanted only stainless steel touching the water and not plastic. It was one of the only affordable highly rated ones I could find. The plastic base/switch seem more lightweight and flimsy than our last one, but the kettle itself seems great. It heats enough water really quickly to fill a pot of tea or two-three big travel mugs. the interior is really sleek and easy to clean. Have only had it for 2 weeks.Hopefully this one will last a long time.

title: Exactly what I wanted
body: Loved the sleek look & finish. Liked the double walled stainless steel interior for food safety. Light weight. My favorite feature is the start & stop attachment. It lights up blue when heating & turns off when done . Very fast . Heats water very hot or just flick the piece up to stop it earlier for less hot . Very pleased .

title: Reliable electric kettle
body: This is my second Cosori electric kettle. I purchased the first one in 2019. I used this kettle everyday for 3 years sometimes twice a day. The quality is excellent, easy to clean and a very attractive design. It looks beautiful on my coffee bar. This electric kettle has been one of the most reliable appliances in my kitchen. However, after 3 years the auto shutoff switch seems a little slower than when it was new. This kettle is simple to operate and brings water to a rapid boil very quickly. There is a safety auto shutoff and is easily turned off and on. The water stays hot for a long time after it boils. I have since gifted this electric kettle to most of my family members, everyone loves it. Shipping is always in a timely manner and the packaging is very good. I would recommend Cosori electric kettles.

title: Works great
body: Nice looking style, works well, a bit larger than expected but kept it.

title: Excellent tea kettle
body: Heats the water super fast. It is a bit noisy, but you are only listening to it for about a minute. The mineral buildup on the very bottom is a bit of a pain but easy to remove. I just add about 8 ounces of water and about a tablespoon of lemon juice to the kettle, heat to a boil, and then let it sit for about 20 minutes to clean it. I just rinse it afterwards and it is good to go. I do this once a week. Not a bother at all. I really like that the boiling water does not come into contact with any plastic. This was very important to me.

title: Useful
body: I have been using this product every day for over a year. It has become a part of my life. There are no strange smells, the water does not come into contact with the plastic. I recommend it.

title: Works great
body: My previous electric kettle did not have a base that you lift the kettle off of. You had to juggle the kettle with the cord connected or else unplug it. This kettle is so much easier to use and it’s very quick and efficient. Looks nice on the counter as well.

title: so far its ok
body: Nice design and all stainless inside. However, the bottom started corroding and I am not sure how bad will this will be after a few months. I will keep my eye on it.

title: Cool to Touch
body: I love everything about this COSORI electric tea kettle. First of all it looks great! I got the 1.5 L in stainless steel finish. It is Cool Touch so I won’t burn myself. It is fast to boil and automatically turns Off when it’s done. I won’t worry about boiling my tea kettle dry. The switch illuminates with a blue light when it is on. The cord wraps neatly in the base. Includes a nice instruction booklet and has 2 year warranty. It was packaged securely and arrived on schedule. Looking forward to many nice cups of tea!

title: Good Product
body: While it longer works lol had to write a review. This was a very good product had it 4y8m of daily multiple use before it gave up the ghost. LOL We were so happy we wanted to repurchase it, but no longer available but our replacement is by same maker. Here's hoping it will last as long and perform as well.

title: Very good tea kettle
body: This is my first tea kettle, and it’s definitely a game changer. The only thing I don’t like about it is the base. The base is flimsy, and moves a bit when you remove the kettle to pour.

title: Perfect
body: The fact that there’s no plastic that contacts the water makes this a no-brainer. So far, so good. Heats up fast. Automatic shut off works. Surface is cool enough that if you accidentally touch it you won’t get burned.

title: PLEASED! Exactly as advertised
body: Received today. Can’t speak to durability yet, although it seems to be well constructed at 1st examination & 1st use. Pros: 1. 7 minutes 5 seconds from start, to boil. That’s with pot completely filled with very cold water. (My plan is to fill it at night, let it come to room temperature, then plug it in next morning - which should cut that time 2. Easy to fill. The lid does not detach (good thing), but does open to at least 80 degrees I would say. 3. Will be easy to clean - very smooth inside. 4. Spout is large & easy pour. When pot is full, pour slowly - it’s possible to slosh water out around the lid. But it’s not a defect. Just gravity LOL. 5. I’m going to get a bottle brush to clean out the spout. I don’t think it will be necessary, but I plan to give this pot a lot of use. 6. Outside does not overheat. It is warm when water is at full boil, but not hot. 7. Heavy enough to feel sturdy, but not too heavy. Just right, actually. 8. Quiet. I can hear it, but it’s not annoying. Just pleasant background sound. 9. Blue light in the “on switch” is nice color & brightness. Also excellent indicator as to boil status. (Auto off when it reaches a boil). Con (minor): 1. It’s not a matte finish, so fingerprints will show.

title: (Updated Review) Rusting after just 2 months of use. Buyer Beware!
body: Edited Review (October 18, 2023): We received the new kettle directly from Kosovo and have been using it for a year. It’s generally been a positive experience. Our usage has been on average about once a day with the kettle filled with RO water upto the “max” mark. Its held up quite well with no rust or pinholes observed. As others have pointed out, it is quite noisy as it heats up but becomes very silent several seconds before autoshutoff when the water starts to boil. While I am still not sure why we had such a bad first experience with the new kettle purchased from Amazon, I am leaning toward recommending this kettle and have updated to 3 stars. —————————————————————- I am very disappointed with the kettle quality. The water contact layer inside is most certainly not “food grade” stainless steel as the company advertises on Amazon. We used the kettle to boil filtered water for less than 2 months and observed rusting and small pin holes on the bottom surface. Quite sure we’ve been drinking water that has been contaminated. I contacted the company and they were quick to blame Amazon for selling me a “used” kettle. I asked them what that has got to do with the kettle rusting and they didn’t answer. They are shipping me a new kettle which is fine, however, I am not convinced that’s going to change the situation. I will update the review if I find the new kettle to be different. Please use your good judgement before purchasing this kettle and potentially putting your family’s health in danger!

title: Everything I was looking for

Not a tall order at all, right? :) This teapot is actually perfect. I saw teapots for more than twice as much that had bad reviews, and the good reviews on this one convinced me to take a chance. We drink a lot of tea in my house (and often need boiling water for other things as well) and I didn't want to fire up the gas stove all the time. This sits plugged in right next to my stove tucked into a corner, is always cool to the touch and incredibly easy to use, which I do several times a day. For $40, it's a steal. I love that there is no plastic whatsoever inside the pot, and the indicator light is lovely and easy to see when it goes off (plus it's easy to hear the water boiling). I didn't think a teapot could make me so happy!

After about 1.5 years the kettle would no longer shut off automatically because the lid would kind of bend upward with the heat of the boiling water. It would just boil forever and never turn itself off. I contacted Cosori about this and they replaced it under their 2 year warranty that covers this item. They just needed me to send them a video showing the problem and they sent out another one. Hopefully the new one lasts longer than the original.

title: Parts NOT missing and Stains disappear
body: First let me say we have and have had numerous stainless steel appliances over our 46 years of married life and understand that stainless can be stained by certain substances along with hard water. Additionally, let me state our water is softened (current hardness level is 1.5 gpg, or 25 ppm, measured as CaCO3). Following the manual’s instructions for initial cleaning before use, (fill with water, heat the water, discard water and wipe clean) resulted in stains!!! Tolerable, but not happy about it. Then noticed kettle wobbled on the base: caused by rubber feet missing on the base and (apparently) the kettle! How does someone supposedly inspect and item and put it in a box and miss this?! Not confident this will last very long when obvious exterior items are missing and the “stainless steel(?)” is stained by soft city water after heating just 1.7 l of water! We have a stainless steel Soyajoy G4 that is used twice a week and is several years old that uses the same water and has yet to stain! We probably won’t be buying any more Cosori products. On the positive side, it is pretty and does heat the water, but we didn’t buy it for a decoration, and we have other ways of heating water for our tea. UPDATE: After contacting the maker it turns out that it is only suppose those one rubber foot on the bottom of the base and, the next day the stains were gone! With the makers response and the wonderful way it works, (even though I'm confused as to why only one foot?) I've upgraded my rating to 5 stars!

title: If you are looking for an honest review, here it is.
body: 3.5 stars isn't an option but it would be my most honest choice but I am not looking to discourage people so I went with the 4. So, to start, if you are hunting for an honest review to help make your decision, here goes... I apologize in advance I can be a bit long winded but, I want to offer the best information I can. I am a person who doesn't buy things for myself, not that I can't I just don't. I am a firm believer that money spent on something I want would be better spent on needs. Bills, food, something my wife wants, ect. I had seen the FrostBuddy on tiktok for a month+ I had watched the price go up and down, nearly bought it a few times, especially when it was down to $24.99. Along comes the weekend of Christmas, with the push of my wife I decided to pull the trigger. Justified to my inner crazy as a Christmas gift from my wife. So, I ordered it. It arrived early the evening of Thursday after Christmas. I opened it right up, initial thoughts. I like the look, color texture ect. Looks and feels good. Let's try it out, I put a 12oz redbull in it straight away. It fit well, no movement. My first issue was found right away, the can sits very low to the "lid" as a result when I drink my bottom lip contacts the silicone lid rather than the can. Minor concern I assumed I would get used to, I have. Tried a 12oz can of my dew next, it sits a touch higher lessening the lip to lid vs can issue, which again I am already used to. Now comes day 2, I get to address/verify a couple other concerns 1. does it fit in the cup holder of my truck (22 Colorado), it is snug but it does fit. 2. Does the 16oz redbull fit, it does but... The lid has to be "forced" over the can, now I understand in order to be universal the lid is going to need to "adapt" to address different size cans. This development leads to a new issue and my first real complaint, upon finishing the first 16oz can I go to remove it and as I said the lid was forced on as a result it had to be forced off. I assume this is not a big deal, remove the can with the lid still attached, apply equal pressure with my fingers and thumb around the bottom of the lid. The force required to get the lid off caused the silicone to detach from the bottom of the lid in a small spot. This was my first disappointment as I know that small spot will for sure get worse with use and my $40 investment is damaged less than 24 hours in. Now my 2nd concern, the claim is drinks keep cold 12 hours and hot 6 hours. I have no intention of using it for hot so that is irrelevant but the 12 hours of cold was/is the point of buying for me. I like my drinks very cold but I don't care for using cups of ice and a straw so I figure this is the next best thing to all the tumblers out there everyone loves so much. I assume the 12 hours is optimistic at best but my drink will not last that long so half (6 hours) would be more than sufficient. I will say, this does by all means help keep the drink cold compared to nothing or a basic soft can coozie. That said, it does not maintain the starting temperature but maybe 2 hours at 4-5 it is still colder than room temperature by all means but not exactly cold anymore. I generally finish a drink in less than an hour so all things considered it does keep majority of my drinks cold long enough. However if you are someone who makes a drink last several hours and you expect this to keep it icy cold for anywhere near the 12 hours it claims you should expect disappointment. If you are hoping for your drink to stay colder than it would without assistance it will. I will continue to use it until the lid fails me, and unfortunately I'm sure it will. Perhaps I just got a dud, with all things mass produced there are sure to be some that don't meet the same standard as others it is just part of the deal. I am not willing to spend another $40 to see if a different one would work better so I may never know. I had high hopes/expectations, I am disappointed that I am disappointed. I will update when the lid fails, or if I find any other issues. If you made it this far, sorry for the book but that was the only way I could feel like I gave the best "advice" I had. I wouldn't not recommend it, I would just advise you to lower your expectations a bit. Again, I may have received a dud. Best of luck, thanks for reading.

title: DO NOT OVERFILL ABOVE FIVE CUPS! OR IT WILL LEAK.. AND BE NOT SAFE.

The manual is in your order record while you click the support button and follow instructions. I bought this pot some 6 months ago. Love it totally. I was very careful with choosing a pot as I love all things organic, clean, no plastic and non leaching materials, no aluminum and no coatings of a non stick type. So this felt like a good choice and it is indeed a healthy choice as I had a chance to browse ton of all different kinds. I finally settled for this one because: * I love the elegant design, in person is just gorgeous. It reminds me of those offered at Williams Sonoma site but this one is even nicer and cheaper. * I love the stainless steel interior. That was an absolute must for me as I don't like aluminum or glass as there are all kinds of impurities in glass. I also did not like the ones that have mixed materials inside, some glass, some metal, some plastic. This one is just that: PLAIN STAINLESS INSIDE. Not seams, no welding that could be contaminated, nothing, just plain one surface sleek and smooth. *The top is also stainless steel inside so no contamination. I often open the top for cooking anyway to let my water air as it boils to release any volatile chemicals that can go with the steam. * I love the design that is so practical and easy to use: - the holding arm is designed in funny way and I was wondering how pracitcal it will be but it is quite easy to use and hold and the angle is good. - The white finish is perfect gorgeous car like.. very good hard finish that will last. So easy to clean and does not attract dirt. - I love the little crystal accents, the handle of the top and the lever that you turn it on and off. - The turn on of lever is so perfect. I really love that little blue light that shines through the glass like lever that looks like a piece of ice.. so beautiful. It is on when the pot is boiling water and off once finished. MY most favorite function of course is the fact that it AUTOMATICALLY SHUTS OFF. Total pece of mind. I just pour water, turn it off and can walk away and forget it knowing it will not keep boiling till the end of times, it will boil the water and promptly turn itself off once done. It is Rocket fast!!! I did not time it but It is has to be around minute or two or so or three tops.. as I barely can manage to connect it, walk away to do something and come back a nd it is done. Love it! I just came back to get a second one for different area in the house so I have my second tea station near the work space. Along with few bottles of water, I don't need a sink to make my tea whenever I fancy.

title: Interior: 100% Glass. Finally, Someone Gets It.
body: The main thing we needed was a kettle that wasn’t plastic or metal where it contacts the water—something that shouldn’t be revolutionary but apparently is. The product description was vague, but it hinted at glass, so we took a chance. Pleasant surprise: it’s 100% glass inside. Finally, something that delivers what it quietly implies. Living in Colorado, where water boils at 202°F instead of 212°, I appreciated the temperature display creeping upward like a suspense scene. Lid open, eyes on the prize—right at 202°, it hit a boil. The temp gauge is dead accurate, and honestly, it’s just nice when tech works like it says it will. Now for the nitpick: coffee is best at 195–196°, but the “Coffee” button stops at 194°. Tragic? No. Irritating? Slightly. But that’s the only knock I’ve got. Gave it four stars—for now. Let’s see how long it lasts before I start regretting being optimistic.

title: Not 100% What I Wanted
body: MANUFACTURER: WHY CAN'T YOU MAKE A GLASS POT WITH A GLASS LID OR METAL LID, ANYTHING BUT PLASTIC!? PROS: Glass body, looks nice, blue light when in use is also a nice touch, affordable. CONS: Lid is still plastic, and a plastic mesh filter is not detachable. How I use: First I cut off the mesh filter with a pair of cutting pliers as this filter is completely useless to me. I suppose if you brewed tea in the pot the filter would have a purpose, but I only just boil water. Then, as the lid is still plastic and hot condensation water collects at the underside of the lid and drops back into the pot, probably carrying microplastics from the lid, I leave the lid open when I boil water. It might extend the cooking time a few seconds, but doesn't seem to make a big difference. I only use the pot once or twice a day and just stay around until the water boils, so I can turn it off immediately (before too much steam escapes).

title: It does the job of heating water
body: It does the job of heating water. It takes 9 minutes to raise it to boiling if the water starts at 70°F. Might be a little slower than my old kettle that looked just like this but I dropped it and broke the glass… they’re alike enough that the base for the old one works for the new one. But there are some other differences, namely in the preset temperatures. They temps are in Fahrenheit, but jump up according to +10°C. So if you were looking to memorize the what 90°C is in Fahrenheit, this kettle will help you do it. One little nitpick, and I had it with the old one too, is that you can’t move down the presets from boiling down. If you want to set it to 203°, you have to press the plus button like 9 times, instead of just one minus button, which is like the most first world of problems, but how hard is it to count down? Between that and the extended time it takes to boil, I’ve taken off one star, if it could only be half a star... It’s still a good kettle for the price, and as long as you remember to turn the kettle on well before you actually sit down to tea, you won’t have to spend the time it takes to boil writing a review. If there is one thing that would move this product to 5 stars for me more than anything else would be a programmable button for your favorite temp setting. Cause I use the 203°F (95°C) the most, and pressing up 8 times to get to my favorite setting is obnoxious. Maybe keep the boil button but have the other 3 be programmable by holding it down while you use the arrows to set the temp. Cause I never use the white or coffee temps. Idk how doable it is, but it’d definitely improve the functionality for me. Not everyone wants the same temp presets.

title: Nice but Overpriced
body: Arrived today. Out of the box, it seemed overall a reasonably quality made product. Nice weight. Pretty colour---NOT WHITE more of a beige colour, which is fine by me. Looks nice on the stove top. Has a sort of romantic, girly looking theme to the design with the faux diamond pieces which are plastic not glass. For this price point, would it have killed them to make the knob out of glass? It would have helped justify the high price. Would make a nice wedding or anniversary present. Even empty, the pot is fairly weighty. The cord and base look well made but the base is lightweight plastic. Directions were to fill the kettle with cold water to the max fill level, boil, empty, and repeat before consuming water boiled in it. It boiled the water quickly as expected---5 cups worth. The lever lights up blue whilst it is turned on. Automatically shuts off once the water reaches the boiling point. I awarded three stars only because of the high price point for what one is getting and because this kettle is awkward in the hand---not ergonomically designed at all. This kettle is OVERPRICED. $30 or even $35 would be an equitable price point although $35 is really pushing it. I expect the overpricing is based not on functionality but looks. Instead of this kettle, I would rather have had another of Maxi-Matic's Elite Cuisine Hot Pots which do the same job and more, and are really excellent value for money by comparison. The hot pots are plastic, and you cannot remove them from their bases, and they do not have an on/off switch and do not turn themselves off automatically, but they are VERY functional. They heat water very fast for beverages and for cooking, and with the removable egg rack and steamer rack which come standard with the hot pots, they are great for boiling eggs and steaming veggies and fish, and for steaming rolls and reviving stale bread, etc. The hot pots are also good for heating soups and broths and keeping them warm because the pots have a variable heat control unlike this kettle. They are excellent units to keep by the bedside if you are ill. You can easily heat food in them and keep the food warm right by the bedside instead of walking back and forth from the kitchen with plates/bowls of food. If you are sick, you can limit trips to the kitchen to twice per day or less if you do not mind leaving your used plate/bowl in the bedroom overnight. The hot pots are white plastic, though, so some foods, e.g. carrots and tomato based soups and stews, etc., will stain the white plastic, but that is true of any white plastic products. Best of all, I only paid $15 for each one of my two Maxi-Matic hot pots. They are not especially pretty, but they are versatile workhorses that lasted a good 3-4 years with every day use. PLEASE BRING BACK THE HOT POTS!! They are very good value for money. ETA: I have used this kettle for a few days now, and I have found it awkward to handle, which surprised me. Holding it at the top of the handle it does not feel secure or easy to pour. Holding it at the base of the handle it feels more secure in my hand, but it is not easy to pour. I have decided to return it for this reason. Your milage may vary of course, but it just does not work for me. Also wanted to add that the outside of the kettle gets much warmer than the outside of the Miroco kettle I bought to replace this one by Elite Gourmet.

title: NO PLASTIC TOUCHING WATER!!!
body: I have been searching for years for an electric teakettle with no plastic inside, and finally I have found one! When I first got it, it had a plasticky, chemical smell. It had some sort of coating. After about 10 attempts at merely boiling water, then dumping it out didn’t remove the smell, I researched how to get rid of it. It turns out the best method is to cut up some lemons and/or limes and boil them in clean water in the teakettle, then let that sit (I let it sit over night), dump it out, then boil fresh water again. Finally, that worked. The smell was still barely perceptible to me, but I am a super smeller. No one in my family noticed it, and I couldn’t smell it once it was in the cup, not in the kettle anymore. After about a day of two of use, I could no longer smell it at all. I have had the kettle for about 2 months, and it still works well. It holds enough water for 4 mugs of tea, coffee, etc. The exterior of the kettle stays cool, such that my kids can use it without me having to worry. The way the auto-shutoff works is by a magnet that stops being magnetized when the boiling temperature has been reached. Apparently, that is how most analog kettles work. My autodidactic homeschooled son explained that to me. While I find that pretty cool, the real appeal is the lack of computers that will stop working before the actual mechanics of the appliance do. Reliably analog! I did drop it last week, when I was trying to take the lid off while I was holding the kettle. It still works, but the seam is slightly wonky now. It is not really noticeable. Top marks for taking a lickin’ and keeping on tickin’! The only cons are the initial smell, the fact that you can’t set the temperature or even know it, and the appearance is slightly tacky. I say slightly, because the handle is silver colored plastic, and that plastic jewel on the top is a little princessy for me. I hate the logo in silver. That is so tacky. However, I can abide by the pan-European-as-interpreted-by-the-Chinese aesthetic in exchange for WATER NEVER TOUCHING PLASTIC!!! You did it, guys!!! Wooo hooooo!!!! This company makes a more English-looking kettle with a thermometer, but apparently there is a little bit of plastic in that one, where the thermometer penetrates the kettle. Now, all my actual meat thermometers are metal probes, so I can’t quite figure that one out. The cream color is fine — pretty enough. Overall, it is attractive enough — except for that stupid dorky logo , but it isn’t a deal breaker. In conclusion, I recommend this tea kettle, but be prepared to do a little work to get the plasticky smell out, at first.

title: Good quality, 12 hours cold water
body: I got the midnight berry color. I have used this brand and model of cup for years. This is my third one in like 7 years. My second 24oz. The newer ones have grip issues. I bought my bf one 2 years ago and the grip is loose. We had to get him another because he dropped the seal and it was never to be found again so it leaked, and that grip was also loose. This one that I ordered, again the grip is loose. It twists and actually will slide up with minimal effort when bottle is dry, and even more so when its wet. My old ones didnt do this, but the newer model does. I have included a photo showing that it slides. I have carpal tunnel so its not like I strong armed it. Aside from that, its not nearly as sparkly as the image suggests. Which i was sad about but im more about the function. I LOVE it because it stays cold forever. I fill it halfway with ice, and still have a small chunk of ice left after 10 hours if im drinking out of it, and if I leave it closed and untouched overnight( I take it to bed with me so I have cold water at night) it has most of its ice by morning. I typically sleep 9-10 hours for reference. The lid is pretty easy to over screw and gets really tight. My old one started leaking after like 4 or 5 years. Thats why I got the new one. Its pretty durable. I dropped this baby on concrete from 12ft high. It got rather dented on the bottom and I just took a hammer to it to flatten it back out. My lid dented near the mouth piece. But I probably dropped it on concrete at work over 60 times. It scratched, it dented but still worked just fine for years. I have rather small hands but it seems yo be fine to hold, even if I do have carpal tunnel. I dont use it for anything hot so I cant vouch on that topic. I hand wash the lid daily and the cup itself weekly. The little rubber seal in the lid can be a bit of a pain to pull out, but you can GENTLY get it out with a toothpick and some patience. Its very important to throughly wash and dry that little rubber seal. You can get sick if you dont. OK, review over.

title: Hands down the best. Even if you just need a new lid gasket, Contigo takes care of their customers.
body: I get tired of writing detailed reviews because I buy so much from Amazon. I usually just give "Star" ratings now. I'm updating this with details because I'm so impressed with Contigo as a company. So here goes! 4 years ago, I bought 2 of the Contigo Kenton travel mugs. I’ve never had better mugs. Earlier this year, I needed new stoppers and gasket seals for the lids. Other than that, they are just as functional as the day I got them. I couldn't find and still haven't found gasket seals for the Kenton model that actually fit the lids. Even though they look exactly like the Byron lid, the gasket doesn't fit. I looked everywhere with NO luck. So I looked for a replacement lid. Couldn't find that either. I was mad! I'm a spend thrift. I keep things, take care of them and keep using them until there is absolutely no more useful life. These are not cheap mugs! I didn't want to buy a whole new mug just because the old ones need new gaskets. A good mug that DOES NOT LEAK is something that makes my life A LOT EASIER. I was mad about the gasket issue so I looked for another brand that would meet the same high standards as Contigo. I read reviews until my eyes were red and watering. I didn't want to buy another mug if I couldn't replace something as simple as a replacement gasket. I came across this one on sale for a good price. I knew it would be good at least until the gasket needed to be replaced. I love the color. With gritted teeth, I placed my order. I can throw these mugs across the room and none of my coffee would be spilled. I mean that. I tried it! A couple of months later, the gasket broke. I wasn't happy about that, but I had all those gaskets that wouldn't fit my old lids. They worked fine. Two months ago (7 months after buying), the flip part of the lid wouldn't stay closed. A lot of work was destroyed by the coffee that flooded out of the mug. At first I thought I just forgot to snap it closed. Not so. The snap on this lid is not as secure as the other ones. Out of sheer stubbornness, I was determined to either MAKE the gaskets fit my old lids or find something that would. Try as I might they just wouldn’t fit. In exasperation, I called Conitigo. Maybe they could tell me where I could find gaskets. That was my only reason for calling them. In my conversation, I mentioned the problems with the Byron mug I bought 9 months ago. I assumed it was too late to ask for a refund from Amazon. She told me that Contigo has a 5 year warranty on their mugs. After asking me for the manufacturers’ ID on the bottom of the mug, she told me they would send a brand new mug in 5 days. Not just a lid, an entire mug! But it gets better. They are also sending replacements for my old Kenton travel mugs. The ONLY thing I had to do was send one picture of all three mugs side by side. They are sending me 2 entirely new mugs because the gaskets need replacing??? No questions, nothing. 2 brand new mugs. Within a week, I’ll have 3 brand new Contigo travel mugs. I'm blown away. I have to say it again. I am totally blown away. As long as their standard of customer care and product quality remains the same, I will never ever buy a travel mug from any other company.

title: Mediocre So Far
body: Only giving three stars for this one. Mine arrived today and no issues there (the one that came yesterday for my mother had a dent it). It looks very attractive, I got the Blueberry. It is too big for my cup holder for one which is a drag. Other issue I have is I just made a cup of coffee an hour ago and put it into the contigo to see how long it would stay hot. After 40 minutes I tried it and the coffee was a 'warm-hot', not hot but not tepid warm either...honestly I thought it would stay hotter longer, at that rate it would be bleh in little over an hour. Decided to go ahead and return it, I dont think hot up to two hours is too much to ask. I like the cap, the hole for the coffee to come out isnt as wide as some mugs which I hate because sometimes you get a little dribble if you're angle is off a bit. This is less wide, a round hole really....more oblong but almost round....anyway had no issues drinking from it and closing lid back. Ill test it some more with other cups that I can heat extra hot to see...I'll update this once I do. UPDATE - So last night I thought about it and figured maybe only having put 1/3 of the way with coffee made it cool faster so I made two pods last night. Put the first pod in and closed the mug, made the second and opened the cup and added it then closed the lid tightly. I waited 2 hours and 20 minutes without opening the mug at all, so then I opened it and tried the coffee. It was 'almost hot', still had enough heat to make it drinkable but thats it. They state this keeps it hot up to 6 hours which you assume is not what you will actually get just because thats advertising but if they claim 6 then less than 2.5 hours without the mug being opened at all should have resulted in a still pretty darn hot cup of coffee, it was not even close.

title: Perfect for Meal Prep and Storage, with Some Minor Considerations
body: Pros: Generous Quantity and Value: The Freshware Food Storage Containers come in a set of 50, which is fantastic for meal prepping, storing leftovers, or organizing food. The quantity ensures you'll have enough for multiple uses, and at this price point, you get great value for your money. Durable and Leakproof: These containers are well-made and sturdy, offering reliable storage without worrying about leaks. The lids seal tightly, making them ideal for soups, stews, and even dishes with sauces, ensuring no messes or spills in your fridge or bag. Microwave, Dishwasher, and Freezer Safe: A huge benefit of these containers is that they are safe for the microwave, dishwasher, and freezer. This versatility makes them incredibly convenient for reheating meals, easy cleaning, and long-term storage. I’ve used them for both freezing meals and microwaving leftovers without any issues. Stackable Design: The stackable nature of these containers makes them easy to store when not in use, helping you save space in your kitchen. They fit well in most cabinets or drawers, and you can stack them neatly in the fridge or freezer without them taking up too much room. BPA-Free and Safe: For anyone concerned about harmful chemicals in food storage, these containers are BPA-free, offering peace of mind that your food is stored safely. They’re a much healthier alternative to some other plastic containers on the market. Cons: Not as Thick as Some Alternatives: While these containers are durable for everyday use, they aren't as thick as some higher-end alternatives. If you’re looking for heavy-duty, long-term storage or containers that can withstand a lot of rough handling, these might feel a bit flimsy in comparison. They’re fine for regular meal prep, but you may want something more robust for extremely heavy or bulky food items. Lids Can Be Hard to Line Up: Sometimes, the lids don’t align as easily as I’d like. While they seal well once you get them on, there’s a slight struggle to make sure the lid is lined up perfectly, especially when stacking or storing. This could be a minor inconvenience for users who need to seal containers quickly. Limited to 16oz Capacity: While 16 oz is a great size for most snacks, salads, or small portions, it may be a bit too small for larger meals or family-size servings. For those who meal prep larger portions, you may need to buy a larger size to complement these. Suggestions for Improvement: Thicker Construction for Durability: A slight improvement in thickness would go a long way in making these containers feel more durable. Reinforcing the material slightly could increase their longevity and ability to handle bulkier or more challenging food items without cracking or warping. Smoother Lid Design: Slight adjustments to the lid design could make it easier to line them up without much effort. If the lid could snap on more easily or have a clearer indicator for proper placement, it would improve the overall ease of use. Larger Size Options: While the 16 oz size is ideal for snacks and small portions, adding a few larger size options in the same set would make these containers more versatile for different meal prepping needs. Final Thoughts: Overall, the Freshware Food Storage Containers are a great choice for anyone looking for affordable, leakproof, and versatile food storage. They excel at meal prep, storing leftovers, and organizing food, with a design that’s microwave, dishwasher, and freezer safe. While they’re not the thickest or most robust containers on the market, they do the job well for most everyday needs. If you’re looking for a practical and cost-effective solution for food storage, I’d highly recommend these, just be mindful of the size and occasional lid alignment issues.

title: Stylish and Efficient Kettle with a Minor Aesthetic Flaw
body: I recently purchased the DmofwHi Gooseneck Electric Kettle, and overall, I am quite pleased with its performance and stylish design. The kettle works exceptionally well, providing fast and efficient boiling capabilities. However, there is one minor drawback that prevents me from giving it a perfect five-star rating—the appearance of the brown plastic parts. Let's start with the positives. The functionality of this gooseneck kettle is excellent. It heats up water quickly and efficiently, saving me valuable time in the morning or whenever I need a hot beverage. The gooseneck spout offers precise pouring control, allowing me to achieve the perfect pour-over coffee or tea without any spills. The temperature control settings are accurate and easy to use, ensuring that I can select the ideal water temperature for different brewing methods. In terms of performance, this kettle truly delivers. Moving on to the design, the overall aesthetic of the kettle is visually appealing. The sleek shape and vibrant color add a touch of modernity to my kitchen countertop. The stainless steel body is solid and well-constructed, instilling confidence in its durability. The gooseneck spout design, while functional, also adds a distinctive and elegant touch to the kettle's appearance. However, my only qualm lies with the brown plastic parts of the kettle. While they don't affect the kettle's performance or functionality, they do give off a slightly cheap plastic appearance. This is particularly noticeable in contrast to the otherwise sleek and premium stainless steel body. It would have been preferable if these brown parts were made of a material that better matched the overall quality and aesthetic of the kettle. That being said, I must emphasize that this aesthetic flaw does not detract from the kettle's performance or functionality. It is purely a minor issue related to visual appeal. The kettle still serves its purpose admirably, and the plastic components do not affect the taste or safety of the boiled water. In summary, the DmofwHi Gooseneck Electric Kettle is a stylish and efficient appliance that excels in its primary function of quickly boiling water. The vibrant color and sleek design make it an attractive addition to any kitchen. While the brown plastic parts may look somewhat cheap, they do not compromise the kettle's performance. If you can overlook this minor aesthetic flaw, you'll find a reliable and functional kettle that meets your needs with ease. I would recommend it for its performance, but deducting one star due to the plastic's appearance.

title: UPADATE: Still excellent after 5 months
body: Update: 5 mos later, everything below is still true! After exhaustively searching Amazon, Walmart, Target, etc., and considering name-brands, I settled on this kettle, with low-ish expectations. My main priorities were: a lid that was removable, not on a hinge; a volume that worked well for 1-2 people, and would hold up under daily use. I originally wanted a shorter spout, but am now very happy with the curved, but not overly-long spout for pouring over filter coffee. After daily use for 2 months, it is still working as well as the day out of the box. Things that have not been a problem: It has never failed to shut itself off upon boiling (and I click down on the tab more than once each use). The lid fits very securely - snug, but not hard to remove - and therefore never any leakage. The steam holes in lid are easy to position away from handle, and so hot fingers not a problem. Likewise, handle is sturdy and easy to hold. Interior is easy to clean. Tab to press down is plastic, yes, but not flimsy. Never had any odor, even from outset. Yes, the outside of kettle gets hot with boil.... but that's what the handle is for! Water stays hot long enough, if you don't like to re-boil. Boil time is plenty fast. And noise? Not even noticeable. IDK, my cats yowling to be fed are 10X the noise! I like the orange light that indicates it is on, and which turns off when boil completed. Only one quibble: wish the cord was about 3-4 inches longer. Overall, very happy with purchase. Hopefully will last for many months more.

Also the button does not turn off after you lift it so you could empty the kettle but it will keep heating.
