title: Exactly what I wanted
body: When I ruined my last stove kettle, I knew it was time for an electric one that would shut off automatically if I forget about it. But most of those are the same shape, and I really wanted a gooseneck spout for my coffee pour-overs. Which brought me to this guy! And so far it’s perfectly met my expectations. Heats up in a reasonable time, shuts off on its own, looks super cute. My only wish for improvement is that I wish the plastic on top was enamel like the rest of it. When the steam goes through the plastic vent it makes a bit of a heated plastic smell. I’m not really worried health-wise since that part doesn’t touch the inside water. But it’s ever-so-slightly unpleasant if you’re sensitive to scents and chemicals.

title: Terrific tea kettle
body: At a recent stay at Salamander Middleburg, the DmofwHI gooseneck tea kettle was at the coffee / tea bar in our room. Not only is it elegant looking, but it brings water to a high temp in minutes. I loved it and when we got home, I ordered one for our kitchen. I plan to order a couple more for Christmas gifts. LOVE IT!!!

title: A Non Plastic Electric Tea Pot in a Retro Green
body: I drink hot tea everyday so I was searching for a electric tea kettle in some shade of green with the tea spout. This was the perfect color green. It also comes in three other finishes. Copper, Black and White. I don't mind keeping it on my kitchen counter because the cool green and the retro look. In just a quick switch you can have hot water in minutes. You do have to be careful because it's steel so the tea pot does get really hot and do not touch that part. The handle, top of tea pot and base do not get hot and is defined with a brown color. You will also need a three prong outlet. This is great to have when you want to clean out your garbage disposal and need super hot water or you just want that cup of chamomile tea before bed.

title: Heats up fast
body: This pot takes up very little room and heats up fast. It also has an auto shut off once it reaches boiling!

title: Darker green than the photos
body: I've only used it a few times so far, so can't speak to longevity yet. It's nice and small, but large enough to heat water for at least our two bowls of morning oatmeal. I like that the lid comes off, as my previous (Aroma brand) kettle's flip-top stopped locking closed. It came well-packaged, with even a rubber tip on the end of the spout. It seems solid enough to do the job. My only disappointment so far is the color, which still works fine for my kitchen, but potential buyers should be aware that it's not as light as the photos lead you to believe. It's definitely not olive green, but it is a darker version of mint. Even in the sunlight, it's not as bright as the photos.

title: Good quality, love the design but spills when boiling
body: Good quality, love the design but spills when boiling. That is why 4 stars. It spills even when its 3/4th full.

title: So pretty
body: Heats quickly, very nice appearance I thought the price was right

title: Impossible to clean
body: This worked well at first. It’s stylish, looks good on the counter and heats up well. But eventually mold grew in it which doesn’t make sense to me since only water was ever put into it and it’s boiled. The problem is that there is no good way to clean it. There is a heating element inside that you can’t clean behind, and it’s also impossible to thoroughly clean the spout as it’s blocked off from the inside. There are only a bunch of little holes that are too small to push a brush through. I think if this had been an open hole where you could push a cleaning brush all the way down the spout and into the kettle it would have been fine, but the way it’s made I don’t trust that I can ever get the spout truly clean and I can’t even see if mold is growing inside of it. I bought a different one where I can see what’s going on inside and there are no dark areas that I can’t reach with a brush or sponge. It gives me peace of mind that I can get it properly clean. I can’t recommend this kettle, unfortunately.

title: It heats up quickly.
body: And it is aesthetically pleasing on my counter.

title: Nice looking, but can't activate \"500 day Warranty\"
body: Tired of our old kettle that rusted inside after a few years and this is much better looking - matches my copper-accented kitchen. The "500 Day Warranty" activation asks for an "Order ID" - what exactly is that if not the Amazon order number? Their website is not intuitive and full of terms and conditions, but nowhere does it tell you how to submit your warranty info. I dislike when companies waste my time, so I'm not as happy with this purchase as I might have been.

title: Good stuff
body: Just done pour to fast

title: Love this cute tea pot.
body: Just the right size for a couple cups of tea or instant hot chocolate. It heats up super fast. It is pretty enough to stay on my countertop. I love that it automatically turns off when the water is hot. It is light weight and easy to clean

title: Works great - boils water
body: I normally heat up my water in the microwave. Now my water is boiling before I put it in the cup. I would like the option of an earlier shut off, but kettles don’t work that way. This one is just as designed though.

title: Easy to use electric kettle
body: Recieved electric kettle and almost returned it. I thought pic showed more turquoise color, this kettle is definitely light green. All pieces are plastic on outside. Due to those reasons had intended to return it. Started using it and decided to keep it. Wish wasn't so plasticky looking but works well. ONly issue I have is when I add tea bags to it to steep my tea it tends to overflow (doesn't matter how much I fill it). If I don't add teabags it doesn't overflow. Does not whistle when done have to watch for tiny red light to go out.

title: Was Great for a Year, But Is Rusting Now :(
body: This is such a cute kettle. It heats up water quickly and looks great. I was excited about the copper color because it goes with the deocrating scheme in my kitchen. The top knob is plastic, but since the whole lid is metal you had to be very careful or you might burn yourself when taking off the lid to refill after boiling. The kettle would get scale deposits from time to time and i would heat up a full pot with 50% white vinegar to remove it all. Easy peasy. However, after just one year of daily use it is starting to rust at the bottom! There is a little circle of rust that is slowly growing everyday. I thought this pot was made of stainless steel throughout, which shouldn't rust after just one year of use. I have to question the quality of the metal one year is just not that long for this kettle to start to fail. I am disspointed with this kettle. My past kettles have lasted 3-10 years with similar daily use and cleaning habits.

title: Eventually Dies
body: This is my SECOND time purchasing this kettle. The first time it conked out I thought ok, maybe it was faulty, maybe I did something - who knows. But I loved the look so much I ordered again. And Lo and behold: it conked out again. It warns you too - that it’s about to die. It starts “huffing and puffing” steam escaping from the top lid, switch being finicky. I thought I could deal with that if it kept chugging, but it didn’t. For the price of two of these I could have invested in a much better kettle that I would still have around. With better functions. Needless to say I’m disappointed and won’t be ordering this style ever again

title: 2 years on- still fantastic. Gooseneck pours like liquid silk
body: UPDATE: Coming up on 2 years of using this multiple times daily and it's still going strong. Still beautiful. Still pours like silk BUT if you have hard water, you'll definitely want to boil vinegar water in it now and then to get rid of the scaling. ***** Maybe all gooseneck kettles are this amazing but I can't get over the way this pours compared to the other electric kettles I've had with regular short spouts. No splatter whatsoever. Pours silently like I imagine liquid silk would. It's actually difficult to describe but it still makes me smile every time and I've been using it daily for nearly two months. Are they all like this? If so, I'm a convert for life. Otherwise, it heats quickly and quietly.

title: Works great!
body: Update 05-25-24 ... still works great! Update 05-28-23 ... same as last update :) Update 01-13-2022 ... still love it and still use it daily. Looks like new when I clean it out [see previous update]. Update 12-29-2020 ... still love it and use it at least twice a day; I just wanted to share how I keep the inside looking like new. I pour in enough white vinegar to cover the bottom to about 1/2", turn it on and allow to heat until it turns off on its own, and let it sit until I feel like rinsing it out. See the photo ... like new. :) Original review: I dragged my feet about purchasing an electric kettle ... for several years! Now I wish I would have gotten one sooner. I love this kettle - it's just right for me and heats up quickly. For the record, I am a single person who occasionally makes tea or coffee for two. This kettle does not hold a huge amount, but makes plenty for two or three. Also, I used to use a gooseneck kettle on the stove for my pour-over coffee water. It had a thermometer built in that had the perfect temp highlighted. This electric kettle gets the water right in the middle of the perfect temp for pour-over coffee :) :) Bonus! (gooseneck kettles are best for making pour-over coffee ... that's why I purchased this electric kettle)

title: Love it
body: When I first ordered this I received a kettle that appeared to be used because of a rusty water spot inside. I returned and got another one that seems to be new. I love the look of it and it’s so simple to use. The lid does get a little difficult to take off and it feels a bit cheaper then I would have expected. I do wish it was higher quality material. The plastic is very cheap and I don’t think it’s something that would last a long time. Overall though I do like this a lot and would recommended .

title: Saves on gas bill!
body: Gas bill was significantly reduced after a month of switching from my stovetop kettle to this electric kettle (I would say how much but, commodities like this fluctuate so much, I don't want to give anyone a false impression; let's say about 30% reduced). I originally got this kettle because running the gas stove to heat water for hot beverages would make my kitchen hotter than it already was in the summer but, an unexpected and very welcome surprise came when I got my gas bill! That said, the kettle itself is built well, the sides wipe clean strangely easily with no water spots; it boils a full kettle in about 3 - 5 minutes depending on the water temp when it goes in. Yep, I really like it!

title: sleek little kettle
body: I have black fixtures and accents in my kitchen so the matte black looks very on trend for my taste. Its a very nice size- not one of those giant kettles that would have looked bulky on my countertop. The gooseneck is perfect. Most seem a little too small in the spout which makes for much slower pour-overs. This dispenses water at the correct speed IMO. Heats more quickly than my last kettle (which a house guest put on an electric heating element and melted!). I'm actually happy now because this is an upgrade! Only had it a few days so I can't speak to longevity but its working great straight outta the box.

title: Making coffee and Tea like a Barista
body: I love my electric kettle!! I use it multiple times every day to make pour over coffee in the mornings and then we make hot chocolate or tea in the evening to take away the chill. I have had it over 3 months and waited to write this review to see if it was what I wanted and liked and it has met and exceeded expectations on every occasion!! I would highly recommend to anyone interested!! It is fast and efficient and very reliable.

title: unique, distinctive, highly functionable
body: Used it 3 times after it arrived. It heated water very quickly and retained heat longer than I expected. I have other kettles that work as well, but this one has the smaller volume I want, and looks so distinctive that I want it out on my counter.

title: Good First Kettle
body: I’ve never had an electric kettle before and I got this after having a spinal surgery that kept my in a wheelchair and made it difficult to boil water on the stove. It was almost worth having surgery to experience having an electric kettle! It does have a plastic smell/taste when you first get it, so we ran it over and over to break it in. I can’t taste it anymore. Its soooo easy to pour and it’s perfectly light. It matches my kitchen and its so cute! It does leak a little bit of water when it gets down to the last few drops, but it isn’t a big deal for me. I love my little kettle!

title: It works really quickly!!!
body: It works quickly!!! the top gets extremely hot after heating so don’t try to take it off til it cools, even the plastic knob. i’d give it a 4.5 if possible. fill line inside is a little awkward. overall a good purchase!

title: Matched my kitchen beautifully, and works great!
body: We had remodeled our kitchen and chose a granite that had a lovely shade of light sage green in it. So naturally, I chose to decorate in this color palette. I drink hot tea daily and needed an electric water kettle. This one fit the bill entirely. I do love the functionality and design. However just 2 small changes would elevate this to a perfect purchase. First the brown accents, would be better in a stainless/silver finish and also, perhaps, improve longevity. Secondly, is the noise when it’s boiling the water. Mine makes a very loud noise that tends to irritate my husband 😂. However neither of these has limited my love of this tea kettle. I hope to enjoy it for years to come.

title: Auto Shut Off failed
body: Purchased this lovely copper kettle in June 2024. Yesterday the auto shut off failed. Tried to use again today just to be sure and it has absolutely failed. I really liked it when it worked. Sad that it only lasted 5 months.

title: Nice looking and efficient Kettle
body: It was love at the first look. Vintage, very fast and decorative. The only but is the botton shows some crystallization which I am not sure what it is with the time. Need to clean constantly

title: Loved it, only lasted 7 months before dying!
body: This was our household’s introduction to electric kettles, and the hub and I enjoyed its ease a great deal. I noticed a plastic taste some months in, but my taste buds aren’t what they used to be and my man didn’t complain. One big flaw that may have led to its eventual demise is that the kettle can be turned on when there’s no water in it, which shouldn’t be possible. Obviously, turning it on without water in it isn’t smart, but mistakes happen—a safety detector of some sort internally is needed. And then it takes a while to realize what’s happening/overheat itself and click off. Immediately afterward, despite adding water, it would take a while to recover. It eventually got to the point where we would turn it on with water in it, and it would begin to heat up, then sort of fall asleep, then sort of wake up and begin to heat up again, and in the end would produce either warm water or hot water, unpredictably, and with no satisfying clicking off of the lever, indicating it was hot. There’s no reason this kettle should’ve lasted only seven months… More cheap crap from [fill in the blank].

title: Great Buy for the Price
body: I did a lot of searching around for an electric kettle that both looked aesthetically appealing, functioned well, was high quality, and a reasonable price. This kettle is the jackpot! It's very well made, the enamel will not easily chip off and the plastic pieces do not look tacky. The color is very nice overall. As for the function, it works very well and heats water very quickly. The base doesn't have much weight to it but it's not too much of an issue. The gooseneck spout is also perfect for pouring, the water comes out smooth without any sputtering or drops until it gets to the last of the water in the kettle. I've been using it for 2-3 weeks now with no issues at all, so currently my review is 5 stars! Update: 2+ years later and this thing is still kicking. About a year into using it every day, sometimes multiple times a day, the only thing that went wrong was the auto off function stopped working when the water comes to a boil, but otherwise it is wonderful and I highly recommend it.

title: Does the trick but don't expect premium quality
body: This kettle does it's job and looks fashionable while doing it. It doesn't feel particularly great quality though. The metal is thin and the plastic base is cheap. The worst part about it is the plastic smell. I cleaned it before first use, but it still took several weeks of infrequent use for the plastic smell to fade when boiling water. I almost didn't want to drink the water because of the smell, but after a few weeks it's finally calmed down. If you want a less stinky kettle there are plenty more out there, but I don't think you can beat the look of this one for the price.

title: cheap plastic crap and unresponsive seller
body: This kettle has broken twice. The first time I was sent a new one, only to have it stop working again a few months later. The first time, it just completely died. The base that it sits on and gets its power from stopped working. The second time, the base also stopped working but not completely. It heats but it no longer shuts off automatically - resulting in a burning plastic smell that I luckily caught wind of from the other room. This thing is a major fire hazard. It looks cute but it’s not worth your house burning down. Also, seller did not respond to the message I sent ocean a week ago.

title: Perfect!
body: This is a great kettle that heats water pretty fast. I like the automatic shut off mechanism. Perfect size for multiple cups. Does not keep the liquid hot. But that is ok, because it heats the water quickly

title: Beautiful does what it’s supposed to
body: Pretty and functional

title: Works great so far but color is ugly
body: The photos must be enhanced because the “copper” is not copper colored at all, it’s dull, brown plastic. I understand that certain parts have to be plastic and not metal for a reason but the photos were very misleading. I would suggest getting a different color like black or white because the copper is UGLY. But it works just like any other electric kettle.

title: Heats Quickley
body: Avid tea drinks here and this is a great addition to our kitchen counter. Provides hot water quickly. Only downside is next time I will purchase a kettle that is insulated so the water stays hot in the kettle longer.

title: Exactly what I needed!
body: I use this electric kettle at least once a day, every day. It's become the centerpiece of a lovely little coffee and tea station in my kitchen. Heats quickly, retains the heat well and is incredibly simple to operate.

title: Heats Super Fast
body: I purchased this teapot a year and a half ago and use it every single day and it STILL heats the water for my tea in about one minute. I LOVE this and would purchase this again and again and again. It’s SO easy to use and really nice as well. I get many compliments on it and have to demonstrate it’s magic to anyone who will let me make them tea. Lol! I promise you if you’re looking for hot water quick this is the kettle you’ll want. Did I mention how nice it is? Well it’s worth a second mention :)~

title: Quiet and Simple
body: I haven't used this for long but I tested it when I got it. It's beautiful, simple to use, boiled water quickly and quietly (only sound was boiling water, very very slight whistle/hiss from the vent holes in the lid), and NO BEEPING. I chose this model because I didn't want any beeping buttons or alarm when kettle is done. I think it will be perfect in my sound healing studio.

title: Not Happy
body: Not Happy with it It leaks as you pour it

title: Pretty and practical
body: Packaged well so no issues. I can't speak to it's longevity but it DOES work well right out of the box. I have a small space, and this fits great. It's compact, and looks lovely next to my plants. The cord is relatively short, and thick but sturdywith a 3 prong plug in. I wanted an electric kettle because I'd forgotten about the last stove top kettle and left it on the stove too long. It's lid had broken (4 years old and used daily) so it no longer screamed when the water was boiling. The electric kettle with it's automatic shutoff eliminates that issue. I also make pour over coffee sometimes and know the gooseneck spout is supposedly helpful with bringing out the full flavor of coffee, eith the correct pour over. It could be bs, but I'm looking forward to trying it. Either way, the gooseneck thus far is less messy with less splatter and it's actually beautiful to watch. What can I say, the little things can make such a difference even in the use of an every day kettle. Overall as a new purchase I'm very happy with it.

title: Love the color!
body: I have a coffee bar and this copper kettle looks great with my other equipment. But looks wouldn’t matter if it didn’t work well. This kettle is great!

title: Warranty?
body: It seems my order # is not accepted by the website when trying to activate the warranty. The kettle works well and heats water quickly, though it feels less sturdy than my previous kettle. I'd really like to activate the warranty...

title: Early review of this electric kettle
body: I've only been using the piece for about 2 months now but my family and I are regular tea drinkers. The device probably cycles through 5-10 boilings per day. So far so good. The thing is a work horse and boils a full kettle in about 6 mins. I'm pleased with its performance - but again, it's only 2 months old. I'll write another review at the one year mark.

title: This is a great electric kettle overall.
body: It is exactly as expected and works great! Pros: It looks pretty and functions very well. Water heats up quickly and is very hot. It shuts itself off when water is to temperature. Cons: My husband considers it too loud to heat up while watching TV in the sane room 🙄🤣. If you don’t want plastic parts this isn’t the kettle for you as it has a plastic top and base.

title: Cool Color
body: I hesitated to get this copper color out of fear it would be too bright. I love the color! Have yet to use the kettle. Will update on functionality.

title: Perfect size!
body: I love this kettle for several reasons. It fits inside my cabinet when I’m done with it. It heats really quickly, absolutely no aftertaste like plastic leaves behind, and it’s very pretty!

title: Likes the kettle
body: Very pretty color and design, well matches my kitchen. Perfect size for serving tea or coffee one or two people. Precise water pouring.

title: Heats up fast, great pot!
body: I do not normally write reviews. I wanted to give some time before writing a review since I received this in October 2022. I work at home and wanted to have a tea pot in my office since I love tea throughout the day. This pot is amazing. It heats up so quickly! I use it a lot and I have had no issues. The only thing I would change is to make the cord a bit longer. I have it sitting on top of a min fridge and I barley reaches the plug right beside the fridge. The price is great and I am very pleased with my purchase.

title: Retro Find
body: Love this, well made and works FAST, great for tea, drip coffee or just when you need hot water FAST. Love this design as it's mid-century modern with modern technology. Great purchase.

title: Perfect
body: I picked this up for my parent who was forgetting to check on boiling kettles on the stove (safety issue!) … he can’t hear them plus the water takes a long time to boil - he uses this multiple times daily and loves it - tells me every time I call now.

title: Pretty Color
body: The color is fantastic on this water heater. Unfortunately, the logo is big on the front and I found myself always looking at before I even used it. Because of this, I returned it. It does have a beautiful color combination to be displayed if the logo doesn't bother you.

title: Beautiful!
body: The copper color is bright and beautiful. Works really fast. I’m very pleased with this purchase!

title: Great product
body: The copper colored kettle matches my kitchen perfectly. It is a good size and boils water very quickly. It is also easy to clean any water spots with just vinegar. Very happy with my purchase!

title: Very nice!
body: I love the look of this kettle and have used it every day for the past couple of months. There are other models with more elaborate features but this one works just fine for me.

title: Love the Design and Color and Heats Fast
body: We love the classic design for this kettle. It holds a good amount of water and heats it up relatively quickly. Not many options with this one. Just on or off. Can't set to specific temps. But for what it does, it does a really good job. Good quality. Use it every day for my tea.

title: Wish it lasted longer
body: The on/off switch stopped working after just 2 years. Design is good, fast boiling time, nice pour flow.

title: No plastic parts, but tiny bit of rust.
body: I was thrilled to FINALLY find a stainless steel kettle with no interior plastic parts. The copper color also looks great on my countertop. This kettle is the perfect size for 2 cups of tea. However, within a week of purchase I noticed a small rust spot (1mmx3mm) where the stainless steel meets the silicone seal. I decided to give it a few weeks to see if the rust spot expands. After 2 weeks the size of the rust has not increased. A tiny bit of rust outweighs plastic. I will probably keep it!

title: Great space saver and organizer
body: Super easy set up & great space saver! I didn’t even realize how much more I can fit after setting them up and reorganizing. Very lightweight & easily slides in and out for easier reach. I love that it’s a clear bin, so you can see what’s in each slot. *note: if you have deeper cabinets, you may want to consider getting ones with longer bins, I do have null space. That’s not a product flaw, just a tip.

title: Useful!
body: I bought this when it went on sale and I wish I had bought a few more! It fits perfectly under our sink and keeps ALL of my items organized. I love that the bins are clear so I can see every item that I need quickly. Now all I need is a label maker!

title: Sturdy and spacious organizer
body: My favorite organizer that easily fits under the bathroom sink or kitchen . Sturdy enough to fit big heavy items but structured to organize smaller items . This helps increase the space and organization in my home

title: Good for price
body: It was how I expected it, not super sturdy but for that price it is to be expected. I have it for 4 months now and it is still going strong, and keeps my Bathroom tidy! I bought 4 of those!

title: Buy it NOW!
body: I needed to get more space under our restroom sink & these were perfect. They are super sturdy and I love the tray can be removed easily making it convenient to restock.

title: Amazing Organizers – Functional and Sleek!
body: These clear cabinet organizers are great! They’ve totally transformed the way I store things, everything looks neat, and I can actually see what I have. They slide in and out really easily, which makes grabbing things quick and hassle-free. Super sturdy and sleek-looking too. Absolutely love them!

title: Perfect Bathroom Storage Solution
body: Why did you pick this product vs others?: These Vtopmart 4 Pack Bathroom Organizers have been perfect for under my sink. The two-tier design maximizes space and keeps everything neatly organized. They've definitely served their purpose, and I highly recommend them!

title: Smaller than appears, easy to assemble
body: Definitely smaller than I thought it would be. It barely fills up the space under my sink. I ended up going up three levels to take advantage of the space however, that means I have two pairs of leftover trays that can’t really be stacked without the poles. The plastic is decent quality, but the poles are thin metal so probably can’t hold a lot of weight.

title: Cute, Compact, and Functional!
body: This bathroom organizer is just the right size for small spaces—cute and practical! It fits perfectly without taking up too much room and helps keep everything neat and accessible. A great addition to any compact bathroom setup.

title: Easy Under Sink Storage
body: Easy to assemble. Great under sink size. Great to have drawers that slide. Not super sturdy but gets the job done. The walls aren’t very high so bigger bottles can tip when sliding out.

title: Useful
body: These are great and worked perfectly to organize my products. I wish the sliding function was a bit less sticky but it works.

title: Great Organizers

title: Great storage

title: That everything is organized
body: Just got them set up under my vanity. So far they are working fine. Keep my makeup and beauty aids together neatly.

title: Fits well
body: I recently renovated my bathroom and needed to organize my clutter. Works well, plastic scratches easily but no one will look underneath the sink.

title: THE VERY BEST!
body: These shelves are exceptional! Get 'em. I started out with ordering (2). After I got them I ordered (4) more. They are absolutely the best for straightening out the mess under your sinks, weather in the bathroom or kitchen. I didn't care for them on the top of my bathroom vanity, but they worked underneath. Easy to put together too. I love 'em!

title: Eliminate bath counter clutter.
body: Why did you pick this product vs others?: New home, no in wall medicine cabinets. Purchased two of these for under sink. Problem solved. Works well. Holds a lot , even taller things. Eliminating bath counter clutter.

title: Recommended!
body: These keep the under sink area organized and they let me see clearly what is there. The drawers slide easy on their tracks. They were easy to put together. I've had them now for two years and they are holding up quite well. I just wish they came in different sizes, cause my cabinet's space could accept bigger ones.

title: Easy to Install
body: The organizers are super easy to install and great for under the sink storage!

title: Versatile and effective
body: Easy to put together and helps with organization under my sink. Worth buying!

Flat irons and curling irons seems to fit, but a good blow dryer is too big. The drawers don't slide as easy as I would like. On the one hand, it's nice there is a little grip so things don't fall apart, but if you have things kind of stacked they're likely to fall over when you try to use the drawer to slide in and out. That said, they do fit well under the pipes, and are narrow enough to go on either side of the pipes. It wouldn't be hard to reconfigure them into a taller tower, either. You could stack sets up as high as you wanted, or just use a single drawer. The versatility is nice, because the current setup in my kids' bathroom seems functional, but who knows once they actually start using the new organized setup? title: Best when used as intended
body: I'm not sure what aspect of my being this comes from, but I was finding myself constantly grabbing a cold mug when I finally remembered it was there. I'd make a pot of tea, make my cup, intentionally let it cool, and one way or another it was too cool / cold by the time I got to it. I can't say that I've been monitoring how long it took for the mug to cool down, but it always seemed too quick. I was already looking for a reason to get a new mug as the rounder handle resulted in holding it in a painful way and it was frankly getting heavier to my hands as well (being ceramic). So I had a few reasons to look anyway. And with that in mind, I decided to look for something that might help with those issues or at the least, not let the cup's contents drop below a certain temperature Long enough for me to get around to drinking it, while also having a more comfortable weight and handle. Initially, I thought about those coasters that heat up, but felt that that'd be too much of a burn / fire hazard and likely not able to control the temperature as well. Seeing as how I didn't know what temperature I was waiting for it to cool down too, I knew that I'd want something with a measured setting. I was also looking for something that could heat up a cold cup to the desired temperature. When I first saw this listing, I was taken back by the price, but not so much that it kept me from looking into it. Especially since I have a habit of deciding on things that one way or another tend to push the budget. I looked at the various aspects of the design and saw that it was basically self-contained, so there was a little to no chance of being hurt by the mug (unless I spilled the contents on the upper two settings). Being able to choose from a known selection of temperatures was a must on this purchase. I also liked that the handle appeared (correctly) to be large enough to fit my average sized, closed grip. While I've not weighed it, it definitely feels lighter than a comparably sized ceramic. Most of its weight is, of course, the battery at the bottom. I was a bit bummed that the charger was a barrel plug as that doesn't allow me to just grab the nearest USB-C cord from my station (where I sit). That said, if it Did have USB charging, then it would have only been to the base anyway, so that would be a moot point since it would likely never get unplugged unless moved. While I don't know how much my old mug held, it's quite apparent that this is likely a few ounces less, but it's also exactly 1/3rd of the 1L pot when brewed vs ~2.5 fills with my old mug. I'm sure I'll get used to the difference eventually. Now, when evaluating the performance of this, it became apparent that I was running into my desired functionality vs its design. It has become obvious that this is designed to start with a hot liquid and keep it at the chosen temperature until empty or the battery runs out. It does that quite well, but I can't say how long the battery actually lasts for sure because I lose track of time too easy. So when I say that it 'feels' like it's losing power (not temperature) quicker than advertised, I can't quantify that statement, but it 'feels' closer to 2-2.5 hrs vs 4 hrs (lid on). I can say that I figured out that my comfortable temperature is the lowest setting and that the middle temperature more closely resembles my freshly brewed pot. The charging time feels like forever, but definitely a couple hours from depleted. Now when trying to see how it does with 'heating from cold', that definitely seemed to drain the battery much faster while also taking a long time. I even tried setting it to that middle choice and then turning it back down, but that still drained the battery rather quickly. So if That is how you want to use it, then leave it on the charger until it's hot again (and expect to wait a bit). I did have to stop myself from walking it over to the microwave the first few times until I got myself better trained with how it's designed. Because of this, as much as I hate adding to an already pretty penny, I chose to purchase a 2nd base to sit where I eat / drink. I thought about moving the original base, but then I realized that it was better to leave that there for when I've cleaned the mug (default storage location and all that). What improvements would I like to see? 1) Make a slightly larger (16oz?) mug, but have it be taller so that the base and lids don't change. 2) Source a higher density battery if possible. 3) Increase the speed at which it warms up (if feasible). 4) Add a little more texture to the handle / housing as it is metal smooth and slides a bit easy in the hands. 5) Offer a closeable lid as that should prevent spills and likely assist in keeping it warmer longer.

title: This cup is DIVINE!!!
body: Wow this cup is AMAZING? I have been looking for a cup that can self heat for a long time. Sadly, I am in the hospital frequently because I have lupus. Last year I was in the hospital 95 days. 😭 I really enjoy having a cup of hot tea but when I am in the hospital, I can’t leave my room because I’m usually REALLY sick. After the cafeteria closes, I can’t get a cup of hot tea in the evening (when I want it the most). My only option has been for a nurse to microwave a styrofoam cup in a microwave which automatically makes me not even want the cup of hot water. I have been looking for a long time to find a travel mug that could be my “hospital mug”. I’ve tried several options all of which failed. I came across this cup and thought it looked interesting and the reviews were really good. My first thought was “a $100 coffe cup ??? What has this first world self indulgent country come to??? Holy fart blossom that’s alot of money!!” However, 95 days of my life in a hospital SUCKS! And during that time there is very little joy or peace. So I thought to myself “why are you spending all this time lonely and miserable and for $100 you could enjoy a cup of tea and it would bring you so much joy and comfort”. My favorite color is pink and I was so pleased that the cup came in a rose color, which is a lovely shade of rose/pink. The cup is amazing. It has a good grip. The round shape is comfortable to hold in your hands. The handle is the right grip and is comfortable to wrap your fingers around. The weight of the mug feels solid but not heavy. It has the right weight to feel like you are holding a comfort mug. It’s compact enough with the charging base to easily stick in a small hospital travel bag. The texture of the cup is calming and the cup is easy to wash well in a hotel or hospital sink. If I could change anything about the mug it would be that it was just a smidge talker so that the charging cord could travel inside the mug with the lid on it. It just almost will close but not completely. That’s the only rhino I wish was different just because when I travel around I don’t want to lose one of the parts and it would maximum travel efficiency. That’s a small thing in comparison to the quality of this mug. Also, I was curious if I started with cold water (like I will have to do in a hospital), could the cup do more than just keep tea warm but rather could I start with a cup of cold water and get the water hot enough to steep the tea. The answer is YES indeed you can. I did an experiment at home with a cup of refrigerated water and turned the mug setting onto “piping”. I put a kitchen thermometer in the water to measure the temperature of the water when it started and then to see how long it took and how warm the water would get without the help of starting with hot water. It worked! It was a little bit slow (maybe 30 mins or so). But it did the job which is really amazing for such a small “device” of this sort. The water started at 43 degrees and it heated up to 140 degrees in around 35ish minutes. It did steep the tea perfectly! Wahoo. I loved my cup so much that I gave my first mug to a very special friend who works outdoors a lot farming in the north east where it is often very cold. She enjoys a cup of hot coffee to warm her frozen body while she is working. She is young and would have never bought herself an expensive coffee cup. However, she absolute loves the cup. Which means this is a very nice special gift to give someone who really loves warm drinks. Today I am ordering my replacement mug for my hospital bag. This is a very cool cup that works and I think it is absolutely worth spending $100 for the comfort and luxury this mug brings to life enjoyment. My story of my struggle with lupus is on YouTube if you search “Ballerina With Lupus”. It can give you some idea of what my hospital life is like and also my determination to fight to stay alive. God bless you if you have read to the end of this crazy long review. Lol Melly

title: Be prepared to spend another $20
body: I really love the mug — especially the app-free approach. But there’s one issue that feels oddly dismissive of the user experience. The mug is designed to keep your coffee piping hot for extended periods. Great in theory. But here’s the problem: when coffee stays hot too long, it starts to taste awful — mostly due to evaporation. So, what’s the obvious fix? Just put the lid on. Right? Well… not quite. The included lid has a permanently open drinking hole — meaning heat and vapor constantly escape. So if you use the mug and lid as designed, your coffee turns bitter in 10–15 minutes. Want to fix that? You’ll need to go online, hunt down a compatible closeable lid, spend another $20, and generate more packaging waste — all to make the mug function as it should have from the start. Bottom line: The included lid needs to be closeable. Without that, it actively undermines the mug’s main feature. I wanted to bump the review down to 4 stars over this, but that just felt petty. Anyone want a non-closeable plastic lid with no practical use? Didn’t think so. And so it now lives in my junk drawer….

title: Complete turnaround! Customer service saves the day.
body: This mug was a 2023 Christmas present to my wife as she loves her coffee to be hot and stay hot. At first this product was perfect. We even bought a second base so she could have hot coffee no matter where in the house she was. For the first year, all was good. Then, just after Christmas 2024, the mug failed, out of warranty by days. It would keep the coffee warm if on the base, but the moment it was removed, it would start cooling, as if the battery was kaput. Reading the reviews, it seems that this was not unusual-- the mug would fail in about a year. Similar problems are reported elsewhere as well. It seems pretty clear that there was some kind of defect in the 2023 version of the product. I contacted the company through their online form in early January 2025, but given that this product is made in China and that the company, Nextboom, is clearly a small outfit, I was not optimistic. And, I never received any response. But then, towards the end of January, we realized that the credit card with which we paid may have actually doubled the warranty. So we decided to pursue that. To submit the claim, we needed to document what a repair or replacement would cost so, I once again contacted the company. But this time, the response was totally different! Although the mug was slightly out of warranty, the representative, Kaitlyn, immediately responded and after clarifying the mode of failure, initiated a warranty replacement, which arrived within a few days. (It may have helped that we live less than 50 miles from where the company is located in Boulder, CO) The new mug works well and seems to have an even better battery life than the first one did. It's also a slightly different size and shape than the first one was. So, although I have no way to be sure, I suspect there was a product defect that has now been corrected. As a result, and because of the perfect response of Nextboom's customer service, I can offer a recommendation for this product without reservation. I guess time will tell if I'm correct, but for now, we could not be more satisfied.

title: Awesome purchase, I will buy more for friends and family.

I am going to look for some kind of handle cover... maybe just do a French knot over it with yarn or paracord... I didn't see a way to lower the temperature. If there is a way, it isnt intuitive. title: Fantastic, better than an Ember cup!
body: I have an Ember and Nextmug. I’ve had the Ember over two years and the base broke. One of the tiny little spring-loaded nibs lost its springiness. A weakness in design if you ask me. But, the Nextmug uses the same little nibs. Their design is a little stronger in that one nib is right in the center of the cup-base. But still, a weakness in design that you cannot (and I stress CANNOT) get the baseplate wet. I’m not sure what happened to my ember, but I ended up making a solid nib out of solder for the one that lost its spring. It’s holding, but I’m not confident in it. I’m guessing at some point, the Nextmug base will do the same thing. That aside, the Nextmug is superior for a few reasons. One, it has a definitive on and off option. Where the Ember has a sensor to know when you’ve added liquid, it’s hit or miss. The Ember on/off switch is also inconveniently located underneath the cup. And it also is hit or miss. Where it gives you a tactile response that you’ve clicked it, it’s unclear most of the time what you’ve actually done. Sometimes a light comes on, sometimes not. Sometimes it’s blinking red, sometimes it’s solid red, green, white, blinking… The Nextmug on/off is located on the side (superior) and it’s easy to know when the cup is off (no lights) and which option you are picking. The Ember app? Garbage. It is unreliable. If it works, it’s fantastic. The trouble is that it rarely connects no matter what you do. When I went shopping for a replacement, I specifically looked for cups that did not have an app. “App” means IT developers, means more cost, and generally for a product like this, average developers (I mean, it’s a cup not an air-traffic control system). Plus, the Bluetooth chips they must use have to be the bottom of the barrel (aka, unreliable). Therefore, all the features that the app provided (heating options most notably), were useless to me. The Ember cup size (10 oz) was a little small. There’s now a 14 oz option, but the train had left the station! The Ember on/off button on the bottom of the cup, again, is a nuisance. And here’s something I didn’t think I would care for… the Nextmug lid! I have to say, it’s great! It helps keep the coffee warmer without using as much energy (longer charge when it’s away from the base). Also, it nearly erases evaporation. And, I’m not 100% sure, but the coffee seems to be much less bitter because of it. Maybe my imagination, but the coffee taste better from the Nextmug cup. Plus, no spills (or at least, less chance of splashing). The Nextmug light indicators where intuitive and having a button for “warm, hot, and piping” versus an app… Way to go Nextmug! Between the Nextmug and Ember, it was an easy decision for me. I’m still concerned about the little nibs losing their springiness… But, there you have it.

title: So nice to have warm coffee
body: This mug is so easy to use. The simple button press is great, no app to hassle with, no bluetooth connection to worry about, it just works. I wouldn't mind if they had a lower temp setting but 130/140/150 seems like an optimal set of temps for most people. It does a really great job keeping my coffee warm for the entire time I'm drinking it. I'm one of those people that takes a few sips, gets caught up in something, then forgets their coffee for an hour or so. It's so nice not needing to worry about cold coffee any more. The mug doesn't get warm at all on the outside which is really, really nice. In fact the mug is fairly good at retaining heat by itself, even when it's off. I've made tea in it before and the tea in my mug was 10 degrees hotter than the tea in one of our standard mugs. The mug will keep the coffee the right temp w/o the lid but you do get a fair amount of boil off and I think the heater has to run hotter/longer to keep things warm. The heat seems to come from the bottom only and you do get a bit of a cooked coffee flavor without the lid. Well, with my 1-2 hour drinking time I do at least. Faster drinkers may not have much problem. The lid is really well designed though. The opening is about perfect for sipping, it's easy to get on and positioned and it's easy to clean. I didn't think I'd use it but I really don't mind it. The mug itself is slightly small. I think I'm used to 14oz coffee mugs that comfortably hold 12oz of coffee, a bit of milk and still have room left so it doesn't spill. This mug is literally 14oz though. Using the lid I get about 10oz of coffee w/ a splash of milk and have to take a sip before putting the lid on. The inside of the mug seems really easy to clean at first but, after a few weeks use, I started to notice an off flavor. Rewashing it didn't seem to help. I ended up using the trick I use on travel bottles--pouring in hot water, a bit of dishwasher machine powder and using an electric whisk to stir (not touching the bottom) at high speed for a while. That did get rid of the off flavor but it needs that kind of washing every few uses. I really wish somebody would make one of these that disassembled so you could put the inner mug into the dishwasher.

title: Great mug - poor battery
body: Edit #2: Reached out to Customer Service. They were excellent. After a few back-n-forths via email they sent me a new mug. So far this one is behaving. The battery still isn’t great but it’s better than my first mug. Bumped to 4 stars. Cant give it any higher because it needs more juice. Edited: I initially gave the mug 3-stars because of the mediocre to poor battery life. I've dropped it down to 2-stars. The battery life on this mug is completely unacceptable. As I edit this review I'm drinking cold coffee because my battery lasted no more than 15-minutes. It was charging all night. I've owned the mug for less than 6-months. Overall this is a decent mug. I like it better than my Ember mug even though it doesn’t have the technology of the Ember. It has a better charging base and overall better ergonomics. I don’t mind the manual temperature setting I have to do every time I fill it - I’ve gotten used to it. The Con - the battery is terrible - thus the 3-Stars. Keeping coffee hot-warm off the base for a reasonable time should be the core function of this product. It doesn’t do that for very long before having to charge it. This mug would easily be 5-stars if they could solve the battery longevity issue.

body: This is a nice looking good quality cup. It is larger than most which is why I bought it. It keeps drinks super hot for a long time. I use if for coffee in the office so if I take an hour to drink it - no problem. It heats the drink from the bottom of the cup (as I assume they all do) and so when you get down to the last half an inch or so it over-heats the drink so you can't enjoy the whole drink unless you turn the heat off, and then it cools very quickly. So given the extraordinary price I am only reasonably pleased with it. I usually just use my double walled Bodum mugs, but if you want something that keeps a drink hot for longer, then this is good.

title: Better than expected!
body: UPDATE: It is now May 2025. About a month ago, I noticed that the mug no longer held a charge after about 5 min. I sit near my coaster all day anyway (desk job) so I just kept it on the coaster and it was fine. Unlike the Ember mug I had, this still kept things hot while on the charger. But now I'm also noticing it seems to auto shut-off after about an hour or two, so I have to keep an eye on it to make sure it doesn't turn off. I'm a sipper so, yes, I do take hours to drink a mug of whatever! *************** I purchased this mug in Nov of 2023 and wanted to give it a good, long use before reviewing. I had previously gotten and used another, more expensive electric mug which is sold in all the stores at Christmas time. With THAT mug, you could set the temp of your mug via their app to a specific number and that was nice so I didn't expect to like this mug as much. But with the other mug, the coating inside the bottom wore off in about 6 months from stirring and after about a year, it really didn't keep my drinks piping hot anymore. With THIS mug, I use the middle (of the 3) setting, "hot" and it is piping hot for me. The hottest, "piping" is too hot (I used the max number on the previous mug to get it to the heat level I wanted). I have also not had a circular path appear on the inside bottom of this mug. And, a year later, it is still going strong. CAVEAT: I do keep it on its coaster the whole time and sip as I work (it takes me hours to drink a mug of something)... when I happen to be up and take my mug, without the lid, the charge lasts on HOT for about an hour. Maybe 90 min with the lid on. I am still quite satisfied! The previous mug's charger was concave and this one is convex, so I just had to get the hang of placing it on the charger correctly without it toppling over, but that was an easy adjustment. Both mugs are heavier than a standard mug (obviously - there is a battery in the bottom!) but I got used to their weight. I am very happy with my Nextmug and would buy it again!!

title: First impressions... great so far!
body: I've only had it for a day, and this is my first experience with the mug. Will update as I go further with it. So far, it may be just what I was looking for as I prefer coffee in a cup without a lid, and it's constantly getting cold if I don't drink it in like 15 minutes. Positives: I was skeptical that this mug could keep my coffee warm enough, but the "piping" setting works very well for me, though apparently impacts battery life when away from the coaster. Some like it hot. I like it very hot. The color I picked is just right. I got the burgundy color, and it's dark enough but still gives a nice morning color. I considered "spice" but glad I got the darker one. It makes the black at the bottom blend in better. Battery life is good enough for me to get through my coffee at my preferred heat when sitting outside on my back porch. Good enough for even a second cup, which I loved. The coaster is on my WFH desk, and the adapter has a nice long cord. Might have been better to be a USB-C connector, but that is a minor criticism. Something I didn't see in the other reviews is that when you put in your hot coffee, it shows you on the LEDs where the temp is so you can pick the corresponding temp setting to keep it there. Nice! I considered the Ember for years, but the long-term reviews kept me away. Didn't want to use an app. Is that the dumbest thing ever or what? The LEDs are not overly bright. That's a great thing. I did get the 3-year warranty for this for only $13, so there's piece of mind with it. Comes with a lid, which will be nice for traveling. This fits into my cup-holder, which was a concern. Really love how the last few sips in the cup are still hot. So used to contorting my face to drink that last lukewarm sip. May get an extra coaster for when I go into the office. We'll see. Negatives (short list): I guess battery life could be better. I'm sure it will go downhill, especially if I leave it on the charging base. My wife saying "You paid WHAT for a coffee cup?" :) It advertises being 14 oz, but the 12 oz setting on my Kuerig fills it almost to the top... too high to even put the lid on. I'll have to drink a few sips before putting on the lid and heading to my car. Would have been more portable if a USB connector could have powered the base, which I already have in my laptop bag. It is a bit expensive, but worth it as the black coffee lover I am, and I'll use it every day!

body: I find the Nextmug to be an acceptable addition to my lifestyle. My house is quite cold, and it was difficult to keep my coffee warm. Prior to this, I had just a heated base that I would keep a variety of mugs on. It was okay, but I wanted to be able to move around with my coffee and not be relient upon being an arm's length from the base. One thing I've noticed is that choosing the "hot" temperature as the level of coffee goes down is it not the best idea if you add milk like I do. At a certain point an unwelcome film begins to form on the surface. I counter this by switching to the "warm" setting halfway through. Used this way, uncovered, the mug stays warm for a little over an hour, which is fine for me. The only thing I miss from a standard mug is the comfort of holding a warm mug in my hands on a cold morning--this mug is safe to place directly on furniture, so the exterior does not get warm. The line of battery lights along the bottom will go down to just one quite quickly, which sometimes makes me a bit anxious and compels me to keep checking but, like I said, it doesn't take me over an hour to drink from a mug this size (14 oz.) anyway. I also like that this mug will turn off when empty, whereas with my old warmer I was always wondering when I left the house if I remembered to turn it off.

title: I LOVE this mug!
body: I have been considering purchasing this mug for over a year, and I always hesitated because of the price. I finally gave in because I got tired of drinking cold coffee, and I'm so glad that I did! I looked at some of the other similar, cheaper mugs, but decided that if I was going to spend the money, I would buy the one I really wanted. I have tried other options like travel mugs, stainless steel mugs, etc. But I don't like drinking my coffee through a lid and stainless steel mugs seemed to give my coffee a different taste. This mug keeps my coffee hot for as long as I need it to. I like that it has 3 temperature settings, but I have mainly been using the medium setting. The Piping almost seems a bit too hot for me. From a full charge without a lid, it keeps it at the medium setting (and here you can still see the steam rising from it) for just over an hour. This is a little less than the directions list, but that hasn't been a problem for me. I usually drink my first cup in the morning in less time than that. For the rest of the day, my coffee is next to me while I'm working, so I keep it on the charge pad. I have not tested the battery life with the lid because I don't like drinking my coffee with it on. All in all, I love this mug and will recommend it to my friends. This will be used daily so I hope the mug works well for years.

title: OK but not the answer to piping hot coffee
body: After using the Ember for over a year, it started to lose its ability to keep my coffee warm. Because when the Ember mug is off the base, forget it. It goes cold fast. So I thought I would give Nextmug a try in hopes that it would be the answer to keeping my coffee HOT, not just kind of warm. That’s what we all want, right? But after several weeks of use, I'm sorry to report it's not great. Here’s why: 1. Unlike the Ember (would not recommend), you have to press a power button each time you use Nextmug to start heating the coffee. This is separate from the actual mug being charged. Those are two different things for some reason. So there’s a power light which needs to be glowing (red or green depending) before the temperature lights (which are white) can be activated. Ember is easier in that regard. When you see the light on on an Ember mug, you know it’s doing the job of heating your coffee. Not sure why Nextmug complicates this for users. 2. The mug loses its charge fairly quickly so you have to keep it on the base overnight. Otherwise, once you fill it, you will need to immediately place it on its base to start working. If you have the base positioned right next to where you will be (for example, next to your computer while working), then you’re set. If not, you will have to let it charge first on the base before using it, which can take a while. 3. There are three temp settings but 2 are useless because, even at the hottest setting, it doesn’t get that hot. It’s passably warm. Which will probably fine for most people. It helps that they provide a lid to hold in the heat but I don’t really use it unless I’m on the go. 4. Also unexpectedly turns off. When using it off the base, I've noticed that the temp will stop working for some unknown reason. I will put the coffee down, go do a couple of things, go back and pick up the coffee and it's off because the coffee is barely warm. On the plus side, it seems to keep coffee warm when the mug is off the base (again, as long as the mug is charged) longer than Ember. I also like that the base has its heating contacts on a round raised “platform,” unlike the Ember which has a round recessed heating section (think “male” vs. “female” fitting). This matters because if you ever spill or drip your coffee, you don’t have to worry as much about the liquid pooling on the heating coils on the base like you do with the Ember mug. The mug is also fatter than the Ember mug, which I like. Personal preference of course but it feels a little more stable. Bottom line, it’s OK. Not saying don't buy it but if you're searching for a mug that keeps your coffee satisfyingly hot, this isn't it.

title: Updated Review - Again ...
body: I leave all reviews from the past at the bottom... Of the 4 remaining mugs that were working perfectly we have now had 2 where the battery will not hold a charge at all somewhere between the 14-18 month timeline... That being said I still love these mugs just plan the valuation of your purchases with the lifetime of the product. I will be watching sales closely and purchasing at those times... I will leave my original review at the bottom but need to update. Since my Amazon review Kaitlyn had reached out and after following their instructions it appears as though there is a confirmed defect with the mug itself and they are sending out a replacement and return label. Apparently the return/exchange window ends in 1 month. Mug died after 2.5 months and I have gone through NextMug customer support a few times and have YET to hear ANYTHING back from them. title: Keeps liquids hot
body: It's build well and keeps liquids hot as advertised. Comes with a charger so it's always ready for use. Great item.

title: Great customer service
body: This is the third Nextmug that I have purchased. It is also the third brand that I have used. The first was a name brand that lasted six months or so before the base failed. The second brand was from Amazon and was a good product. I have a strong preference for the way the Nextmug feels. The handle is comfortable. The first one I purchased was a little over a year ago and I noticed that the battery didn’t seem to be lasting as long as it initially did. Having one near the coffee machine to charge overnight and one near where I drink coffee has been a game changer. I can now use the mug indefinitely during the day. This model does not have the Bluetooth connectivity which I frankly consider more of a gimmick than a functional feature. I use the mug with the same settings and find it more convenient to use the button on the mug than to open an app and change settings. I highly recommend this brand!

title: Don't Stray Too Far From The Charger
body: I'll give it a "pretty good". Make sure your mug is fully charged and unless you're a coffee gulper, keep close to the charger plate. This is not the mug you're gonna load up and take in the car to sip during an hour commute. Firstly, because the rounded bottom doesn't fit properly in any cup holder and second, most important, the charge runs out pretty quick. There are three heat settings and I go for the middle one. If you go for high heat then keeping the charger in close proximity is absolute must. When I'm just lounging and I can set the mug on the charger between sips ... delightful.

title: Almost perfect
body: Long time user of the similar product from Ember. Chose this when my Ember died (more on that later). It does the heating as designed. No complaints on that. The size, the weight and the grip are convenient too. A HUGE win over the Ember is the design of the charging contacts. The contact on the bottom of the mug is recessed. This protects it from accidentally getting wet while washing. This is VERY important. I believe it was the undoing of my Ember. The one design flaw in my opinion is that the mug curves in at the top. It is an odd feel for the first few times you use it. But your lips adjust and you get used to it. I would have preferred the side of the mug to be straight. An Ember-feature that I wish this mug had is auto-sensing start when hot liquid is poured into the mug. Again not a deal breaker. After the first few uses you get on board and remember that you have to press the button to turn it on. All in all, a good mug. A good replacement for my Ember. And less expensive.

title: If you like your coffee VERY HOT, read on!
body: I like my coffee VERY HOT!... all the time! After several days of careful measuring with several different, accurate liquid thermometers, I determined that my preferred coffee temperature range is 160F - 170F degrees. Above 170F and it starts approaching uncomfortable burning of the tongue. Between 155F - 160F, still enjoyable. Between 150F - 155F has me wishing it was hotter, but on a cold morning, still does the job. Below 150 degrees, yuck! Can't have it! It must be reheated or dumped! Period! After some research, it appears that "150F - 170F" just happens to be the official acceptable temperature range of hot coffee. Supposedly Starbucks and other coffee shops shoot for 150F - 170F when serving hot coffee. My measuring and personal assessment is dead on with this. I'm happy to report that the Nextmug will keep coffee hovering right around 150F degrees (when set to the hottest, "piping" setting), for a minimum of an hour... but ONLY *with the lid on*. Without the lid on, the Nextmug CANNOT hold 150F degrees and instead holds about 143F - 145F-ish. This testing was done in a 60F degree indoor environment. The lid makes all the difference in the max temperature it will consistently hold. When I had first tried out the Nextmug, I hadn't been using the lid. The coffee experience was unsatisfying, not hot enough and I was getting ready to return it. Once I tried using it for a few mornings with the *lid on*, I was instantly happy and am now keeping it. If you need your coffee to be HOT at all times and you don't mind keeping the lid in place while drinking your coffee, you will enjoy the Nextmug. 150F isn't ideal, but it's above the line of acceptability in my opinion, as a fan of very hot coffee... and it sure beats the otherwise 8+ trips to the microwave to reheat a single cup of coffee when using a standard, non-electric mug. Now if one of these electric mug manufacturers would only come out with an electric, self-heating mug that could hold 160F degrees, we'd have a real winner! For now, the Nextmug does a great job at holding 150F (with lid on). The Ember, by contrast, has a max temperature setting of only 145F, that's a shame, instant deal-breaker, what were they thinking? Ember, Nextmug and the rest... please bump up the max temperature settings of these mugs!!! The three settings should be: 140 ("warm"), 150 ("hot") and 160 ("piping"). Then it would actually make sense and be truly satisfying to those who enjoy hot coffee.

title: Good idea but battery life is too short
body: I like the mug and it appears to work well but you get one use out of a full charge that is very disappointing. I was hoping that I didn't have to leave the charging pad out all of the time but you have to use everyday. Short battery life is only reason I am leaving 3 star if it lasted longer rating would be be better.

title: I wish the cup was a little bigger
body: This electric coffee cup is pretty cool and does actually heat up your coffee with the touch of a button. I've owned it for about a year and it still works fine. Also, the cup is sleek and comfortable. My biggest negatives about it are the price, the size. In the past, I used a bigger cup, so by the time I got to the lower half of the cup, it was much less hot, which I can't stand, hence, my purchase of Nextmug. The problem I have is that I actually don't need to use the warmer on this cup that much because it's just an average size and I usually get to the bottom and start another cup of hot coffee without needing to turn on the cup warmer. The levels of heat are Warm, Hot, and Piping. I can't imagine using even the Hot setting, as the warm setting is plenty hot. The Piping setting is perplexing and can't imagine anyone using or wanting this setting. I don't particularly like the blinking battery indicator lights that are always doing something, but it's a small feature at the bottom of the cup. These do make great gifts, although pretty pricey. The product does do what it says and looks and feels great. It would make a lot of sense if the company designed a bigger cup for the obvious reason of not having to fill the cup back up as much and having the heater available to keep your coffee warm the whole time. 4/5 stars

title: Nextmug, Less \"Smart\" But Overall Better Than Others
body: Previously, I had the Ember mug (two of them to be exact) and they both stopped working after a while. I found the app to be buggy and while the concept was great, the execution just wasn't there. Because of this, I was pretty skeptical of this mug. It's been amazing, however, and overall much easier and functional without having to deal with the app. I had considered giving four stars since I've had to replace the coaster and now the mug itself but the customer service was so good, I bumped them to 5 stars. I bought this mug Jan 2024, and they have since, free of charge, sent me a new coaster and new mug. It's a great product but also, great company/customer service. they are super understanding and easy to work with if you have any issues. As for the mug itself, it works completely as advertised and keeps my coffee warm for hours!

title: Like it but has quirks.
body: Nothing worse than coffee which cools. Really love the idea of hot coffee without resorting to microwaving. Like the simplicity of not needing an app to set temperature (i.e. Ember). However, this mug has quirks. Sometimes will shutoff automatically although fully charged. And sometimes, the blinking lights go haywire, particularly after adding coffee to the mug. Perfect mug when these quirks aren't evident!

title: Hot coffee drinker approves !
body: I purchased this for our administrative assistant who loves hot coffee. Everyday I walk into the office, she points at it and smiles. 👍

title: Recommend
body: Wotks great

title: Life saver
body: Has 3 modes, warm, hot, pipping. All 3 work extremely well. I don't like my coffee after heating it up in a microwave, so, this cup is great for when I can't finish my coffee and have to come back to it after sometimes.

title: Reliable Coffee Mug for Warmth and Comfort, But Slightly Smaller Than Expected
body: I've been using the NextMug for a weeks now, and overall, it's been a reliable companion for keeping my coffee warm during my busy mornings. The mug offers three temperature settings: warm, hot, and piping, providing options for various preferences. However, I found the hot setting a tad too hot for my liking, opting to stick with the warm setting, which has been just right for maintaining a pleasant temperature without scalding my tongue. The packaging of this mug was impressive, ensuring that the product arrived intact. Upon inspection, the quality of the cup is evident – it appears well-made, and the lid seals tightly, preventing any spills while on the move. The cup's base is compact, not overly bulky, which I appreciate, and it charges up fairly quickly, ready for use in no time. The finish is sleek and feels good in the hand, offering a comfortable grip. Among its advantages, the cup's small base makes it easy to handle and store, while its efficient charging capabilities are a definite plus. The finish is of good quality, giving it a smooth refined appearance. Moreover, it fits comfortably in hand, making it a joy to use. However, a few downsides have been noted. Despite being labeled as a 14 oz. mug, it appears to hold closer to 12 oz. of liquid, especially when utilizing the lid. Additionally, the battery life, when set to warm, lasts around 2 hours, which might not suit longer periods away from a charging point. Regrettably, I haven't tested the other settings to gauge their respective battery life. One aspect that would have elevated my satisfaction with this mug would be a larger capacity – ideally closer to a 16 oz. size. In conclusion, the NextMug is a well-constructed mug that fulfills its promise of keeping beverages warm. Its multiple temperature settings cater to diverse preferences, although the hot setting might be too intense for some. Its smaller-than-expected capacity and limited battery life on warm settings might be areas for improvement. However, for those seeking a reliable and portable option to keep their coffee warm on the go, this mug certainly fits the bill.

title: self heating mug
body: I purchased this for myself after purchasing as a gift! It's very nice and weighty. It keeps my tea (or any other beverage) piping hot for hours. It comes with a clear sippy lid - I don't use but it probably would keep your beverage even hotter - but I can't imagine. It says that it holds 14 oz... title: Love this mug!
body: I no longer have to continually reheat my coffee. I'm Not a fast coffee drinker. Using the lid expands the heat time but with lid I get 3 hours not the four hours as described but 3 hours is more than sufficient!

title: My NextMug was/is great
body: I have had this cup for 2.25 years, using it nearly every day over that time. It kept my coffee hot for over 2 hours the first year, a little less the next year, and now it is down to half an hour. But, I have no complaint. This cup has been just what I wanted. It is easy to use, I didn't want to mess around with an app to set temps. The 3 that next mug provides are a good range and quick to change. I am going to buy another one. I will report if it doesn't pass muster. The first one sure did.

title: Nextmug- Three temperatures, Warm, Medium, Hot (Dusty Rose Coffee Mug-14 oz.)
body: Pros: The first time I saw this mug, my daughter had in her car to drink coffee. She explained that it keeps the coffee warm with 3 settings that you can set to warm, medium, hot. You place the cup on a plate using the USB cord with wall power adapter to charge it up. It's portable because once it recharges, it stays charged for a while and you can take it anywhere you want. I asked how much it was. At the time, she said her husband bought it as a gift for her, and it was something like $134. It was out-of-my price range. It comes sealed with plastic in a box, well packaged inside the box with a round plate, USB Cord, wall charger (in separate box) and mug with lid. All parts were sealed in plastic. Full instructions with pictures included. The price was around $89 on the October Prime Days (2024). I bought the Dusty Rose color. I usually buy 16 oz. Wawa coffee, but I take forever to drink it, it gets cold, and I throw the rest out. Today was the first day I used it. I set the ceramic mug on warm, poured 14 ozs. of coffee in. It was hot, so I waited, and it cooled a little and drank some, taking like an hour to drink abut 7 ozs. I poured the rest in and set it to hot, in a couple of minutes it heated up and lowered to medium. As I was drinking it, and there was less in the cup, I lowered to warm. I was able to have nice warm coffee for 90 minutes. Will be using this every day. Love it. Cons: Regular Price expensive, not immersible to wash. Have to be careful not to get the bottom wet underneath where you place on top of the charger.

title: Excellent purchase
body: A bit expensive but the quality is worth it. Warm beverage between getting ready to start your day. I have always tried to buy something that is the best in quality and only buy it once. I have had this one for about two months. Totally satisfied.

title: Cup controlled temperature
body: Love the constant temperature but unhappy with the cup staining

title: Great Find
body: Awesome find. Does everything you’d expect and it’s keeps your beverage at the perfect temperature.

title: Pretty good!
body: Had this about a year and it's been great. It does lose charge kind of quickly ~1 hour then needs recharge to keep it hot.

title: Prefer Nextmug to the Ember, read review for why
body: This review is after about 2 months of daily use of both mugs. I purchased and ember mug first and although it works fine, you can't adjust the temperature on it unless you install the app. In order to install the app, you need to give it access to your contacts and your phone. I sent ember an email asking why and never got any response beyond "Thank you for reaching out to Ember support! Your request has been received. We are currently experiencing longer reply times, but our team is working diligently to get back to you! ...". I've never installed the app. Here are some other key points: 1. Nextmug is bigger 2. Nextmug comes with a lid which helps with battery life. You can buy a lid for the Ember (another $15) 3. Nextmug is $15 cheaper 4. Ember has straight sides (better), Nextmug's side are smallest at top and bottom, widest in the middle. E.g. You have to tip the Nextmug further to empty the cup, especially with the lid on. 5. My Nextmug temp range is 130F to 150F set in 5 degree increments. The Ember is 120F to 145F with the app and can be set in 1 degree increments (I have not confirmed this). Without the app the ember is set at a default 135F. 6. Both keep the coffee hot. Nextmug his its 150F, Ember 135F. 7. I started both mugs with warm (117F) water. After 13 minutes Nextmug (with lid on) got to 140, Ember (no lid) 132. In 17 minutes, Ember reached 135 and Nextmug his 150F. 8. Ember turns on automatically - nice feature. You have to turn on the Nextmug each time. Both shut off if they're empty. Conclusions: If you don't mind adding an app that can access your phone and contacts then this comes down to features and pricing. Note since I don't have the app, I cant speak to its other features - you may want to research and add that to your considerations. For me I like the 150F setting, so even disregarding the app, I prefer the Nextmug. (Ember max is 145F)

title: Almost perfect...
body: I really like the Nextmug. It's a great alternative to that pricey Em***r mug. The "Piping" hot setting does indeed keep your beverage VERY VERY HOT - which I love. But that being said, it's not perfect. My biggest gripe is the 14 oz. mug is JUST BARELY 14 ounces... to a point where you need to rely on surface tension to actually get 14 ounces in there. Secondly, I do wish the battery life was a bit better when the mug is not sitting on its charging pad. Other than those fairly minor gripes, it's a great product overall. Also keep in mind this is not app-controlled. The mug has a physical button which controls the settings.

title: Highly Recommend!
