title: Keeps coffee hot
body: This cup keeps my coffee hot. I love it.

title: Great Cup, limited battery life.
body: I'm only giving this cup 3 stars because the battery has lasted only 11 mo. I did read other reviews saying the same thing. I owned an Ember, and the battery lasted about a year also. While I had it, I loved it. I am a stickler for hot coffee. I am also a multi tasker, so it was nice to be able to do things around the house while my coffee stayed hot. I have recently ordered two for friends as gifts ( before mine died). While it was working, the battery does keep the coffee hot for a long time. At first I was disgusted at the amount of money I spent for less than a year of use, however, if you put things into perspective...$9-$10 a month for hot coffee is probably worth it, I can spend that much at Starbucks in one trip!

title: Warm or hot it never fails
body: I have been using the heated cup now for 5 months with absolutely no problems. The heat setting works great. If you like warm or very hot coffee it’s always there when you need it. I used it daily and it never fails to keep my coffee warm the way I want it.

title: Great ,except for battery life.
body: Very user friendly. But the battery does not last long. If you need it to last more than an hour, you have to keep it on the charging plate. The mug is a good size. And I like the design.

title: Keeps my coffee hot to the last drop
body: I couldn't possibly be any happier with these mugs! We got two, one for me and one for my wife. She likes to keep it on the medium setting, I like the hottest. Being able to grab this and take it on the road is great. It's not a great fit for the standard cup holder but the rounded bottom sits neatly at the top of ours and it stays put. Plus having the included sippy top is great for the road warrior. I am definitely most pleased with this cup.. I can truly sip and enjoy my coffee all the way down to the last drop without having to stick it in the microwave for a reheat. For example, I filled it this morning and took a 20 minute car ride, finally finishing my coffee about 10 minutes after we arrived. I turned it off and now that I'm back home a number of hours later, I get another cup and turn it on to see I still have 3 green lights on the power meter. And that was running it piping hot with the top on it. My understanding is that it lasts even longer if you run it at the lower settings. 6-Month Update: I am still loving this mug. I use it every day at my desk and every morning in the car when I take my kids to school. I especially like that I can reheat my coffee from room temp and it tastes just as good (to my perhaps slightly non-discerning palate) as when I first poured it. Much better than my experience with plate-based heaters on which you would place a standard mug. I still highly recommend this mug! 1 Year update: I still use this mug every single day and enjoy it so much I want to come back to update my review here to share that. It's really quite outstanding! Just can't really say much more than I already have. Definitely a great mug for the price.

title: Worth it!
body: I have replaced at least 2 ember parts and 2 mugs due to either chipping paint, not working anymore and abhorrent app got on my nerves. I decided to give this mug a try, I loved it so much, I purchased one for my husband. I had one issue and the customer was so impressive and responsive. It is so refreshing to see a company stand behind their product. I am purchasing another mug for my daughters birthday, since she is always commenting on mine. Get the mug, it's worth every penny!

title: Great if you don’t plan to take it far from the charger
body: Why did you pick this product vs others?: I got this as a mother’s day gift and was thrilled to finally enjoy hot coffee without repeated trips to the microwave. Unfortunately after 2 weeks of use it doesn't seem to hold a charge, thus defeating the purpose.

title: Excellent mug and customer service
body: Reviewing this mug 2 years later because first, my husband loves this mug! He was always notorious for reheating his coffee again and again. Secondly, this company has incredible customer service. After an accident involving his mug, my husband contacted the company who graciously offered to replace it.

title: LOVE this mug & base.
body: Finally, something that keeps my coffee hot enough that is nice & compact. The base is small enough I usually keep it plugged in. As my coffee level goes down, I lower the heat because it will get start to get like coffee left on a burner - not a bad thing - it means its keeping it hot. Customer service was AWESOME!! I had posted a prior question and they jumped in and took care of my issue. I would not hesitate to recommend. I bought an extra base so I can keep in on the base in two places. It does stay charged off the base, but its so easy to use the base for me, I tend to keep it on a lot. I don't care for drinking through a lid, but that is key to help keeping it the hottest. Same with any mug. I usually pop it off for sips.

title: Excellent product worth the money.
body: I have purchased 6 mugs in the last two years. WHY? Because it is an excellent product!! I purchased a Ember mug approximately 3+ years ago it was a great purchase and was for the first year. (The temperature setting is done using an app on your phone). I tried to resuscitate the mug, as the app had failed to where the temperature could no longer be maintained. I did like what the Ember provided. I was ready to invest in a second Ember when I read a review where a purchaser mentioned the Next mug. I am so glad I did! I bought one and am still using it 2 years later. I am so impressed with this mug that I bought one for a co-worker this summer and for Christmas, I purchased 4 more, two for cousins and two for my grandsons. While working at my desk and getting involved with my job so much that my coffee got cold. This mug maintains the heat with three different settings. "Piping setting" is HOT!! My go to is the "hot" setting and keeps my coffee hot for FOUR hours!! Hot coffee happy worker!! Tip: If you are a creamer user, do not stir with a metal spoon. I've found the ceramic mugs will scratch. I add the creamer first and let my Keurig do the stirring as the coffee is poured in the mug. Enjoy!!

title: Better than the Ember mug
body: I had an Ember mug but returned it. This is so much better. I don't need to adjust the temperature to 129 degrees like the Ember mug. The three settings on here are more than enough. This mug comes with a lid, while the ber lid is sold separately. Using the middle setting, with the lid on this keeps it hot for many hours off the charger.

title: Perfect gift for coffee lover
body: Best gift for my mom!!! She loves her coffee and now she doesn’t have to keep reheating it! This mug charges pretty quick and she uses it each morning. The color was so pretty too.

title: Not great battery life
body: This was a less expense alternative to the Ember, after 14 months the batter only lasts about 15 min, while my mothers ember lasts for over an hour. The batter life even in the beginning was only about 30 min. Inow wait to turn it on until about 30 min into my cup of coffee so it is ok as it heats it back up without cooking the coffee.

title: Super Hot & efficient
body: Stays super hot !! Great and hold a nice 10oz of coffee and still leaves room for nice froth milk if you like !

title: The best temp control mug available
body: Now that I have used this mug for 6 months, I feel I can provide a completely honest, inclusive review. I had been using Ember mugs for several years and when my latest Ember stopped working, I wasn’t willing to shell out the big bucks on another and began searching for alternatives. I found Nextmug and decided to give it a shot. Nextmug vs. Ember Mug: A Comprehensive Comparison 1. **App-Free Experience**: Unlike the Ember Mug, which relies heavily on its companion app for customization and temperature control, the Nextmug offers a hassle-free experience with no app dependency. This simplicity appeals to me and I much prefer straightforward functionality without the need for additional software. 2. **Extended Battery Life**: One of the standout features of the Nextmug is its impressive battery life, surpassing that of the Ember Mug. With longer intervals between charges, I find I can enjoy my coffee throughout the day without constantly worrying about recharging. 3. **Convenient Lid Design**: The inclusion of a handy lid adds practicality to the Nextmug, providing spill-proof protection and heat retention capabilities. This feature enhances my experience by offering added convenience and functionality. 4. **Temperature Control**: While both mugs excel in maintaining beverage temperature, the Nextmug offers competitive performance without the need for constant app monitoring. Its intuitive design allows me to enjoy my coffee at my preferred temperature without any fuss. I find I don’t need the ability to pick a super specific temperature, the 3 settings are adequate for finding my perfect temperature preference. 5. **Design and Build Quality**: Both mugs exhibit sleek and modern designs, but the Nextmug's durable construction and thoughtful design elements, such as the ergonomic grip and spill-resistant lid, contribute to its overall appeal. In conclusion, the Nextmug emerges as a commendable alternative to the Ember Mug, offering a seamless user experience with its app-free operation, extended battery life, and convenient lid design. The Nextmug delivers on both functionality and convenience, making it a worthy investment for anyone in search of a smart beverage companion. And with a price that is quite reasonable compared to my ember, it’s worth the investment in my opinion.

title: nice coffee mug
body: I got the wine color and its nice. The mug has some weight due to the bottom battery but it not bad to handle. Easy to use and set up. My only complaint is the description states 14 oz. but I used my k-cup machine and set it for 10 oz so I can add my creamer and the fluid reached almost to the top. I have to drink some and then add my cream and then I was able to put the cap on. Without drinking a bit the cap would have pushed the coffee over the edge. Got this on Prime day for a large discount but still $80. I'll keep for work use since theirs no way to keep coffee hot unless microwave it. I keep it at Hot setting which is just perfect for me. I tried the Pipping setting and that is too hot. I have to keep the mug on the base because if not after 2 hours or so the mug shuts off and the coffee cools down.

title: A good product, hopefully with a bit more longevity
body: This is my second Nextmug. I use it in the evenings while watching TV. The first one quit working after 14 months, just beyond the one year warranty I look for others for replacement, but this product was still rated the best by many. For this purchase, I added a four year warranty.

title: Built-in Battery is Insufficient
body: When not on the supplied coaster charger, the battery will be exhausted in less than two hours if you keep the setting on the hottest "piping" set point. Setting to the "Warm" set point can extend the time the battery will keep the mug content warm, but the battery will be exhausted after 3-4 hours. Moreover, the mug's No Activity feature turns off ALL heating after two hours of no physical motion of the mug. Overall, the Nextmug mug is a bit pricey, but it is well made and I would purchase it again if damaged. One distracting feature is the placement of the LEDs. Because the LEDs are placed to focus on the black coaster, it is very difficult to see them when viewed from any angle above the LEDs. A chrome polished outer circle on the coaster would act as a mirror for the LEDs.

title: Coffee Cup for coffee lovers
body: I absolutely love this coffee cup, I use it at work and when I am in meetings it keeps my coffee warm. At home keeps it warm and don't have to warm it up in the microwave.

title: Absolutely love this mug. Use it every day.
body: It took me a while to justify spending this kind of money on a coffee mug but I am so glad I did. It is exactly what I have been wanting. I am not a fast drinker so by the time I go drink my coffee, it is cold and I am having to reheat it. Those days are done. I turn it on the lowest temperature after making it and it stays warm until I am done. It's the only coffee cup I use and want to get one that will fit in my car for when I am traveling now.

title: SHOULD be a great idea...
body: So in theory this is a great idea, I wish it worked the way it should. My hubby got me one of these for Christmas. I was excited about it as I am an interior designer and tend to work away from my desk a lot with clients so my coffee always gets cold. With this I should be able to have hot coffee through a meeting..."should" being the key word here. When I remove the cup from the charger and try to work away from my desk the battery will only last about 20min on the "Hot" setting, so no way I am making it through a 2-3 hour design meeting with hot coffee. Sure seems like the battery should last longer than this, especially for over $100! I used to have a small "hot plate" thing you could set a regular mug on to keep coffee hot, not sure how this is better as I basically have to keep it on the charger to have hot coffee for any length of time....might as well have saved the money and just kept my hot plate. I am still attached to my desk with either option if I want my coffee to stay hot. This expensive mug was supposed to free me from having to be at my desk, being able to walk around with a hot cup of coffee! Also, what leads me to maybe think I got bad one...when I turn it on, all the lights start flashing and it shuts off. I have to turn it back on sometimes several times before it actually stays on and heats up. I know this isn't supposed to happen, so maybe I just got a defective product. So, I don't know if I got a lemon or something, but for the price sure seems like this thing should work better. Being it was a Christmas present I didn't notice these issues until after the return window closed so I am screwed now. My hubby was thinking about getting one for himself but if a battery only lasts 20min what's the point of spending all this money? Very disappointed.

title: It’s nearly perfect
body: This is the BEST! I used to re-heat my coffee and tea in the microwave multiple times a day. This mug is a dream come true. I put my tea on Hot and my coffee on piping. The battery lasts me 2 hours. Two negatives: 1 The handle is uncomfortable, I have to hold it in a certain way to avoid it digging in to my middle finger. 2 The cup is very cold to begin with on the outside so to get rid of that I prime it with hot tap water; just a comfort thing.

title: Perfect simple gift and for yourself with no app hassle.
body: Makes for a great gift for anyone for any occasion AND it's also a great product. You don't have to mess with an app or connect it to some Bluetooth bs. You charge it and turn it on and it's done. I wish the battery lasted a little longer, but it lasts forever on the coaster obviously. It absolutely stays hot as per what you set it at. Yeah you can't set it to exactly 176 degrees, but like who TF needs that anyway? You either want it warm or HOT AF or in between. VERY easy and simple to use for your aging boomer parents or Grandma that still doesn't know what a cell phone is. It's really easy to clean too. Just get it. Ember's lame. Be aware though. You cannot expect this to go from cold coffee that's sat for an hour to piping hot on its own. I thought something was wrong with mine when I first got it. Put it on the coaster thingy if you wanna try that.

title: Pretty good mug overall
body: What we liked: Instructions are clear and concise and easy to follow. The mug does a pretty good job of maintaining temperature. We liked the design of the mug and its weight felt solid in our hands. What we didn't like so much: The control button is very hard to see. Paint the steam icon on the button white or silver so it can be found without having to feel around for it. Although using the lid helped the mug maintain its temperature for longer, we are not crazy about the idea of drinking from a cup with a heated plastic lid. Finally, I'd definitely buy this again but I'd spring for the 18 oz mug this time.

title: temp controls are perfect
body: Really like this mug. Temp setting seem right on whether you want your beverage piping hot, just warm or perfectly in between. My only regret is I wish I had purchased the next size up because even though this cup says its 14oz, when I select the 12oz brewing option on my coffee maker it fills it to the very tippy top of the rim, with no room to put on the lid.

title: Perfect Gift
body: Delivery was quick and packaged appropriately. This was a gift for someone and they have reported it was the best, most useful gift they've ever received. It's perfect to keep a coffee/tea hot for a long time. Nice weight for hands and easy care. I may purchase for myself.

title: Great Cup
body: Love almost everything about this cup. There are a couple of things I would like to see changed. The first one is just personal preference. I would like the handle to be a bit wider. Would make it more comfortable with the weight. It would also be nice if the temperature could be set so that it didn’t have to be set with each use. A couple of more options on temp would be nice as my ideal would be between the hot and piping settings. Outside of those 3 picky items, it is a great cup. Very much recommend!

title: Ease of use.
body: If you like your coffee or tea to stay hot while you drink it, you definitely need one if these.

title: I love this mug!!
body: I have used this mug 5 times since I got it and I have nothing but good things to say! I read a ton of reviews about this mug compared to other options and ultimately settled on this one because I didn’t want to bother with an app. The mug has 3 settings - warm, hot, and piping. The mug itself doesn’t feel hot which was important to me. It also has an auto-off feature if it’s left on without any liquid in the cup. It does a great job of keeping drinks hot, and I really like the included lid. I feel that the smaller size is sufficient for me, but just be mindful that the heating element takes up some space in the bottom of the mug, so the mug looks a bit bigger on the outside than the actual liquid volume it can hold. title: works very well
body: I was skeptical after issues with the other major brand of heated coffee cups. The features on this cup actually work as described. When set to the "piping" hot mode, it really does keep your coffee very hot. The different heat settings and the on/off button seemed gimmicky, but work as expected and are a nice additional feature. The materials and construction of the cup feel substantial. The lid is a nice touch that seems to keep the heat in and help prevent spills. The true test will be longevity of the coating on the inside of the cup. All the cups from the other major brand would begin to peel on the inside within months of use. Their customer service would argue this was chipping due to use of a metal stirring spoon. Even with a plastic spoon, the coating would still peel off. I believe the peeling issue was due to the rapid change of temperature when pouring in the hot coffee in a cold cup. I will report back if this cup begins to peel. Update 1/23/2025: This cup is still working better than expected. The surface coating inside and out still looks new. The battery life for heating is more than adequate. The software (software in a coffee cup??) is simple but well though out. It seems to know when the cup is empty or has been sitting unused for too long and shuts off the heating to save battery power. It heats the coffee quickly to the desired temperature if you happen to pour in some less than hot coffee. I look forward to using it each morning.

title: Near Perfect Machin
body: Let me start this review by mentioning that I drink one, or rarely two, cups of coffee/day. I buy whole beans and grind them to Turkish blend. I needed to replace a drip pot that quit working after 15 years. In researching my purchase, I found that the name brand K-cup machine is waaaay overpriced. The off brand ones are cheap plastic. I wanted something smaller than the last one just for ease of handling and counter top space saving. At only 9 inches tall, this one is. It just so happens to go with my kitchen appliances which are stainless/black. There are a lot - 85% worth of four and five star reviews. I can't add much to those so I'm going to comment on the ones that are 3 -1 and perhaps lend themselves to unrealistic exceptions of a simple coffee pot. One comment is that it makes weak coffee. That's a product of the quality of the coffee and the amount added to the basket. It is also a fact that perculated water does stay on the grounds as long as drip water. Heavier water drops vs lighter ones. I did needed to add a small amount more coffee to basket to overcome the heavier water drops perculated. There were conflicting reviews concerning the top. It's was too loose or it was too tight. Standard manufacturing process = one or the other. There were complaints that it was hard to remove the top. It does take just a tad bit more pull to get the lid off. But I would ask: do you want it to be secure or drop off when you pour and have to clean up a grounds mess on the counter? A comment was made that the parts are inferior. Absolutely not true. It is stainless steel and heavy polly plastic. There was a concern that the reperk/keep warm feature didn't work as expected. I don't use that feature so it could be true. But I would ask a basic question. Why not just brew another fresh cup? It only takes two minutes start to finish. There was a concern that it is nearly impossible to clean inside because the opening is narrow. I am a man with descent sized fist/hand. I can get it inside the pot with ease. At first, I thought that having an electrical plug that you needed to plug into the pot and also to the outlet was not a good design technique. But then I thought that if that plug gets damaged...probably by me...or has a default then I can just replace it instead of rewiring the whole thing. I will say that I use a normal paper filter cut down to the size of the coffee bowl with a small hole in the center. I insert that into the coffee basket before brewing. It is easy on the clean up process by dumping that into the trash. I am tight on my 5 star ratings. This one missed the final star because the pot does not have an On/Off switch. The world's industry standard is to have an On/Off switch on all electrical equipment.

There's just something about the way it brews that brings out the full flavor of the coffee beans. It's rich, robust, and incredibly smooth. No bitterness, no weak flavor – just pure, delicious coffee. It's the kind of coffee that makes you want to savor every sip. And it's so simple to use! Just add water, coffee grounds, plug it in, and let it do its thing. No complicated settings or buttons to worry about. It's perfect for those mornings when you just want a good cup of coffee without any fuss. Clean-up is a breeze too. The parts are easy to remove and wash, unlike some of the more complicated coffee makers out there. I also love the classic, retro look of this percolator. It looks great on my countertop and adds a touch of vintage charm to my kitchen. If you're a coffee purist who appreciates a truly great cup of coffee, I highly recommend giving this Farberware percolator a try. It's not fancy, it's not high-tech, but it makes exceptional coffee. It's become my go-to coffee maker, and I wouldn't trade it for anything. Seriously, my mornings have never been better!

title: Not for coffee snobs
body: I'm a a bit of a coffee snob and apply the snobbery every morning to prepare one cup of pour-over coffee. I tried this 4-cup electric percolator as a nostalgic alternative for the occasions I might want to make a little more coffee. I used high quality dark-roast coarse ground coffee and prepared a pot according to manufacturer instructions (water to the 4-cup line which is only about 18 oz of water, and 4 T of coffee). It was insipid and undrinkable. I made a second pot using 5 T of coffee, and it was still very weak. I prepared a third pot using 7 generous tablespoons. It was finally strong enough, and I drank the first cup (but without much enjoyment). However, when I poured the second cup, it was vile. The 'keep warm' setting lets the remaining coffee and sludge continue to audibly simmer, so it tasted even worse than coffee that sits on the hot plate of a drip coffee maker all day. I had no desire to experiment further, but if I were truly invested in keeping the percolator, I would try coffee ground just slightly less coarse, which may have improved the taste somewhat. It was a bit of a mess to dispose of the spent grounds, and not easy to properly clean the pot when you can't immerse it in water (which would be the case with any electric percolator, to be fair). The coffee is barely worthy of one star, but I'm giving the percolator 3 stars, because it does produce coffee; it's just not coffee that this admitted coffee snob would ever enjoy. One thing I did like about the percolator is that it smelled divine while it was perking, and for a short while after it was done. The coffee aroma in the air was 5 stars (until it the 'keep warm' setting ruined it). It also did provide the nostalgic percolator experience I'd imagined (minus the glass knob). But, since I can't drink aroma or nostalgia, I will be returning the percolator.

title: My new favorite appliance
body: When my little drip coffee maker kicked the bucket and I needed a replacement, I decided to try a 4 cup electric percolator instead of a new drip coffee maker, with the following hopes: - It would be easy to keep clean. - It would make a hotter cup of coffee. - It would be quick. - I wouldn't need to use filters. - The coffee would taste good (I like strong coffee, but not bitter). After about a month of use, I'm happy to say that most of my hopes have been fulfilled. - It is so easy to keep clean, which of course contributes to consistently good coffee. - The coffee is so hot that I have to wait for it to cool before I can drink it. If I want milk, I don't have to worry about it cooling my coffee too much! - It's pretty quick, 3 or 4 minutes to brew 2 cups. About the same as my little drip brewer used to be. - I find that I still prefer to use a paper filter, although when I don't, there are still fewer grounds in my coffee than there used to be when I used the mesh filter that came with my old drip machine. - The coffee is wonderful. I don't mind Folgers and Maxwell House; I drink either on weekday mornings to save money, and they do taste much better perc'ed. But on the weekends, I treat myself to fresh ground "specialty" beans, and I can really taste the difference! With the drip maker, everything tasted kind of the same. Additionally, I've found that I use less ground coffee to make the same strength of brewed coffee (I don't know if that's because the water temperature is hotter). A few tips that I've found helpful (found either from reviews here or elsewhere online): - Make sure that the washer at the base of the tube is free and rattling, not stuck to the fixed washer. Otherwise, the coffee will not perc long enough and it'll be weak. - Wetting the basket before adding the ground coffee keeps the grounds in the basket better. - If you don't want to use a filter and you don't want sediment, use an ounce or so more water than you want, and don't pour the dregs into your mug. I'm very happy with my new percolator. And it's cute, too! Update: The percolator worked beautifully for more than 5 years, but has now stopped working. 5 years is not terrible for a small appliance that sees daily use, but I'd hoped for better. I debated replacing it with a new one exactly the same, but I've decided to try a Hamilton Beach percolator instead.

So, when a family member requested a coffee percolator for Xmas, THIS is what I chose for them... I love it for several reasons. First, and most important, it makes wonderful, VERY hot coffee. Because it makes such hot coffee, the taste of even a "so-so" brand is significantly improved, and the taste of a great coffee becomes OUTSTANDING! (You cannot get the high brewing temperatures from an automatic drip coffee maker, thus making this percolator far superior to all of them, even though it lacks a few "handy features" like an automatic timer) Second, it is reliable. As noted above, we've had this model for at least five years and have never had a single problem with it... It works as designed every time! Third, it is fast! It takes less than five minutes from start to finish to have a full pot of steaming hot coffee ready to drink. Fourth, No waste! It makes one large mug and one regular mug of coffee for each full pot (or four small cups)... So, say goodbye to wasted coffee! With the price of coffee, wasting it is almost a crime... (We have its "big brother" for when we have company and that one makes four large mugs or 8 small cups) Fifth, it is EASY and very simple to use. There's nothing complicated about it, in fact, a 6 year old can easily do it for you if you let them. Sixth, it is easy to clean. All the parts except for the body of it can go into the dishwasher or be washed in hot, soapy dishwater. I recommend scrubbing it thoroughly at least once a week to keep the stains away as it is always easier to keep them at bay than to get rid of them once they appear. If one is fairly lazy and doesn't want to do more than just rinse it out daily, then you can run vinegar through a cycle once a week to keep it shiny too... The only downside that I can think of are that it does not have an automatic timer, but it's so fast, who cares? To be even faster, it can be prepared at night and simply plugged in when you get up. It is fairly small, which is perfect for two good sized cups or 4 small ones, but if you want more than that, you have to refill it or simply buy a larger pot instead or in addition. That's why we have two sizes. Normally, the small pot is just perfect for us. But several times a year, we have overnight guests (or dinner guests) and need more coffee. We'd normally only buy the larger one, BUT the larger sized percolators really are NOT good at making small pots of coffee~! I'm guessing it is because of the inaccuracy of water to coffee ratio not being "just right" when trying to use a large model to a small model's job. Bottom line: this small model works perfectly, is just the right amount, and is well worth the purchase price for those couples who each just want one, fairly large, great cup of coffee each every morning or for the single person who wants two big cups every morning...

title: Stopped working after 5 months

The coffee from this little brewer comes out piping hot and tastes better than the coffee from my Mr. Coffee. If I were blindfolded, I could tell the difference. They're both good coffee makers, but the Faberware makes it hotter and a tad richer. Surprisingly, the Faberware maker is faster than the Mr. Coffee. There is no ON/Off button. You plug it in when ready and it goes to work. When you're done, you unplug it. The coffee grounds do not fall through the stainless steel basket when brewing. And when you pour out the last drop, and the brewer is upside down, the coffee grounds stay inside the basket. So you don't need a disc coffee filter, though I use one because they are supposed to be healthier. Overall, I'm quite happy with the little beast.

title: These are great little 2
body: These are great little 2.5 cup coffee pots. I have been using them for well over 25 years. Great for one person. I have had a few over the years. I have experienced failure only when I have dropped them on the floor and have either broken the wire heating element in the bottom of the percolator or shattered the black bottom ceramic. I have had a power plug failure but that is because I have left the thing plugged in for hundreds of hours and after that amount of time the plastic at the end of the plug has just worn out from the constant heat it is exposed to (sort of like tire rot on a tire that has lasted too long). Basically my view is the things are built like a tank as long as they are not abused. They make great coffee--people at work are constantly bumming my coffee because it is so much better than drip. But there are two points that are crucial. First, you need to use a standard coffee drip filter inside the coffee holder (which you can get for super cheap in any grocery store). Just tear a little hole in the middle and slip the filter over the stem. Nothing to it. Secondly, the pots brews inside of five minutes and is done. This results in weak coffee. But this is easily overcome. Just keep a glass measuring cup on hand. Pour half a cup of brewed coffee into the measuring cup, remove the top of the percolator, and pour the coffee back through being careful not to overflow beyond the top of the filter. That boosts the color--the strength--of the coffee. If first pour through is not enough, do it again and so on until color is up to snuff. Usually one or two pour throughs is all that is needed. Here is another tip. To make good strong coffee, fill percolator with tap water to a point just below the cage. Insert the coffee filter as described above. I use 2.5 teaspoons of coffee per standard cup of coffee, so put about 7-8 teaspoons of coffee into the tray. Plug in and allow to brew. After brewing is done, pour some coffee and check color. If weak, do one or two pour throughs bringing the color up to desired point. That is it. These pots make outstanding coffee. You just have to understand these few points. Nothing to it. The downside of all is that if you allow others to try your coffee, they will constantly be coming back and bumming it. The solution. Either run them off or get the larger model of the same pot. Same simple rules apply, just use more water and more coffee grounds.

But with research showing the health hazards of plastic (black, in particular) touching hot water, I decided to go back to the old-fashioned percolator made of aluminum (including the filter). It took me a little while to find what I wanted since I wanted a small 4-5 cups maker that met my requirements. I’m happy to report I love the Farberware There’s only one small annoyance (but doesn’t warrant knocking off a star) and that’s the fact that the lid is so tight that I sometimes have a slight problem removing it (it could have something to do with my wrists have weakened with age).

Overall I think it’ll be a great cooler for my family(3) and I 👍🏼 will have to update in the future after using it .. and I think I got it on sale? But the price was reasonable to me. Update: 11/27/24 It has been two years since I got this cooler bag and I have no complaints about it. It’s still in great condition and all in tact. I’ve used it all up until August of this past year because my other half is using it as his full time lunch bag since our child is in school, and I don’t necessarily need to pack as much for outings. title: 32 oz are the Big Guns of Meal Prep! -- but 64 oz are Almost Great, but Not Quite Airtight!
body: 5/5 When it comes to food storage, these 32 oz containers are the big guns I never knew I needed! They’ve swooped in to save my fridge from the chaos of oversized leftovers and half-finished dishes. The uniform lid size with my other Freshware sets means I can stack them high and save precious shelf space while avoiding lid confusion. They clean up easily, hold a hearty portion of whatever deliciousness I whip up, and look fabulous while doing it. Say goodbye to those flimsy old containers—these heavyweights are here to stay, keeping my meals fresh and my kitchen blissfully organized! 3/5 While I’ve been incredibly happy with the other Freshware sets—the 8, 16, and 32 oz varieties—this 64 oz set caught me off guard. Perhaps I missed a detail in the listing, but each lid has a small vent hole in the lid, which makes their claim of being 100% airtight a bit dubious. I was really hoping for an airtight seal to keep my leftovers and freezer meals fresh, but it seems like I’ll need to manage my expectations here. They’re still functional for storing food, but they don’t quite meet my intended needs. Plus, they feel like a different plastic than the other sets. I’ll still use them, but I’ll probably only recommend the smaller sizes to friends—after all, sometimes size matters, but so does a proper seal!

title: best food containers I've ever had
body: I've had many food containers over the years, and these are by far the best. They tick so many boxes: sturdy material, non-leaking, can handle extremes in temperature (both tolerant of hot foods as well as freezable without damage), dishwasher-friendly, microwave-friendly, clear (can easily see what's in them at a glance), fits a good amount of food without being too big, don't seem to hold onto smells or stains thus far. We have far less food waste than before, our fridge is constantly organized, and these go from fridge to lunchbox to dishwasher without a hitch. I just can't think of anything bad about these. I would like to respond to some other reviews I saw that talk about breaking lids: It's possible you got a bad batch, but I think it's more likely that those who had lid breakage are not used to leakproof lids that need to be gently worked off while turning the container (much like Lowe's or Home Depot 5 gallon bucket lids, which use a similar gripping mechanism and have similar lid breakage reviews like this). It requires a few extra seconds of patience, but it's absolutely worth it for the leakproof capability.

body: Absolutely great. I've been doing a lot of travel as of late, and I'm a big tea drinker. Which is a real problem when you live and mostly travel in the US, because the vast majority of the tea you get in hotels is crap, and they almost never have a decent way of just getting the hot water you need. I bought this thing as an experiment, and I'm glad I did. It works flawlessly. Does about a cup and a bit, which makes it perfect for either your own mugs or hotel sized insulated disposable cups. It's nice and quick, and it's astonishingly quiet. When I used it the first time I wasn't entirely sure I had it turned on, because it didn't make any noise at all till almost the moment it finished. A single loud beep is your indication the water's done boiling, at which point you can just unscrew the lid and pour. I do wish it had some kind of spout, but that's a minor gripe at most. Once dried out, you can store the plug inside it and stick it in your suitcase, ready for the next trip. I'll be using this thing for a good long time to come.

title: Passed its first trial with flying colors
body: I'm going to give my opinion of the travel kettle but first let me digress to this point: I'm a coffee snob. Whenever I travel, I bring my own coffee setup with me (which attracts unlimited derision from some loved ones and others, but I digress even further with that). "My own coffee setup" involves a pour-over kit (in this case an "OXO Single Serve 12 Ounces Pour-Over Coffee Maker" that I also bought on Amazon). Occasionally I even bring my own coffee grinder, but not this trip. "This trip" was a five-day trip to another US state where I knew I was going to be out in the middle of nowhere in a cheap (but charming) little hotel with nothing but an in-room coffee maker and no coffee to buy in town except watered-down gas station or diner coffee. And for that I'd have to walk 20 minutes. I wanted a way to heat my water, take out some beans I'd already ground, put them in my pour-over and have some coffee going in my room within minutes of getting up (but avoid using the questionable room coffeemaker). And all these devices needed to be portable enough to go into a piece of luggage for a plane trip. So ... enter the "Travel Electric Kettle" from the almost-unpronounceable, nonsensically named Chinese company. The first thing I noticed and very much like is the carry case; sleek and just big enough to fit the kettle (plug can go in the unit). The unit itself looked great -- mine is in white. The operation is simple. Fill it with water no higher than a fill line, secure the cap, plug it in, turn it on, make sure you have it set for the water temp you want (mine was 212 Fahrenheit) and then let it do its thing. In a few minutes it will get your water to the desired temp and beep, showing the temp on the display. I would then unplug the device (not strictly necessary but that's me) or at least make sure I could execute a pouring motion without getting fouled up in the cord, and then I would pour the hot water into the reservoir of my pour-over funnel and within minutes I was drinking strong, fresh hot coffee having never had to leave my hotel room. I used the unit six days in a row (and others did too, for other hot water needs) and now that I'm it is sitting in my cupboard, awaiting my next outing. For those who wonder about these things, it heats up to (about) 370ml of water in one go. That's roughly what filling to the fill line gets you. And, you have to be a little careful taking off the lid once your water is hot; it's a bit like taking the radiator cap off a car once it's been operating. I wait a minute and carefully unscrew it. All in all, I was very pleased with this travel electric kettle and only avoid giving it five star because I can't speak to its longevity yet (It was delivered to me the day before my trip).

title: Disappointed
body: Disliked: A crucial piece of information that was not included in description but was on instruction sheet that came with item was: "This product can be used at altitudes of less than 1200 meters (3937 feet) with the lid on to boil water. When altitude is higher than 1200 meters, open lid to boil water, do not close to boil water." I live at almost 6000 feet in altitude. The spill proof design if tipped over is null and void if I have to boil water with an open lid and it can potentially be a hazard for burns if accidentally knocked over. In description it said it would heat water to set temperature within 5-7 minutes. Not true. More like 7+ minutes. It says if using the lid (which I couldn't because of the altitude but I think it is important to note for those that can use the lid) that you must wait 2-3 minutes before opening lid. If you choose a temperature setting and you have to wait 2-3 minutes before opening the lid the water temperature begins cooling immediately upon shut off. Technically you won't get the desired temperature. Instructions that came with item also stated that this kettle will maintain temperature up to two hours without power. Not true. To begin with, I set the kettle at 212° and it never reached that temperature with lid on (I only tried this once because of the instructions about the altitude). It only reached 206° and with power on, mind you, following the instructions of waiting the 2 minutes before opening the lid the temperature dropped to 200°, at 3 minutes it dropped to 196°. I also tried this without the lid. It took longer than 8+ minutes to boil and shut off and it only reached 206°. Without the lid at the 2 minute mark the temperature dropped to 196° and at the 3 minute mark it was at 192°. I know I wouldn't have to wait the 2-3 minutes without the lid but as a reference, if I wasn't right there when it shut off to get the water at it's peak heat, the water would be cooling off rapidly. Instructions also stated that the kettle will maintain temperature at minimum of 113° for up to 12 hours with power on, then automatically switch off after 12 hours and slowly cool down. I don't know if this feature is true. I didn't bother to try it. The instructions say not to plug the kettle in without water. But it's easier to plug it in and then use a glass /cup to fill it with water. If you try to fill the kettle from the sink and then try to plug it in, it's not easy to keep the plug cover open, hold the kettle at a tilt to see where the plug goes in. I am returning this product for these reasons and... Side note: I bought this for my 98 year old mother. Up to now she was using our stove top whistling tea kettle for her every morning tea. She has been struggling to hold on to things because she has very deformed hands from her arthritis and is dropping things. This tea kettle was getting too big for her to handle with water in it. She also is deaf without her hearing aids and is exhibiting dementia type memory loss. If she forgets to put her hearing aids in she won't hear the whistling tea kettle. With and without the hearing aids she has forgotten that she turned the whistling tea kettle on. Time to get rid of the stove top tea kettle. Why I bought this kettle: I was looking for something for Mom that was small, lightweight and safe from spills. I liked the readable temperature display feature and easy temperature settings and of course the automatic shut off to prevent boiling dry. I thought this would work for Mom. Unfortunately with issues I had after trying out the product that I've listed above, this won't work for her. I also didn't take into consideration that with her crooked hands she would struggle to open and close the lid and struggle plug and unplug the kettle. And without a handle she would struggle to hold the kettle to pour the water. So add these physical limitations Mom has to the faults in the product I am returning the product.

title: Great Little Kettle
body: I am a person who reads reviews meticulously before buying online. I had hesitations about this one, but I’m glad I took the chance on it! This little kettle is perfect for my needs. When I read the reviews talking about how short the plug was, I was a little worried but I knew it wouldn’t affect my specific situation, so I bought it (the price point is great). When I got the kettle, it was well-packaged and came with a manual and plenty of warning and instruction labels. I also love the color! My favorite part is that, upon inspection, I realized that the cord is actually retractable into the base of the kettle! So if you hesitate like I did on that point, don’t worry about it. The cord is about 24” long when fully extended and winds back up into the base for easy storage (this has become one of my favorite features!) It fits right in a drawer when not in use, very nice for small spaces like mine! Apart from that, this little thing is great, makes hot water in just a few minutes. It holds just enough for one cup of tea or coffee so if you’re looking for something more, this little guy is not for you. When you take it off of the base after heating, the outside and bottom of the kettle is warm, but not hot — no need for potholders! It pours well, without leaking, except for a bit of steam coming out from the top at times (which it has a warning label for). It can be a tad noisy at times as it heats, but it doesn’t bother me in my situation. I could see it being a distraction or nuisance in a quiet office setting or something like that, though. If you’re looking for a safe, cheap, compact kettle for a single cup of boiling water, this is for you! I’ve had this for 4 months now, using it daily (multiple times per day) and it has stood the test, it works wonderfully and I am very satisfied with it for the price. Definitely fits all my needs!

I like the size for my purposes- however- all of the other electric kettles I've ever used have a release button for the lid and this one does not. It sounds like a stupid issue to have, but you must open the lid manually, which turns filling and rinsing this kettle into a two-handed operation as opposed to one-hand. Minor detail, but when in a hurry- like EVERY MORNING- it's an extra step, just a little clunky. Additionally, there is not a light to indicate when it's on- so it's easy to accidentally turn on and not know it since the switch is so sensitive and located on the handle itself. That's a problem, especially since it draws a ton of power. Redeeming feature: a recoiling cord = double-plus good. Every kettle should have that.

title: Finally—No More Cold Coffee!
body: I had been eyeing this House Gem Mug Warmer for a few weeks and finally decided to buy it—and I’m so glad I did. I work from home and love having a warm beverage nearby, but my coffee always ends up going cold before I finish it. This totally solved that problem. It came overnight so the moment it arrived; I plugged it in right away to read some e-mails with my morning coffee. When I came back with my coffee, it was already warm and ready to go. It’s very simple to use, and I love that it has three heat settings that correspond with night light colors: red (150 to 176 degrees Fahrenheit), purple (130 to 150 degrees Fahrenheit), and blue (105 to 130 degrees Fahrenheit). I assumed I would need the highest setting, but it actually heated my coffee too much, so I dropped it down to the middle temperature, which ended up being perfect. I also set the timer for four hours, which allowed it to automatically shut off—something I really appreciate when I get caught up in work. The warmer is attractive and modern looking. While it's slightly larger than some other versions I looked at, it’s still compact enough to fit on my desk without taking up too much space. And for once, the instructions were actually very user-friendly, which made setup quick and easy. Overall, this was a great purchase. It’s a small but meaningful upgrade to my home office setup, and I honestly wish I had gotten it sooner.

title: Does the job, but cord needs to be longer
body: I make my coffee by pour over. So, when I complete making a full cup (mug), it has already cooled down slightly. I guess I could place my mug on this warmer while I go through the process, but that is awkward. Anyway.... the first thing I do after the mug is full is place it on this warmer at the highest temperature setting. It takes about 5 minutes to get it to where I like it. I turn the warmer on before I start making my coffee so it is at max temperature when I place the mug down. I do have a flat surface mug. I have read reviews complaining about the temperature of the bottom of the warmer getting so hot it destroys the surface it is sitting on. I have not had the issue. When touching the bottom of the warmer, it is indeed warm, but not scorching hot. I guess it depends on the material and quality of surface you are setting it down on. Anyway, to be on the safe side, I place the warmer on a bowl, and set the bowl down on my table. The only complaint I have is the length of the power chord. My closest outlet at any of my seating positions leaves the cord floating in the air. I would not fret about the warning regarding use of an extension cord. The warmer is a low power device. Extension cords should not be used for things like microwaves, toaster ovens, refrigerators, etc. I use a 1,350 watt rated extension cord for this 36 watt warmer. I never leave it unattended. The advantage of the extension cord is not only keeping all cords flat on the floor, but it is also long enough where I can move the warmer to another location without unplugging.

First even though the warning area is drastically larger the overall unit is not much differences in overall size, good to not be to large for a desk. The 3 temps. are so handy, throw on a cool cup of coffee and set it to high. The cup heats up in maybe 10 minutes, then I turn it to low. My old one could not warm up a cooled down coffee at all. The old coffee warmer had a slide switch at the top of the warmer so you needed to remove the coffee cup before turning it off or on. The new ones switches are on the front edge and even though they are not touch switches an soft push controls them. I would buy this again.

title: Very nice device, but could be improved for elder use
body: This cup warmer does the trick, keeping drinks warm for hours, and taking little room. The controls are easy as well, and the display very readable. My elderly mother uses it, and she does struggle a bit with the controls, mainly that the temp control is part of the on/off cycle, so her preferred temp can’t be made the default but instead must be cycled to via repeated button presses. She often forgets to do that, setting the warmer on its hottest setting (the initial temp when turned on), which is too hot for her. It’d also be better if the last timer set was the default used when turned on, rather than always go back to 4 hours. So, the controls could be better for the elderly with poor memory.

body: This is the second cup warmer my husband has bought for me. Since we’re retired now we have a lot more time to drink our coffee, but unfortunately it gets cold and we have to keep warming it up in the microwave. The first one he bought me was nice, but nothing like this one, with all of its’ extras. I really loved it!, However, my husband was the first to notice a strange odor to his coffee. After awhile I picked up on it too. Upon further investigation, I realized it was coming from under the coffee warmer. I don’t know if it has anything to do with the wood. I went back to using my first one, and being more aware, I also noticed a smell coming from underneath that one too, but not quite as strong. title: (stop shopping) 3rd Brand of Coffee Warmers, 1st one that WORKS
body: Does everything as you would expect. Buttons are great, functionality, options to choose from. Please don't change the product. Couple of tips from an old guy that likes hot coffee: - Standard coffee cups have CONCAVE bottoms, so you want to cover your coffee cup. I have tried 3 warmers now, and my "favorite mug" will still lose heat with any desktop mug-warmer other than my STOVE. I spent a lot of money on a stainless, flat-bottom mug, but its not as big as I would like, and I still like my 30-year-old Dad Mug anyway. I am using the thermal lid that came with some random product (on top of my ancient mug), and I'm very happy. - (just saying) if you were to buy a flat-bottom mug, and use a LID for your cup, it will be TOO HOT to drink. The highest setting of this product is hot, and if you fix the heat escaping from the top, it will be hard to get any coffee into your body. It is that hot. - If you take your coffee seriously, and you get this product, you will want a PAD of some sort under this product. (See attached picture). This thing is a heater, it is excellent, and it normally sits 1/8" off of your desk. Your desk will get hot. I put 1/8" plexiglass/plastic under mine and my desk still gets hot. I went to hardware store and found some raised sticky FEET to raise that plexi, 1/8" off of my desk also. Now I'm not concerned about multiple years of extreme heat to 1 spot on my desk. - When I'm halfway done with my coffee, I can discard the lid, because the warmer will suffice on highest setting. I like my coffee to be hot. Sipping hot. With the lid on, and when coffee is low in my cup (easier to heat), I WOULD need to reduce the heat to be able to enjoy my coffee. - Now I have gotten lazy, and I just bring the coffee to the warmer (no lid) and if it starts off HOT, I enjoy it without a lot of delay, and then when it is 1/2-way down the cup, the heater can keep the temperature that I like anyway. - If you have a flat-bottom coffee cup, many heater-products can keep your coffee at a temperature that you like. I have 2 other warmers, both with great customer reviews, but without a lid none of them are great. This is the best one I have found, and with a LID on my cup, it works better than I want it to. Nice problem to have. I've finally found a way to drink coffee over 30 minutes. I'm buying another one for my other desk.

title: Almost Perfect Mug Warmer
body: Yes, I like this Mug Warmer very much; it's a lot better than my old one, even though (or maybe because) it doesn't have as many "features." My old one, which died giving birth to many sparks and sputterings, had 5 heat settings and a switch underneath to shut the unit off when the cup was removed. Many times I thought of taking that unit apart to bypass that bottom switch, because it was constantly annoying me by forcing me to turn the unit on again over and over in the same morning; this often happened when I was reheating coffee left over from the day before. I'm glad that this mug warmer doesn't have that feature; I found it more irritating than helpful, though I'm sure someone would want it. Another feature of my old warmer was that it had 5 different heat settings; not useful to me, as I only used one of them, and to get to that one setting I had to press the "on" switch four times, and twice more to turn it off. That's why I said this Mug Warmer is "almost" perfect: to be absolutely perfect I'd be able to set the temperature where I wanted it & then turn it on & off with one button press. Alas, this almost perfect unit still requires me to press the "on" button twice to turn it on to my temperature setting (150, or middle) and twice more to turn it off. This excellent Mug Warmer has more features that I don't really care about. It has LED lights which change color with different temperatures, or the lights can be turned off. I leave 'em on, but I don't change temperatures so they're not a lot of use (except to show me where the warmer is, when the room is dark.) There's also a button to change the length of time before the shut-off timer turns the unit off; for me that's totally unnecessary, as I always turn the warmer off manually, but I guess it's nice to know that eventually it'll turn itself off- though the settings are all way longer than I'd find useful. You can have times of 2 hrs, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 hours; I don't know why anyone would want a 12 hour shutoff, but maybe someone does for reasons that I can't think of. I do know my coffee would be undrinkable if I left it on the warmer for that long! For the TL:DR crowd, here's the bottom line: this excellent Mug Warmer keeps my mug warm just like I like it; I like its features, though I don't use them all & would prefer a one-button press on/off. All in all, I'm delighted with this Mug Warmer!

title: Love the size! Perfect for Soccer practice and games!
body: The Dysanky 1 Gallon Insulated Water Bottle is the ultimate hydration companion for those who need a larger volume of water on the go, whether you're at the gym, soccer practice, or simply running errands. With a sleek design and impressive functionality, this water bottle has a lot going for it. Design and Build Quality: At first glance, the bottle looks robust and built to last. The one-gallon capacity might seem intimidating at first, but it’s designed to be surprisingly portable. The high-quality stainless steel construction feels durable, and the matte finish adds a modern, stylish touch. The bottle is double-wall vacuum insulated, which means it’s not just tough on the outside but also effective at maintaining the temperature inside. Love the carry on case also! Insulation Performance: This is where the Dysanky really shines. It keeps your drinks cold and hot the whole day. Whether you’re dealing with summer heat or winter chills, this bottle does a great job of regulating temperature. For those long days out in the sun, you’ll appreciate the fact that your water stays cool and refreshing throughout the day. Ease of Use: The wide-mouth opening is a huge bonus, making it easy to fill, pour, or add ice cubes. The screw-on lid ensures that it stays securely sealed, so there are no leaks or spills even when you’re tossing it in a bag or car. The handle is comfortable, making it easy to carry, and while it’s larger than most bottles, it’s still relatively portable considering the size. Capacity: A gallon might seem like a lot, but it’s perfect for anyone who needs to stay hydrated for extended periods. Whether you're working out, on a road trip, or camping, you won’t need to worry about refilling your bottle constantly. That said, it’s not the most convenient for everyday use if you're just running errands, or you are at soccer practice or game, it's fantastic. Downsides: There are a couple of things to note. Due to its size, it can be a bit cumbersome if you're trying to fit it into a smaller bag or backpack. Additionally, it might be too large for someone who prefers a smaller, more compact water bottle. It’s also on the heavier side when full, but that’s to be expected given its capacity.

title: Keeps Water Cold, Built Like a Tank – Great for the Gym or Outdoors
body: I’ve only had the DYSANKY 64 oz insulated water bottle for a day, but it’s already proven to be exactly what I needed. This thing is solid. From the first time you pick it up, you can feel the quality—thick stainless steel, secure lid, and thoughtful design all around. The insulation works really well. I filled it with ice water in the morning, went through a full workout, ran errands, and still had ice hours later. That’s exactly what I wanted in a bottle of this size—cold water that actually stays cold. It’s ideal for long gym sessions, hikes, or just keeping hydrated throughout a busy day. The included straw lid is a nice bonus. It’s comfortable to use, doesn’t leak, and makes sipping easy without unscrewing anything. The carrier bag and handle strap are more useful than I expected—especially since this bottle holds a half gallon and can get heavy when full. The strap makes it super easy to carry around or sling over a shoulder while walking or hiking. The overall construction feels tough and durable, but still looks clean. I like that it’s BPA-free, and everything seems designed with actual user convenience in mind. The wide mouth also makes it easy to clean and load with ice. ⸻ Pros: • Keeps water cold for hours (ice retention is excellent) • Straw lid is easy to use and leak-free • Includes carrier bag and handle strap for portability • Sturdy, thick stainless steel construction • Holds a full 64 oz—perfect for workouts or all-day hydration • Easy to clean Cons: • It’s big, and heavy when full (not a con for me, but worth noting) • Might not fit easily in standard car cup holders due to its size ⸻ Final Thoughts: If you’re looking for a high-capacity water bottle that actually keeps your drinks cold and can handle being tossed around in a gym bag or taken on a trail, this is a great choice. After one day of use, I can already tell it’s going to become part of my daily routine. Comfortable to carry, easy to drink from, and built to last—definitely happy with this purchase.

title: I am impressed
body: I live in Arizona, it was 117 degrees yesterday. I put ice water in this water bottle, went to a baseball double header, came home, left my water bottle in the car for the next day and a half and it still had ice. The water bottle itself is great, keeps things cold for hours and hours, even sitting in the direct AZ 111 degree sun. The 40 oz isn't bulky like some others and I really appreciate not only the 2 lid options but the extra straws and everything to clean them and the water bottle. Love the corded handle with a compass which is separate from the carrying bag so you don't have to choose one or the other. The carrying bag is the exact color of the waterbottle, gradient and all and comes with a longer strap you can wear over your shoulder and pockets for snack bar money or credit cards. Extra clips and a carabeaner on the eater bottle itself. Overall this thing is so cool and I couldn't find anything close, especially at this quality for such a great price.

title: Ice cold all day!!
body: I bought this back when it was still fairly cool out, wasn't really expecting it to be anything extraordinary once it started heating up outside, just wanted to be able to have alot of water on me that wouldn't be warm halfway through the day. Well we're just now at the end of a severe heat wave, (102-105° for 4-5 days straight) and this thing has stayed ICE COLD every single day. I work in a truck that has no A/C and is also a cab over, and this thing sits on my dash in the direct sunlight all day while also being baked from the engine heat underneath for 12-13 hours a day, and not once has it been any less cold than it was when I filled it in the morning. Only issue I've found is the sleeve it's inside of is not very durable, and the bottom has already started to fray from the sliding around on my dash, but other than that it's a tank. 550 cord grip is solid as well as the handle built into the spout top. I'll definitely be buying another if I can find an excuse to.

Download the following apps:
1. Autohidedesktop icons (self explanatory)
2. Powertoys (allows you to take advantage of the massive screen by splitting up your windows into whatever sections you want.  Then you can simply drag and snap each into place.
3. Autohidemousecursor (self explanatory)

In addition. Have a black background so when your mouse and icons disappear,  your monitor essentially "turns off. "  Also a minimal screen saver in case your on a program and it stays idle.

There are some additional options on the LG TV options such as screen shift.  As a safety precaution run pixel cleaner once a week.

title: Read Before Unboxing
body:
Unboxing - The thin tv is more fragile than you are used to.  Read the instructions and watch the youtube videos.  The included instructions are decent but the videos show tricks for making sure you don't crack your screen.

Important - Before you do anything, take a photo of the TV's serial number and file it and a downloaded copy of the manual and a copy of the receipt somewhere secure. If you bought extra insurance (I got five years), add that.  If you put it on a credit card (the best way to insure it if you break it), have a copy of that.

Adding the base - Written instructions did not work for me.  Instead of laying the TV on a table to add the base, use the box it came in with some of the packing materials in it. The TV has to be high enough from the floor such that the stand clears it, otherwise the screws won't tighten (clearly the case with one reviewer).  I watched three videos, all with slightly different approaches, to figure out how to do this.  I added the base and stood the TV up by myself by keeping the tv in the styrofoam until I was done. It was not easy.

TV - This TV was a clear favorite among the experts (e,g, tvfinder.com).  Our old Samsung TV was over 15 years old and still working fine but we needed better audio. The improvement in video is pronounced with this TV but not as dramatic as it was the first time we watched high def.  Voices are definitely clearer but music was much improved once I set up the LG SPD7Y sound bar and subwoofer.

I am sure there is an explanation for it but Adele's One Night Only and the CMA Music Awards sounded better and much louder when I played it from my Amazon Fire Stick than through the LG Smart App for Youtube TV.  Visuals were about the same. That's good because I already know how to use the Fire Stick remote.

I suppose I will like their Magic remote more after I have learned how to use it but right now I can't easily go from the cursor to the ring and the cursor makes unintended selections.  I also don't know why they didn't put backlghts on the thing. Being able to program all of the number keys to go directly to desired locations is a useful addition. I needed a second remote but decided to buy a $10 EWO Universal Remote Control for All LG Smart TVs rather than $50 for a replacement magic remote just to avoid the cursor issue (and to save money).

title: Hard to beat this price for a solid 4K TV.
body:
I’ll start by stating the obvious, this isn’t the best 4K TV out there.....BUT......at $300 for a 55” 4K TV delivered to your door it’s one heck of a deal!

I’ve put a solid 2 weeks use into this TV and I’m pleased with it so far! I’m coming from a 52” 1080p Samsung television and this TCL picture blows it away with 4K PlayStation gaming and watching TV through my 4K Firestick.

Negatives:
- Screen brightness is definitely an issue and could be a deal breaker if you can’t position TV away from windows or bright lighting. Even the top brightness isn’t super bright for some situations, Luckily windows aren’t an issue with where our stand is.

- Remote is HORRIBLE and required to keep handy. Every time you turn TV on it defaults to the Roku home screen and you have to select the input you want to use. They are strong arming you to use their interface. I would do that if their apps or “channels” as the call them weren’t washed out looking.

- Amazon Prime channel and other “app” interfaces through Roku home menu looks horrible. The videos themselves play fine but the menus look washed out compared to on a Firestick. To remedy this I just use my Firestick to run everything on this TV and it looks great in full 4K. Btw be sure to use the ARC enabled HDMI 3 slot for your Firestick as that’s the only slot that supports HDCP 2.2 and will allow full playback of 4K.

Warranty!
We opted to add a 3 year warranty bringing our total price to $326 + tax. Hopefully we don’t have to use the warranty but lots of reviews point to longevity issues around 1-2 years of ownership. These prices are crazy so it makes you wonder how they can sell these so cheap.... Warranty is a good idea!

title: Excellent picture,  OLED allows brightness for viewers sitting oblique QLED does not do as well
body:
Ultra slim, reasonably lightweight, economic on electricity. Trade journals and repair locations I consulted say what was predicted is happening, namely that these Organic LED screens will BURN-IN. Something we haven't seen since the HD Plasma's first hit the market in 1997. People old enough to buy these since burn-in went out of existence may never have heard of burn-in and LG doesn't tell them it's back. Sales manuals don't inform sales teams about this, so sales people won't mention it, and when told of it they are in denial. When you pause on a brilliant image for a phone call, to answer a door, or have dinner IF the TV's "fireworks screensaver" doesn't kick-in, then burn-in is a risk.  When will the screen saver not engage? When your OEM DVR or Blu-Ray is not under the command of the LG processor and they are paused (see also screen ratios below that cause black borders).

All of that aside even if the LG can activate a screen saver it won't do it if you are using the TV playing shows or movies with a screen ratio like 2.5:1, 4:3, or 16:x9 (widescreen) for example, or any other ratio where IF you don't zoom to fill the screen with the full  image. In other words Burn-In can occur when black borders are appearing on the TV for the duration of a show or movie in those screen ratios. LG's screen saver won't prevent burn-in for the prolonged dark areas. If you do a lot of watching some network that keeps its logo up repeatedly that's a risk that extends across multiple viewings even if watching different movies.  While LG doesn't mention burn-in, they do suggest when you have borders in something you are viewing that you zoom in to eliminate the borders. Great, so  when you are watching Lawrence of Arabia or the Ten Commandments, or worse How The West Was Won you have to zoom in and clip out Omar Sharif, Gregory Peck ,or Charlton Heston and the held back images of the Red Sea when they are in the periphery. Zooming in the older & lower ratios clips headroom and floors. I would call that zoom suggestion by LG's manual a "patch" for a serious problem LG did not solve. One reviewer here suggested buying the extended warranty for OLEDs of any brand, I say ditto! If LG can prevent Burn-In without telling you to zoom everything then OLED would be the best picture you can get now.

The remote for this set tries to be universal, but it won't do the TiVo DVR remote. It handled my Panasonic Blu-Ray DVD player, but not all of its functions. In my opinion/experience LG support was weak.

The pictures are OLED screens with burn-in from the Internet. The picture's show both typical, and the  extreme. Both screens are being fed only a monochromatic color so that the burn-in ghost image stands out in these pictures.

title: Great TV with bad CEC integration
body:
I purchased a new LG C1 65" OLED about a week ago.  The TV picture is fantastic.  I'm coming from an old $800 TCL LED TV, so I could only go up from there, but the LG is absolutely stunning.  My favorite part (and my favorite part of any OLED) is the black pixels are as black as you can get.  Makes watching a movie with black bars or dark scenes just POP.

So before you read the next part, know that I WOULD recommend this TV.  However, I think it's Achilles heel is the janky CEC "SimpleLink" integration.  If this isn't something you will use, then stop reading here and BUY THIS TV!

Ok - on to the major annoyance.  I've been having a lot of issues getting the CEC / SimpleLink connection to work correctly with all of my devices.  This is something that my 5 year old TCL Roku TV was able to do without so much as a stutter, so it's unfortunate I'm having so many issues with my 2021 model.

The main issue is the TV turning on to the last input, waking up that device, then switching to the source that woke the TV.  For example, from an "off" state, if I press power on my Apple TV remote but was using my PS5 last, the TV boots for a second to the PS5 source which wakes up/turns on the PS5, then switches to the Apple TV.  I'm having the same issue with the Apple TV being turned on when using my PS5 (but while that's less of an issue because I don't mind if the Apple TV is on, it's still annoying).  I'm also having issues getting the TV to turn off when powering down a CEC connected device.  When turning off my Apple TV, the TV shuts off correctly.  However, when turning off my PS5 or Nintendo Switch, the TV shows a "no source detected" screen and must be manually shut down by finding the remote and hitting the power button.  Yeah, I know - first world problems.

The only way around this that I've found (that only works sometimes) is first by turning off QuickStart+, and then putting the TV in "hotel" (commercial) mode where I set the default start-up channel to HDMI 1 (my Apple TV).  Though the TV still turns on to the PS5 HDMI input for a second (assuming I was using it last), it quickly switches to HDMI1 without turning on the PS5.  Again, this ONLY works when using the commercial mode with a default start-up input AND QuickStart+ to off.  Without having the TV in "Commercial" mode and turning quickstart+ off, the TV still turns on my PS5 whenever I turn it on.  Two downsides to "commercial/hotel" mode.  I can't use any of the "smart" Alexa and Google-enabled features on my TV because when in commercial mode it doesn't seem to allow app/smart speaker connections.  It also removes some options from the settings (obviously things you wouldn't want someone in a hotel room messing with).

It seems like the CEC SimpleLink connection in the LG is the Achilles heel in an otherwise great TV.  There are hundreds of threads about this issue on Reddit and other support sites across the internet.  It kills me that LG hasn't added more granular control to allow, for example, devices to change inputs without being started up automatically by the TV.  Or allowing devices that shut off their input to also automatically shut down the TV.

If they could make my connected devices (Apple TV, Nintendo Switch, PS5, and ARC connected Vizio soundbar) work as intended without using a janky workaround like commercial mode and disabling quickstart+, this TV would EASILY have 5 stars.

I hope this review makes it to the engineers - I have no doubt this could be fixed with a software update.  If my 5 year old cheap Roku TV could do it, this one should be able to as well.

title: The negative reviews: a fact check...
body:
I really like these rugs in the runner size and have one in the hall, and another in the bedroom, at the base of the bed. For what you pay, you get tremendous value. Both are the burgundy color, and add a lot of color and warmth to my home.

Some facts:

- They do off-gas, and that's what folks complaining about the smell are talking about. Almost any rug that you buy with a non-slip backing or a glue binder will do this for a while after they've been opened. Carpet will also do this after it has been installed. It's definitely noticable for a day or two, and I recommend you try to keep it outside for a bit, opened and unrolled, if possible before bringing it in. I'm sure it's not healthy, but I have asthma and haven't been triggered by the runners, that I'm aware of.

- The folks upset about washing this: why are you putting a rug like this in a washer? If you have a very large front-loading drum washer, MAYBE. But it's not the manufacturer's fault it falls apart of you're using a top-loading washer, it's your own. Vacuuming and spot cleaning seems like enough, even for a high traffic hallway. I use a Roomba on it daily and it's holding up. I also have a cat and the hairballs are easy to clean with a little water, soap, and a rag.

- OK, so, the big thing I keep seeing is the colors are faded or inconsistent: and they're supposed to be. Folks, this is supposed to have a weathered vibe, it's part of the aesthetic and trend with this style. So, neither rug I bought is precisely identical even though they were purchased on the same date, same size, same color. The color is the same, but the fading is what's a little different. It's not extreme, not like part of it was exposed to the sun, while the rest wasn't; it's a style choice, look it up.

Because of the off-gassing, I would be hesitant to buy a very large rug from this brand unless it was summer and I could safely let this rest outside for a bit before bringing it in. But the brand is solid, you get great bang for your buck, and it's a hard recommend-you-buy from me. Four stars overall because these aren't the fanciest rugs in the world; but they're pretty dang good.
